classes.name: stzAgentDeclaration
classes.brief: Reads and judges a .pia agent file at load, then builds the runnable agent it declares if, and only if, no rule is broken.
classes.description: An agent is a file: name, kind (pi acts, llm proposes), a coverage sentence, a reversibility class, a schedule, optional seed facts, governance, skills in a small closed vocabulary (always, fact, no-fact, recall, learn, forget, propose, ring:), or a proposal for an llm agent. The declaration is judged in the constructor and every broken rule becomes a finding: IsValid, Findings and CiteFindings read the verdict, and ToAgent refuses to build from a refused one. Reading never calls a model or a network. The format version is 2; version 1 is still read.
classes.receiver: c = "pia: 2" + char(10) + "name: kitchen-bot" + char(10) + "kind: pi" + char(10) + "coverage: watches stock" + char(10) + "reversibility: compensable" + char(10) + "schedule:" + char(10) + "  timer: 20" + char(10) + "skills:" + char(10) + "  - name: restock" + char(10) + "    does: learn stock level ordered" o1 = new stzAgentDeclaration(c, "kitchen.pia")
classes.example:
? o1.IsValid()
#--> 1
? o1.Name_()
#--> kitchen-bot
? o1.Schedule()[:timer]
#--> 20
? o1.NumberOfSkills()
#--> 1
? o1.ToAgent().Cycle()
#--> 1

A changed .ring file is NOT re-evaluated, because Ring cannot unload a function and re-loading it is a C22 redefinition that takes the library down. classes.name: stzAgentHost
classes.brief: Supervises agents as cancellable, traced, quarantinable and decommissionable jobs ticked on a timer or on events.
classes.description: A host owns a reactor, or shares one. It ticks each supervised agent through its Cycle, on its own timer or once per event of a bus channel, and records a trace. Cancel is a pause anyone can undo; Quarantine is a containment act that only an effectful actor can lift with Release; Retire is permanent and earned, refused until the declared decommission obligations are fulfilled. SetActionBudget caps the acts an agent may take in a window and quarantines a runaway. UseEngineLoop hands the scheduling decision to the engine, which refuses an agent that states neither what it covers nor how reversible it is. UseAgentsFrom mounts agents written as files. The host keeps a copy of each agent: configure it fully before Supervise and reach it afterwards through AgentQ.

classes.name: stzAmount
classes.brief: Holds an amount of money as whole minor units and an ISO 4217 currency, so it can never be a bare number.
classes.description: An amount cannot be built without a currency, and the library refuses what could not be paid exactly: a fraction finer than the currency's minor unit (50.5 in XOF, because a franc has no fraction), a fractional number, a currency it does not know, and arithmetic or ordering across two currencies. It is never rounded. Money is spelled as text, "12.50", never computed as a float. The exponent is ISO 4217's: 0 for XOF and XAF, 2 for EUR, 3 for TND. An amount is immutable: Plus, Minus, TimesInteger and Negated answer a new amount. Nothing is converted between currencies, and no rate exists.
classes.example:
? o1.Display()
#--> 150 000 FCFA
? o1.MinorUnits()
#--> 150000
? StzAmountQ("12.50", "EUR").MinorUnits()
#--> 1250
? o1.Plus(StzAmountQ("40000", "XOF")).Display()
#--> 190 000 FCFA

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an amount from a value and an ISO 4217 currency code, refusing any value that could not be paid exactly.

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the amount as text such as "12.50", or as a whole number of major units

parameters.name: pcCurrency
parameters.role: an ISO 4217 code such as XOF or EUR, in any case

notes: a whole number is read in major units, so 5 in EUR is 5.00; trailing zeros past the exponent change nothing, so "5000.00" in XOF is 5000
warnings: raises an error for a missing or unknown currency, for a fraction finer than the currency's minor unit ("50.5" in XOF), for a fractional number (50.5), for a value that is neither text nor a number, and beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; an amount is never rounded

methods.name: Currency
methods.brief: Returns the ISO 4217 code of the amount, in capitals, whatever case it was built with.

methods.name: Exponent
methods.brief: Returns the number of decimals of the currency's minor unit, as ISO 4217 gives it: 0 for XOF, 2 for EUR, 3 for TND.
notes: the exponent is ISO 4217's, not the country table's: a franc CFA has none

methods.name: MinorUnits
methods.brief: Returns the amount as a whole number of the currency's smallest unit: 150000 for 150 000 XOF, 1250 for 12.50 EUR.
methods.returns: a number, negative for a negative amount
notes: this is the figure a payment carries; keep the amount object and read it last

methods.name: IsZero
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is exactly zero.

methods.name: IsPositive
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is strictly above zero; zero is not positive.

methods.name: IsNegative
methods.brief: TRUE if the amount is strictly below zero.

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the amount as plain decimal text with its currency's own number of places and its sign, with no grouping and no currency.
methods.returns: a text such as 1250.50, or 150000 for XOF

methods.name: Display
methods.brief: Returns the amount as a reader of the UEMOA reads it: thousands grouped by spaces, then the currency, FCFA for both XOF and XAF.
methods.returns: a text such as 150 000 FCFA or 1 250.50 EUR

methods.name: Plus
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is the sum of this one and another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to add, in the same currency

methods.returns: a new amount; neither operand changes
notes: the symbol + between two amounts calls this
warnings: raises an error for another currency, for something that is not an amount, and for a result beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; francs and euros are never added

methods.name: Minus
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is this one less another of the same currency, negative when the other is larger.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to take away, in the same currency

methods.returns: a new amount; neither operand changes
notes: the symbol - between two amounts calls this
warnings: raises an error for another currency, for something that is not an amount, and for a result beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units

methods.name: TimesInteger
methods.brief: Returns a new amount that is this one repeated a whole number of times, which may be zero or negative.

parameters.name: pn
parameters.role: the whole-number multiplier

notes: a rate would need a rounding rule, and a payment has none to give
warnings: raises an error for a fraction or for something that is not a number, and beyond 2^53 - 1 minor units; there is no rate and no rounding

methods.name: Negated
methods.brief: Returns a new amount of the same size and the opposite sign.

methods.name: Equals
methods.brief: TRUE if the other value is an amount of the same currency and the same size; anything else answers FALSE without an error.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the value to compare, normally an amount

notes: 150000 XOF and "150000.00" XOF are equal; 150000 XOF and 150000 EUR are not

methods.name: IsGreaterThan
methods.brief: TRUE if this amount is larger than another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to compare with, in the same currency

warnings: raises an error for another currency or for something that is not an amount: amounts of two currencies have no order

methods.name: IsLessThan
methods.brief: TRUE if this amount is smaller than another of the same currency.

parameters.name: poOther
parameters.role: the amount to compare with, in the same currency

warnings: raises an error for another currency or for something that is not an amount: amounts of two currencies have no order

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Answers the sum or the difference of two amounts of one currency when they are written with the symbol + or -.

parameters.name: pOp
parameters.role: the symbol, + or -

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the other amount

notes: a + b is Plus and a - b is Minus
warnings: any other symbol raises an error naming TimesInteger for multiples; the symbol = is deliberately not defined, so compare with Equals

classes.name: stzApp
classes.brief: Holds an application as a world of meaning: its things, instances, flows, reactions, goals, screens and reach, declared in plain words.
classes.description: Declare things with AddThing and their fields with Has, then instances and relations with AddInstance and Relate: these form a graph. Flows, reactions, goals, screens and refinements are cursor builders, each plain verb acting on the one declared last, and each verb has a Q form that returns the world so a brace can follow: AddGoalQ(:Visited) { Means = "every :Client Has(:visited)" }. A goal is a wanted state of the graph; Pursue measures its gap and proposes how to close it through the reactions, and Live and Pulse fire the reactions themselves. Explain prints the whole world in words. The world only describes: a stzPlatform wraps it to build, generate shells and serve it.
classes.example:
o1.AddThingQ("Client").Has([ "code", "name" ])
? o1.Things()[1][1]
#--> Client
o1.AddInstance("anna", "Client")
o1.AddReactionQ("Client").Propose("Visit")
? o1.Pulse()
#--> 1
? o1.Proposals()[1][4]
#--> anna

classes.name: stzAppBackend
classes.brief: Serves a solution's datasets as live shared state over a real loopback server, so every part reads and writes the same records.
classes.description: A solution model gives each part a role over a dataset, but the datasets are frozen lists. Start turns them into sqlite tables served by a real server in this process, and the parts then Create, Rows, RowCount and Dashboard by real HTTP round trips on the loopback: what one part writes, another sees. Writes are governed (SetActor: only an effectful actor commits; reads stay open) and every crossing is recorded in Traffic with its duration. The same API also drives a backend in another process (ConnectTo, SpawnRemote), signed with a shared key (SetSigningKey), which is required to leave the loopback. Known limits: the reply is parsed by splitting on commas, so a cell containing a comma splits in two; Dashboard expects a dish and a quantity.
classes.receiver: oT = new stzAppTopology("demo") oT.AddDatasetQ("menu", [ [ "Tajine", "clay pot", 15 ] ]) oT.SetDatasetColumnsQ("menu", [ "name", "descr", "price" ]) oT.AddDatasetQ("orders", [ [ "Tajine", 1 ] ]) oT.SetDatasetColumnsQ("orders", [ "dish", "qty" ]) oT.SetPartRoleQ(:phone, "menu", "menu") oT.SetPartRoleQ(:admin, "dashboard", "orders") o1 = new stzAppBackend("demo", oT) o1.Start(0)
classes.example:
? o1.IsLive()
#--> 1
? o1.RowCount(:admin, "orders")
#--> 1
? o1.Create(:phone, "orders", [ [ "dish", "Tajine" ], [ "qty", 2 ] ])
#--> 1
? o1.RowCount(:admin, "orders")
#--> 2
? o1.Dashboard(:admin)[2]
#--> 45
? o1.TrafficCount()
#--> 4
o1.Stop()

classes.name: stzAppCluster
classes.brief: Declares a fleet of worker processes by facet and proxies requests to them round-robin, with failover, circuit breakers, rate limits and latency telemetry.
classes.description: Ring's virtual machine runs one thread, so CPU-bound work is spread over processes: a cluster is a front object plus worker processes, each its own Ring program serving health and work addresses, started and queried through the reactor. Declare the fleet with WithNLP, WithMath, WithSearch, WithVision or WithFacet (any facet of the catalog), AddProfile for a custom one, or RegisterExternalWorker for a worker that already runs. Start spawns the processes, WaitReady waits for their health answers, and Route sends a path to a ready worker of a facet, failing over to the next worker and opening a circuit on a worker that keeps failing. The declaring, reading and refusing parts of this reference were run; Start, the success path of Route and the scale, restart and kill methods start or contact real processes and were read from the code only.

methods.name: init

parameters.name: nWorkers
parameters.role: how many processes to declare, at least 1

notes: declaring the same tag again adds to its worker count, and every row waits with port 0 until Start
warnings: it raises an error for fewer than one worker

parameters.name: nThreshold

parameters.name: nCooldownMs

classes.name: stzAppServer
classes.brief: Hosts routes, a REST floor over a database, raw device streams and supervised agents on one resident event loop, served on a localhost-first HTTP listener.
classes.description: The server is a persistent host rather than a per-request library: Start binds a listener on a reactor (an engine thread), and the serve loop (ServeOne, RunFor or Run) drains framed requests, runs the matching handler and writes the answer back; no callback ever crosses into the Ring VM. One host serves four shapes. WEB: Get_, Post, Put_ and Delete add routes whose handlers receive a request and a response. MBaaS: Expose and ExposeWithKey turn a stzDatabase table into list, count and read, create, update, delete routes. IoT: ListenRaw opens a raw TCP listener whose handler answers with RawWrite. AGENTS: HostAgents attaches an agent host that shares the loop and ticks between serve slices, with a read-only view at GET /agents. /health is always answered and /metrics appears once Observe attaches a perf monitor. Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless the server must be reached from outside, and then call RequireSignedRequests; MountAuth and MountOidcProvider serve a login router and an identity provider from the same listener. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Use and Static store their arguments but never act, and Stop leaves Port and Uptime unreset.
classes.example:
o1.Get_("/greet", func oReq, oResp { oResp.Text("hello") })
o1.Start(0, "127.0.0.1")
? o1.IsRunning()
#--> 1
o1.Stop()

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a stopped server with an empty route table; nothing listens until a start method is called.
notes: Routes, mounts and observation can all be set up before Start

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Binds an HTTP listener to a host and port, port 0 meaning any free one; raises an error if it cannot bind or already runs.

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

notes: Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless the server is meant to be reached from other machines, and then require signed requests

methods.name: StartTls
methods.brief: Binds an HTTPS listener that decrypts each connection before routing; raises an error when a certificate, key or CA file cannot be used.
usage: StartTls(nPortNum, cHostAddr, cCertPath, cKeyPath, cCaPath, bRequireClient)

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: cCertPath
parameters.role: the server certificate file

parameters.name: cKeyPath
parameters.role: the private key file

parameters.name: cCaPath
parameters.role: the CA file that checks client certificates, "" for none

parameters.name: bRequireClient
parameters.role: 1 to demand a valid client certificate (mutual TLS)

notes: The failing path was run with missing files (error -13); the success path was read from the body, as no certificate was available

methods.name: StartHttps
methods.brief: Binds a one-way HTTPS listener, with a server certificate and key but no client certificate check.

parameters.name: nPortNum
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free port

parameters.name: cHostAddr
parameters.role: the address to bind, "" for 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: cCertPath
parameters.role: the server certificate file

parameters.name: cKeyPath
parameters.role: the private key file

notes: Same as StartTls with an empty CA and no client check

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Closes the HTTP and raw listeners and destroys the reactor; does nothing when the server is not running.
methods.returns: the server, so calls can be chained
notes: Routes and mounts are kept for the next Start, but Port and Uptime are not reset (see their notes)

methods.name: IsRunning
methods.brief: TRUE if a listener is bound, from a successful start until the next stop.

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the HTTP listener is bound to, the real one when 0 was asked for.
methods.returns: a number; 0 before the first start
notes: The value is kept after Stop, so it names the last port used rather than a live one

methods.name: Host
methods.brief: Returns the address given to the last start.

methods.name: Uptime
methods.brief: Returns the seconds since the last start, as a number with decimals.
methods.returns: a number of seconds; 0 before the first start
notes: It keeps growing after Stop, because the start time is not cleared

methods.name: RequestCount
methods.brief: Returns how many HTTP requests the server has handled, including malformed ones answered with 400.
notes: The counter is never reset, not even by Stop

methods.name: ReactorQ
methods.brief: Returns the stzReactor that runs the listeners, to read or drive it directly.
methods.returns: an stzReactor; an empty string when the server is not running

methods.name: ServeOne
methods.brief: Waits for one request, HTTP or raw, answers it, and returns; gives up after the timeout.

parameters.name: nTimeoutMs
parameters.role: the longest wait, in milliseconds

methods.returns: TRUE if a request was handled, FALSE on timeout
notes: Accept and close events are drained along the way and do not count as work
warnings: Raises an error when the server is not running

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Serves every request that arrives within a number of milliseconds, ticking hosted agents between slices.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: how long to serve, in milliseconds

notes: With agents hosted, each wait on the socket is cut to AgentSlice ms so the agents keep ticking on an idle socket

methods.name: Run
methods.brief: Serves requests until Stop is called from a handler or the process is killed, ticking hosted agents between slices.
methods.returns: the server, once the server is stopped
notes: Not run here because it blocks: described from its body, a loop of ServeOne(1000) while the server is running

methods.name: RequireSignedRequests
methods.brief: Refuses with 401 every request that lacks a valid HMAC signature, /health included; raises an error for a skew under 1 ms.

parameters.name: poSigner
parameters.role: the stzRequestSigner that holds the shared secrets

parameters.name: pnMaxSkewMs
parameters.role: the clock-skew window in milliseconds, at least 1

methods.returns: nothing; the server is changed in place
notes: The signature travels in the query parameters _kid, _ts, _nonce and _sig; a replayed nonce and a wrong signature are refused too. The server keeps a copy of the signer, so its replay ledger is the server's own

classes.name: stzAuth
classes.brief: Authenticates the users of an app: keeps salted password hashes, opens and ends sessions, and resolves a login into roles and an actor.
classes.description: It holds a credential store (user name to a salted Argon2id hash, never the plaintext) and issues opaque 64-character session tokens. Around the password it offers a second factor (TOTP with recovery codes), passwordless doors (magic link, emailed code, passkey), external sign-in (OpenID Connect, SAML), a brute-force lockout, an administrative lock, password reset by mail, and roles that turn a live session into the stzSystemActor that governance reasons about. The store is in memory unless SetStore is given a database store. Every flow has an At form that takes the moment as epoch seconds, which makes expiry and lockout testable; the plain forms read the clock. Failures answer an empty text, 0 or [ ] instead of raising, except for a missing mail port, relying party, provider or client, which raise.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an authenticator with an empty in-memory store, the four built-in roles and a one-hour session lifetime.
notes: defaults: sessions last 3600 s, no idle limit, 5 failed logins lock a user out for 900 s, magic links and codes last 900 s, reset links 1800 s, a new password needs 8 characters

classes.brief: Keeps the users, sessions, two-factor rows, challenges, roles, passkeys and locks of stzAuth in a sqlite database, so they outlive the process.

classes.name: stzBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws a list of numbers, or labelled numbers, as vertical bars: as text for a terminal, as SVG, or as a PNG picture.
classes.description: One plot object answers three ways. ToString (and Show) draws block characters, axes and labels in text; ToSVG needs no graphics device; ToPNG draws on the GPU. The setters (height, bar width and spacing, axes, labels, values, percentages, average line, characters) shape the text picture only: the SVG and PNG carry the values, the labels, AddValues and AddAverage and nothing else, and print no text unless a :Font option is given. Bars are scaled so the largest value fills the height. Setters answer nothing, so they cannot be chained. stzHBarPlot (sideways bars) and stzMBarPlot (grouped bars) inherit from it. Several settings store a value no picture reads today (SetWidth, SetMaxWidth and the width of SetSize), SetMaxLabelWidth does not truncate, and SetLabelChar renames labels taken from the keys; see their warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzBarPlot/basic.png (average line), values.png (values above twelve bars) and nofont.png (no font: bars and gridlines only), each with its .ring script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

classes.name: stzBinaryNumber
classes.brief: Holds a number written in binary and converts it to decimal, octal and hexadecimal, or builds it from them.
classes.description: It is the binary form behind stzNumber.ToBinaryForm: a stzNumber builds one with new stzBinaryNumber(cText), and you can build one yourself with new stzBinaryNumber("0b1011") or StzBinaryNumberQ("0b1011"). The text starts with b or 0b, followed by binary digits and optionally a dot and more digits; an empty text gives zero. Content returns the text as given, prefix included. ToDecimalForm, ToOctalForm and ToHexForm convert (by hand 0b1011 is 8+2+1 = 11 = 0o13 = 0xB), and FromDecimalForm, FromHexForm and FromOctalForm replace the number in place, the last two needing the 0x and 0o prefixes. The Bitwise methods work on the decimal value and answer a number. Whole numbers convert exactly; the fractional part is exact in decimal and octal but ToHexForm drops it. Several methods are broken today and each says so in its own entry: IntegerPart and Reversed raise R24 when a dot is present, WithPrefix doubles the prefix, the reversals reverse the prefix with the digits, ToScientificNotationForm raises R14, and an uppercase 0B prefix reads as 0.
classes.example:
? o1.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 11
? o1.ToOctalForm()
#--> 0o13
? o1.ToHexForm()
#--> 0xB
? o1.BitwiseAND(6)
#--> 2
? o1.BitwiseLeftShift(2)
#--> 44
o2 = new stzBinaryNumber("0b101.11")
? o2.ToDecimalForm()
#--> 5.75
o3 = new stzBinaryNumber("")
o3.FromDecimalForm(12500)
? o3.Content()
#--> 0b11000011010100

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a binary number from a text such as 0b1011, or a zero binary number from an empty text.

parameters.name: cNumber
parameters.role: the number as a text starting with b or 0b, followed by binary digits and optionally a dot and more digits, or an empty text for zero, anything else raises an error

notes: an empty text gives the content b0; it is reached from stzNumber.ToBinaryForm and from StzBinaryNumberQ(cNumber)
warnings: the uppercase prefix 0B is accepted but its value is read as 0: new stzBinaryNumber("0B101").ToDecimalForm() answers 0 where 5 is right; -0b101 is accepted and reads as -5, but 0b-101, the text FromDecimalForm(-5) builds, is refused

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the binary number as it was written, prefix included.
notes: Value and BinaryNumber are the same call

methods.name: BinaryNumber
methods.brief: Returns the binary number as it was written, prefix included.
notes: the same call as Content

methods.name: WithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the content with the binary prefix put in front of it.
notes: use Content to read the number; the prefix comes from BinaryNumberPrefix(), 0b by default
warnings: the prefix is added even though the content already starts with one: 0b1011 answers 0b0b1011 and b1111 answers 0bb1111

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Applies a bitwise operator written as text to the number and a second number.

parameters.name: pOp
parameters.role: the operator as text, one of & (and), a pipe (or), ^ (xor), ~ (complement), << or >>

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the second operand, ignored by ~

methods.returns: a number, the result of the operation; an empty text for an operator that is not listed
notes: 0b1011 with & and 6 gives 2, with << and 1 gives 22
warnings: an unknown operator such as + answers an empty text without an error

methods.name: BitwiseAND
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise AND of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 and 0110 give 0010: 0b1011 with 6 answers 2

methods.name: BitwiseOR
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise OR of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 or 0110 give 1111: 0b1011 with 6 answers 15

methods.name: BitwiseXOR
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise exclusive OR of the number and another number.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: the second operand, a decimal number

notes: by hand 1011 xor 0110 give 1101: 0b1011 with 6 answers 13

methods.name: BitwiseOnesComplement
methods.brief: Returns the bitwise complement of the number, which is minus the number minus one.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: required by the signature but ignored

methods.returns: a number, negative for a positive number
notes: 0b1011 (11) answers -12 and 0b110 (6) answers -7, whatever the argument is

methods.name: BitwiseLeftShift
methods.brief: Returns the number shifted left by some bits, which doubles it once per bit.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: how many bits to shift

notes: 0b1011 shifted by 2 gives 44, by hand 101100

methods.name: BitwiseRightShift
methods.brief: Returns the number shifted right by some bits, which halves it once per bit, dropping the remainder.

parameters.name: nOtherNumber
parameters.role: how many bits to shift

notes: 0b1011 shifted by 1 gives 5, by hand 101

methods.name: IntegerPart
methods.brief: Returns the part of the content before the dot; a number without a dot is returned whole.
methods.returns: a text, with its prefix kept
notes: the prefix is part of the answer: 0b1011 gives 0b1011
warnings: with a fractional part it raises error R24 (uninitialized variable _oTempStr_) instead of answering the part before the dot: 0b101.11 and b10.1 both raise

methods.name: FractionalPart
methods.brief: Returns the binary digits after the dot, or an empty text when there is no dot.
methods.returns: a text of digits, without the dot
notes: 0b101.11 gives 11

methods.name: Reversed
methods.brief: Returns the number written backwards, integer part and fractional part each reversed, joined by a dot.
notes: use IntegerPartReversed on a number without a fraction only to turn the digits, and ignore the prefix at its end
warnings: the prefix is reversed with the digits, so 0b1011 answers 1101b0, which is not a binary number, and with a fractional part it raises error R24 as IntegerPart does

methods.name: HasFractionalPart
methods.brief: TRUE if the number has digits after the dot.
notes: ContainsFractionalPart is the same call

methods.name: FractionalPartReversed
methods.brief: Returns the digits after the dot written backwards.
methods.returns: a text of digits; empty without a dot
notes: 0b11.01 gives 10

methods.name: IntegerPartReversed
methods.brief: Returns the integer part written backwards, prefix included.
notes: with a fractional part it raises error R24 as IntegerPart does
warnings: the prefix is reversed with the digits: 0b1011 answers 1101b0 and b1111 answers 1111b

methods.name: ToStzNumber
methods.brief: Returns the value as a stzNumber, read from its decimal form.

methods.name: ToStzString
methods.brief: Returns the binary text, prefix included, as a stzString.

methods.name: IntegerPartToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the integer part converted to decimal, as text.
notes: by hand 1011 is 8+2+1: 0b1011 gives 11 and 0b101.11 gives 5; IntegerPartToDecimal is the same call

methods.name: FractionalPartToDecimalForm
methods.brief: Returns the fractional part converted to decimal, as a text such as 0.75.
methods.returns: a text; 0 when there is no fraction

methods.name: FractionalPartToDecimalFormWithoutZeroDot
methods.brief: Returns the decimal digits of the fractional part without the leading 0.

methods.name: ToOctalForm

classes.name: stzBuildPlan
classes.brief: Holds the rehearsed placement plan of a solution: per part, each capability with its delivery vector, its reason and its size.
classes.description: It is what stzDelivery.Plan returns, and it changes nothing when read. VectorFor says how a capability reaches a part, EngineCapsFor and EngineKbFor say what the on-device engine of a part carries and weighs, and Explain tells the whole story in plain lines, with the external dependencies, the fakes that remain and the credentials production will need, by name. It is plain data, so it survives copying, and the emulator reads its Parts to render each part.

classes.name: stzCalendar
classes.brief: Holds a period of days (a year, a quarter, a month or a date range) with working days, holidays, breaks and business hours, and counts available days and hours.
classes.description: Build it from a year (2026), a month ([ 2026, 3 ] or the text 2026-03), a quarter (2026-Q2 or [ 2026, "Q2" ]), a date range ([ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ]) or a single date. Set the working weekdays with SetWorkingDays (Monday to Friday is the default, set the first time IsWorkingDay runs), the hours with SetBusinessHours (09:00:00 to 17:00:00 by default), and add holidays with AddHoliday and daily breaks with AddBreak. Then ask for working days, available days and available hours of the whole period or of one day (AvailableHoursOnN), check that a task fits (CanFit, FirstAvailableSlot), attach a stzTimeLine to look for conflicts, compare two calendars, and export the facts with ToHash, ToJSON and ToCSV or draw them with Show, ShowHeatMap and ShowTable. Hours are whole hours, rounded down day by day. Month and year navigation moves the calendar itself. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: only the FIRST day of a period is checked against the holidays when days are counted (the next days are produced as dd/MM/yyyy text, while holidays are compared as text with the date as added); about twenty methods are stubs that raise Not yet implemented!, or call a method that does not exist (the Between families of breaks, working days and available days, GoToNext, ConflictsWithSpan, ContainsBreaksBetween); AvailableHoursBetweenN overwrites the whole-calendar cache; FirstAvailableSlot ends its slot from midnight; ContainsBusinessHours is always FALSE; going to the next month from December raises; a year or quarter calendar cannot be drawn.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the calendar of a year, a month, a quarter, a date range or a single date, with Monday to Friday and 09:00 to 17:00 as defaults.

parameters.role: what the calendar covers: a year above 1900 such as 2026, a text such as 2026-03, 2026-Q2 or 2026-03-15, a list such as [ 2026, 3 ] or [ 2026, "Q3" ], or named pairs such as [ [ "Start", "2026-03-10" ], [ "End", "2026-03-20" ] ] or [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3 ]

notes: named pairs accept Start or From, End or To, Year, Month, Quarter; the working days stay empty until SetWorkingDays or the first IsWorkingDay, which sets Monday to Friday; the locale key is never read
warnings: a year of 1900 or less, a number with decimals, [ ] and [ 2026, 13 ] raise; 2026-q4 with a lowercase q raises R41 (only Q3 as the second list item is case- free); [ 2026, "Spring" ] silently gives the whole year; a plain list of two dates [ "2026-03-10", "2026-03-20" ] and a list holding only a Start pair leave the calendar empty; any other text, such as gregorian, becomes a one-day range whose dates cannot be read

classes.name: stzCanvas
classes.brief: Holds a 2D picture described once, as shapes and text, and gives it back as vector SVG or as pixels drawn on the graphics device.
classes.description: The Add methods remember the shape instead of posting it, so Fill, Stroke, Color and SetFont can still reach the last shape added; the shape is posted when the next one arrives or an output is asked for. Fill and Stroke called before any shape set the default for every shape added after. The plain form of a method acts and answers nothing, and its Q twin answers the canvas so calls can be chained; only the pick, identity and region setters answer the canvas without the Q. Text needs a font from SetFont. ToSVG needs no device and is the floor of the tier ladder; ToPNG and ToPixels go through the GPU and answer an empty string when none is available. Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner, sizes run from 1 to 16384, and the SVG output draws circles, rounded rectangles, ellipses and strokes as polygons and polylines.

classes.name: stzCapabilityCatalog
classes.brief: Holds what the delivery planner knows about each Softanza capability, as data, and decides how a capability reaches a target.
classes.description: Each record says whether a capability is unique to Softanza, whether it is compute or ergonomics, how heavy it is, how well a browser, a server and a microcontroller already do it, and how many KB its engine adds. VectorFor reads those records and answers native, engine, construct or server with the reason in words: a server hosts the engine, a heavy capability goes to the backend, a strong non-unique one defers to the platform, an ergonomic one becomes a construct on the web, the rest folds into the on-device engine. A name the catalog does not know is assumed to be Softanza- differential and platform-weak.
classes.example:
? o1.Has("PivotTable")
#--> 1
? o1.SizeOf("neural")
#--> 900
? @@( o1.VectorFor("Json", "browser") )
#--> [ "native", "Json: the target-platform is strong at it -> use its own" ]

classes.name: stzCapabilityResponder
classes.brief: Performs the :RevokeCapability action of a response plan by cutting an actor's paths to the effectful capability in a security graph.
classes.description: The graph is what audits and incidents ask, the live actor is what the runtime gates ask, so the responder cuts both: the graph edges, and the effectful kind of each registered live actor of the same name. Register live actors one at a time with AddLiveActor, because an object placed in a list literal is copied and revoking a copy changes nothing. It answers no other verb: each of those raises an error that names the responder to wire. Other actors that use the same tool keep their capability.
classes.example:
g.AddActor("billing-agent", "trusted")
g.AddTool("deploy-tool")
g.AddCapability("effectful")
g.Uses("billing-agent", "deploy-tool")
g.Grants("deploy-tool", "effectful")
? g.ReachesEffectful("billing-agent")
#--> 1
o1.RevokeCapability("billing-agent")
? g.ReachesEffectful("billing-agent")
#--> 0
? @@( o1.LastCut() )
#--> [ [ "billing-agent", "uses", "deploy-tool" ] ]

classes.name: stzCardPaymentsAdapter
classes.brief: Plays a card gateway in memory with the state machine a real one enforces, so double captures and over-refunds fail in a test.
classes.description: Authorize gives an authorized or declined answer, Capture takes an authorized amount once, and Refund gives back only what was captured, never more. The rules are yours and deterministic: a ceiling under which everything is approved, a ceiling over which everything is declined, tokens that always decline, and one outage on demand. Every movement is recorded, so a test asserts on what happened to the money and not on a return value. Money is a positive whole number of minor units, 4200 for 42.00, never a float. This is the double only: the live side, a client of a real card processor, is not shipped, and the registry refuses a double in production. It is not the UEMOA payments port, whose verbs are pay, request to pay, return, cancellation and bulk: see stzPaymentsPort.
classes.example:
aA = o1.Authorize(4200, "tok_visa")
? aA[:status]
#--> authorized
o1.Capture(aA[:id])
o1.RefundAmount(aA[:id], 1000)
? o1.NetCaptured()
#--> 3200

notes: its state lives in a global table, so a copy of the object (w = o) is the same gateway; money is in whole minor units, 4200 for 42.00
warnings: build it with parentheses or with StzCardPaymentsAdapterQ(): a paren-less new skips this step, and every object built that way shares one gateway and one ledger

methods.name: Authorize
methods.brief: Asks the gateway to approve an amount against a payment token and answers approved or declined, recording the movement.

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount in minor units, a positive whole number

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the payment token the customer presented

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is authorized or declined, id is auth_1, auth_2 and so on, why says the cause of a decline
notes: nothing is captured yet: Capture takes the money
warnings: an amount that is zero, negative, fractional or not a number is refused with ok = 0, status refused and an empty id; a decline is an answer that takes an id and counts in NumberOfDeclines, and the rules apply in the order token, decline ceiling, approval ceiling

methods.name: Capture
methods.brief: Takes the whole amount that was approved on an authorization; the money can be taken only once.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is captured, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: a declined, unknown or already captured authorization is refused and the ledger does not move

methods.name: CaptureAmount
methods.brief: Takes part of an authorization, or all of it when the amount is 0; a capture may not exceed what was authorized and happens once.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to take in minor units, 0 for the whole authorization

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is captured, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: capturing less than the authorized amount closes the authorization: the rest cannot be captured later

methods.name: Refund
methods.brief: Gives back the rest of what was captured on an authorization.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is refunded, or refused with the cause in why
notes: StatusOf still reads captured after a refund; the refunded sum is read with RefundedOf
warnings: an authorization with nothing left to refund is refused, but the reason says an amount must be a positive whole number, which is true and is not the cause

methods.name: RefundAmount
methods.brief: Gives back part of the captured money, or all that is left when the amount is 0; the total refunded never exceeds what was captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to give back in minor units, 0 for what is left

methods.returns: a list [ ok, id, status, amount, why ]: status is refunded, or refused with the cause in why
warnings: an authorization that was never captured, or an amount over what is left, is refused and the ledger does not move

methods.name: StatusOf
methods.brief: Returns the state of an authorization: authorized, declined or captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a text; empty for an unknown id
notes: a refund does not change it: the state stays captured

methods.name: AmountOf
methods.brief: Returns the amount that was asked for in the authorization.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 for an unknown id

methods.name: CapturedOf
methods.brief: Returns how much of an authorization was captured.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 when nothing was captured or the id is unknown

methods.name: RefundedOf
methods.brief: Returns how much of an authorization has been given back.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the id returned by Authorize

methods.returns: a number in minor units; 0 when nothing was refunded or the id is unknown

methods.name: NumberOfAuthorizations
methods.brief: Returns how many authorizations the gateway holds, declined ones included.
notes: a call refused before an id was given, such as a bad amount or an outage, is not counted

methods.name: TotalAuthorized
methods.brief: Returns the sum asked for by the authorizations that were approved, whether or not they were captured since.
notes: declined authorizations are left out, and a refund does not lower it

methods.name: TotalCaptured
methods.brief: Returns the sum captured across every authorization.
notes: a refund does not lower it: NetCaptured does

methods.name: TotalRefunded
methods.brief: Returns the sum given back across every authorization.

methods.name: NetCaptured
methods.brief: Returns what the merchant keeps: the captured sum less the refunded sum.

methods.name: NumberOfDeclines
methods.brief: Returns how many authorizations were declined, by a token or by a ceiling.

methods.name: Movements
methods.brief: Returns the ledger of what happened to the money, oldest first, one record per authorize, decline, capture or refund.
methods.returns: a list of records [ seq, kind, id, amount ] where kind is authorize, decline, capture or refund
notes: a refused call leaves no record: a test asserts on what the money did, not on the return value

methods.name: NumberOfMovements
methods.brief: Returns how many records the ledger holds.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one summary line of the gateway: how many authorizations, and the captured, refunded and net sums.
notes: the line begins with stzPaymentsSandbox, whatever the class used

classes.name: stzChainOfTruth
classes.brief: Wraps one value in a chain of near-natural questions, such as _("ring").Is(:String)._, whose closing underscore answers 1 or 0.
classes.description: Each step (Is, Which, Where) puts one question to the value and tags the chain true or false, and returns the chain, so steps read as a sentence; the closing _ attribute returns 1 or 0. A chain that was tagged false stays false: later steps do not run, so build a new chain for a new question. The surface is frozen legacy: the same idea lives on as interrogative narrations in stzNatural, and part of this class does not work today: the negative forms (IsNot, IsNotAn, IsNotThe, IsNotA), Containing, ContainingNo, the function-call forms of Is and IsA, and the ordinal forms (st, nd, rd, th, Nth).

classes.name: stzChainOfValue
classes.brief: Watches one variable of the caller and runs a piece of code only if the variable meets a condition, written as a near-natural chain.
classes.description: A chain is born from an initiator function (Whatever, OnlyWhen, Until, Since, SometimesWhen) that names the variable as a symbol, and each link returns the chain itself: Is compares the value, DoThis runs the code. A link that is not satisfied does not raise an error, it stops the chain: ChainStatus then answers stopped, WhyChainStopped carries the reasons as a list of texts, and DoThis on a stopped chain runs nothing. OnlyWhen runs the code once when the values are equal; Until repeats it until the variable equals the stop value; Since waits for Becomes to name where it ends. The loop mode, the run flag and the stop value are shared by every chain of the process, and a new initiator call resets them. The value held is a snapshot taken when the chain is built. IsANumber, IsNotANumber, IsAList, IsAnObject and ToStzObject on a number do not work today.
classes.example:
? o1.ChainStatus()
#--> ongoing
o1.DoThis('{ v = v + 10 }')
? v
#--> 15
? o1.CodeStatus()
#--> hasbeenexecuted
? @@( OnlyWhen(:v).Is(6).WhyChainStopped() )
#--> [ "Because value provided is not equal to main value!" ]
Until(:v).Is(20).DoThis('{ v = v + 1 }')
? v
#--> 20

methods.section: getting the code of the chain of value

classes.name: stzCodeDeepRuleSet
classes.brief: The DEEP set: the project set PLUS no-cyclic-calls, which is expensive (measured ~36s over base/graph -- the code graph's CyclicCalls is O(calls^2 . methods)).
classes.description: Opt-in via StzCheckProjectDeep, for a periodic audit rather than a per-commit gate. No silent cap: the default gate documents that it omits this.

classes.name: stzCodeGraph
classes.brief: Turns source code into a graph of classes, methods, functions, imports and calls, and answers questions about inheritance and impact.
classes.description: This is the shared head of the code graph family: it holds the model and every query, and each language is a subclass that knows how to read its source (stzRingCodeGraph, stzPyCodeGraph, stzJsCodeGraph). Build a graph with one of their functions, such as StzPyCodeGraphFromSource, then ask: Classes, MethodsOf, OwnersOf, AncestryOf, SubclassesOf, DescendantsOf, ImpactOf (who defines a method and who inherits it) and Cascade (how far a change to a class reaches). The call questions, CallersOf, CalleesOf, DeadCode and CyclicCalls, need call edges, which only a real parse such as ScanSourceViaTreeSitter records; without them DeadCode and CyclicCalls raise an error instead of guessing. The base class cannot parse by itself: Language raises, and so do Stats and any scan. CheckRules and RulesAreSound work on a Ring graph only.
classes.receiver: o1 = StzPyCodeGraphFromSource('class Animal:' + char(10) + '    def speak(self):' + char(10) + '        return 1' + char(10) + 'class Dog(Animal):' + char(10) + '    def speak(self):' + char(10) + '        return 2' + char(10) + 'class Puppy(Dog):' + char(10) + '    pass')
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Classes() )
#--> [ "Animal", "Dog", "Puppy" ]
? @@( o1.AncestryOf("Puppy") )
#--> [ "Puppy", "Dog", "Animal" ]
? @@( o1.DescendantsOf("Animal") )
#--> [ "Dog", "Puppy" ]
? @@( o1.OwnersOf("speak") )
#--> [ "Animal", "Dog" ]
? @@( o1.ImpactOf("speak")[:inheritedBy] )
#--> [ "Puppy" ]
? o1.Cascade("Animal")[:blastRadius]
#--> 2

classes.name: stzCommitScope
classes.brief: Bounds what an update plan may commit: the operation types, the path prefixes and the number of operations.
classes.description: A human usually commits with no scope; a script or an agent commits only inside a declared, auditable one, by the same mechanism. A new scope admits everything. Each AllowType and AllowUnder narrows it: once a type is allowed, any other type is refused, and once a prefix is allowed, every path an operation touches must start with one of them. Reason says why an operation is refused and Allows says whether it is. The limit on the number of operations is applied by the plan while it commits.
classes.example:
o1.AllowUnder("/w/").AllowType("create_file")
? o1.Allows(new stzVirtualOperation("create_file", [ [ "path", "/w/a.txt" ], [ "content", "" ] ]))
#--> 1
? o1.Reason(new stzVirtualOperation("delete_file", [ [ "path", "/w/a.txt" ] ]))
#--> operation type 'delete_file' is not allowed by this scope

classes.name: stzConditionalRegexMaker
classes.brief: Builds an if-then-else regular expression, a conditional pattern, from a condition, a then part and an optional else part.
classes.description: The condition is one of the If calls (IfMatch, IfNotMatch, IfStartsWith, IfEndsWith, IfContains, IfPrecededBy, IfFollowedBy); the last one called wins. ThenMatch and ElseMatch give the two branches, and Pattern joins them as (?(?=condition)then|else). The pattern stays empty until a condition is set. IfStartsWith, IfEndsWith and IfContains take literal text and escape it; the other calls take a pattern. IfCaptured does not build a conditional today, and the pair forms of IfCaptured and IfPrecededBy raise an error.
classes.example:
o1.IfMatch("\d").ThenMatch("\d+").ElseMatch("[a-z]+")
? o1.Pattern()
#--> (?(?=\d)\d+|[a-z]+)
o2 = new stzRegex(o1.Pattern())
o2.MatchFirst("abc 123")
? @@( o2.Matches() )
#--> [ "abc", "123" ]
o1.Reset()
? o1.IfStartsWith("+").ThenMatch("\d+").Pattern()
#--> (?(?=^\+)\d+)

methods.detail: Returns a Ring list of N values produced by cycling through (@nStartAt, @nStep) under the wrap-around modes :WhenYouReach and :AfterYouSkip. The cycle itself is built by the Zig engine in O(N) (see ring_bridge_intseq.zig), then marshalled into a Ring list via the engine bridge. classes.name: stzCourse
classes.brief: Holds one course of a program as a path through its chapters, and answers what a learner or a teacher asks of it.
classes.description: A learner opens a chapter in a language (ChapterQ) or runs it (RunChapterQ); a teacher asks what a chapter needs first (Prerequisites), what it trains (Trains), where a name is first taught (TeachesWhere) and which planned chapters have no text yet (UnwrittenChapterIds). The course is made of two manifests: course.zknw says what ships, in order, and curriculum.zknw says what is planned, with its trains and requires facts; an overlay's course.zknw is merged into the core's, never shadowing it. A course is taken from a program with CourseQ and holds a COPY of that program, so the overlay and the world must be set before. A chapter with no text in a language raises an error, never a quiet fallback to English. LIMITS, stated where you meet them: the translations (fr, ar, ha) are drafts, 0 of 35 units of each reviewed by a person when this was written; the cells of a chapter run on the desktop only, not in a browser, and the Run methods start Ring processes whose executable path must not contain a space; no institution has adopted the system.
classes.example:
? o1.TitleOf("find-then-apply", "fr")
#--> Trouver, puis agir
? @@( o1.Prerequisites("say-it-in-your-language") )
#--> [ "read-the-name-as-a-sentence", "a-first-sentence", "find-then-apply" ]
? o1.TeachesWhere("FindDuplicates")
#--> find-then-apply
? @@( o1.Trains("find-then-apply") )
#--> [ "ex-01", "ex-02", "ex-03" ]

classes.name: stzDataSet
classes.brief: Holds a list of numbers or categories and answers descriptive, distribution, relation and quality questions about it, with rules that turn the figures into written insights.
classes.description: The data type is detected when the set is built (numeric, categorical, mixed or empty) and missing markers such as NA are dropped. Numeric statistics answer 0 for data that is not numeric, and the count-based ones need two to four values. The methods fall in groups: the descriptive ones (Mean, Median, Mode, spread, quartiles, Percentile), frequency and diversity for categories, shape and outliers (Skew, Kurtosis, Outliers, ZScores, TrendAnalysis), relation to a second data set given as an argument (CorrelationWith, RegressionCoefficients, ChiSquareWith, MutualInformation), scaling (Normalize, Standardize, RobustScale), and the insight layer: domain rules (AddInsightRule, InsightsOfDomain), plans (MakePlan, ExecutePlan) and Summary. The tables of rules and plan templates are global, shared by every data set of the process, and ExecutePlan and AdaptiveAnalysis print as they work. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Percentile makes the engine panic for a percent below 0 or far above 100, WMean overflows the stack, NonParametricCorrelation and PlanSummary raise errors, and MutualInformation misreads values that contain an underscore.

classes.name: stzDate
classes.brief: Holds one calendar date (year, month, day) with no time of day, moves it by days, months or years, compares it and writes it in several formats.
classes.description: A stzDate is three numbers. Build it from a text (2026-03-15, 15/03/2026, 15.03.2026, 15032026, today, in 3 days), from a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], from a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or from an empty text for today. A text with a 4-digit first part is read year-first, any other text day- first, so 03/15/2026 raises. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and return nothing (the Q forms answer the object so calls chain); the Next, Previous, Start and End methods answer a text in dd/MM/yyyy and leave the object alone (their Q forms answer a copy). Measure with DaysTo, WeeksTo, MonthsTo and YearsTo, compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween, and write it with ToString (dd/MM/yyyy), ToISO8601, ToAmerican, ToLong or ToStringXT with a format such as yyyy-MM-dd. Dates before 1970 work, because the engine counts civil days and not Unix seconds. Today follows StzFreezeClock, so a test can pin it. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: MonthsTo, YearsTo, IsSameWeek, IsSameMonth, IsSameYear and IsBetween raise for anything but a stzDate object; DaysTo and the Is comparisons overwrite a list or hash variable of the caller; PreviousWeekday answers a Saturday from a Sunday; Age counts year numbers only; a language given with a capital (French) falls back to English; a list or hash given to the constructor is not validated.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the date from a date text, a [ year, month, day ] list, a hash with :Year, :Month and :Day, or today when the text is empty.

parameters.name: pcDate
parameters.role: a date text such as 2026-03-15 or 15/03/2026, the words today, yesterday or tomorrow, a phrase such as in 3 days, a list [ 2026, 3, 15 ], or a hash [ :Year = 2026, :Month = 3, :Day = 15 ]

notes: text with 4 digits first is read year-first (yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy/M/d), otherwise day-first (dd/MM/yyyy, dd.MM.yyyy, ddMMyyyy); an empty text is today and follows StzFreezeClock; dates before 1970 are fine here, unlike stzDateTime
warnings: a text is checked (2026-02-30 raises Invalid date provided!) but a list or hash is not (13 as month is stored and IsValid answers FALSE); text with the month first such as 03/15/2026 is read day-first and raises; a number, or a list that is not 3 numbers, raises Can't create the stzDate object; a two- digit year (15-03-26) raises R41; a phrase with a unit other than day, week, month, year, decade or century leaves the date empty without an error

warnings: a text with an impossible day (2026-02-30) raises Invalid date provided! only AFTER the fields were overwritten, so the object keeps the invalid date; a phrase with an unknown unit changes nothing

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Applies one of the operators + - < <= > >= = between the date and a number, a text or another date.

parameters.name: op
parameters.role: the operator text: + - < <= > >= =

parameters.name: v
parameters.role: the right-hand value: a number of days, a phrase such as 2 weeks, a date text or a stzDate object

methods.returns: for + and - with a number or text, the new date as dd/MM/yyyy text; for - with a date, the number of days between; for a comparison, TRUE or FALSE
notes: a number means days: date + 3 moves 3 days; comparisons accept a date object or a date text
warnings: + and - change the object itself, unlike arithmetic on numbers; date minus date is the absolute number of days, never negative; a unit other than days, weeks, months or years raises Invalid unit!; a list as right-hand side of - or a comparison raises Unsupported value!; + with a list and any other operator answer nothing

methods.name: ParseOperation

parameters.name: cOperation

parameters.name: cOperator
parameters.role: the operator text: - subtracts, anything else adds

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: does not return the new date
warnings: raises Invalid operation format when the text is only a number, and Invalid unit! for hours or fortnights; a space doubled between number and unit reads as an empty unit

methods.name: DaysTo

parameters.name: _oOtherDate_

methods.returns: a number of days; 10 from 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-25
notes: works across 1970: 25822 days from 1955-07-04 to 2026-03-15
warnings: a list or hash held in a variable is REPLACED in the caller by a stzDate object (the call assigns to its own parameter, which Ring shares with the caller); a number raises Parameter must be a stzDate object or date string

classes.name: stzDateTime
classes.brief: Holds one date and time, to the millisecond, and adds to it, compares it, measures distances from it and writes it in many formats.
classes.description: A stzDateTime is made of seven numbers (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond) that read as one instant with no time zone: ToUTC and ToLocalTime change nothing. Build it from a text (2026-03-15 14:30:00, 15/03/2026 2:30 PM, an ISO text with a T), from a number of seconds since 1970, from a hash of parts, or from an empty text for the current clock. The Add and Subtract methods move the object itself and answer the new text; the Q forms answer the object so calls chain. Compare with IsBefore, IsAfter, IsEqualTo and IsBetween; measure with the DurationTo family (against another datetime) and the DurationSince family (against a named origin such as :UnixEpoch or :YearOne). The To... methods write it as text: ToIso for storage, ToStandard and ToAmerican for display, ToHuman and ToRelative in words. Instants before 1970 and origins such as :YearOne are read as dates like any other.

methods.name: init

methods.name: ToIsoWithMs

methods.name: ToTextDate
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month and day with a 24-hour time and the year, in ddd MMM d HH:mm:ss yyyy order.
methods.returns: a string such as Sun Mar 15 14:30:00 2026
notes: the day of the month is written without a leading zero

methods.name: ToSimple
methods.brief: Returns day/month/year with the hour on a 12-hour clock and an AM/PM marker, without seconds.
notes: the hour is not zero padded; the marker texts come from the default locale

methods.name: ToSimple24h
methods.brief: Returns day/month/year with a 24-hour time, without seconds.

methods.name: ToLong
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name, day, year and a 12-hour time with seconds and an AM/PM marker.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March 15, 2026 2:30:00 PM
notes: the day and month names are English; the hour is not zero padded

methods.name: ToLong24h
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name, day, year and a 24-hour time with seconds.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March 15, 2026 14:30:00
notes: the day of the month is written without a leading zero

methods.name: ToLongDate
methods.brief: Returns the weekday, month name, day and year without a time.
methods.returns: a string such as Sunday, March 15, 2026
notes: the day of the month is written without a leading zero

methods.name: ToString12h
methods.brief: Returns yyyy-MM-dd with the time on a 12-hour clock, seconds and an AM/PM marker.
notes: the hour is not zero padded

methods.name: ToHuman
methods.brief: Returns a sentence such as Sunday, March 15th, 2026 at Half past 2 PM, with the time said in words.
notes: whole times read 12 o'clock, quarter hours read Quarter past or Quarter to, other times read like 9:05 AM

methods.name: ToRelative
methods.brief: Returns how far the datetime is from the system clock in words, such as 5 minutes ago, in 3 hours or just now.
notes: under 60 seconds is just now; then minutes, hours, days, weeks, months of 30 days and years of 365 days, rounded to the nearest unit; depends on the clock when it is called

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new stzDateTime holding the same date and time, so the copy can change without touching this one.
notes: the object is not changed

methods.name: SetComponents
methods.brief: Sets year, month, day, hour, minute, second and optionally millisecond from a list, and answers the object itself.

parameters.name: aComponents
parameters.role: a list [ year, month, day, hour, minute, second ] with an optional seventh number for the milliseconds

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls can be chained
notes: the SetComponentsQ form gives the same result
warnings: does not check ranges, so a month of 13 is stored and IsValid then answers FALSE; a list shorter than 6 numbers is ignored

extensions.name: SetComponentsQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: Returns the parts as the list [ year, month, day, hour, minute, second, milliseconds ].

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the month is 1-12, the day exists in that month (leap years included) and the time fields are in range.
notes: checks hour 0-23, minute 0-59, second 0-59 and milliseconds 0-999

methods.name: IsAStzDateTime
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is a datetime object, which is always the case here; callers use it to tell classes apart.

methods.name: IsNaturalEpochString
methods.brief: TRUE if the text contains from epoch or since epoch, in any case.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to examine

notes: only the phrase is tested, not the amount before it

methods.name: ParseNaturalEpoch
methods.brief: Sets the object to 1970-01-01 plus a duration in words such as 3 days 2 hours, each unit counted once.

parameters.name: _cNatural_
parameters.role: the duration in words ending with from epoch or since epoch, such as 3 days 2 hours from epoch

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: FromNaturalEpoch reads the same words correctly; the constructor uses this method for text with from epoch or since epoch

methods.name: SetFromEpochMonths
methods.brief: Sets the object to the first day of the month n calendar months after January 1970, at 00:00:00.

parameters.name: _nMonths_
parameters.role: the number of months since January 1970

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the same as FromMonthsSinceEpoch with the Unix origin

methods.name: SetFromEpochYears
methods.brief: Sets the object to January 1 at 00:00:00 of the year 1970 plus n.

parameters.name: _nYears_
parameters.role: the number of years since 1970

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place

methods.name: SetFromEpochDuration
methods.brief: Sets the object to 1970-01-01 plus a hash of durations, milliseconds included, such as [ :days = 3, :milliseconds = 250 ].

parameters.name: aHash
parameters.role: a hash whose keys are years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds or milliseconds

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: unlike FromEpochHash it reads the :milliseconds key

methods.name: IsCountingFromString
methods.brief: TRUE if the text contains counting from, starting from or since, in any case.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text to examine

notes: since alone is enough, so any text with since in it answers TRUE

methods.name: ParseCountingFrom
methods.brief: Sets the object from a text such as 2 days counting from unix epoch (a duration, a phrase, an origin); does nothing without a phrase.

parameters.name: cStr
parameters.role: the text, a duration then counting from, starting from or since, then an origin name in words

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: the origin words are turned into an origin name by MapOriginName

methods.name: MapOriginName
methods.brief: Returns the origin name that matches words such as year one, atomic age or us independence; unknown words give unixepoch.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the origin in words, any case

methods.returns: an origin name as lowercase text, such as yearone
notes: matching is by phrase: unix, year one or common era, islamic, space age, atomic age, us independence, french revolution, internet
warnings: modern computing is not recognised and answers unixepoch like any unknown text

methods.name: SetCountingFrom
methods.brief: Sets the object to an origin plus a number of seconds, or plus a hash of durations; an empty origin means 1970-01-01.

parameters.name: _nValue_
parameters.role: the seconds after the origin, or a hash such as [ :hours = 5 ]

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: seconds may carry a fraction, which becomes the milliseconds

methods.name: GetOriginBase
methods.brief: Returns an origin's distance from 1970-01-01 in milliseconds, negative for earlier origins; 0 when the name is unknown.

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text, such as :YearOne

notes: the nine origins are UnixEpoch, YearOne, IslamicHijra, USIndependence, FrenchRevolution, AtomicAge, SpaceAge, InternetAge and ModernComputing

methods.name: SetFromNaturalDuration
methods.brief: Sets the object to an origin plus a duration in words such as 1 day 1 hour; an empty origin means 1970-01-01.

parameters.name: _cDuration_
parameters.role: the duration in words, numbers each followed by years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

parameters.name: _cOrigin_
parameters.role: the origin name as a symbol or lowercase text

methods.returns: nothing; the object changes in place
notes: a year counts 365 days and a month 30.4 days
warnings: milliseconds are not read

methods.name: ParseNaturalDuration
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds that a duration in words such as 10 minutes 5 seconds adds up to.

parameters.name: _cDuration_
parameters.role: the duration in words, numbers each followed by years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

notes: a year is 365 days and a month 30.4 days; the object is not changed
warnings: a word instead of a number (two days) raises R41; milliseconds are not read; only the first amount of each unit counts

methods.name: HashToMilliseconds
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds that a hash of durations such as [ :days = 1, :hours = 1 ] adds up to.

parameters.name: aHash
parameters.role: a hash whose keys are years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or seconds

notes: a year is 365 days and a month 30.4 days; the object is not changed
warnings: a :milliseconds key is ignored today

methods.name: DurationTo
methods.section: duration calculations to a target datetime
methods.brief: Returns the distance from the datetime to a target in one unit, or a hash of all units when the unit is empty.

parameters.name: pTarget
parameters.role: the target datetime, as a stzDateTime or a date-time text

parameters.name: pcUnit
parameters.role: the unit as text such as days, or written :In = :Days

methods.returns: a number in the unit, or a hash with keys milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years, decades and centuries
notes: negative when the target is earlier; days and weeks round down, hours and smaller units can carry a fraction, months and years compare calendar numbers
warnings: an unknown unit raises Unsupported unit, and so does in days with a space

methods.name: DurationInMillisecondsTo

parameters.name: pcUnit

notes: the object is not changed

methods.name: DurationInMonthsTo

methods.brief: Returns how many calendar months apart the two datetimes are, by month number and ignoring the day.

methods.returns: a whole number of calendar months

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: THE HELD SET IS LIVE THROUGH HERE.
methods.detail: Ring COPIES an object into an attribute, so the set handed to the constructor is a SNAPSHOT: growing the caller's own object afterwards would NOT reach this learner. Grow it through this accessor -- oLearner.TrainingSetQ().AddExample(...) -- which reaches the real held set (accessor + method call is live in Ring).

methods.name: Train
methods.brief: THE CASE FOLD HAPPENS ONCE HERE, not at every node (numeric phase 5).
methods.detail: ID3 compares categorical values case-insensitively, so "Sunny" and "sunny" are one value. The fold used to live inside _ValuesOf() and _Subset(), which means every row was re-folded once per (node, feature) pair -- and the value never changes. Profiled on 4000 examples x 8 features: _ValuesOf x20 over the set          0.338 s _Subset   x20 over the set          0.356 s StzLower  x20 alone                 0.297 s   <-- of that the same loops without it           0.022 s The fold was THIRTEEN TIMES the cost of the loop containing it, because StzLower builds two engine string objects and frees them -- five bridge crossings to lowercase one character. Folding the whole set once costs 0.129 s and the inner loops drop 4.2x. Third time this phase has found this shape: the CSV module's per-cell regex recompile, the linear solver's per-variable re-parse, and now this. The expensive line is rarely the one the plan names -- the plan said "trees -> engine", and the tree was never the problem.

methods.name: ToGraph
methods.brief: the learned model as a REAL stzGraph: decision nodes + labeled value edges + leaf nodes -- queryable like any other graph

classes.name: stzDeclaredLLMAgent
classes.brief: An llm agent that came from a declaration: it proposes structured facts into its own memory and can cause no effect.
classes.description: On a tick it reads its input from memory, asks its model function for an answer in the declared structure and learns the fields as facts under the declared subject. It holds no effectful capability. An answer that does not satisfy the structure lands nothing. Seed the answer with SeedProposal to run it without a model; with no seed and no loaded model the tick is refused and WhyLastTick says so.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDeclaredLLMAgent("summarizer") o1.SetDeclared("proposes a topic", "reversible")
classes.example:
? o1.CoverageStatement()
#--> proposes a topic
? o1.Cycle()
#--> 0
? o1.WhyLastTick()
#--> no proposal is declared
? o1.ProposalsMade()
#--> 0

classes.name: stzDeclaredSkill
classes.brief: Holds a skill read from a declaration as three data clauses and runs them against an agent memory.
classes.description: A closure cannot be read out of a file, so this skill keeps its when, does and verify clauses as lists of a verb and its arguments and interprets them. Apply checks the precondition, performs the action on the memory it is given and verifies the result, answering a list that says whether it ran and whether it verified.
classes.receiver: m = new stzAgentMemory("demo") m.Learn("stock", "level", "low") o1 = new stzDeclaredSkill("restock") o1.SetClauses([ :verb = "fact", :args = [ "stock", "level", "low" ] ], [ :verb = "learn", :args = [ "stock", "level", "ordered" ] ], [ :verb = "fact", :args = [ "stock", "level", "ordered" ] ])

#--> 1
? o1.Apply(m)[:why]
#--> skill 'restock' ran and VERIFIED
? m.Fact("stock", "level", "ordered")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzDelivery
classes.brief: Plans where each part of a solution runs and what each ships, before a byte is built, by reasoning from the target platform of each part.
classes.description: You describe the solution: its parts, the target of each (a server, a phone, a browser, a microcontroller) and the Softanza capabilities each uses. Plan rehearses the placement: per capability and target it picks a delivery vector, native, engine, construct or server, says why, and sizes the on-device engine. The same capability lands differently per target, so the target platform is the invisible frame the planner makes visible. UseServices adds the external dependencies and the credentials production will need, and Deploy commits the plan: it is refused while a service is still bound to a fake, and an actor that is not effectful only gets a rehearsal. Read Plan freely; Deploy builds and, in production, launches for real.
classes.example:
o1.AddBackend("api", "LinuxServer").AddSuperApp("phone", "Android")
o1.NeedsIn("phone", [ :Unicode, :PivotTable, :Neural ])
? o1.NumberOfParts()
#--> 2
? o1.Plan().VectorFor("phone", "PivotTable")
#--> engine
? o1.Plan().VectorFor("phone", "Neural")
#--> server

methods.name: AttachSlice
methods.brief: ship a part's OWN slice from an emulator bundle -- its app (as index.html), its engine subset (stz_<part>.wasm), and the bridge (stz.js) -- NOT the whole mission-control.
methods.detail: A frontend part deploys only what it needs to run.

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.brief: the governance gate: may this deployment cross to reality?

methods.name: Plan
methods.brief: the deployment plan (rehearsal) -------------------- each part -> [ part, kind, target, siteName, siteKind, protocol ]

methods.name: Store
methods.brief: perform (governed) --------------------------------- store each part's deploy artifact on its bound site. returns [ committed(0/1), [ [part, site, outcome], ... ] ]

methods.name: Steps
methods.brief: the plan of steps (order, gates, rollback) --------- the deployment PLAN as ordered steps.
methods.detail: A simple deployment is the default chain per part -- provision? -> store -> launch -> verify; After() edges add cross-part ordering (a frontend after its backend). Returns [ [name, op, part, siteName, [needs]], ... ], topologically ordered so every dependency precedes its dependants.

methods.name: WasRun
methods.brief: EXECUTE the ordered plan (governed).
methods.detail: Each step runs its op; the verify step is a GATE (the site must be launched). On any failure, the completed store/launch steps are ROLLED BACK in reverse -- the deployment is transactional. Returns [ committed(0/1), [ [stepName, outcome], ... ] ]. No effectful actor -> rehearse. Did Run() execute at all? A deployment REFUSED upstream -- by the service gate in stzDelivery, say -- comes back untouched, and "nothing happened" is then assertable without reading the log.

methods.name: WasCommitted
methods.brief: Did it commit, or only rehearse? Rehearsed steps touch nothing.

methods.name: Feasibility
methods.brief: feasibility (host resources) ----------------------- Per-site admission check: sum the requirements of the parts bound to each site and test the site's capacity (or its ability to PROVISION one).
methods.detail: Returns [ [siteName, requiredText, capacityText, fits(0/1), note], ... ]. This is the same "does the host have room?" question a K8s scheduler / CI runner answers.

methods.name: Feasible
methods.brief: TRUE only if every site can host its parts (fits or can provision).

classes.name: stzDeploymentSite
classes.brief: Describes where a solution is deployed and how to reach and drive that place: kind, endpoint, protocol, authentication, storage, commands and capacity.
classes.description: A site is configuration first: set it with the Set methods (each has a Q form that returns the site to chain), read it back as data with Config, as lines with ConfigText or as JSON with ConfigJson, and see the commands it would run with Commands, TransferCommand and LaunchCommandLine before anything runs. Authentication is a plain reference, a stzSecret kept behind a redacted descriptor, or a secret held by name in a stzSecretStore and revealed through ResolveAuthVia so that the store audits it. Store, Launch, Status and Rollback act on the target: a local folder is written directly, a git site runs git, a server runs scp and ssh, and registry, device and object- store sites have commands listed but no store backend. A stzDeployment drives sites under a governed actor. The runs behind this reference only configured and read sites; nothing was stored to, launched on or rolled back.
classes.example:
o1.SetKindQ("server").SetEndpointQ("deploy@api.example.test:/srv/api")
? o1.Protocol()
#--> ssh
? o1.TransferCommand()
#--> scp -r <staged>/. deploy@api.example.test:/srv/api
? o1.IsLocal()
#--> 0
