classes.name: stzDetection
classes.brief: Declares one rule over a sequence of security events and judges a ledger against it, answering findings.
classes.description: Four shapes, each computable over a bounded ledger without a query language: a burst (n events of one kind inside a window), a sequence (one kind followed by another), any (one occurrence is the story) and unusual (the newest window judged against the same kind's own history, so the threshold is learned instead of written down). The unusual shape is honest: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, a cold start says nothing, and a flood that evicted its own baseline is reported as a warning. Findings come in the unified shape [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ], so they join stzRuleReport. Corroborated holds an error back to a warning until two distinct event kinds agree. A detection with nothing watched raises when asked to judge.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a detection of that name, which watches nothing yet and reports its findings at error severity.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the detection's name, which becomes the rule of its findings

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the detection's name, the rule its findings carry.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the event kind the detection watches, trimmed and in lower case.
methods.returns: a text; empty until WhenKind sets it

methods.name: Shape
methods.brief: Returns which shape the detection has: burst, sequence, any or unusual.
methods.returns: a text; empty until a declaring call sets it

methods.name: Severity
methods.brief: Returns the severity its findings carry, which is error until AsWarning or AsInfo changes it.

methods.name: Meaning
methods.brief: Returns the sentence given by Explaining, which is added to every finding message.
methods.returns: a text; empty until Explaining sets it

methods.name: WhenKind
methods.brief: Sets the event kind to watch, and makes the shape any when no shape was chosen yet.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind to watch, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: start every detection with it
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind watches nothing and never fires

methods.name: Repeats
methods.brief: Makes the detection a burst: this many events of the watched kind inside the window fire it.

parameters.name: pnTimes
parameters.role: how many events make a burst

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the BURST shape of stzDetection
warnings: without Within the window is 0 ms, so only events stamped with the same millisecond count together

methods.name: Within
methods.brief: Sets the window of a burst or a sequence, in milliseconds of event wall time.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window length, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: PerActor
methods.brief: Counts events actor by actor instead of across all actors, for a burst or an unusual rate.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: credential stuffing is per account, not per installation

methods.name: ThenKind
methods.brief: Makes the detection a sequence: an event of this kind must follow one of the watched kind.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the event kind that must follow, trimmed and put in lower case

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
warnings: the kind is not checked against the catalog, so a misspelled kind never follows and the detection never fires

methods.name: BySameActor
methods.brief: Requires both events of a sequence to come from the same actor.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: without it the whole ledger counts as one actor and a sequence gives one finding in all

methods.name: OnAnyOccurrence
methods.brief: Makes the detection fire on any single event of the watched kind, for kinds where one occurrence is already the story.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: one finding per matching event, at most 16

methods.name: Unusual
methods.brief: Makes the detection judge the newest window of the watched kind against the history of that same kind.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the defaults are windows of 60000 ms, a baseline of 12 windows, 3 sigma and a floor of 3 (threat model R9)

methods.name: Buckets
methods.brief: Sets the width of one window of the unusual shape, in milliseconds.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: the window width, in milliseconds, at least 1

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the baseline is this width times AgainstBaseline
warnings: a width below 1 raises an error, and a value that is not a number raises R41

methods.name: AgainstBaseline
methods.brief: Sets how many windows before the newest one form the baseline of the unusual shape.

parameters.name: pnBuckets
parameters.role: the number of baseline windows, at least 3

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the newest window is judged against the windows before it, never against a baseline that includes itself
warnings: fewer than 3 raises an error; until the ledger reaches back over 3 baseline windows nothing is said, because a cold start is not an anomaly

methods.name: Sigma
methods.brief: Sets how many standard deviations above the baseline mean make a window unusual.

parameters.name: pnZ
parameters.role: the number of standard deviations

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: on a flat baseline, where the windows before all hold the same count, sigma is not used: any count above that mean and at or over the floor fires

methods.name: AtLeast
methods.brief: Sets the floor of the unusual shape: a window with fewer events than this never fires.

parameters.name: pnCount
parameters.role: the smallest number of events in the newest window that can fire

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsOf
methods.brief: Judges the unusual shape at a given wall time instead of at the newest event, so a guard can be exact.

parameters.name: pnWallMs
parameters.role: the moment of judgement, in epoch milliseconds, 0 for the newest event

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Corroborated
methods.brief: Marks the detection so that an error finding drops to a warning unless the matched events span two distinct kinds.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain
notes: the corroboration law: one anomalous signal is a rumor, and the message says it is a single signal

methods.name: Explaining
methods.brief: Sets the one-sentence meaning that is added to every finding message and to the explanation.

parameters.name: pcMeaning
parameters.role: what the detection means, as text

methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsError
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to error.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsWarning
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to warning.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AsInfo
methods.brief: Sets the severity of the findings to info.
methods.returns: the detection itself, so calls chain

methods.name: CheckAgainst
methods.brief: Judges a ledger and returns the findings in the unified rule shape, ready for stzRuleReport.

parameters.name: poLedger
parameters.role: the stzSecurityLedger to judge, read through its retained window

methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] findings; [ ] when nothing matches
notes: the subject is security and where is the detection name, then a slash and the actor when there is one; at most 16 findings, so a storm reports and does not flood
warnings: raises an error when nothing is watched, so call WhenKind first

methods.name: LastEvidence
methods.brief: Returns the events that matched in the last check, so an incident can build its timeline from them.
methods.returns: a list of records; [ ] before any check or when nothing matched

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the detection told as lines of text: its shape with its numbers, and its meaning when given.
notes: the first line reads Detection name [severity] followed by the shape

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines Explain returns, one per line.

classes.name: stzDiagram
classes.brief: Holds a flow diagram of typed, coloured nodes and labelled edges, and draws it as SVG or PNG with no graphviz, or exports it as DOT, Mermaid, JSON or the native .stzdiag text.
classes.description: A stzDiagram is a stzGraph with a look: a theme, a layout direction, edge routing, pen and arrow settings, 24 node shapes (AddCircle, AddBox, AddDiamond and so on, each a node with a type and a label equal to its id), clusters drawn as boxes behind their nodes, annotators, and visual rules over node and edge properties. The inherited stzGraph methods (AddNodeXTT, Connect, AddEdgeXT, NodeProperty, Edges) build the content. ToCanvas lays the diagram out and draws it natively; ToSVG, ToPNG and ToPages are the outputs, and after ToCanvas the Render methods report where everything was drawn and PickAt answers what lies under a pixel. On top of that picture sits a headless editor: OnPress, OnMove, OnRelease and OnCancel feed a pointer into a state machine, Edit runs commands that Undo and Redo take back, and Pin fixes a node in the layout. Ids are folded to lowercase. Known defects, each carried as a warning: PenWidth, NodesWith, propertiesLegend and SaveToStzDiagInFolder raise; Explain raises once a visual rule is registered; ComputeMetrics divides by zero for a diagram with no path of two nodes; ToSVG and ToPNG leave the last picture freed, so picking fails after them; ImportDiag into a diagram that holds the first node adds duplicates; the pen-width setters are named the wrong way round. Display and View need graphviz and a viewer and Step and RunIn need a window; none of the three was run.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDiagram("flow"); o1.AddNodeXTT("start", "Order Received", [ :type = "start" ]); o1.AddNodeXT("validate", "Validate"); o1.AddNodeXTT("done", "Done", [ :type = "endpoint" ]); o1.AddEdgeXT("start", "validate", "next"); o1.AddEdge("validate", "done")

classes.name: stzDiagramToDot

classes.name: stzDuration
classes.brief: Holds a length of time, independent of any date, and reads it back as parts, as words or as clock text.
classes.description: A duration is built from a number of seconds, from a text such as 1 hour 30 min, or from a hash list of days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds. It answers totals (TotalHours counts past one day) and parts (Hours is the hour of the day), compares with other durations, numbers or texts, and is changed in place by Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide, which return the duration so calls chain. Limits today: the fraction of a second is lost when it is built from a number or a text, and AddMilliseconds, Copy and the operator results do not carry milliseconds; a negative duration answers wrong parts.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzDuration("1 day 2 hours 3 minutes 4 seconds")
classes.example:
? o1.TotalSeconds()
#--> 93784
? o1.ToHuman()
#--> 1 day, 2 hours, 3 minutes, and 4 seconds
? o1.ToString()
#--> 26:03:04

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a length of time from seconds, from text such as 1 hour 30 min, or from a hash list of parts.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length: a number of seconds, a text of numbers followed by day, hour, minute, second or ms units, or a hash list with the keys days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds

notes: an empty text gives a zero duration
warnings: the fraction of a second is lost today for a number or a text: 90.5 and 90 seconds 250 ms both answer Milliseconds 0; only a hash list with a milliseconds key keeps it, and Copy or Add then drop it

methods.name: TotalSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in seconds, dropping any fraction.
notes: 1 day 2 hours 3 minutes 4 seconds is 93784

methods.name: ToSeconds
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in seconds, dropping any fraction.
notes: the same value as TotalSeconds

methods.name: TotalMinutes
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in minutes, rounded down.
notes: 93784 seconds is 1563 minutes

methods.name: ToMinutes
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in minutes, rounded down.
notes: the same value as TotalMinutes

methods.name: TotalHours
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in hours, rounded down, and without wrapping at one day.
notes: 93784 seconds is 26 hours, where Hours answers 2

methods.name: ToHours
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in hours, rounded down, and without wrapping at one day.
notes: the same value as TotalHours

methods.name: TotalDays
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in days, rounded down.
notes: 93784 seconds is 1 day

methods.name: ToDays
methods.brief: Returns the whole length counted in days, rounded down.
notes: the same value as TotalDays

methods.name: Days
methods.brief: Returns the number of whole days in the length.
notes: the same value as TotalDays
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Days -1, not 0

methods.name: Hours
methods.brief: Returns the hours left over after whole days are taken out, from 0 to 23.
notes: 26 hours total is 2 here
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Hours -1

methods.name: Minutes
methods.brief: Returns the minutes left over after whole hours are taken out, from 0 to 59.
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Minutes -2

methods.name: Seconds
methods.brief: Returns the seconds left over after whole minutes are taken out, from 0 to 59.
notes: 90 seconds answers 30
warnings: a negative duration gives a wrong part: -90 seconds answers Seconds -30

methods.name: Milliseconds
methods.brief: Returns the milliseconds part kept with the length, from 0 to 999.
warnings: stays 0 for a duration built from a number or a text, and AddMilliseconds does not change it: only the milliseconds key of a hash list sets it

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: Returns the length split into its parts, as a hash list of days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys days, hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds
notes: 93784 seconds gives 1, 2, 3, 4 and 0
warnings: a negative duration gives negative parts, which do not add back to the length

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the length as clock text, hours in total then minutes and seconds in two digits, such as 26:03:04.
methods.returns: a text, h:mm:ss by default; ToStringXT takes a format of your own
notes: ToStringXT reads d, H, h, m, s and z for the parts and dd, HH, hh, mm, ss and zzz for the padded ones, where H is the hour of the day, h the total hours and zzz the milliseconds; a letter that touches another letter stays as written, and Duration and Content are the same call

extensions.name: ToStringXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: ToHuman
methods.brief: Returns the length in words, such as 1 day, 2 hours, 3 minutes, and 4 seconds.
methods.returns: a text; 0 seconds for a zero length
notes: whole weeks and a few long spans have their own phrase: 7 days is 1 week, 14 days is 2 weeks, 30 days with 23:59:59 is 1 month, 183 days with 23:59:59 is 6 months and 365 days with 23:59:59 is 1 year, while exactly 30 or 365 days stay in days
warnings: a negative duration answers 0 seconds

methods.name: ToCompact
methods.brief: Returns the length in short units, such as 1d 2h 3m 4s, leaving out the parts that are zero.
methods.returns: a text; 0s for a zero length
notes: milliseconds are not shown; 100 days is 100d

methods.name: ToSimple
methods.brief: Returns the length as h:m:s, or as m:s under one hour, with minutes and seconds padded by spaces.
notes: the padding is a space, not a zero, so 90 seconds gives a leading space; ToString pads with zeros

methods.name: operator
methods.brief: Combines or compares the duration with another value by a sign, giving a new duration or TRUE or FALSE.

parameters.name: cOp
parameters.role: the operator as text: +, -, *, /, <, <=, >, >=, = or !=

parameters.name: pValue
parameters.role: the right-hand side: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration, where * and / take a number only

methods.returns: a stzDuration for + - * /, TRUE or FALSE for < <= > >= = !=, an empty text for any other operator or a division by zero
notes: 90 seconds plus 2 minutes is 210 seconds
warnings: the duration itself is not changed; the result of + - * / drops the milliseconds

methods.name: Compare
methods.brief: Compares the length with another and returns -1, 0 or 1.

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

methods.name: IsLessThan

parameters.name: pOther
parameters.role: a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration

methods.name: IsGreaterThan

parameters.name: pOther

parameters.name: pMax

warnings: a reversed range, with pMin above pMax, is never satisfied

methods.name: IsZero
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is exactly zero seconds.

methods.name: IsPositive
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is above zero.

methods.name: IsNegative
methods.brief: TRUE if the length is below zero, as after subtracting more than was there.

methods.name: Add
methods.brief: Adds a length to the duration in place; the length is a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length to add

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Subtract
methods.brief: Takes a length off the duration in place; the length is a number of seconds, a text of units or a stzDuration.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: the length to remove

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
warnings: the duration can go below zero

methods.name: Multiply
methods.brief: Multiplies the duration by a number, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the factor, a number

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: 100 seconds times 3 is 300

methods.name: Divide
methods.brief: Divides the duration by a number, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the divisor, a number

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: 300 seconds divided by 4 is 75
warnings: a division by zero is ignored without an error

methods.name: AddDays
methods.brief: Adds a number of days to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of days, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddHours
methods.brief: Adds a number of hours to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of hours, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddMinutes
methods.brief: Adds a number of minutes to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of minutes, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddSeconds
methods.brief: Adds a number of seconds to the duration, in place.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of seconds, which may be negative

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain

methods.name: AddMilliseconds
methods.brief: Adds a number of milliseconds to the duration, in place, but the sub-second part is not shown.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the number of milliseconds

methods.returns: the duration itself, so calls chain
notes: adding 1500 ms to 93784.5 s gives 93786 s
warnings: the milliseconds go into a hidden fraction of the total: 500 ms added to 93784 s leaves Milliseconds 0 and ToString unchanged, and only a later carry into a whole second shows

methods.name: ParseDurationString
methods.brief: Returns the number of seconds written in a text such as 2 hours 30 min, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cStr_
parameters.role: the text to read: numbers followed by the units day, hour or hr, minute or min, second or sec, millisecond or ms

methods.returns: a number of seconds, which may have a decimal part; 0 when no unit is found
notes: 1.5 hr is 5400 and 250 ms is 0.25
warnings: the units week, month and year are not understood and give 0; a number with no unit is ignored

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new duration of the same length, independent of the first.
notes: changing the copy does not change the original

methods.name: Clone
methods.brief: Returns a new duration of the same length, independent of the first.
notes: the same call as Copy
warnings: the milliseconds are dropped from the copy

methods.brief: Joins phrases such as 1 hour and 2 minutes into one sentence, with commas and a last and.

methods.returns: a text: one phrase as it is, two joined by and, three or more separated by commas ending with and

classes.name: stzEarcons
classes.brief: Turns a meaning (danger, warning, info, success, muted) into a short sound and decides when it may play, so a screen state is corroborated by ear.
classes.description: An author names a meaning and gets a motif: ToSoundOf returns it as data, with no audio device, and the audibility and priority questions are answered by pure functions (WouldFireAt, IsAudible, PriorityOf). Muted renders as silence. Start opens a sound pool and Fire plays a cue through the device, dropping it when the same value repeats inside the refractory period or a louder alert is still sounding; Say queues a cue and a spoken phrase, which are only heard through TickSpeech or SpeakQueueToEnd. A sound is not the acknowledgement: it arrives about 419 ms after Fire, against the 100 ms the screen has, so it must repeat what another channel already shows. Every example of this reference rendered to buffers; none played through a device, and what a person hears of the motifs has not been recorded here.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the vocabulary of four motifs for danger, warning, info and success, with muted left silent; no device is opened.
notes: the motifs are rendered by the engine at 48000 Hz into ordinary sample buffers

methods.name: ToSoundOf
methods.brief: Returns the motif that a meaning sounds like, as a sound buffer that needs no audio device.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value (danger, warning, info, success, muted) as a name or a text, optionally followed by .cue or .alert

methods.returns: a stzSound; an empty text for muted and for a meaning that is refused, with LastError telling which half was wrong
notes: the danger motif lasts 0.18 seconds at 48000 Hz

methods.name: IsSilentValue
methods.brief: TRUE if the meaning is muted, the one value whose rendering is silence.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an unknown meaning

methods.name: ToStepOf
methods.brief: Returns the step a meaning asks for, cue when none is written.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally followed by a dot and a step

methods.returns: a text, cue or alert or ambient; an empty text when the meaning is refused

methods.name: PriorityOf
methods.brief: Returns how severe a meaning is, from 4 for danger down to 1 for success.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number: danger 4, warning 3, info 2, success 1, and 0 for muted or an unknown meaning

methods.name: SetAmbientFloor
methods.brief: Declares the loudness of the room in dB against which audibility is judged; it is never measured.

parameters.name: pnDb
parameters.role: the declared ambient level in dB, -40 being a quiet office

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: a louder floor lowers every margin and can turn IsAudible to FALSE

methods.name: DeclaredFloor
methods.brief: Returns the ambient level in dB that margins are measured against.
methods.returns: a number, -40 until SetAmbientFloor changes it

methods.name: MarginMetric
methods.brief: Returns the name of the loudness measure that the audibility margin uses.
methods.returns: a text naming a K-weighted level over the sound's own length, which the text says is not an integrated LUFS figure

methods.name: LevelOf
methods.brief: Returns the K-weighted level of a meaning's motif over its own length, in dB.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number; -1000 for muted and for a refused meaning
notes: the danger motif measured -13.13 and the success motif -14.31

methods.name: AudibilityMarginOf
methods.brief: Returns how many dB a meaning's motif lies above the declared ambient floor.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number; -1000 when the meaning has no sound
notes: the danger margin was 26.87 over the default floor of -40

methods.name: RequiredMarginOf
methods.brief: Returns the headroom over the floor that a meaning must have: 10 for a cue and 20 for an alert.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally followed by .alert

methods.name: IsAudible
methods.brief: TRUE if the meaning's motif clears the required margin over the declared floor; muted counts as audible.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for an unknown meaning
notes: muted answers TRUE because silence is lawful

methods.name: WouldFireAt
methods.brief: TRUE if the playing rules let the meaning sound at the given time, and records the reason.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time in seconds on the player's clock

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; LastReason says why, ok when TRUE
notes: it refuses ambient steps, muted, the same value twice inside the refractory period, and a quieter meaning while an alert is still sounding

methods.name: RecordFireAt
methods.brief: Records that a meaning sounded at a time, so later decisions see the refractory period and any alert in force.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time in seconds when it sounded

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: an alert holds the floor for three times its motif length, and nothing happens for a refused meaning

methods.name: CountDropAt
methods.brief: Adds one to the count of dropped cues for a meaning.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain
notes: Fire calls it for you when WouldFireAt says no

methods.name: DropsOf
methods.brief: Returns how many cues of that meaning were dropped.

parameters.name: pMeaning
parameters.role: a semantic value, optionally with a step

methods.returns: a number, 0 for an unknown meaning

methods.name: LastReason
methods.brief: Returns why the last decision about a cue or a phrase went the way it did.
methods.returns: a text such as ok, muted renders as silence, or a refractory message; empty before any decision

methods.name: SetRefractory
methods.brief: Sets the period in seconds inside which a repeat of the same value counts as one event; it starts at 0.15.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the refractory period in seconds

methods.returns: the earcons object itself, so calls chain

classes.name: stzEduReader
classes.brief: Builds one self-contained HTML page for a course, which stores no output and says where each cell runs.
classes.description: The page follows the chapters that were run and observed, one article per language edition, switched by the URL hash; it needs no build tool and loads nothing from the network. It never holds an output: each cell carries a fixed sentence saying so, and keeps the author's promise lines, which are an expectation and not a result. Each cell is labelled where it ran as the guard observed it, and the cells run on the desktop, not in the browser: running them in the browser waits on ringscript. A translation is marked a draft until a native speaker has signed the unit off: the fr, ar and ha editions are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person in each language. No institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
o1.AddChapter( oC.RunChapterInQ("find-then-apply", [ "en" ])[1] )
? o1.NumberOfWorldPages()
#--> 0
? StzFindFirst("stores no output", o1.Html()) > 0
#--> 1

classes.name: stzEnvironmentState
classes.brief: Holds an in-memory environment: variables with their origin, a working directory, and a queue of commands waiting to run.
classes.description: It is the state the environment twin changes. Each variable is a [ name, value, origin ] row, the origin being mirrored for a value read from reality and virtual for one born in the twin, which is what a diff against reality needs. Apply is the hook the generic twin calls to rehearse an operation, and Clone gives the independent copy a snapshot or a rebuild starts from. Names are matched with case. Nothing here touches the real environment.
classes.example:
o1.PutVar("MODE", "dev", "virtual")
o1.SetCwd("/srv/app", "virtual")
o1.AddSpawn("make test")
? o1.VarValue("MODE")
#--> dev
? o1.Cwd()
#--> /srv/app
? o1.NumberOfPendingSpawns()
#--> 1

methods.name: EventCount
methods.brief: Total events emitted on the channel SINCE IT WAS CREATED -- the signal an event-driven consumer polls to detect new work.
methods.detail: It rises and never falls WHILE THE CHANNEL LIVES, which is not the same as monotonic, and the difference bites. DestroyChannel and ClearAll below put a channel back to zero, so a consumer holding a previous count sees a SMALLER number and, if it only tests for "bigger than last time", decides there is no new work -- for good. A DECREASE means the channel is new and the consumer must re-baseline; stzAgentHost.TickDue does exactly that.

methods.name: ChannelGeneration
methods.brief: WHICH channel currently holds this name -- a number unique to this process, or -2 when no channel does.
methods.detail: EventCount alone cannot tell a consumer that a channel was remade: the count restarts at zero, and by the time anyone polls it may already have climbed back above the value they remembered, so "did the number go down" misses it. The generation never repeats and never resets, so comparing it is exact rather than a race. stzAgentHost.TickDue re-baselines on it.

classes.name: stzFalseObject
classes.brief: Stands for a premise that did not hold: the object a failed natural chain returns, which keeps the chain going without turning true.
classes.description: A check written as a chain, such as Q("AnnIE").AtMost(2).VowelNBQ(), answers a stzFalseObject when it fails, so the next words of the sentence can still be read without raising an error. It carries two things: the sentence that tells why the chain stopped (WhyStopped) and the object that was judged (Origin). Every counting, comparing and quantifier device answers 0 or the false object itself, so a false premise absorbs the rest of the chain. Two devices bring it back to life: Otherwise runs an action on the origin and returns it, and OrQ returns the origin so a second alternative is tried. A false object has the content 0. A chain that fails without giving a reason reads a premise in the chain did not hold. To build one honestly, let a real check fail; SetOrigin and SetWhyStopped build one by hand.
classes.example:
? o1.WhyStopped()
#--> no: expected atmost 2, found 3
? o1.Content()
#--> 0
? o1.IfSo(:Uppercase).Content()
#--> 0
? o1.Otherwise(:Lowercase).Content()
#--> annie

classes.name: stzFileBlobStore
classes.brief: Stores binary objects by key in a folder on disk, the four verbs of an S3 bucket over a flat key namespace.
classes.description: Save, Fetch, Exists and Remove are the whole port; listing is by prefix. A key is never a file name: each object is a file named by the SHA-256 of its key, with the real key kept in a .key file beside it, so keys that differ only by case stay distinct, a key such as ../x cannot leave the folder, and slashes are ordinary characters. Keys are limited to 1024 bytes, as in S3. It is a real store, not a fake, and it survives a restart. It has no presigned URLs, no versioning and no replication.
classes.example:
o1.Save("photos/2026/a.jpg", "abcde")
o1.Save("Photo.JPG", "XY")
? o1.NumberOfBlobs()
#--> 2
? o1.Fetch("photos/2026/a.jpg")
#--> abcde
? o1.Exists("photo.jpg")
#--> 0
? @@( o1.KeysWithPrefix("photos/") )
#--> [ "photos/2026/a.jpg" ]
o1.Clear()

classes.name: stzFileModifier
classes.brief: Changes parts of an existing file line by line, or by text, and rewrites the file after each change.
classes.description: Reach for it to edit a file in place: ModifyLine, InsertLineAt, RemoveLine, Modify (every occurrence of a text) and ReplaceLineContaining each rewrite the file at once. The object keeps its own copy of the text and lines, kept in step with its changes (OriginalContent shows the latest text, not the text at open time), so use one modifier per edit session. Lines are joined with a line feed and no final one is added. InsertLine and the :With form of Modify raise errors today.
classes.receiver: write("demo_note.txt", "alpha" + char(10) + "beta gamma" + char(10) + "end") o1 = new stzFileModifier("demo_note.txt")
classes.example:
o1.ModifyLine(2, "BETA")
? o1.OriginalContent() = "alpha" + char(10) + "BETA" + char(10) + "end"
#--> 1
o1.InsertLineAtEnd("fin")
? o1.OriginalLineCount()
#--> 4
? o1.RemoveLine(9)
#--> 0

classes.name: stzFileTree
classes.brief: Holds an in-memory tree of files and folders: a flat map of paths to nodes, each with a type, content and origin.
classes.description: It is the state the file twin changes. A node is [ path, type, content, origin ], the origin being mirrored for a node read from the disk and virtual for one born in the twin, which is the seam a diff against reality needs. A node keeps its first origin when its content is replaced. Apply is the hook the generic twin calls to rehearse an operation, and Clone gives the independent copy a snapshot or a rebuild starts from. Paths are matched exactly and the tree is flat: removing a folder does not remove the nodes below it. Nothing here touches the disk.

classes.name: stzFolder
classes.brief: Holds a folder as a position you can walk, and lists, finds, searches, edits, creates, copies and deletes the files and folders under it.
classes.description: A stzFolder is built on a path, created when it is missing, and keeps a current position, a home to return to (GoHome) and a history (GoBack). Listings are of the position, in lowercase: Files and Folders give the direct children as /name and /name/, DeepFiles and DeepFolders walk the whole tree. Find, Search and Modify come in three reaches: this folder (FindFiles, SearchInFiles, ModifyInRoot), one named child folder, and the Deep forms below. A path given to a method is read from the current position, never from the process folder, so sub1/d.txt, /sub1/d.txt and the absolute path name the same file; only the constructor, the In methods that take a folder path to search (DeepCountFilesIn and the like) and the file functions outside the class read the process folder. Whether a path is held here is decided on disk, at any depth below the position, and the . and .. segments are folded first, so a path cannot step out of the position. Many file methods finish by moving the position into the folder of the file when it is below the position; SetBatchMode(1) turns that off. The delete methods are real: DeleteFolder, DeleteAll, Erase, DeepRemoveAll, DeepErase, DeepDeleteFile and DeepDeleteFolder remove what they name, and GoUp can lift the position above the home, so point an object at a folder you can afford to lose. GoTo does not check that the folder exists, and CollapseFolders has no visible effect, each carried as a warning on its method.

methods.name: IsBatchMode
methods.brief: TRUE if batch mode is on, so file and folder operations leave the current position alone.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE by default

methods.name: SetBatchMode
methods.brief: Turns batch mode on or off; on, the create, delete, read and write methods no longer try to move into the folder they touched.

parameters.name: b
parameters.role: 1 to turn batch mode on, 0 to turn it off

methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place
notes: With it off (the default) the file methods end by moving the position into the folder of the file they touched, when that folder is below the position
warnings: Raises an error for any value but 1 or 0

methods.name: GetDirectoryPath
methods.brief: Returns the absolute path of the folder that holds a path, read from the current position.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: a file or folder name or path, relative to the position or absolute

notes: Pure text work; the path need not exist

methods.name: CurrentPath
methods.brief: Returns the current position as text with a trailing slash, so a relative name can be joined to it directly.
notes: WorkingDirectory and pwd are the same method

methods.name: GoTo
methods.brief: Moves the current position to a folder below it, writing the old position to the history; the folder is not checked to exist.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: a name or a path strictly below the current position

notes: MoveTo and cd are the same method; GoTo('..') is accepted as text and leaves a path with .. in it
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path that is not strictly below the position, an absolute path included when it is the position itself or above

methods.name: GoUp
methods.brief: Moves the current position to its parent folder, writing the old one to the history; it may leave the home folder.
notes: Nothing stops it going above the folder the object was created with, and the delete methods then act on that parent; Up and cdUp are the same method
warnings: Raises an error at a drive or filesystem root

methods.name: GoHome
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the folder the object was created with, writing the old one to the history.
notes: GoToHome, GoToRoot and GoRoot are the same method

methods.name: GoBack
methods.brief: Moves the current position back to the last one in the history and removes that entry.
notes: Back and Previous are the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the history is empty

methods.name: PathHistory
methods.brief: Returns the positions the object has left, oldest first.
notes: NavigationHistory is the same method; every GoTo, GoUp, GoHome adds one

methods.name: ClearHistory
methods.brief: Empties the history of positions.
methods.returns: nothing; the object is changed in place

methods.name: IsAtHome
methods.brief: TRUE if the current position is the folder the object was created with.
notes: IsAtRoot is the same method

methods.name: RelativePathFromHome
methods.brief: Returns the path that leads from the home folder to the current position, "." at home.
methods.returns: text, such as sub1/deep1; one .. per level when GoUp has left the home folder

methods.name: DistanceFromHome
methods.brief: Returns how many folder levels lie between the home folder and the current position, 0 at home.
methods.returns: a number; a level above home counts as one, like a level below

methods.name: NavigationInfo
methods.brief: Returns pairs describing the position: home, current, relativefromhome, distancefromhome and history.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.name: CreateFolder
methods.brief: Creates a folder below the current position, with every missing level, and moves into it unless batch mode is on.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a folder name or path below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); also 1 when the folder already exists
notes: FolderCreate and MakeFolder are the same method; a relative path is joined to the position the object is at, which is inside the previous folder after a first CreateFolder
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path outside the current position

extensions.name: CreateFolderQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreateFolders
methods.brief: Creates several folders below the current position, each with its missing levels, without moving.

parameters.name: paNames
parameters.role: a list of folder names or paths below the current position

notes: MakeFolders and CreateSubFolders are the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

extensions.name: CreateFoldersQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: CreatePath
methods.brief: Creates a deep folder path below the current position, every missing level included, without moving.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: a path below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); also 1 when the path already exists
notes: MkPath and CreateDeepPath are the same method
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or for a path outside the current position

extensions.name: CreatePathQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: MkPathQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: CreateDeepPathQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DeleteFolder
methods.brief: Deletes a folder held here with everything inside it, then moves to its parent when that is below the position.

parameters.name: _cFolder_
parameters.role: the folder to delete, by name, sub-path or absolute path below the position

notes: FolderDelete, RemoveFolder and FolderRemove are the same method
warnings: Raises an error (Folder does not exist.) for a name not held here, and an error (Can't navigate outside the folder!) for the position itself or a path above it

methods.name: DeleteAll
methods.brief: Deletes every file and every subfolder held directly here, subfolders with their contents, keeps this folder, and goes home.
notes: DeleteAllFiles, DeepDeleteFiles, FilesDeepDelete and AllFilesDeepDelete are the same method; despite those names it removes subfolders too
warnings: Raises an error when something cannot be removed

methods.name: RemoveAll
methods.brief: Deletes every file and every subfolder held directly here, keeps this folder, and goes home.
notes: RemoveAllFiles, DeepRemoveFiles, FilesDeepRemove and AllFilesDeepRemove call DeleteAll
warnings: Raises an error when something cannot be removed

methods.name: DeepRemoveAll
methods.brief: Removes this folder itself with everything in it; the object then points to a folder that no longer exists.
notes: DeepRemove and RemoveTree are the same method

methods.name: Erase
methods.brief: Deletes the files held directly here and keeps the folders.
notes: RemoveFiles is the same method; the position does not change

methods.name: DeepErase
methods.brief: Deletes every file of the whole tree below and keeps all the folders.

methods.name: DeepDeleteFile
methods.brief: Deletes every file of that name anywhere in the tree below, ignoring case, and tells whether one was deleted.

parameters.name: cFileName
parameters.role: the file name to delete, with or without a leading slash

methods.returns: TRUE when at least one file was deleted, FALSE when none bears that name
notes: FileDeepDelete, DeepRemoveFile and FileDeepRemove call it; only files below the current position are touched
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a non-empty text

methods.name: DeepDeleteFolder
methods.brief: Deletes every folder of that name anywhere in the tree below, with its contents, and answers 1 unless a deletion failed.

parameters.name: _cFolderName_
parameters.role: the folder name to delete, with or without slashes, ignoring case

methods.returns: 1, also when no folder bears that name; 0 when a deletion failed
notes: DeepRemoveFolder, FolderDeepDelete and FolderDeepRemove are the same method; only folders below the current position are touched
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a non-empty text

methods.name: FileRead
methods.brief: Returns the text of a file held here, at any depth below the current position.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name, a sub-path such as sub1/d.txt, or an absolute path

notes: ReadFile is the same method; FileReadQ gives the reader object; with batch mode off the position then moves into the folder of the file
warnings: Raises an error for a path that is not a file held here, a folder name included

extensions.name: FileReadQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: ReadFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileCreate
methods.brief: Creates an empty file below the current position and answers 1; it raises an error when the name is taken.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: the file name or path to create, in a folder that exists

notes: CreateFile is the same method; with batch mode off the position then moves into the folder of the file
warnings: Raises an error when the name is taken or when its folder does not exist (nodir/n.txt); CreatePath makes the folder first

extensions.name: FileCreateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: CreateFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FilesCreate
methods.brief: Creates the listed files and reports which were created and which failed, with the error of each.

parameters.name: acFileNames
parameters.role: the list of file names to create

methods.returns: a list of two pairs, [ "created", [ names ] ] and [ "failed", [ [ name, error ] ... ] ]
notes: CreateFiles is the same method; a name that already exists, or whose folder is missing, is reported as failed with its own error

methods.name: FileOverwrite
methods.brief: Replaces the whole content of a file held here by a text and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text that replaces the content

notes: OverwriteFile is the same method; FileOverwriteQ gives the overwriter object
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

extensions.name: FileOverwriteQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: OverwriteFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileErase
methods.brief: Empties a file held here, keeping the file, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

notes: EraseFile is the same method; FileRemove deletes the file itself
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

extensions.name: FileEraseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: EraseFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileSafeErase
methods.brief: Copies a file held here to a .bak file beside it, then empties the file, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

notes: SafeEraseFile is the same method; an older .bak of the same file is replaced
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

extensions.name: FileSafeEraseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: SafeEraseFileQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FileRemove
methods.brief: Deletes a file held here, at any depth below the current position, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name, a sub-path such as sub1/d.txt, or an absolute path

notes: FileDelete, RemoveFile and DeleteFile are the same method; with batch mode off the position then moves into the folder the file was in
warnings: Raises an error for a path that is not a file held here

methods.name: FileBackup
methods.brief: Copies a file held here to a .bak file beside it, replacing an older copy, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

notes: BackupFile is the same method; FileCopy writes a copy under another name
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

methods.name: FileSafeOverwrite
methods.brief: Copies a file held here to a .bak file beside it, then replaces its content by a text, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text that replaces the content

notes: SafeOverwriteFile is the same method; an older .bak of the same file is replaced
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

methods.name: FileModify
methods.brief: Replaces every occurrence of a text in a file held here, case-sensitively, and answers 1 even when none was found.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: an existing file held here

parameters.name: cOldContent
parameters.role: the text to replace

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text to put in its place

notes: ModifyFile is the same method
warnings: Raises an error when the file is not held here

methods.name: FileCopy
methods.brief: Copies a file held here to a new name, replacing a file that is already there, and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cSourceFile_
parameters.role: the file to copy

parameters.name: _cDestFile_
parameters.role: the name or path of the copy, below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); 0 when the destination folder is missing
notes: CopyFile is the same method; an existing destination is overwritten without warning
warnings: Raises an error when the source is not held here or the destination is outside

methods.name: FileMove
methods.brief: Moves a file held here to a new name or into another folder below the position and answers 1.

parameters.name: _cSourceFile_
parameters.role: the file to move

parameters.name: _cDestFile_
parameters.role: the new name or path, below the current position

methods.returns: 1 (TRUE); 0 when the destination folder is missing
notes: MoveFile is the same method; a move into a missing folder answers 0 and moves nothing
warnings: Raises an error when the source is not held here or the destination is outside

methods.name: FileSize
methods.brief: Returns the size of a file held here, in bytes.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name, a sub-path, or an absolute path below the position

notes: FileSizeInBytes is the same method; an empty file answers 0
warnings: Raises an error for a path that is not a file held here

methods.name: FileInfo
methods.brief: Returns pairs describing a file held here, such as its size, suffix and last modification time.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name, a sub-path, or an absolute path below the position

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs, the keys in lowercase: name (without suffix), size, suffix, path, exists, iswritable, isreadable and lastmodified
warnings: Raises an error for a path that is not a file held here

extensions.name: FileInfoQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: FileInfoXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: FindFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that match a name, a pattern with * or a list of names, ignoring case.

parameters.name: pPattern
parameters.role: a file name, a pattern with * as a wildcard, or a list of file names

methods.returns: a list of "/name" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: FindFile and FindThisFile are the same method; a.txt finds /a.txt and *.txt finds every .txt file
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text or a number; a lone * finds nothing

methods.name: FindFolders
methods.brief: Returns the folders held directly here that match a name or a pattern with *, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a folder name with or without slashes, or a pattern with * as a wildcard, such as sub*

methods.returns: a list of "/name/" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: FindFolder and FindThisFolder are the same method; raises an error for an empty text

methods.name: FindFilesByExtension
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that end with an extension, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cExt_
parameters.role: a file extension, with or without the leading dot

notes: FilesByExtension is the same method
warnings: Raises an error for an empty text

methods.name: FindTheseFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files held directly here that match any of a list of names or patterns, each file once.

parameters.name: acFilesNames
parameters.role: a list of file names or * patterns

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

methods.name: FindTheseFolders
methods.brief: Returns the folders held directly here that match any of a list of * patterns, each folder once; plain names match nothing.

parameters.name: acFoldersNames
parameters.role: a list of * patterns, such as sub*

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list; a plain name answers nothing for the reason given at FindFolders

methods.name: Find
methods.brief: Returns the files and then the folders held directly here that match a name or a pattern with *, as one flat list.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a name or a pattern with * as a wildcard

methods.returns: a list of text: the file entries "/name", then the folder entries "/name/"
notes: FindFiles and FindFolders give the two halves apart

methods.name: DeepFindFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files of the whole tree below that match a name or a pattern with *, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a file name, or a pattern with * as a wildcard

methods.returns: a list of "/folder/name" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: DeepFindFile and DeepFindThisFile are the same method; a name is matched on its last segment, a * pattern on the whole entry
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not text

methods.name: DeepFindFolders
methods.brief: Returns the folders of the whole tree below that match a name or a pattern with *, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a folder name, or a pattern with * as a wildcard

methods.returns: a list of "/folder/name/" entries; [ ] when none match
notes: DeepFindFolder and DeepFindThisFolder are the same method; unlike the top-level search, a plain name matches here
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not text

methods.name: DeepFindTheseFiles
methods.brief: Returns the files of the whole tree below that match any of a list of names or patterns, each file once.

parameters.name: acFilesNames
parameters.role: a list of file names or * patterns

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

methods.name: DeepFindTheseFolders
methods.brief: Returns the folders of the whole tree below that match any of a list of names or patterns, each folder once.

parameters.name: acFoldersNames
parameters.role: a list of folder names or * patterns

warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not a list

methods.name: DeepFind
methods.brief: Returns the files and then the folders of the whole tree that match a name or a pattern with *, as one flat list.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a name or a pattern with * as a wildcard

methods.returns: a list of text: the file entries "/folder/name", then the folder entries "/folder/name/"
notes: DeepFindFileOrFolder and DeepFindThisFileOrFolder are the same method; the two finders give the halves apart

methods.name: SearchInFiles
methods.brief: Returns, for each file held directly here, the numbers of the lines that hold a text, ignoring case; files with no match are left out.

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ "/name", [ line numbers ] ] pairs
notes: A line matches when it holds the text anywhere in it
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not text

methods.name: SearchInFile
methods.brief: Returns the numbers of the lines of one file that hold a text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name, or a path below the current position

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of line numbers, 1 for the first; [ ] when the file is missing or nothing matches
notes: SearchInThisFile is the same method; a sub-path such as sub1/d.txt is read from the current position
warnings: Raises an error when an argument is not text

methods.name: SearchInTheseFiles
methods.brief: Returns, for each listed file, the numbers of the lines that hold a text; files with no match are left out.

parameters.name: _acFiles_
parameters.role: a list of file names

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ name as given, [ line numbers ] ] pairs
warnings: Raises an error when the files are not a list or the text is not text

methods.name: SearchInFolders
methods.brief: Returns, for each file of the folders held directly here, the numbers of the lines that hold a text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ file name, [ line numbers ] ] pairs; files with no match are left out
notes: The folders inside those folders are not entered; DeepSearchInFiles goes all the way down
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not text

methods.name: SearchInFolder
methods.brief: Returns, for each file of a child folder, the numbers of the lines that hold a text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cFolder_
parameters.role: a child folder, as a name

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ file name, [ line numbers ] ] pairs; files with no match are left out
notes: SearchInThisFolder is the same method; the folders inside it are not entered
warnings: Raises an error when an argument is not text

methods.name: SearchInTheseFolders
methods.brief: Returns, for each file of the listed child folders, the numbers of the lines that hold a text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _acFolders_
parameters.role: a list of child folder names

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ file name, [ line numbers ] ] pairs; files with no match are left out
warnings: Raises an error when the folders are not a list or the text is not text

methods.name: DeepSearchInFiles
methods.brief: Returns, for each file of the whole tree below, the numbers of the lines that hold a text, ignoring case; files with no match are left out.

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ absolute path, [ line numbers ] ] pairs
warnings: Raises an error when the argument is not text

methods.name: DeepSearchInFile
methods.brief: Returns the line numbers that hold a text in every file of that name found anywhere below, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: the file name to look for

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ absolute path, [ line numbers ] ] pairs
notes: The file name is matched ignoring case
warnings: Raises an error when an argument is not text

methods.name: DeepSearchInTheseFiles
methods.brief: Returns the line numbers that hold a text in every file below that has one of the listed names.

parameters.name: _acFiles_
parameters.role: a list of file names

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ absolute path, [ line numbers ] ] pairs
warnings: Raises an error when the files are not a list or the text is not text

methods.name: DeepSearchInFolder
methods.brief: Returns the lines that hold a text in the files of every folder of that name found anywhere below, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _cFolder_
parameters.role: a folder name, with or without slashes

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ absolute path, [ line numbers ] ] pairs, one per file with a match
notes: Only the files directly in those folders are read; DeepSearchInFiles reads every file below
warnings: Raises an error when an argument is not text

methods.name: DeepSearchInFolders
methods.brief: Returns the lines that hold a text in the files of every folder bearing one of the listed names below, ignoring case.

parameters.name: _acFolders_
parameters.role: a list of folder names

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to look for

methods.returns: a list of [ absolute path, [ line numbers ] ] pairs, one per file with a match
warnings: Raises an error when the folders are not a list or the text is not text

methods.name: Matches
methods.brief: TRUE if a name fits a pattern whose star is at the start, the end or both ends; a lone star fits everything, anything else must be equal.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a pattern such as *.txt, a*, *b* or a plain name

parameters.name: _cName_
parameters.role: the name to test

notes: A star in the middle, as in a*c, is not supported and only matches an equal name, read from the body
warnings: The test is case-sensitive, and a question mark is not a wildcard although it is converted

methods.name: GetFoldersContainingFileMatches

parameters.role: the folder to search, as an absolute path

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: the file pattern

methods.returns: a list of folder names, each once, such as [ "sub1", "deep1" ]
notes: VizDeepFindFiles opens exactly those folders in its drawing

methods.name: CountFileMatches

parameters.role: the folder to count in, as an absolute path

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a pattern with * as a wildcard

warnings: A pattern with capitals such as *.TXT counts 0, because the names are listed in lowercase

methods.name: CountFolderMatches
methods.brief: Returns how many folders held directly in a folder match a pattern; the match is case-sensitive against lowercase names.

parameters.name: _cPath_
parameters.role: the folder to count in, as an absolute path

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: a pattern with * as a wildcard

methods.name: ModifyInFile
methods.brief: Replaces every occurrence of a text in a file held under the current position, and answers 1 if the file exists, 0 if not.

parameters.name: _cFile_
parameters.role: a file name or a sub-path below the current position

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to replace

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text to put in its place

methods.returns: 1 or 0; 1 even when the text was not found
notes: The replacement is case-sensitive and covers every occurrence; the file is rewritten
warnings: Raises an error when an argument is not text

methods.name: ModifyInFiles
methods.brief: Replaces a text in each listed file and returns how many of them exist.

parameters.name: _acFiles_
parameters.role: a list of file names

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to replace

parameters.name: cNewContent
parameters.role: the text to put in its place

notes: Missing names are skipped
warnings: Raises an error when the files are not a list or a text argument is not text

methods.name: ModifyInFolder
methods.brief: Replaces a text in every file held directly in a child folder and returns how many files were rewritten.

parameters.name: _cFolder_
parameters.role: a child folder name

parameters.name: cContent
parameters.role: the text to replace

parameters.name: cNewContent

classes.name: stzFont
classes.brief: Holds a loaded TTF or OTF typeface and measures text with it: widths, glyph positions, caret rectangles, and which glyphs a fallback chain had to borrow.
classes.description: The font is bytes you loaded, shaped by the engine's own pipeline (bidirectional analysis, HarfBuzz, stb_truetype), so a width can be trusted for layout in any script, Arabic included. Sizes are in pixels. A text that one font cannot draw comes out as hollow boxes, one per character; AddFallback puts other fonts behind it and CoverageOf counts what was borrowed and what is still missing. The caret and hit-test queries (RectsOfRange, CaretRectAt, IndexAtPoint) count bytes, not characters. The object holds one number, the engine's id for the face, so copies of the object share the same loaded font; after Free every measurement answers 0 or an empty list (and DrawsEveryGlyphOf answers TRUE, which is misleading). A stzCanvas draws text with a font set by SetFont.

methods.brief: EACH OF THESE IS ONE ENGINE CALL, not a transform this class then walks.
methods.detail: The readings are what callers actually want -- raw complex bins are rarely the answer -- so they belong to the engine and every language over it, not to a loop written once per binding. |X_k| per bin: "how much of this frequency is present". classes.name: stzGeoAtlas
classes.brief: Binds the names and codes a caller types to the shapes of a boundary file the caller loaded, and reports what did not bind instead of guessing.
classes.description: A business table has a column of place names and wants a map: the user types USA and a shape appears. This class does the tedious and safe half: folding case, accents and punctuation, knowing that Burma and Myanmar are one country (about 50 aliases, each a fact about language, not about a border), finding a numeric id in a file that writes names, and a 2 or 3 letter code through the library's country table. The shapes are the CALLER'S file, never vendored here: the boundary data carries a position on every disputed border, a vintage and a licence the library will not own (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). A near miss is reported by Unresolved and never guessed, because a map that silently colours Niger for Nigeria is worse than one with a hole. IndexOf tries, in order, the file's id as written, the file's own name folded, an alias in either direction, then a country code. ValuesFor answers one value per feature, in the file's order, with the empty text where nothing bound: exactly what stzGeoMap.SetValues takes, so a table becomes a choropleth in two calls. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoAtlas/table_to_map.png, a typed table drawn on the world with the unbound keys listed and the unmentioned countries hatched, RIGHT; how_a_key_resolves.png, the page of 21 keys and what each found, RIGHT; niger_regions_table.png, a table with a misspelt region, RIGHT (the misspelt region and the forgotten one are hatched and named). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoEllipsoid
classes.brief: Holds one reference ellipsoid by name and measures on it: shortest and constant-bearing paths, destinations, meridian and parallel lengths, ECEF and ENU frames, areas.
classes.description: Fifteen ellipsoids are known (WGS84, GRS80, WGS72, GRS67, Airy1830, AiryModified, Bessel1841, Clarke1866, Clarke1880, International1924, Krassovsky1940, Everest1830, AustralianNational, SouthAmerican1969 and Sphere) and WGS84 is the default everywhere, because it is what a GPS reports. The engine speaks metres and degrees: a method ending Km answers kilometres, one ending M metres. Mind the axis order: the point methods take LATITUDE FIRST, then longitude (DistanceKm, Azimuth, DestinationKm, MidpointOf ...), while every flat list of places (AreaKm2, PathLengthKm and the Flat methods) and every stzGeoProjection method take LONGITUDE FIRST; swapping them raises nothing and measures another pair of places. Niamey to Paris is 3919.43 km on WGS84 and 3931.58 km if the arguments are swapped. A shortest path (geodesic) is not a constant-bearing path (rhumb line): New York to London is 5585.2 km by the first and 5809.8 km by the second. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/geodesic_vs_rhumb.png, a geodesic and a rhumb line on a Mercator, RIGHT (the rhumb line is straight, the geodesic bows toward the pole); doc/gallery/stzGeoEllipsoid/rings_and_areas.png, rings made with DestinationKm on an azimuthal equidistant map, RIGHT (they are true circles); ellipsoids_compared.png, six ellipsoids as the gap from WGS84 in metres and km2, RIGHT (the Sphere is 10.8 km long on Niamey to Paris). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoFeatures
classes.brief: Holds the polygons, lines and points of a boundary file whole, every part and every hole, read from GeoJSON or TopoJSON, and answers what lies where.
classes.description: Build one with StzGeoFeaturesFromJson, StzGeoFeaturesFromTopoJson or StzGeoFeaturesFromJsonWhere, which also compute the boxes that make point-in-region tests fast. Each feature is a kind, an id, a hash list of properties and its parts; a polygon part is a list of rings, the first the outer edge and every one after it a hole. Every ring is closed, whichever format it came from. Coordinates are longitude then latitude, degrees, as both formats require, and every place-taking method here is LONGITUDE FIRST (Contains, IndexAt, Within). Nothing is simplified or reprojected, and this library vendors no boundary data: the atlas files are the caller's (test/graphics/atlas/README.md). Areas are measured on WGS84. One trap in the windows: a feature that crosses the antimeridian (Fiji, Russia, Antarctica) has a bounding box 360 degrees wide whose middle falls anywhere, so Within and IndicesWithin take Fiji for an Africa window. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/parts_holes_lookup.png, parts, holes, an IndexAt raster of Niger and South Africa's hole, RIGHT; doc/gallery/stzGeoFeatures/window_and_areas.png, the areas panel RIGHT and the Within panel WRONG (Fiji is taken, see FINDINGS_geo.md); lines_points_kinds.png, a river, wells and a lake with a hole read from GeoJSON, RIGHT. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoField
classes.brief: Holds a quantity that has a value everywhere, a grid of numbers over longitude and latitude, and draws it as a classed raster, as contours and with its legend.
classes.description: The grid is [ lon0, lat0, dlon, dlat, nx, ny ] with row 0 the SOUTH row, and an unknown node is the empty text, never a number: the commonest way an elevation map acquires a trench eleven kilometres deep is a NODATA of -9999 read as a depth. A field comes from StzGeoDensityField (the kernel density of a stzGeoPoints, in places per km2, edge-corrected and clipped to the window), from StzGeoFieldFromAsciiGrid (an ESRI ASCII grid, whose first text row is the north row and whose xllcorner is turned into a node centre) or from stzGeoSamples (inverse distance weighting and kriging). Classes must be set before DrawOn, which raises otherwise. The raster is resampled through the projection pixel by pixel, so a conic does not turn cells into wrong quadrilaterals. A field in per km2 refuses a projection that does not preserve area (FindingsOn). Set classes, ramp and unit on the field BEFORE putting it in a list: Ring copies an object it stores, so a change made through the list does not reach the original. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoField/rain_kriging.png, IDW, kriging and kriging variance of invented gauges, RIGHT (the variance is low at each gauge and high in the gaps); density_and_contours.png, a kernel density as raster and contours, RIGHT; ascii_grid_terrain.png, an ASCII grid read three ways, WRONG in one detail (a scatter of white pixels in the lowest class, see FINDINGS_geo.md). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoMap
classes.brief: Holds a map made of layers: a projection and a set of features, with values, classes, groups, labels, insets, legends, scale bar, sun and flows drawn on a canvas.
classes.description: Build it with StzGeoMap(oProjection, oFeatures) after fitting the projection to the features. The data layer takes one value per feature (SetValues, from stzGeoAtlas.ValuesFor, CountPointsIn or ValuesFromArea) or named groups (SetGroups), the classes are the author's (SetClasses, SetRamp, SetOpenTop) and a region with no value is hatched, never coloured as zero. SetPaper tells the map its sheet and should be the first call: labels are kept on it and the scale bar and the stream- density raster are measured over it. DrawSheetOn is the statistical map: dark hairline borders, the no-data hatch and the selection outlined; DrawLabelsOn writes a name inside its region or numbers it with a key; AddInset magnifies a place too small to label. A map judges itself (Findings, IsSound): a choropleth, a membership map or hexagon bins on a projection that is not equal-area is an error, as is a number with no key. Known gaps: with values set and no classes, ClassOf, ColourOf and the Draw methods that colour raise error R2; an inset does not copy SetOpenTop; DensityPointsIn is per 10000 km2. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoMap/niger_density.png, a density choropleth with inset, legend, scale bar and north arrow, RIGHT except the Niamey inset, which is grey instead of red (WRONG, see FINDINGS_geo.md); world_area.png, country areas on Equal Earth with a hatched no-data region, RIGHT; africa_blocs.png, a membership map, RIGHT; daynight_world.png, the night side and twilight on 2026-10-05, RIGHT; hexbin_flows.png, hexagon bins, area-true circles and great-circle routes, RIGHT; wind_streams.png and wind_arrows.png, an invented wind field, RIGHT as far as a picture can say. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.brief: Holds a list of places and the window they were observed in, and answers whether they are clustered, scattered or random, where their middle is and which way they spread.
classes.description: A pattern is never a bare list: it is the places AND the region, because a hundred wells in Tunisia and the same hundred in Niger are one list and two opposite answers. The places are one flat list lon, lat, lon, lat, ... (longitude first); distances are kilometres on a sphere of 6371 km, areas on WGS84. The measures are Clark-Evans (edge-corrected by Donnelly), Ripley's K, L, G and F, the null band by simulation (Envelope, 39 simulations being the classic count), the mean centre, the spatial median and the standard deviational ellipse. Three generators make patterns whose truth is known, all seeded so a picture does not move: Sample (uniform), SampleClustered (Matern) and SampleDispersed (hard core); StzGeoProcess is the general form. A point outside the window is reported by Outside and Findings, never dropped. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib- docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoPoints/three_patterns.png, three invented patterns in Niger with ellipse, centres and Clark-Evans verdicts, RIGHT (random, clustered and dispersed are named as the patterns were made); ripley_g_f.png, L with its band, G and F, RIGHT (L climbs far above the band for clusters, G stays at 0 below the hard-core distance for the dispersed pattern); outside_the_window.png, places across the border counted but flagged, RIGHT. Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoProcess
classes.brief: Holds one of seven point processes, a mechanism for putting points down, with its parameters, and generates patterns from it and judges a pattern against it.
classes.description: The seven are Poisson (no interaction, random count), Binomial (the same with a fixed count), Inhomogeneous (no interaction, varying intensity from a surface), MaternCluster (parents you never see, children in a disc), Thomas (children scattered by a Gaussian, so a cluster has a scale but no edge), MaternII (inhibition by deletion, which has a ceiling) and SSI (inhibition by refusal, which keeps packing). Asking whether a pattern is more clustered than a model that already explains something, not than complete spatial randomness, is the point. The setters write three shared slots, shown by Content: a (intensity, count or parent intensity), b (mean children) and c (radius, sigma or hard-core distance). GenerateIn throws one pattern in the window of a stzGeoPoints; EnvelopeOf, EscapesOf and VerdictOn judge an observed pattern against the band the process makes: 39 simulations being the classic count, and the band widens with the count. Counts of the cluster processes vary widely between seeds (a standard deviation of about 90 on a mean of 190). Known gaps: PatternIn raises today, and ExpectedCount for Inhomogeneous is the mean of the whole grid times the window area. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoProcess/seven_processes.png, one pattern from each process, RIGHT (clusters compact, inhibited processes evenly spaced, the inhomogeneous one follows its field); null_models.png, one pattern against three nulls, RIGHT (it escapes Poisson and Binomial everywhere and never the MaternCluster that made it); matern_ii_ceiling.png, survivors against proposal rate, RIGHT (MaternII levels off near the ceiling, SSI packs about twice as many). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.
