classes.name: stzGeoProjection
classes.brief: Holds the choice of how to flatten the sphere: one of 44 named projections with its rotation, parallels, scale and clip, and answers where a place goes on paper and what place a pixel is.
classes.description: The object keeps eleven numbers (Params) and crosses the bridge to the engine with them on every call, so the Ring object is the single source of truth. Project takes LONGITUDE FIRST, then latitude, and answers paper units with y growing downward, or an empty list for a place behind a globe or without an image; Invert goes back. A new projection has scale 150 and translation 480, 250: use a Fit method (FitToSphere, FitSphereIn for the world, FitFeaturesIn, FitPointsIn, FitFeatureIn for a place) to put the picture in the box you draw in. Lines come back as pieces, cut where a flat map's seam or a globe's horizon cuts them. The sphere is a sphere: no projection here uses an ellipsoid (stzGeoEllipsoid measures on one). IsEqualArea and IsConformal say what the projection claims, Distortion and HoldsItsClaim measure it, and stzGeoMap refuses a choropleth on a projection that is not equal-area. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoProjection/projections_compared.png, six projections with Tissot circles, RIGHT (Mercator circles swell toward the poles, the equal-area ones keep their size and squash); globe_routes.png, an orthographic globe with great-circle routes and range rings, RIGHT; niger_conic_utm.png, Niger on a conic and on a Mercator, RIGHT (the printed area scales 1.06 and 1.18 are the secant squared of 13.5 and 23 degrees). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGeoSamples
classes.brief: Holds measurements at places, rain gauges say, and estimates the value in between by inverse distance weighting or ordinary kriging, with the error kriging owes.
classes.description: The measurements are one flat list lon, lat, value, ... and the window is the ground the estimate is made over and clipped to. Three answers, in the order an analyst uses them: IDWField (needs no model, tells nothing of its error, never leaves the measured range), Variogram with FitVariogram (the curve everything else is read from: nugget, sill and range) and KrigeFields, which returns TWO fields, the estimate and its variance, together on purpose: the variance depends only on where the gauges are and on the variogram, never on the values. A model must be adopted (FitAndUse) before GammaAt, KrigeAt, KrigeFields and CrossValidate, which raise otherwise. Kriging expects a field without a trend: for gauges whose value falls steadily to the north the fitted range is longer than the window, and the estimate leaves the measured range by tens of thousands, with only a warning from Findings. Pictures, each looked at by 'stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG)' on 2026-10-05: doc/gallery/stzGeoSamples/variogram_and_fit.png, gauges over an IDW surface beside the variogram and its three fitted models, RIGHT; kriging_transect.png, the estimate with isohyets and the doubt along a line, RIGHT (the band pinches at gauges and swells in gaps); kriging_on_a_trend.png, the same method on a trend, WRONG (white inside the country marks kriged values far outside the classes, see FINDINGS_geo.md). Index: doc/gallery/INDEX_geo.md.

classes.name: stzGovernance
classes.brief: Holds governance as declared contracts: risk tiers, permissions, authority levels, commitments, decommissioning, postures and reversibility, with a decision lineage.
classes.description: Permission (what an actor can do) is kept apart from authority (what it should do alone). MayProceed composes both with the action's risk tier before anything happens, and every verdict is explained by Why. The same object holds forward-only commitments, decommission contracts, trust postures, reversibility classes (MayExecuteFor composes the last two) and a registration gate (MayRegister). Every decision can be recorded with the authority and risk of that moment, kept in a bounded lineage you can query by id, actor, action or time. Save and LoadFrom keep the regime and the lineage in a .zgov file. The data lives in a shared table, so copies of the object see the same regime.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGovernance("kitchen-ops") o1.DeclareRisk("send-invoice", 3) o1.GrantPermission("billing-agent", "send-invoice") o1.SetAuthority("billing-agent", :Delegated)
classes.example:
? o1.MayProceed("billing-agent", "send-invoice")
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> refused: 'billing-agent' holds 'delegated' authority (level 2) but 'send-invoice' is risk tier 3 (SHOULD does not cover it)
o1.SetAuthority("billing-agent", :Autonomous)
? o1.MayProceed("billing-agent", "send-invoice")
#--> 1

methods.name: Calibrate
methods.brief: Measure where the GPU actually starts winning ON THIS MACHINE, store the crossover in the calibration store, and persist it (the faces auto-load it in later sessions).
methods.detail: Warm-min discipline throughout -- G0's clock inversion means sustained numbers flatter the GPU. Returns [ nThreshold, [ [nProblemSize, nCpuMs, nGpuMs], ... ] ].

methods.name: CalibrateWith
methods.brief: The same, on a caller-chosen ladder of corpus sizes (d fixed at 64: a representative embedding width; problem size = n*d).

methods.name: Verify
methods.brief: Verify a CANDIDATE kernel against a REFERENCE one: same inputs, same device, plus a HIDDEN second shape over DIFFERENT data the candidate was never shown; both timed the same way by the ENGINE (never by this face); and a refusal for any time faster than the measured bus. The report is DATA -- the verdict is the engine's, this face only reads it.
methods.detail: aR = oG.Verify(kRef, kCand, [ :a = aData ]) ? aR[:verdict]   # "verified" | "mismatch" | "mismatch-hidden" | # "impossible" | "reference-impossible" | "error" pCand may be an stzKernelMaker on the SAME declarations, or raw WGSL on the same binding contract (how a hand-written variant -- or a cheat -- gets checked). Options: [ :reps = 7, :band = 0.000001 ].

methods.name: VerifyJudge
methods.brief: The roofline alone: could a dispatch touching nBytes finish in nMs on this device? Pure judgement over the MEASURED floors -- exposed so a guard can hand it an impossible number and watch it refuse.

methods.name: VerifyFloors
methods.brief: The measured floors themselves: [ :floorgbs, :submitfloorms ]

methods.name: FirstError
methods.brief: one rung: warm-min per-query ms through the REAL seam, both routes Measured 2026-09-09 on this laptop's RTX 3050: after ~10 s idle, every submit pays a fixed ~2 ms and the copy floor reads 13 GB/s instead of 85 -- and hundreds of tiny queries never lift it, while ~150 ms of heavy work does.
methods.detail: Wake() is that work, ADAPTIVE: it copies until a copy runs at full speed, settles, and stops -- the budget is a cap. Every timing this face takes calls it first; a caller measuring on its own should too. Returns the copies it took (an awake device answers in ~20). THE CAUSE AND THE SYMPTOM. A shader that fails validation raises two errors: the parser's, with the offending name and line, and then the pipeline's, which only says the module is invalid. FirstError() is the parser's; LastError() is whatever came last. A compile clears both first.

methods.name: CalibrateKnnResident
methods.brief: The semantic index (stzSemanticIndex) routes its resident corpus to the GPU under the key "knn_resident" -- ITS OWN line, because a line is a comparison against a CPU alternative and this face's alternative is the multicore SIMD top-k (cluster.topK), not the vector index's scan the "pairdist" line was measured against. This pass walks corpus sizes at one dimension through the REAL face on synthetic unit vectors (no model needed), both routes, search-by-vector (the query embedding excluded), warm-min, the device woken before every GPU timing, the first rung re-measured last as the control. It stores a shaped class per rung and the flat line from the most conservative crossover, and persists both -- unless the control moved, in which case nothing is.
methods.detail: Measured 2026-09-09 on the RTX 3050 laptop at 384 dims: the GPU loses at 1,000 (0.39x) and 4,000 (0.98x) and wins at 16,000 (1.42x); the multicore top-k switches on at n*d >= 8M and the window may close again above it -- which is why the rung above that gate is measured too, and why the store is SHAPED: a class that wins carries its win, and the flat line stays beyond the ladder where a class lost.

methods.name: ConvolveReal
methods.brief: The linear convolution of two real signals -- convolution reverb's arithmetic -- as ONE batched pass on the device: both operands packed and transformed (Stockham radix-2, twiddles from a table computed in f64), multiplied pointwise, transformed back, the real part scaled. SN0 measured it at 19-23x over fft.zig for 60 s of audio on the 3050.
methods.detail: This is the ONE-SHOT doorway: upload, run, download. A plane holding its signal on the device uses the buffer form (StzEngineGpuOpConvolveReal over buffer ids) and pays no marshalling -- the sound desk's route.

methods.name: FoundryPairdist
methods.brief: The op library carries VARIANTS of pairdist (a straight row kernel, a vec4 one, one with the query staged in workgroup memory) beside the generic 16x16 tile. This pass lets the ENGINE enumerate them under GK0's checker: each is verified against the generic on the same device buffers at the visible shape AND a hidden one (different size, different data), timed on the GPU clock with the device awake, and the winner -- if it beats the generic by 1.3x -- is recorded for the SHAPE CLASS in the variant table the op consults at dispatch, and persisted. A variant the checker refuses cannot win, whatever it timed. Scope: m <= 16, the single-query family the seams dispatch.
methods.detail: Report: [ :m, :n, :d, :hiddenn, :clocks, :refgpums, :refwallms, :variants = [ [name, verified, gpums, wallms, ratio, ratiowall], ... ], :winner = name, :ratio = generic/winner on the GPU clock, :stored = bool ]

methods.name: FoundryAttention
methods.brief: THE ATTENTION FOUNDRY (GK2c).
methods.detail: The backbone's fused attention -- one workgroup per (head, query row) -- against three reduction-form variants at workgroup widths 64, 128 and 256, under the checker on the neural DLL's device; the winner recorded for the (tokens, width, head_dim) class under the op name "attention", persisted, and pushed into the neural DLL's table so the next forward dispatches it.

methods.name: FoundryMatmul
methods.brief: THE MATMUL FOUNDRY (GK2b's matmul leg).
methods.detail: C(m x n) = A(m x k) B(k x n): tile16 (the generic), tile8, reg2, reg4 under the checker at the asked shape and a hidden one; the winner recorded for the (m, n, k) class under the op name "matmul" and persisted. The backbone compiles the table's winner for its own shapes with the bias fused.

methods.name: FoundryUmapKnn
methods.brief: THE k-NN FOUNDRY (GS6e).
methods.detail: The UMAP k-NN kernel lives in the stats DLL on its own device, so its enumeration runs there; the verdict is recorded in that DLL's variant table AND persisted here under the op name "umap_knn", beside pairdist's rows, so the next session finds it. The stats DLL reads the persisted rows back through StzUmapKnnVariantsSync() at its first fit.

methods.name: FoundryPairdistGrid
methods.brief: The kill line, per adapter: a grid of single-query shapes; TRUE if any class found a variant worth the margin.

methods.name: CalibrateShaped
methods.brief: The flat pass above walks one dimension (d = 64) and stores one number. GK1's probe (gk1_shape_probe.ring, 2026-09-09) measured that the number on disk routed half the grid WRONG, and that on the Intel iGPU the crossover moves 4x with the dimension. So this pass walks a GRID of dimensions x corpus sizes through the real seam, both routes forced, records the measured cpu/gpu RATIO per shape class (powers-of-two buckets -- the engine's store), keeps the whole LADDER as the trace, sets the flat line to the most conservative crossover the grid saw (unmeasured classes fall back to it), and then CHECKS ITSELF at two shapes that were NOT on the grid: one inside a measured class, one in an unmeasured class. A threshold is trusted only if a shape it was not calibrated on agrees with it.
methods.detail: Report: [ :cells = [[d, n, cpuMs, gpuMs, ratio], ...], :flat = the flat line stored, :flatwhy = "crossover" | "beyond-ladder", :hidden = [ [d, n, cpuMs, gpuMs, predicted, measured, agree], ... ], :adapter = name ]

classes.name: stzGraph
classes.brief: Holds a directed graph of named nodes and labelled edges, and answers questions about its paths, metrics, rules and changes.
classes.description: A node has an id (folded to lowercase, no space), a label and properties; an edge runs from one node to another with a label and properties. The graph is simple: a second edge between the same ordered pair is refused. Paths, components and the centrality metrics run in the engine, on a copy that is rebuilt after most changes (a few removal methods do not refresh it, see their warnings). Rules come in two forms: the three typed stores filled by UseRulesFrom, and attached stzGraphRule objects judged by CheckRules. The graph reads and writes .stzgraf, .stzrulz and .stzsim files and writes DOT, JSON, YAML and GraphML; reading GraphML back is broken today. Many methods fold an id to lowercase and some do not (the removals, Incoming, SetNodeProperty), so ids are safest given in lowercase. The file also holds stzGraphFinder, stzGraphAsciiVisualizer and stzGraphComparison, which the graph builds for you. A number of methods carry a warning today.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGraph("g1"); o1.AddNodeXT("a", "Alpha"); o1.AddNodeXT("b", "Beta"); o1.AddNodeXT("c", "Gamma"); o1.Connect("a", "b"); o1.Connect("b", "c")

extensions.name: EdgePropsXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: ToCanvas

methods.brief: Returns the stzGraphCanvas behind the drawing, for its metrics and node positions rather than only the picture.

methods.name: PathExists

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.name: FirstNode
methods.brief: Returns the first node added, as a hash list [ :id, :label, :properties ]; raises an error on a graph with no node.

methods.name: FirstNodeId
methods.brief: Returns the id of the first node added; raises an error on a graph with no node.

methods.name: LastNode
methods.brief: Returns the last node added, as a hash list; raises an error on a graph with no node.

methods.name: LastNodeId
methods.brief: Returns the id of the last node added; raises an error on a graph with no node.

methods.name: NthNode
methods.brief: Returns the node at a position, counted from 1 in the order added; a position of 0 or past the end raises error R2.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The position of the node; 1 is the first.

methods.name: NodePosition
methods.brief: Returns the position of a node in the node list, counted from 1; 0 when the node does not exist.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: FindNode
methods.brief: Returns every simple path from the first node to the given node, as lists of ids; a path of more than 10 edges is not found.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: PathsTo
methods.brief: Returns every simple path from the first node to the given node; another spelling of the path search.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: Paths
methods.brief: Returns every simple path between every ordered pair of distinct nodes, as lists of ids; the answer grows fast with the graph.
notes: enumerating all simple paths is exponential, so use it on small graphs
warnings: the search gives up beyond 10 edges, so longer paths are missing

extensions.name: PathsXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

extensions.name: PathsWF

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the first path found from one node to another, following the edges in the order added; it is not always the shortest.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none is found
warnings: a path of more than 10 edges is not found, even when PathExists says the node is reachable

extensions.name: PathXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Neighbors
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that a node points to, in the order its edges were added.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for a node without out-edges

methods.name: Incoming
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that point to a node, in the order their edges were added.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] when nothing points to it
warnings: the id is not folded to lowercase, so "C" finds nothing for a node stored as "c"

methods.name: HasCyclicDependencies
methods.brief: TRUE if the graph holds a directed cycle, a self-loop included.

methods.name: ReachableFrom
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the other nodes you can reach by following edges from a node; the start node is never listed.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.returns: a list of text, in node order; [ ] when the node is unknown

methods.name: BottleneckNodes
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose in-degree plus out-degree is above the average over all nodes.
warnings: raises error R1 (divide by zero) on a graph without nodes, which also stops Show, AsciiArt and Explain on an empty graph

methods.name: NodeDensity
methods.brief: Returns the share of possible directed edges that exist: edges divided by n times n-1; 0 for fewer than two nodes.

methods.name: NodeDensity100
methods.brief: Returns the directed density as a percentage, from 0 to 100.

methods.name: UndirectedNodeDensity
methods.brief: Returns edges divided by the number of node pairs, n times n-1 over 2, as if edges had no direction.
methods.returns: a number; above 1 when edges run both ways

methods.name: UndirectedNodeDensity100
methods.brief: Returns the undirected density as a percentage.

methods.name: IsSparse
methods.brief: TRUE if the directed density is below 0.5.

methods.name: IsDense
methods.brief: TRUE if the directed density is 0.5 or more.

methods.name: DensityCategory
methods.brief: Returns a word for the density: "empty" at 0, then "very sparse" below 0.25, "sparse" below 0.5, "dense" below 0.75, else "very dense".

methods.name: LongestPath
methods.brief: Returns the largest number of nodes reachable from any one node, which is not the hop count of the longest path.
warnings: known defect: the name promises a path length, but the body counts reachable nodes, so a node that reaches two branches of two nodes each answers 4, though no path is longer than 2 hops

methods.name: CyclicNodes
methods.brief: Returns an empty list today instead of the ids of the nodes that lie on a cycle.
methods.returns: [ ] today, even for a graph with a cycle
warnings: known defect: it looks for the node among the nodes it reaches, but ReachableFrom never lists the start node, so the test is never true; use HasCyclicDependencies for the graph

methods.name: ParallelizableBranches
methods.brief: Returns pairs [ a, b ] of out-neighbours of one node whose onward reach shares no node, so the two branches could run in parallel.
methods.returns: a list of pairs of ids; [ ] when every pair overlaps

methods.name: DependencyFreeNodes
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that nothing points to, the ones that depend on no other.

methods.name: ImpactOf
methods.brief: Returns how many nodes a node can reach, the nodes that fail with it; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: FailureScope
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes that depend on a node, those it reaches; [ ] for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: NodeCriticality
methods.brief: Returns one hash list [ :id, :criticality ] per node, the criticality being its in-degree plus out-degree.

methods.name: MostCriticalNodes
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes with the highest in-plus-out degree, the most critical first.

parameters.name: pnCount
parameters.role: How many nodes to return; 5 when empty.

methods.returns: a list of text, at most the count asked for
notes: an empty count means 5

methods.name: FindQ

methods.brief: Returns a stzGraphFinder on the nodes or the edges, to chain Where, Having, WithProperty and WithTag, then Run.

parameters.name: pcWhat
parameters.role: What to search: "nodes" or "edges".

methods.name: NodesByType
methods.section: rich querying - based on stzgraphfinder class
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose :type property equals the given text.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: A type name, as text.

parameters.name: pcOp

notes: NodesW is the short spelling

methods.name: NodesByProperty
methods.section: rich querying - based on stzgraphfinder class
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose property equals the value.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: The property to test, as text; label, id and the node's own properties are accepted.

parameters.name: pVal
parameters.role: A value.

methods.name: EdgesWhere
methods.section: rich querying - based on stzgraphfinder class
methods.brief: Returns the [ from, to ] pairs of the edges whose property or label meets a comparison, such as weight > 2.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: The property to test, as text; label, id and the node's own properties are accepted.

parameters.name: pcOp
parameters.role: The comparison, such as "=", ">", "<", "contains" or "between".

parameters.name: pVal
parameters.role: A value.

methods.returns: a list of [ from, to ] pairs
notes: EdgesW is the short spelling

extensions.name: EdgesWhereF

methods.name: EdgesByProperty
methods.section: rich querying - based on stzgraphfinder class
methods.brief: Returns the [ from, to ] pairs of the edges whose property or label equals the value.

parameters.name: pcProp
parameters.role: The property to test, as text; label, id and the node's own properties are accepted.

parameters.name: pVal
parameters.role: A value.

methods.returns: a list of [ from, to ] pairs

methods.brief: Returns the paths of Paths for which a function answers TRUE.

notes: the function is called once per path of the whole graph

methods.name: QueryQ
methods.section: advanced quryies - based on stzgraphquery class
methods.brief: Returns a stzGraphQuery on this graph, for queries the finder cannot express.

methods.name: ShortestPath
methods.brief: Returns the path with the fewest edges from one node to another, as ids; [ ] when there is none or an id is unknown.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

notes: the same node twice answers a path of that one node

methods.name: BFS
methods.brief: Returns the node ids in breadth-first visit order from a node, the start first; [ ] when the node is unknown.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: DFS
methods.brief: Returns the node ids in depth-first visit order from a node, the start first; [ ] when the node is unknown.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: IsBipartite
methods.brief: TRUE if the nodes can be split into two groups so that every edge joins the two, reading edges without direction.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE for an empty graph

methods.name: StronglyConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns the groups of nodes that all reach one another, as lists of ids; a node on no cycle forms a group of its own.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text

methods.name: NumberOfStronglyConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns how many groups of mutually reachable nodes the graph has.

methods.name: MSTWeight
methods.brief: Returns the total weight of a minimum spanning tree over the undirected graph, using the :weight property, 1 by default.
methods.returns: a number; -1 when the graph has no edge or is not connected

methods.name: MSTEdges
methods.brief: Returns the edges of a minimum spanning tree as [ from, to, weight ] triples; a graph in several pieces gives a forest.
methods.returns: a list of triples; [ ] when there is no edge
notes: the pair order is the engine's and may be the reverse of the edge's direction

methods.name: ArticulationPoints
methods.brief: Returns the ids of the nodes whose removal would split the graph, reading edges without direction.

methods.name: Bridges
methods.brief: Returns the edges whose removal would split the graph, as [ u, v ] pairs, reading edges without direction.
methods.returns: a list of pairs of ids

methods.name: WeightedShortestPath
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path from one node to another by the :weight of the edges, 1 when an edge has none, as ids.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: WeightedShortestPathLength
methods.brief: Returns the total weight of the cheapest path from one node to another, by the :weight of the edges.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a number; -1 when unreachable or unknown

methods.name: ShortestPathLength
methods.brief: Returns the number of edges on the shortest path from one node to another.

parameters.name: pcFromNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcToNodeId
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

methods.returns: a number; 0 when there is no path, which cannot be told from the same node

methods.name: ConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns the groups of nodes found by walking out-edges from each node not seen yet, as lists of ids, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text
warnings: edges are followed in their direction only, so b to a and c to a give three groups, although IsConnected, which ignores direction, answers TRUE

methods.name: TopologicalSort
methods.brief: Returns the node ids ordered so that every node comes before the nodes it points to; [ ] when the graph has a cycle.

methods.name: InDegree
methods.brief: Returns how many edges arrive at a node; the id is matched in lowercase, and an unknown node gives 0.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: OutDegree
methods.brief: Returns how many edges leave a node; the id is matched in lowercase, and an unknown node gives 0.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: NumberOfConnectedComponents
methods.brief: Returns how many groups ConnectedComponents finds, counted by the engine, following edge direction.

methods.name: IsConnected
methods.brief: TRUE if every node can be reached from the first when edges are read without direction; one node or none is connected.

methods.name: BetweennessCentrality
methods.brief: Returns how often a node lies on the shortest paths between other node pairs, computed by the engine; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: BetweennessCentralityAll
methods.brief: Returns the betweenness of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: ClosenessCentrality
methods.brief: Returns how close a node is to the nodes it reaches: reachable count over the sum of distances; 0 when unknown or isolated.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: ClosenessCentralityAll
methods.brief: Returns the closeness of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: CoreNumber
methods.brief: Returns the core number of a node: the largest k for which it stays in the k-core of the undirected view; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: CoreNumbers
methods.brief: Returns the core number of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: PageRank

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: PageRankAll
methods.brief: Returns the PageRank score of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: AStarPath

parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown
notes: without coordinates it behaves like the weighted shortest path

methods.name: AStarPathManhattan
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path from a start to a goal by A* with the Manhattan heuristic over the :x and :y of nodes.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: AStarPathWeighted
methods.brief: Returns the cheapest path by A* with a heuristic scaled to the edge weights, so the path stays optimal when weights are not distances.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

parameters.name: nMode
parameters.role: The heuristic: 1 for Euclidean distance between the :x and :y coordinates, 2 for Manhattan.

methods.returns: a list of node ids; [ ] when none or unknown

methods.name: SetEdgeWeight
methods.brief: Overrides the weight of an edge in the engine copy only, the stored :weight property staying as it is.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge starts from.

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: The id of the node the edge ends at.

parameters.name: nWeight
parameters.role: The new weight, as a number.

methods.returns: 1 when the edge is known, 0 when it is not
warnings: the override is lost when the engine copy is rebuilt, which most graph changes cause, and the ids are matched in lowercase

methods.name: AStarPlan
methods.brief: Returns the route and the explored nodes of one A* search as [ route, explored ], mode 0 being plain Dijkstra.

parameters.name: pcStart
parameters.role: The id of the node the search starts from.

parameters.name: pcGoal
parameters.role: The id of the goal node, where the search ends.

parameters.name: nMode
parameters.role: The heuristic: 1 for Euclidean distance between the :x and :y coordinates, 2 for Manhattan.

methods.returns: a list of two lists of ids; [ [ ], [ ] ] when a node is unknown
notes: when the goal cannot be reached the route is [ ] and the explored list still shows the nodes visited

methods.name: Diameter
methods.brief: Returns the longest of all the shortest paths between reachable pairs, counted in edges.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a graph without edges

methods.name: Radius
methods.brief: Returns the smallest eccentricity among the nodes that reach others.

methods.name: Eccentricity
methods.brief: Returns the length in edges of the longest shortest path from a node to any node it reaches; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: Eccentricities
methods.brief: Returns the eccentricity of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.name: AveragePathLength
methods.brief: Returns the mean length of the shortest paths over all reachable pairs of nodes.

methods.name: MaxFlow
methods.brief: Returns the maximum flow from a source to a sink, taking the :weight of each edge as its capacity, 1 by default.

parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a number; 0 when a node is unknown or no flow can pass

methods.name: MinCut
methods.brief: Returns the saturated edges that separate the sink from the source, as [ from, to ] pairs, by max-flow and min-cut.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a list of pairs of ids; [ ] when a node is unknown

methods.name: Communities
methods.brief: Returns the communities found by label propagation on the undirected view, as lists of node ids.
methods.returns: a list of lists of text

methods.name: NumberOfCommunities
methods.brief: Returns how many communities label propagation finds.

methods.name: MinCostMaxFlow
methods.brief: Returns the maximum flow from a source to a sink and its cost, :weight being the capacity and :cost the price per unit.

parameters.name: pcSource
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow starts from.

parameters.name: pcSink
parameters.role: The id of the node the flow ends at.

methods.returns: a pair [ flow, cost ]; [ 0, 0 ] when a node is unknown

methods.name: ClusteringCoefficient
methods.brief: Returns the share of the possible links among a node's neighbours that exist, on the undirected view; 0 for an unknown node.

parameters.name: pcNodeId
parameters.role: The node id, as text.

methods.name: ClusteringCoefficients
methods.brief: Returns the clustering coefficient of every node as [ id, value ] pairs, in node order.
methods.returns: a list of [ id, value ] pairs

methods.brief: Raises error "Incorrect Id" today instead of importing a GraphML file into the graph.

warnings: known defect: it only calls LoadFromGraphML, whose parser fails on every file written by SaveToGraphML and leaves garbled nodes behind

methods.name: Rendition

methods.name: RenditionKinds
methods.brief: Returns the kinds of rendition a graph can give: graph and text.

methods.name: Veiw

notes: not checked here: it starts an external Graphviz viewer

methods.name: ShowV

classes.name: stzGraphAsciiVisualizer
classes.brief: Draws a graph in the console as boxed labels joined by arrows, vertically or horizontally, or hands the drawing back as text.

The vertical drawing starts a tree at every node that nothing points to and writes a CYCLE marker where a path comes back; the horizontal drawing follows the first out-edge of each node. classes.brief: Compares a baseline graph with several variations and ranks them by what changed: nodes, edges, density, cycles and bottlenecks.
classes.description: Built by stzGraph.CompareWithManyQR(..., :stzGraphComparison) or directly. It runs the comparison once when built and answers from the stored rows: Summary for a text report, MostImpactful and LeastImpactful, ByMetric to sort, Recommend for a suggestion, ToStzTable for a table. The cycle questions (WithCycles, WithoutCycles) and the acyclic bonus of Recommend do not work today; see their warnings.

classes.name: stzGraphex
classes.brief: Matches a graph pattern written as text, such as {@Node(a) -> @Edge(x) -> @Node(b)}, against a stzGraph and answers TRUE or FALSE.
classes.description: The pattern is compiled into a small graph of tokens (@Node, @Edge, @Cycle, @Path, with an optional label, a {property constraint}, a quantifier, an alternation in parentheses, a @! negation and a @cs: case mark). A match flattens the target graph into label paths and looks for the pattern labels in order along one path, then checks the property constraints on the target nodes. Labels match without regard to case by default, results are cached per target graph, and the quantifiers are parsed but not yet used by the match.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXT("n1", "Start"); g1.AddNodeXT("n2", "Done"); g1.ConnectXT("n1", "n2", "flows"); o1 = new stzGraphex("{@Node(start) -> @Edge(flows) -> @Node(done)}", g1)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Compiles a graph pattern into a pattern graph and keeps the target graph; a non-text pattern or a non-graph raises an error.

parameters.role: The pattern, as text, such as "{@Node(a) -> @Edge(x) -> @Node(b)}"

parameters.name: oTargetGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph the pattern is matched against

notes: Match takes the graph again, so the target given here is only the default

methods.name: NormalizePattern
methods.brief: Returns the pattern trimmed and wrapped in braces when it is not already.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The pattern, as text

methods.name: BuildPatternGraph
methods.brief: Parses a pattern and adds one node per token to the pattern graph, joined by sequences edges; an alternation fans out to every branch.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The braced pattern, as text

notes: init calls it once; a second call grafts the new tokens onto the first pattern
warnings: the nodes are added to the graph already held, not in place of it, and their ids restart at :p1

methods.name: ParsePattern
methods.brief: Splits a braced pattern at -> into token lists, one per part, with an alternation in parentheses becoming a single alternation token.

parameters.name: _cPattern_
parameters.role: The pattern, as text, with its outer braces

methods.returns: a list of tokens, each a hash list
notes: each token holds type, label, min, max, setvalues, unique, negated and cs
warnings: the first and last characters are removed without a check, so a pattern without braces loses its first and last letters

methods.name: ParseSingleToken
methods.brief: Parses one token such as @Node(a)+ into a hash list of its type, label, quantifier, set values and flags; [ ] if unreadable.

parameters.name: _cTokenStr_
parameters.role: One token, as text: @Node, @Edge, @Cycle or @Path, with an optional (label), {set}, quantifier and @! or @cs: prefix

warnings: the quantifier gives min and max (+ is 1 to 999999, * is 0 to 999999, ? is 0 to 1) but matching never reads them

methods.name: ListifyGraph

parameters.name: oGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph to turn into label paths

warnings: paths run between every pair of distinct reachable nodes, so a chain of three nodes gives three branches

methods.name: Match
methods.brief: Tells whether the pattern occurs in a graph: its labels in order along one path, no negated label on it, and the property constraints met.

parameters.name: oTargetGraph
parameters.role: The stzGraph to look in

notes: labels match without regard to case unless the token starts with @cs:; a negated label only rules out the path that holds it, so another path may still match
warnings: the result is cached under a signature made of the node and edge counts and the node ids, so a second graph with the same ids but other labels answers from the cache: call ClearCache between graphs; labelless tokens (a bare @Node or @Edge, @Cycle, @Path) match anything and quantifiers are not read

methods.name: CacheStats
methods.brief: Returns how many target graphs are cached and how many matches were answered from the cache.

methods.name: CacheEntries
methods.brief: Returns the number of target graphs held in the match cache.

methods.name: ClearCache
methods.brief: Empties the match cache and sets its hit count back to 0.

methods.name: SetCacheSize
methods.brief: Sets how many results the match cache keeps, the oldest dropped first; a value that is not a number is ignored.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.role: The most results to keep

methods.returns: the matcher itself, so calls can be chained
warnings: with 0 or a negative number the cache is no longer trimmed and so has no bound

methods.name: CacheInfo
methods.brief: Returns the cache state: entry count, size limit and hit count.

methods.name: ListifyPatternGraph
methods.brief: Returns the pattern graph as label paths from each root to each end, one path per branch of an alternation.
warnings: the labels read node(Start) or edge(flows), with the token type and its label in parentheses

methods.name: TraversePatternNode
methods.brief: Walks the pattern graph depth-first from a node and appends each complete label path to the list given as third argument.

parameters.name: _cNodeId_
parameters.role: The id of the pattern node to start from, such as :p1

parameters.name: aCurrentPath
parameters.role: The labels already on the path, as a list

parameters.name: _aBranches_
parameters.role: The list that receives each finished path

parameters.name: acVisited
parameters.role: Ids already visited, kept for the call and not read

methods.returns: nothing; the branches list is filled
notes: give [ ] for aCurrentPath and acVisited
warnings: an id that is not a pattern node raises error Node does not exist, because the check after the lookup never runs

methods.name: MatchBranches
methods.brief: Tells whether any pattern branch has its labels in order inside any target branch, with none of its negated labels there.

parameters.name: _aPatternBranches_

classes.name: stzGraphPlanner
classes.brief: Plans the cheapest route through a graph under named plans, criteria and profiles, then explains, compares and filters the plans.
classes.description: A planner takes a copy of a stzGraph when it is built. Each plan has a start and a goal (a node, or a function that tests nodes), criteria to minimise or maximise over the edge properties (or a profile: fastest, safest, cheapest, shortest, balanced, efficient) and, once executed, a result: the actions, their total cost and the route. The search runs in the engine as a uniform-cost search, so the route is the cheapest for non-negative costs. Every execution is also kept in a history. The comparison, ranking, filtering and history calls work on the executed plans, and stzGraphPlanner has a very large set of alternative spellings for the same calls.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "A", [ :x = 0 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "B", [ :x = 1 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("c", "C", [ :x = 2 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "b", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 1 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("b", "c", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 9 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "c", "r", [ :distance = 20, :cost = 2 ]); o1 = new stzGraphPlanner(g1); o1.AddPlan("short"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("distance"); o1.Execute(); o1.AddPlan("cheap"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("cost"); o1.Execute()

classes.name: stzGraphQuery
classes.brief: Builds a MATCH, WHERE, SELECT query over a stzGraph with a chain of calls, runs it and returns the matching rows.
classes.description: A query is a definition, a hash list of 11 parts that the Match, Where, Select, OrderBy, Create, Set and Delete calls fill in; nothing touches the graph until Select, Execute, ToGraphQ or ToViewQ runs it. Rows are lists of [ field, value ] pairs, or of [ alias, node ] pairs for a bare alias. Queries that create, set or delete change the source graph on every run. For plain filters on nodes or edges, stzGraphFinder is lighter.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "Person", [ :name = "Ann", :age = 30 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "Person", [ :name = "Bob", :age = 25 ]); o1 = new stzGraphQuery(g1)

classes.name: stzGraphRule
classes.brief: States one rule about a graph, as clauses over node properties or as a checker function, and reports its findings in the house shape.
classes.description: A rule has a name, a type, a domain, a severity and a message. Its scope is the When clauses, which select nodes by a property test and are combined with AND. With no Then clause, every node in scope is a finding, a prohibition; with Then clauses, each node in scope that fails a requirement is a finding, an implication. A rule too rich for clauses takes a checker function with UseChecker, which owns the whole decision. Check returns rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ], the shape stzRuleReport gates on, and Register compiles the rule into the shared registry. The setters have a plain form that returns nothing and a Q form that returns the rule, so chains use SetSeverityQ, WhenQ and ThenQ; SetReadsQ, SetWritesQ and SetOrderQ exist only in the Q form. Known defects: the greaterequal and lessequal operators match every node when the property or the value is text, and Register called twice adds the entry twice.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzGraphRule("llm-needs-owner"); o1.WhenQ("kind", "equals", "llm_actor"); o1.ThenQ("owner", "exists", ""); o1.ThenViolationQ("an LLM actor must name an owner")
classes.example:
oG = new stzGraph("agents")
oG.AddNodeXTT("planner", "Planner", [ :kind = "llm_actor" ])
oG.AddNodeXTT("deployer", "Deployer", [ :kind = "service" ])
? @@( o1.SubjectsIn(oG) )
#--> [ "node:planner" ]
? o1.NumberOfFindings(oG)
#--> 1
? o1.Check(oG)[1][:message]
#--> an LLM actor must name an owner

classes.name: stzGrid
classes.brief: Tracks a position on a grid of columns and rows, moves it in six directions, and finds routes around obstacles.
classes.description: A grid holds no data of its own. It keeps a current position counted from 1 at the top left, a direction, a set of obstacles and a stored path, and draws them as text. Positions are always [ column, row ], the column first. Reach for it to walk a board, a maze or a map: move by steps, ask for the cell above, below or beside, list the neighbours, test whether two cells connect, split the grid into regions, or ask for a route. Moves that would leave the grid or land on an obstacle change nothing, without an error, while the Node and NthNode readers raise an error outside the grid. ManhattanPath and ZigZagPath raise when an obstacle is on the way; see their warnings.

classes.name: stzHBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws a list of numbers, or labelled numbers, as horizontal bars with their labels at the left.
classes.description: It is stzBarPlot turned on its side: one row per bar, the longest bar as long as the width, the labels in a column at the left. It inherits the data, the value, percentage and character settings, ToSVG and ToPNG from stzBarPlot and overrides only the size and layout settings and ToString. The average line is not drawn in the text picture, SetBarHeight spaces the bars out instead of thickening them, and SetBarInterSpace and SetHeight change nothing; see their warnings. In the pixel pictures the label column has a fixed width, so a long label is clipped at the left edge. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzHBarPlot/ranked.png (six bars with values), seen right by stzlib- docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; longlabels.png (long labels clipped at the left edge), seen wrong by the same pass; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

classes.name: stzHistogram
classes.brief: Bins a list of numbers into equal-width classes and draws the counts, or another aggregate, as touching bars.
classes.description: Built from raw measurements, it cuts the range into 5 or more bins by Sturges' rule, or into the number SetBinCount gives, and each bar shows how many values fall in its bin; UseSum, UseAverage, UseMin and UseMax make it show another aggregate. ToString draws the text picture (bin edges in two rows under the bars), ToSVG and ToPNG the pixel picture; Mean, StandardDeviation, Median, Mode and DataCount describe the data. The text picture is drawn by the engine, except when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off, when the slower Ring renderer takes over and obeys SetHeight, SetMaxWidth and AddValues, which the engine route ignores. SetBinRange gives the wrong number of bins, SetAggregation with an unknown name leaves the histogram unusable, and the X and Y axis names are the reverse of the usual ones; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzHistogram/normal.png (200 values, 9 bins), bins20.png (20 bins) and sums.png (UseSum), each with its script, seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right.

methods.brief: Draws the histogram on the graphics device and returns the PNG bytes, writing them to a file when a path is given.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: The file to write, or an empty text to write none

parameters.name: paOptions
parameters.role: A list of options [ :Width = , :Height = , :Title = , :Font = an stzFont, ... ], as for ToCanvasQ

methods.returns: the PNG bytes as a string, empty when no device is available

methods.name: SetBinCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins again; a value of 0 or less is ignored.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change
notes: the default is 5 or more by Sturges' rule
warnings: A count that is not a whole number drops the largest values, because the last bin then ends before the maximum

methods.name: SetBarCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, under the bar name.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: SetClassCount
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, under the class name of statistics.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: DivideToNClasses
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, worded as a division into classes.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: DivideToNGroups
methods.brief: Splits the data into n equal-width bins, worded as a division into groups.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of bins, ignored when 0 or less

methods.returns: nothing; the bins and the picture change

methods.name: SetBinRange
methods.brief: Cuts the data into ceil((largest count - smallest count) / n) bins, usually one, instead of bins n wide.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The wanted width of a bin, ignored when 0 or less

notes: use SetBinCount for a number of bins
warnings: The bin count is worked out from the range of the bar heights, not of the data, so SetBinRange(10) on values from 12 to 70 gives one bin and SetBinRange(3) gives two

methods.name: SetClassRange
methods.brief: Cuts the data into the same wrong number of classes as SetBinRange does, usually one, instead of classes n wide.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The wanted width of a class, ignored when 0 or less

warnings: Same cause: the count comes from the bar heights, so the result is one or two bins

methods.name: SetHeight
methods.brief: Sets the height the Ring renderer draws, which the engine renderer fixes at 10 rows and so ignores.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The height in rows

methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
notes: the default is 10
warnings: The usual ToString ignores it, and obeys it only when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off, since those use the Ring renderer

methods.name: SetValues
methods.brief: Shows or hides the count above each bar, but only the Ring renderer draws it.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to write the counts, 0 to stop

methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
notes: the counts appear when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off
warnings: ToString never draws the counts because the engine renderer reads a flag nothing sets, so use AddPercent or ToStringInRing

methods.name: IncludeValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar on, but only the Ring renderer draws it.
methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
warnings: ToString never draws the counts

methods.name: AddValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar on, but only the Ring renderer draws it.
methods.returns: nothing; only the Ring renderer changes
warnings: ToString never draws the counts

methods.name: WithoutValues
methods.brief: Turns the count above each bar off.

methods.name: SetAggregation
methods.brief: Chooses what each bar shows: the count of values in the bin or their sum, mean, smallest or largest.

parameters.name: cType
parameters.role: The aggregation, in lower case: "frequency", "sum", "average", "min" or "max"

notes: an empty bin shows 0
warnings: Any other text, "SUM" with capitals included, raises R2 from max() and leaves the histogram empty, so ToString then raises too

methods.name: AggregationType
methods.brief: Returns which aggregation the bars show now.
notes: the default is "frequency"

methods.name: Aggregation
methods.brief: Returns which aggregation the bars show now, under a shorter name.

methods.name: AggregationTypes
methods.brief: Returns the five aggregations a histogram accepts.

methods.name: UseFrequency
methods.brief: Makes each bar show how many values fall in its bin.
notes: this is the default

methods.name: UseFreq
methods.brief: Makes each bar show how many values fall in its bin, under a shorter name.

methods.name: UseSum
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the sum of the values in its bin.
notes: Mode then names the bin with the largest sum

methods.name: UseAverage
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the mean of the values in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: UseMin
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the smallest value in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: UseMax
methods.brief: Makes each bar show the largest value in its bin, 0 for an empty bin.

methods.name: SetStats
methods.brief: Shows or hides four lines under the picture giving the mean, standard deviation, median and count of the data.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to add the lines, 0 to remove them

notes: it switches the drawing to the Ring renderer, which obeys SetHeight and SetValues

methods.name: AddStats
methods.brief: Adds four lines under the picture giving the mean, standard deviation, median and count of the data.

methods.name: IncludeStats
methods.brief: Adds the statistics lines under the picture, under the Include name.

methods.name: SetVAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the vertical axis with its arrow, the one that runs up beside the bars.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show it, 0 to hide it

notes: the bars and labels keep their place

methods.name: AddVAxis
methods.brief: Shows the vertical axis with its arrow.

methods.name: IncludeVAxis
methods.brief: Shows the vertical axis with its arrow, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutVAxis
methods.brief: Hides the vertical axis and its arrow.

methods.name: SetXAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.

parameters.name: bShow

notes: SetYAxis is the horizontal one
warnings: The X name here means the vertical axis, the reverse of the usual X for the horizontal axis

methods.name: AddXAxis
methods.brief: Shows the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.
warnings: The X name here means the vertical axis

methods.name: IncludeXAxis
methods.brief: Shows the VERTICAL axis, under the X name and the Include name.
warnings: The X name here means the vertical axis

methods.name: WithoutXAxis
methods.brief: Hides the VERTICAL axis, under the X name kept for old code.
warnings: The X name here means the vertical axis

methods.name: SetHAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the horizontal axis line under the bars, with its arrow and the origin mark.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show it, 0 to hide it

notes: hiding it switches the drawing to the Ring renderer and keeps the bin labels

methods.name: AddHAxis
methods.brief: Shows the horizontal axis line under the bars.

methods.name: IncludeHAxis
methods.brief: Shows the horizontal axis line under the bars, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutHAxis
methods.brief: Hides the horizontal axis line, its arrow and its origin mark.

methods.name: SetYAxis
methods.brief: Shows or hides the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show it, 0 to hide it

notes: SetXAxis is the vertical one
warnings: The Y name here means the horizontal axis, the reverse of the usual Y for the vertical axis

methods.name: AddYAxis
methods.brief: Shows the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.
warnings: The Y name here means the horizontal axis

methods.name: IncludeYAxis
methods.brief: Shows the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name and the Include name.
warnings: The Y name here means the horizontal axis

methods.name: WithoutYAxis
methods.brief: Hides the HORIZONTAL axis, under the Y name kept for old code.
warnings: The Y name here means the horizontal axis

methods.name: SetLabels
methods.brief: Shows or hides the two rows of bin labels under the bars, each giving a bin's lower and upper edge.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to show the labels, 0 to hide them

notes: an edge is rounded to one decimal

methods.name: AddLabels
methods.brief: Shows the two rows of bin labels under the bars.

methods.name: IncludeLabels
methods.brief: Shows the two rows of bin labels under the bars, under the Include name.

methods.name: WithoutLabels
methods.brief: Hides the two rows of bin labels under the bars.

methods.name: SetPercent
methods.brief: Shows or hides each bar's share of all the data above it, such as 40%.

parameters.name: bShow
parameters.role: 1 to write the percentages, 0 to stop

notes: the share is of the total of all the bars, so after UseSum it is each bin's share of the overall sum

methods.name: AddPercent
methods.brief: Writes each bar's share of all the data above it.

methods.name: IncludePercent
methods.brief: Writes each bar's share of all the data above it, under the Include name.

methods.name: SetBarWidth
methods.brief: Sets how many characters wide each bar is drawn.

parameters.name: nWidth
parameters.role: The width of a bar in characters, raised to 1 when smaller

notes: the default is 2

methods.name: SetMaxWidth
methods.brief: Sets the widest picture the Ring renderer accepts, which the engine renderer does not check.

parameters.name: nWidth
parameters.role: The largest total width in characters

notes: the default is 132
warnings: The usual ToString ignores it, while a wider Ring-rendered picture (statistics on, or no horizontal axis) raises "Histogram width (n) exceeds maximum (m)"

methods.name: SetBarInterSpace
methods.brief: Sets the blank columns between neighbouring bars, which add to the label spacing.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns

notes: the default is 1

methods.name: SetBarChar
methods.brief: Sets the character the bars are drawn with; a text of more than one character raises an error.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: The single character to draw bars with

notes: the default is a full block

methods.name: SetFinalBarChar
methods.brief: Sets the character that draws the top row of each bar; a text of more than one character raises an error.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: The single character for the top row

notes: an empty top character, the default, uses the bar character
warnings: Raises "Incorrect param type! c must be a char." for a longer text

methods.name: SetTopBarChar
methods.brief: Sets the character that draws the top row of each bar, under the Top name.

parameters.name: c
parameters.role: The single character for the top row

methods.name: SetLabelInterSpace
methods.brief: Sets the extra blank columns kept between neighbouring bin labels, which add to the bar spacing.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: The number of blank columns

notes: the default is 1

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the arithmetic mean of the raw data.

methods.name: StandardDeviation
methods.brief: Returns the sample standard deviation of the raw data, dividing by n minus 1.
notes: 0 for one value or none

methods.name: Median
methods.brief: Returns the middle value of the raw data, or the mean of the two middle ones.

methods.name: Mode
methods.brief: Returns the lower and upper edge of the bin with the largest bar, the first one when several tie.
methods.returns: a list of two numbers [ low, high ]

methods.name: DataCount
methods.brief: Returns how many values the histogram was built from.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the histogram as text on the console.

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the histogram as text, with bars that follow the bins, a vertical axis, and the bin edges written in two rows.
notes: it hands over to the Ring renderer when statistics are on or the horizontal axis is off

classes.name: stzHistoricalComparison
classes.brief: Compares an executed plan with the planner's history of executions: its gain over the average cost and the best past plan.
classes.description: It is built by stzGraphPlanner.CompareWithHistoryQ. The history includes the compared plan's own run.
classes.receiver: g1 = new stzGraph("g1"); g1.AddNodeXTT("a", "A", [ :x = 0 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("b", "B", [ :x = 1 ]); g1.AddNodeXTT("c", "C", [ :x = 2 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "b", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 1 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("b", "c", "r", [ :distance = 5, :cost = 9 ]); g1.AddEdgeXTT("a", "c", "r", [ :distance = 20, :cost = 2 ]); o1 = new stzGraphPlanner(g1); o1.AddPlan("short"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("distance"); o1.Execute(); o1.AddPlan("cheap"); o1.Walk("a", "c"); o1.Minimize("cost"); o1.Execute(); o2 = o1.CompareWithHistoryXTQ("short")

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a comparison of a plan's result with the planner's history of executions, which the planner supplies.

parameters.name: poPlanner
parameters.role: The stzGraphPlanner whose history is used

parameters.name: pcCurrentPlan
parameters.role: The name of the plan compared

parameters.name: paCurrentResult
parameters.role: The result list of that plan

parameters.name: paHistory
parameters.role: The history entries of the planner

warnings: usually reached through stzGraphPlanner.CompareWithHistoryQ

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the plan's cost and steps next to the history's averages, an observation in percent and the best past plan.
warnings: the history includes the plan's own run, so the average is never fully independent of it

methods.name: IsImprovement
methods.brief: TRUE if the plan's cost is below the historical average cost.

methods.name: Improvement
methods.brief: Returns the plan's gain over the historical average cost as a ratio: positive when cheaper, negative when dearer.
warnings: 0 when the average is 0; ImprovementRatio is the same call

methods.name: ImprovementPercentage
methods.brief: Returns the plan's gain over the historical average cost in percent: positive when cheaper, negative when dearer.
warnings: 0 when the average is 0; Improvement100 is the same call

classes.name: stzHtml
classes.brief: Parses HTML text with the engine and finds its elements by tag, id or class, giving their text and attributes.
classes.description: Reach for it to read a page: Find takes a tag name, #id or .class and returns node handles (stzHtmlNode) whose Text and Attr read the element. Text on the document gives all the visible text with scripts and styles removed. The parser is read-only, so the document cannot be changed, and there are no selector combinators: use ElementsWhere to combine a tag, a class and an id. It holds text, it does not fetch pages; HtmlQ(text-or-file) is the shortcut.
classes.receiver:
o1 = new stzHtml('

Hello

Two
')
classes.example:
? o1.CountByTag("div")
#--> 2
? o1.FindFirst("#main").Klass()
#--> box big
? len(o1.Find(".box"))
#--> 2
? len(o1.ElementsWhere([ :Tag = "div", :Class = "big" ]))
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a document object by parsing HTML text with the engine; a value that is not a text raises an error.

parameters.name: pcHtml
parameters.role: the HTML source as text

notes: the error text is Incorrect param type! pcHtml must be a string.; broken markup is accepted and repaired by the parser

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the HTML source the object was built from, unchanged.

methods.name: Reload
methods.brief: Parses new HTML text and drops the previous document.

parameters.name: pcHtml
parameters.role: the new HTML source as text

notes: Content, Text and every Find now answer for the new source

extensions.name: ReloadQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the visible text of the whole document, without tags, scripts or styles; neighbouring elements run together.
notes: a div holding two p elements, Hello and World, reads HelloWorld; a document without any element gives its plain text back

methods.name: NumberOfElements
methods.brief: Returns how many elements the parser found, html, head and body included when the parser adds them.
notes: text without tags answers 0

methods.name: CountByTag
methods.brief: Returns how many elements have a given tag, ignoring the case of the tag.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as div

notes: CountByTag("DIV") and CountByTag("div") agree

methods.name: Find
methods.brief: Returns the elements matching a selector: a tag name, #id or .class; an empty text, a non-text or no match gives an empty list.

parameters.name: pcSelector
parameters.role: a tag such as div, an id such as #main, or a class such as .box

notes: only these three forms exist: no combinators and no attribute selectors

extensions.name: FindQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: FindFirst
methods.brief: Returns the first element matching a selector, in document order.

parameters.name: pcSelector
parameters.role: a tag, #id or .class, as for Find

methods.returns: a stzHtmlNode; the empty text when nothing matches
notes: test the result with isObject before calling a method on it

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the parse succeeded and produced at least one element.
notes: the empty text and plain text without tags answer FALSE

methods.name: Elements
methods.brief: Returns every element of the document as a node, in document order.
notes: a page of 12 elements gives 12 nodes, the first being html

methods.name: HasTag
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if at least one element has the tag.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as table

notes: the case of the tag does not matter

methods.name: HasBody
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the document has a body element.

methods.name: HasHead
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the document has a head element.

methods.name: TagsUsed
methods.brief: Returns the distinct tag names, lower case, in the order they first appear.
notes: for a full page it starts with html, head, title

methods.name: ElementsWhere
methods.brief: Returns the elements matching every given constraint among :Tag, :Class and :Id.

parameters.name: paCriteria
parameters.role: a hash list such as [ :Tag = "div", :Class = "box" ]

notes: an empty list of criteria gives every element; a value that is not a list gives an empty list; a class matches one word of the class attribute

classes.name: stzHtmlBuilder
classes.brief: Is meant to assemble an HTML document from nodes, but returns an empty text today because appended nodes never reach the root.
classes.description: The builder holds a root container and a current node. Because Ring copies an object on assignment, the current node is a copy of the root and AppendToCurrent adds to the copy, so Build and BuildToFile give nothing. Build the tree on stzHtmlBuildNode objects instead and call ToHtml on the top node, which works.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Starts an empty document: a tag-less root container that is also the current node.

methods.name: CreateNode
methods.brief: Returns a new detached node with the tag; it is not part of the document until it is appended.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, such as ul

notes: the node is a separate object: changes made to it after it was appended are not seen in the document

methods.name: AppendToCurrent
methods.brief: Adds a node as the last child of the current node and returns the builder.

parameters.name: poNode
parameters.role: the node to add

notes: build a tree on a stzHtmlBuildNode and call its ToHtml instead
warnings: defect: the current node is a copy of the root made at birth, because Ring copies an object on assignment, so the node lands in the copy and Build, Root and BuildToFile still show nothing; checked with two different nodes and after SetCurrent(Root())

extensions.name: AppendToCurrentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetCurrent
methods.brief: Makes a node the one that AppendToCurrent adds to, and returns the builder.

parameters.name: poNode
parameters.role: the node that becomes current

notes: the builder keeps a copy of the node, not the node itself

extensions.name: SetCurrentQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Current
methods.brief: Returns the node that new children are added to.
notes: it is a copy: a change made to it does not reach the builder

methods.name: Root
methods.brief: Returns the tag-less root container of the document.
notes: because of the copying noted at AppendToCurrent its children stay empty

methods.name: Build
methods.brief: Returns the HTML text of the document: the children of the root, one after the other.
notes: the text of a node tree built apart is available as ToHtml on the node
warnings: defect: it answers the empty text after AppendToCurrent, whatever was appended (see AppendToCurrent)

methods.name: BuildToFile
methods.brief: Writes the HTML text of the document to a file and returns the builder.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, which is replaced if it exists

warnings: defect: the file is created empty after AppendToCurrent, for the same reason as Build

classes.name: stzHtmlBuildNode
classes.brief: Holds one element of an HTML tree to be written out: a tag, a text, attributes and child nodes.
classes.description: Reach for it to produce HTML without pasting strings: create a node, SetText, SetAttr and AppendChild, then call ToHtml on the top node. A node whose tag is the empty text is a container that writes only its children. Texts and attribute values are written as given, with no escaping, and a child is stored as a copy, so build each child fully before appending it.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzHtmlBuildNode("ul") li = new stzHtmlBuildNode("li") li.SetText("one") li.SetAttr("class", "x") o1.AppendChild(li)

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a node with a tag, no text, no attribute and no child; the empty tag makes a container written without a tag of its own.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name, or the empty text for a container

methods.name: Tag
methods.brief: Returns the tag name as it was given.

methods.name: SetText
methods.brief: Sets the text written inside the node before its children and returns the node.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the text, written as given

notes: the text is not escaped: a < stays a <, so do not pass untrusted text

extensions.name: SetTextQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the text of the node, not counting its children.

methods.name: SetAttr
methods.brief: Adds an attribute and returns the node.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the attribute name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, written between double quotes

notes: the value is not escaped, so a double quote inside it breaks the markup; setting a name twice writes it twice

methods.name: AppendChild
methods.brief: Adds a node as the last child and returns the node.

parameters.name: poNode
parameters.role: the node to add

notes: the child is stored as a copy, so changes made to the original afterwards do not appear in the output

methods.name: Children
methods.brief: Returns the list of child nodes, in the order they were added.

methods.name: ToHtml
methods.brief: Returns the node as HTML: opening tag with attributes, the text, the children, then the closing tag.
notes: a node with the empty tag gives only its children; a node without text or children gives an empty element such as

methods.name: ChildrenHtml
methods.brief: Returns the HTML of the children only, one after the other, without the tag of this node.

classes.name: stzHtmlNode
classes.brief: Points at one element of a parsed HTML document and reads its tag, text, id, class and attributes.
classes.description: A handle is the document, a tag name and the rank of the element among elements of that tag. It is made by Find, FindFirst, Elements and ElementsWhere of stzHtml. The document is read-only, so a node cannot change anything.
classes.receiver:
d1 = new stzHtml('
link
') o1 = d1.FindFirst("#main")
classes.example:
? o1.Tag()
#--> div
? o1.HasKlass("big")
#--> 1
? o1.Text()
#--> link
? d1.FindFirst("a").Attr("href")
#--> /u

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a handle to the n-th element with a given tag in a stzHtml document.

parameters.name: oDoc
parameters.role: the stzHtml document that owns the element

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag name

parameters.name: nOccurrence
parameters.role: which element of that tag, counted from 1

notes: normally made by Find, FindFirst or Elements of stzHtml

methods.name: Tag
methods.brief: Returns the tag name in lower case.

methods.name: Text
methods.brief: Returns the text inside the element, descendants included.
notes: text of child elements runs together: a paragraph with a bold part reads World x; a script element gives its code

methods.name: Attr
methods.brief: Returns the value of one attribute of the element; the empty text when it is absent.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the attribute name, such as href

notes: an attribute present with an empty value looks absent

methods.name: HasAttr
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if the element has the attribute with a value that is not empty.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the attribute name

notes: it is the test of Attr(name) against the empty text

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the id attribute of the element; the empty text when there is none.

methods.name: Klass
methods.brief: Returns the whole class attribute as one text; the empty text when there is none.
notes: the classes box and big come as one text: box big

methods.name: HasKlass
methods.brief: Returns TRUE if one of the words of the class attribute equals the class.

parameters.name: pcClass
parameters.role: the class name to look for

classes.name: stzHttpClient
classes.brief: Sends HTTP and HTTPS requests through the engine and keeps the last answer, with settings for headers, cookies, auth, proxy and timeouts.
classes.description: Configure the client with the Set methods, each of which returns the client so calls chain, then send with Get_, Post, Put_, Delete, Head, Options, PostForm or PostJson and read the answer with ResponseCode, ResponseBody and ResponseHeaders. A status of 4xx or 5xx is an answer, not an error; a request that never reached a server gives ResponseCode -1 and sets LastError. GetMany fetches up to 32 addresses in one parallel call. The requests need a network: to try the class offline, start the engine's loopback fixture with StzEngineTestServerStart(0) and stop it with StzEngineTestServerStop(), as test/network/73_http_loopback_narrated.ring does.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a client with no headers, no cookies, the user agent Softanza-HTTP/1.0 and the engine default timeouts.
notes: every field starts from its declared default

methods.name: SetUserAgent
methods.brief: Sets the User-Agent header sent with every later request, replacing Softanza-HTTP/1.0.

parameters.name: cAgent
parameters.role: the User-Agent text

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetHeader
methods.brief: Adds one request header, sent with every later request, after the headers already added.

parameters.name: cName
parameters.role: the header name

parameters.name: cValue
parameters.role: the header value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: adding the same name twice sends both lines; a header named Authorization reaches the server (a loopback /auth answered 200)

methods.name: SetHeaders
methods.brief: Replaces all the custom headers with a list of ready-made Name: Value lines.

parameters.name: aHeaders
parameters.role: a list of texts, each Name: Value

methods.returns: the client itself, so calls chain
notes: headers added earlier through SetHeader are dropped

methods.name: SetCookie

methods.name: PerformHttpGet
methods.brief: THE BLOCKING PATH, ENGINE-BACKED.
methods.detail: These called Ring's download() and then the raw libcurl.ring API -- curl_easy_init / curl_easy_setopt / CURLOPT_* / curl_easy_perform_silent. The library dropped that extension when HTTP moved into the Zig engine (stzHttpClient and stzNetwork both say so: "previously loaded libcurl.ring"), and nothing loads it now. Every verb here raised R3 "Calling Function without definition" on its first line. This is the path taken when there is no reactor -- which is exactly what SetReactor(NULL) selects, and what the reactor switch falls back TO. The switch had an off position that could not work.
