classes.name: stzItem
classes.brief: Meant to follow an item inside a text; today only its accessors work, because its list methods need a list.
classes.description: It is the text twin of stzItemCS: both the item and the text it belongs to must be texts (new stzItem("an", "banana") or StzItemQ("an", "banana")), and the case flag is fixed at 1. It inherits every method of stzItemCS, but those methods build a stzList from the stored text and so raise the error paList must be a list; only Item, List and CaseSensitive answer. The named form [ :In = text ] is rejected. For an item in a text use stzString.Find; for an item in a list use stzItemCS.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an item-in-a-text object from two texts, the item and the text it belongs to; it works for Item, List and CaseSensitive only.

parameters.name: pItem
parameters.role: the item, which must be a text

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the text the item is looked for in, which must be a text too

notes: use stzString.Find for an item in a text, or stzItemCS for an item in a list
warnings: the object keeps the text as its list, and every method that needs a list (Positions, NumberOfOccurrence, FirstPosition, IsLowercased...) raises an error "paList must be a list"; the named form [ :In = text ] is rejected as not being a text; the case flag is fixed at 1

classes.name: stzItemCS
classes.brief: Follows one item inside a list: where it occurs, how often, and its first, last and nth position.
classes.description: Build one with TheItemInQ(item, list), ItemInCSQ(item, list, flag), StzItemCSQ(item, list, flag) or new stzItemCS(item, list, flag): the three arguments are the item, the list it is looked for in, and a case flag. The reads that work today are Item, List, Positions, NumberOfOccurrence, NthPosition, FirstPosition and LastPosition, IsLowercased and IsUppercased (for a text item present in the list), and NumberOfItems (for an item that is itself a list). Positions count from 1 and an absent item gives 0 or an empty list. The case flag you give is only stored: the plain methods always compare with case, and only the CS forms (PositionsCS(0), NumberOfOccurrenceCS(0)) take the flag; the named form [ :In = list ] is not unpacked. Most of the remaining methods are broken today: Sections, IsBoundedBy, IsBetween, BoundedBy, ReplacedWith, Removed, Uppercased, Lowercased and the whole InsertedBefore and InsertedAfter family raise error R14, because they call stzList methods that do not exist (or misspelled names), and each says so in its own entry. Text items of any script are compared as whole characters.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Positions() )
#--> [ 1, 5 ]
? o1.NumberOfOccurrence()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.PositionsCS(0) )
#--> [ 1, 3, 5 ]
? o1.NthPosition(2)
#--> 5
o2 = new stzItemCS("שלום", [ "שלום", "عالم", "😀", "שלום" ], 1)
? @@( o2.Positions() )
#--> [ 1, 4 ]
o3 = new stzItemCS("😀", [ "😀", "عالم", "😀" ], 1)
? o3.LastPosition()
#--> 3

classes.name: stzJson
classes.brief: Holds a JSON document as a Ring list, as an object of keys or an array of items, and records its mistakes instead of raising them.
classes.description: Built from a JSON text or from a Ring list. An object is read and changed by key (HasKey, Value, SetValue, RemoveKey, TakeKey) and an array by position (At, Add, Insert, RemoveAt, TakeAt ...). A call that does not fit the kind of JSON held, or an index outside the array, leaves the object unchanged and records a message in LastError.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the object from a JSON text or from a Ring list; an empty or invalid text leaves it empty and records an error.

parameters.name: p
parameters.role: a JSON text, or a Ring list (a list of [ key, value ] pairs gives an object, any other list gives an array)

notes: a text that is not valid JSON never raises: read LastError; an argument that is neither text nor list builds an empty object with no error

methods.name: IsArray
methods.brief: TRUE if the JSON held is an array, FALSE if it is an object.
notes: a list given to the constructor counts as an array unless it is a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the object holds no key and no item, as after Clear or after a text that failed to parse.
notes: an empty object and an empty array are both empty

methods.name: IsNull
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is empty and an error has been recorded, as after a text that is not valid JSON.
notes: an empty object built from a valid text is not null

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns how many keys the object holds, or how many items the array holds.
notes: Count gives the same answer

methods.name: ToString
methods.brief: Returns the content as JSON text on one line, without spaces after the colons and commas.
notes: an empty object writes as {} and an empty array as []; true and false held as 1 and 0 come out as numbers; ToStringXT gives the indented form

extensions.name: ToStringXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: HasKey
methods.brief: TRUE if the object has the key; on an array it answers FALSE and records an error.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to look for, as text

notes: the answer is FALSE and LastError reads "Cannot check key on array" when the JSON is an array

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys of the object, in the order they have in the JSON text.
methods.returns: a list of text; [ ] for an array, with an error recorded

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the value stored under the key, or an empty text when the key is absent.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to read, as text

methods.returns: the value: a text, a number, or a list of [ key, value ] pairs for a nested object

methods.name: SetValue

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to set, as text

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the value to store: a text, a number or a list

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: on an array nothing changes and LastError reads "Cannot set value by key on array"

methods.name: RemoveKey
methods.brief: Removes the key and its value from the object, in place; returns the object itself.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to remove, as text

methods.returns: the stzJson itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent key changes nothing and records no error; an array records an error and changes nothing

methods.name: TakeKey
methods.brief: Removes the key from the object, in place, and returns the value it held.

parameters.name: cKey
parameters.role: the key to take, as text

classes.name: stzJwt
classes.brief: Reads one JSON Web Token: its header, its claims and its signature, and checks the signature against a public key.
classes.description: Use it on its own for any signed token with three parts. Reading a claim proves nothing: the token is only data until SignatureIsValidWith has passed against a key you hold, and a token meant for you must also carry your audience and an unexpired exp, which stzOidcClient checks. A malformed token is accepted at construction and simply reads as empty.
classes.example:
? o1.IsWellFormed()
#--> 1
? o1.Algorithm()
#--> ES256
? o1.Subject()
#--> alice
? o1.ClaimInt("exp")
#--> 1800003600
? o1.Audience()
#--> client-demo
? o1.SignatureIsValidWith([ [ "kty", "EC" ], [ "x", "t006lKtxiQpobDOpWwzGDVKazORGwZWNLbK206XQuHc" ], [ "y", "KGMvZoXXlU8YdR3KS-6Q6A8bqVqlwpoZy0Udq9TPUy4" ] ])
#--> 1

methods.brief: a different thing whenever the vote overrules proximity

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: THE HELD SET IS LIVE THROUGH HERE.
methods.detail: Ring COPIES an object into an attribute, so the set handed to the constructor is a SNAPSHOT: growing the caller's own object afterwards would NOT reach this learner. Grow it through this accessor -- oLearner.TrainingSetQ().AddExample(...) -- which reaches the real held set (accessor + method call is live in Ring).

methods.name: SetApproximate
methods.brief: ── APPROXIMATE SEARCH: OPT-IN, AND DELIBERATELY NOT AUTOMATIC ──
methods.detail: Exact search is O(n) per query: every example measured, the true k nearest, the same answer every time. Above a few thousand examples that is the whole cost of a classification, and the projection forest in the engine answers in roughly O(budget) instead. WHY THIS IS A SWITCH AND NOT A SIZE THRESHOLD. UMAP builds neighbours for every point at once, so its n alone decides whether approximating pays -- which is why umap.zig can turn it on by itself at 8192. A CLASSIFIER IS DIFFERENT: it answers one query at a time, and the forest has to be BUILT before it can answer any. That build is amortised over however many queries follow, and only the caller knows whether that is three or three million. Ten queries against 50000 examples are faster exact; ten thousand are not. A library cannot infer the query count, so it must not guess -- it asks. AND IT CHANGES ANSWERS, WHICH A SIZE THRESHOLD WOULD HIDE. Approximate neighbours can shift a vote. Usually they do not -- a vote survives a swapped neighbour far more often than a neighbour list survives it -- but "usually" is a promise no default should make on a caller's behalf. AgreementWithExact() exists so the cost can be measured on the actual data rather than assumed. ── WHAT IT ACTUALLY BUYS, MEASURED, AND IT IS LESS THAN ARITHMETIC SUGGESTS ── 16 features, k = 5, 30 queries, on this machine: 5000 examples    approximate is NOT faster per query 20000 examples    1.355x per query; break-even at ~219 queries Counting flops predicts far more: exact measures all 20000 examples where the forest examines a few hundred candidates, which is some sixty-fold less arithmetic. It does not show up, and the reason is written all over this file already -- THE BRIDGE AND THE INTERPRETER, NOT THE ARITHMETIC, ARE THE COST OF A QUERY at these sizes. Cutting the distance computations sixty-fold cuts a minority of the total. So this is a modest win that has to be asked for, not a free upgrade, and the break-even in QUERIES is the number that decides it. That is also the sharpest contrast with UMAP: there one call needs n neighbour searches, so the forest is amortised immediately and 8192 points is enough to turn it on automatically. Here each query stands alone. Label agreement measured 1.000 in both rows above -- on separable data the vote absorbed every neighbour the forest missed. Do not read that as a guarantee; read it as the reason AgreementWithExact() takes YOUR queries.

methods.name: SetApproximateTrees
methods.brief: More trees, better recall, bigger index and a slower build.

methods.name: SetApproximateBudget
methods.brief: Candidates examined per query before the true distances decide. 0 lets the engine scale it from k. This is the recall dial.

methods.name: AgreementWithExact
methods.brief: THE HONEST MEASURE FOR A CLASSIFIER: not how many neighbours the forest missed, but how often the LABEL still came out the same. Those are very different numbers -- a majority vote absorbs a swapped neighbour that a neighbour-recall figure would count as a loss -- and the label is what the caller actually receives.
methods.detail: Returns the fraction of the given queries on which approximate and exact classification agree. Each mode is built once, not once per query.

classes.name: stzKnowledgeGraph
classes.brief: Holds knowledge as facts, triples of subject, predicate and object, in a graph, with queries, laws, proofs and conversations.
classes.description: A stzKnowledgeGraph is a stzGraph of type semantic: each fact is an edge labelled with its predicate between two entity nodes, so every stzGraph method is also available. Facts are set-like (adding a known fact is a no-op), but only one fact can link a given ordered pair of entities. Laws (:unique, :symmetric, :transitive) are declared per relation with ConstrainRelation, and only :unique and :transitive are acted on here: Admit is the governed door that checks :unique and records a refusal as a named contradiction, and Prove follows :transitive; strict mode makes every fact carry provenance. Prove answers a goal with a replayable proof, and the space can hold stzConversation objects that elicit missing facts. Knowledge is saved and read as .zknw text. A number of methods carry a warning today.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzKnowledgeGraph("zoo"); o1.AddFact("Dog", "is-a", "Animal"); o1.AddFact("Cat", "is-a", "Animal"); o1.AddFact("Dog", "eats", "Meat")

classes.name: stzLearner
classes.brief: Holds one learner's folder: the work they submitted and their progress, which only the checker writes, with its evidence.
classes.description: A learner is a folder: work/<exercise>.ring is what they submitted, as they wrote it, and progress.zknw is a plain text file of facts. A pass is recorded only by Submit or SubmitProject, after the checker has run the program, and it counts only while the sha256 of the work file (or of the project folder) still equals the evidence recorded then: a pass typed by hand, or a file changed afterwards, reads as not passed. A level is earned when every exercise of its chapters and its project have passed. The checker runs programs on the desktop with Softanza, never in a browser, and each submission takes seconds. The fr, ar and ha editions of the course are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person, and no institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
oC = StzProgramQ("../../education/program").CourseQ("elementary-introduction")
oEx = oC.ExerciseQ("ex-01-01")
? o1.ChapterOn(oC)
#--> find-then-apply
? o1.Submit(oEx, read(oEx.RightAnswers()[1])).Passed()
#--> 1
? o1.HasPassed("ex-01-01")
#--> 1
? o1.ChapterOn(oC)
#--> a-first-sentence

classes.name: stzLinearSolver
classes.brief: Solves small linear programs written as text: variables with bounds, constraints such as x + y <= 5 and one objective to maximize or minimize.
classes.description: Declare the variables with addVariable, the constraints with addConstraint and the objective with maximize or minimize, then call solve with a solver name. The simplex solver (Big-M, run in the engine) gives the exact optimum and reports optimal, infeasible or unbounded in status. The greedy solver, the default, is a heuristic that raises every variable as far as allowed: it does not honour minimize and reads every constraint as a limit from above. The genetic solver raises an error as soon as the problem has a constraint, and branch_bound is not implemented, so it always raises. The integer and binary marks are recorded but no solver enforces them. The simplex pivot helpers (BuildSimplexTableau and its kin) are placeholders that answer constants. Pass an empty text to solve for the default solver, since the argument cannot be left out.
classes.example:
o1.addVariable("x", 0, 4).addVariable("y", 0, 6)
o1.addConstraint("x + y", "<=", 5).addConstraint("x + 3*y", "<=", 12)
o1.maximize("3*x + 2*y").solve("simplex")
? o1.solutionValue("x")
#--> 4
? o1.solutionValue("y")
#--> 1
? o1.objectiveValue()
#--> 14
? o1.status()
#--> optimal

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty linear programming problem, with no variable, no constraint and no objective.

methods.name: clear
methods.brief: Empties the problem so a new one can be described: variables, constraints, objective, status and the last solution are dropped.
methods.returns: nothing; the problem is empty again

methods.name: addVariable
methods.brief: Adds a continuous variable with a lower and an upper bound, in declaration order.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: _lowerBound_
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: _upperBound_
parameters.role: the largest value it may take, never below the lower bound

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: an empty text given for one bound copies the other bound (a, "" and 6 gives the range 6 to 6); expressions read names without regard to case
warnings: all three arguments must be given: calling with fewer raises R19 Calling function with less number of parameters, so the defaults coded for a missing bound are never reached; a name that is not text, bounds that are not numbers and an upper bound below the lower bound each raise an error

methods.name: addIntegerVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable whose type is marked integer, with the same arguments and checks as a continuous one.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: _lowerBound_
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: _upperBound_
parameters.role: the largest value it may take

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: all three arguments are needed, as for addVariable
warnings: the mark is only recorded in the variable list: the simplex solver ignores it (maximize n with 2*n <= 5 answers 2.5), the greedy solver floors every value, and branch and bound is not implemented

methods.name: addBinaryVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable bounded between 0 and 1 and marked binary.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the mark is only recorded: the simplex solver ignores it (maximize b with 2*b <= 1 answers 0.5)

methods.name: variables
methods.brief: Returns the declared variables in order, each as a list of name, lowerbound, upperbound and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable; [ ] when none is declared
notes: the keys are lower case

methods.name: variableNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared variables, in declaration order.

methods.name: addConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one linear constraint: an expression such as "x + 3*y", a comparison and a number.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the left side, as text, with terms like 2*x, x*2 or x

parameters.name: operator
parameters.role: the comparison: "<=", ">=" or "="

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the number the expression is compared with

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: constraints are stored as stzHashList objects
warnings: an expression that is not text, another operator, or a value that is neither a number nor text raise an error; a value given as text, such as "7" or "", is stored as 0 because the text is looked up in the variables list

methods.name: constraints
methods.brief: Returns the declared constraints in order, each as a stzHashList holding expression, operator and value.
methods.returns: a list of stzHashList objects; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: maximize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as large as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "3*x + 2*y"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: minimize
methods.brief: Sets the objective to an expression to make as small as possible, replacing any earlier objective.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "x + 2*y"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the greedy solver does not honour it (minimize x with x <= 4 answers 4); use the simplex solver

methods.name: objective
methods.brief: Returns the objective expression as text.
methods.returns: a text; "" before an objective is set

methods.name: objectiveType
methods.brief: Returns whether the objective is to be made larger or smaller.
methods.returns: the text "maximize" or "minimize"; "maximize" before any objective is set

methods.name: solve
methods.brief: Runs one of the built-in solvers and keeps its answer: "greedy" (the default), "simplex", "branch_bound" or "genetic".

parameters.name: _cSolver_
parameters.role: the solver's name, in lower case, an empty text selects greedy

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: on maximize 3*x + 2*y with x + y <= 5 and x + 3*y <= 12, bounds 0..4 and 0..6, simplex and greedy both answer x = 4 and y = 1, value 14
warnings: the argument cannot be left out (R19), pass an empty text for the default; no variable, no objective or an unknown name raise an error; "branch_bound" always raises today and sets the status to unimplemented; "genetic" raises R5 as soon as the problem has a constraint; "greedy" is a heuristic and still reports the status optimal

methods.name: solveWithGreedy
methods.brief: Returns a solution that raises each variable, best objective per resource first, to the largest whole value its limits allow.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
notes: called directly it returns the pairs and sets the status and iterations but does not store the answer; solve does
warnings: a heuristic, reported with status optimal in every case: it raises variables as far as allowed even when minimizing (minimize x with x <= 4 answers 4, the simplex answers 0), it reads ">=" and "=" as "<=" so an equality can be violated (minimize x + 2*y with x + y >= 3 and x - y = -1 answers x = 0 and y = 3, value 6, where the simplex answers 1 and 2, value 5), and it floors values

methods.name: solveWithSimplex
methods.brief: Returns the optimum found by a Big-M simplex run in the engine, after shifting the variables to their lower bounds.

classes.name: stzList
classes.brief: Holds a list of items of any type and finds, sorts, edits, groups and compares them.
classes.description: A stzList wraps a Ring list so that every operation on it has one name that reads like the sentence it stands for: Find, Remove, Replace, Section, Sorted. Active forms change the list in place (Sort), passive forms return a changed copy (Sorted), and the Q forms return the object so calls chain. Reach for it before writing a loop over a list.

classes.name: stzListChecker
classes.brief: Answers yes or no questions about a list: what its items are made of, whether they are unique, ordered, equal or paired.
classes.description: Reach for it to validate a list before using it: AllItemsAreOfType and the IsListOf... family check the type of the items, IsMonotonic and the strict variants check their order, IsHashList and IsListOfPairs check the shape, and HasMoreNumberOfItems compares the length with another list. Most checks answer 1 or 0, a few answer TRUE or FALSE; both work in an if. A check made on the empty list is true for IsListOfNumbers, IsListOfStrings and AllItemsAreEqual, and false for IsListOfLists. Broken today: ContainsItem answers 0 for every item, and with it ContainsAllOfThese and ContainsOneOfThese; ContainsW raises error R3.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a checker over a list or over a stzList object; anything else raises an error.

parameters.name: pListOrObj
parameters.role: a list, or a stzList object, to be checked

methods.brief: Returns the list being checked.

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the checked list has.

methods.name: IsListOfNumbers
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is a number, else 0.
notes: the empty list answers 1; the answer is a number, not TRUE or FALSE

methods.name: IsListOfStrings
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is a text, else 0.
notes: the empty list answers 1

methods.name: IsListOfLists
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is a list, else 0.
notes: unlike IsListOfNumbers the empty list answers 0

methods.name: IsListOfListsOfSameSize
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is a list and all of them have the same length, else 0.

methods.name: IsListOfObjects
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is an object, else 0.
notes: the empty list answers 1

methods.name: IsHybrid
methods.brief: Returns 1 if the items are not all of one type, else 0.
notes: the empty list and a list of one type answer 0

methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item has the given type, else 0; the type can also be a list of items of a type, such as :ListOfNumbers.

parameters.name: pcType

methods.name: IsListOfDecimalNumbers
methods.brief: Returns 1 if every item is a number, whole or decimal, else 0.

methods.name: AcceptMeanings
methods.brief: VC6: the step that closes the loop
methods.detail: §1.1 says a recognised phrase is text, text is a meaning, and a meaning renders to a colour and an earcon and a phrase. Every link in that chain already existed EXCEPT "text is a meaning", and VC6's kill criterion is about exactly this: if the loop needs a step outside these faces, it is a demo rather than an architecture. WITHOUT this verb the step is a `switch` in application code -- outside the faces, rewritten by every caller, and drifting from the grammar it has to agree with. The grammar and the meanings are ONE declaration, so they are declared in one place: oL.AcceptMeanings([ [ "disk full",     :Danger  ], [ "backup done",   :Success ] ]) THE AUTHOR STILL DECLARES THE MEANING. Nothing here infers one from the words -- "disk full" is a danger because somebody said so, not because a classifier guessed. That is the plane's standing rule: do not compute meanings the author should declare. What the face contributes is carrying the declaration, not making it.

methods.detail: This is the consent boundary of the library: it opens an input device and listens. Local only -- nothing leaves this machine -- but a caller should still tell the operator it is listening, because an open microphone the operator cannot see is indefensible (Rule 82, visible state).

classes.name: stzListFlattener
classes.brief: Reshapes a list: opens nested lists, pairs and chunks the items, finds repeated ends, and hands the list to the typed list classes.
classes.description: A flattener is built over a list with new stzListFlattener(aList) or StzListFlattenerQ(aList); stzList has its own Flatten methods and does not build one. It works on its own copy, so the list you passed is never changed. The verbs (Flatten, DeepFlatten, FlattenToDepth, AssociateWith) reshape the held list in place and return nothing, the Q form returning the flattener so calls chain; the past-tense forms (Flattened, DeepFlattened, FlattenedToDepth, AssociatedWith) return the new list and leave the flattener alone. Read the held list with Content. Flatten and DeepFlatten open every level; FlattenToDepth opens only n levels. Paired, Chunked, InterleavedWith, Stringify and Objectified return a new list and never change the held one. The ToStz methods hand the content to the typed class named: ToStzGrid needs a pair [ columns, rows ] and raises an error for other content. The repeated-items methods return the copies after the first item (or before the last), so a run of three gives two. Text items of any script (Hebrew, Arabic, emoji) are kept whole.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Flattened() )
#--> [ 1, 2, 3, 4, "a" ]
? @@( o1.FlattenedToDepth(1) )
#--> [ 1, 2, [ 3, [ 4 ] ], "a" ]
o2 = new stzListFlattener([ 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3 ])
? @@( o2.Paired() )
#--> [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 3 ] ]
? @@( o2.RepeatedTrailingItems() )
#--> [ 3, 3 ]
o3 = new stzListFlattener([ "שלום", [ "مرحبا", [ "😀" ] ] ])
? @@( o3.FlattenedToDepth(1) )
#--> [ "שלום", "مرحبا", [ "😀" ] ]

classes.name: stzListOfBytes
classes.brief: Holds a run of raw bytes in a Ring text, and reads, cuts and converts it byte by byte.
classes.description: Positions and sizes count bytes, never characters, so a character of several bytes is several items here (Chars and the per-character methods are the exception). The bytes can be read as numbers, as hexadecimal, as Base64 or with percent escapes, and written back from those forms. Methods that change the object say so with a verb such as Clear, Trim or Update; the others return a new text. The name stzBytes is the same class.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Bytecodes() )
#--> [ 72, 105, 33 ]
? o1.ToHex()
#--> 0x486921
? o1.ToBase64()
#--> SGkh
? o1.LeftNBytes(2)
#--> Hi

classes.name: stzListOfEntities
classes.brief: Holds a list of entities, each a name with a type, such as apple/fruit, and answers questions about them by name and by type.
classes.description: An entity is a hashlist with a :name and a :type. AddEntity lowercases both and refuses a duplicate, AppendEntity adds without any check, and the finders answer positions (FindEntityByName, FindEntitiesByType) or the entities themselves (EntitiesOfType, FilterByTypeQ). The shared world registry that WhatIs reads is one such list, reached by WorldEntities(). AddEntity refuses too much: a new entity whose name and whose type are both already in the list is refused even when no single entity has both.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the list from a list of entities, each a hashlist with a name and a type; anything else raises an error.

parameters.name: paList
parameters.role: the entities, such as [ [ :name = "apple", :type = "fruit" ] ], or an empty list

notes: the list is stored as given: names and types are not lowercased here, unlike AddEntity
warnings: a list that is not empty and not a list of hashlists raises Can't create the stzListOfEntities object

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the held list of entities, each one a hashlist.
notes: Value is the same call

notes: the same call as Content

classes.name: stzListOfLists
classes.brief: Holds a non-empty list of lists and answers questions about its rows and columns, sizes, padding, sorting and column edits.
classes.description: A stzListOfLists wraps a Ring list whose every item is a list, the lists being allowed to differ in size. Reach for it to treat the lists as rows of a table without the weight of stzTable: take a column (NthColumn), pad the short rows (Extend, AdjustWith), cut them (Shrink, ShrinkTo), sort the rows on a column (SortOn), find an item inside the rows (FindManyInLists) or edit a column (InsertCol, ReplaceCol). Active forms change the lists in place, passive forms (the ones ending in ed) return a changed copy as a plain list of lists. Item searches are case-sensitive. Merge and Flatten always raise an error on purpose: use their passive forms, Merged and Flattened.

classes.name: stzListOfNumbers
classes.brief: Holds a list of numbers and finds, ranks, compares, edits and sorts them, and answers sums, means and differences.
classes.description: A stzListOfNumbers wraps a Ring list that holds only numbers; building it from anything else raises an error. Reach for it when the question is about the numbers as a series: the smallest and largest (Min, Top3), the nearest to a value (Nearest), the steps between neighbours (Diff, Steps), the totals (Sum, Mean, Median), arithmetic on every number at once (AddToEach, MultiplyEachBy), filters (NumbersBetween) and sorting. Active forms change the list in place, passive forms (the ones ending in ed, or beginning with Each) return a changed copy. Rank methods such as Bottom3 and Top3 work on distinct values and answer in ascending order. The random picks draw from the list itself, every position equally likely, and raise when nothing qualifies.

classes.name: stzListOfPairs
classes.brief: Holds a list whose every item is a pair [ first, second ], and answers questions about the first items, the second items and the order of the pairs.
classes.description: Reach for it when the data is naturally two-column: sections [ start, end ], key and value, name and score. It orders the pairs by the first or the second item (Sort, SortOn), exchanges the items of every pair (SwapItems), lists the first and the second items apart and checks their types. Most mutators change the object in place and return nothing; the Sorted, Swapped and Stringified forms return a copy. Some methods are broken today: the key-expression sorts (SortBy and its forms), ReplacePair, AreAnagrams, ExpandedIfPairsOfNumbers and ToStzSetOfSections; see their warnings. The Reverse and Inverse families exchange the two items of each pair, they do not reverse the order of the pairs.

methods.name: MostSimilarByMeaning
methods.brief: These are what make a list of TEXTS more than a list of strings.
methods.detail: They read the MEANING of each fragment (semantic similarity, sentiment), so a fluent chain like Q(text).SentencesQ().MostSimilarByMeaning(query) / .ThatAre( :Positive) works. Semantic ops upgrade to neural embeddings when a model is loaded (StzNeuralModelQ(path)), else degrade to lexical -- see StzSemanticSimilarity(). The text most similar to pcQuery by MEANING. Uses the loaded neural model's sentence embeddings when one is present, else lexical WORD-OVERLAP cosine -- the right notion for sentences/documents. (The inherited MostSimilarTo() uses Jaro-Winkler CHARACTER similarity, better for fuzzy word/typo matching.)

classes.name: stzListOfTimeLines
classes.brief: Holds several named lanes of events on one shared time axis, to ask what happens when across all of them.
classes.description: Build one with new stzListOfTimeLines([ :Lanes = [ ... ], :Start = ..., :End = ... ]); it is also reached as stzTimeLines, TimeLines(p) and StzTimeLinesQ(p). Each lane is a stzTimeLine over the shared bounds. Lane names are stored in upper case and every lookup ignores case, and the dates are read as text, a bare date meaning midnight. What works today: the lane management (AddLane, RemoveLane, Lanes, HasLane), AddPointToLane (and its alias AddMomentToLane), WhatsAt, SetGlobalStart and SetGlobalEnd, Duration, Content, ToTimeLine and Clear. Lane(name) returns a copy of the lane's timeline, and the methods that edit through it silently keep nothing: AddSpanToLane, AddSpansToLane, AddPointsToLane, AddBlockedSpanToLane, AddBlockedPointToLane, RenameLabelInLane and RemovePointFromLane all do nothing, so no span can be stored and the span- based reads (HasOverlapsInLane, CrossLaneOverlaps, UncoveredPeriodsPerLane) were not exercised with real data. Copy keeps the lanes and bounds but not their points. BlockSpanInLane and BlockPointInLane raise R14, and the whole drawing family (Show, ShowShort, ShowUncovered, VizFind) raises R19; each says so in its own entry. Lane names of any script (Hebrew, Arabic, emoji) work.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Lanes() )
#--> [ "TEAM A", "TEAM B" ]
? o1.Duration()
#--> 31449600
o1.AddPointToLane("team a", "Kickoff", "2026-02-01")
? @@( o1.WhatsAt("2026-02-01") )
#--> [ [ [ "lane", "TEAM A" ], [ "events", [ [ "KICKOFF", "point" ] ] ] ] ]
o2 = new stzListOfTimeLines([ :Lanes = [ "צוות", "فريق", "😀" ], :Start = "2026-01-01 08:00:00", :End = "2026-01-01 18:00:00" ])
o2.AddPointToLane("فريق", "اجتماع", "2026-01-01 09:30:00")
? o2.NumberOfLanes()
#--> 3
? o2.Duration()
#--> 36000

classes.name: stzListParser
classes.brief: Walks through a list with a cursor, visiting the positions you choose: from a start to an end by a step, forward or backwards.
classes.description: A parser is built over a non-empty list with new stzListParser(aList) or StzListParserQ(aList); no stzList method builds one. Parse chooses the positions to visit (ParsedPositions) and ParsedItems answers the items there; the cursor, read with CurrentPosition and CurrentItem, moves with NextPosition, PreviousPosition and the Nth forms, which count visited positions, not list positions, so with a step of 2 NextNthPosition(2) advances four list positions. NextItem and PreviousItem move the cursor and answer the item, so two calls give two different items. Reset parses again with the default start, end and step (1, the last position, 1 until a SetDefault... call changes them), not with the last Parse. Positions count from 1. Moving past the last visited position, or before the first, raises a Ring error (R2, array access out of range) and leaves the cursor in place; Parse does not check the positions against the list, and ParsedItems raises when one is outside it. The base class stzParser only keeps a source value; a stzListParser does not fill it, so read the list with List.
classes.example:
o1.Parse(3, 8, 2)
? @@( o1.ParsedPositions() )
#--> [ 3, 5, 7 ]
? @@( o1.ParsedItems() )
#--> [ "c", "e", "g" ]
? o1.NextItem()
#--> e
? o1.CurrentPosition()
#--> 5
o1.Reset()
? o1.CurrentPosition()
#--> 1
o2 = new stzListParser([ "שלום", "مرحبا", "😀", "ok" ])
? o2.NextItem()
#--> مرحبا

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a parser over a non-empty list and parses it from the first position to the last, one step at a time.

parameters.name: paList

notes: after Parse(3, 8, 2) on a list of 8 it is [ 3, 5, 7 ]

classes.name: stzListRandom
classes.brief: Draws positions and items at random from a list, and shuffles the whole list, a section of it or the runs of one kind of item.
classes.description: Built around a list or a stzList. The drawing methods (RandomPosition, RandomItem, NRandomItems and their Except forms) leave the list as it is. Randomize, Shuffle and the section and typed variants change it in place and answer nothing, while Randomized and the other names ending in Randomized answer a shuffled copy. The typed shuffles (numbers, strings, lists, objects) only reorder items of that kind that sit next to each other: [ 1, 2, 3, "a", 4, 5 ] can swap 1, 2 and 3 and swap 4 and 5, but a number never crosses the text. Two cautions: NRandomPositions(0) never returns, and RandomItemExceptPosition on a list of one item raises R2. The draws are random, so promises can only be made about shape and ranges.

classes.name: stzListReplacer
classes.brief: Changes the items of a list in place: one item, every occurrence of a value, a section, or a chosen set of positions.
classes.description: Reach for it when you need to rewrite part of a list and keep the object: the methods act on the held list and return nothing, so read the result with Content. Replace by value (ReplaceAllOccurrences, ReplaceFirstOccurrence, ReplaceNthOccurrence), by position (ReplaceAnyItemAtPosition, ReplaceAnyItemAtPositions), by section (ReplaceSection puts one item, ReplaceSectionByMany splices several) or by a condition (ReplaceItemsW). The ...ByMany forms take a list of replacements: used in order, or round-robin in the XT forms. Text is compared with case, and a position outside the list is skipped without an error. AllOccurrencesReplaced is the one method that leaves the object alone and returns a changed copy.
classes.example:
o1.ReplaceAllOccurrences(2, 9)
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 1, 9, 3, 9, 1 ]
o1.ReplaceFirstOccurrence(1, 0)
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 0, 9, 3, 9, 1 ]
o1.ReplaceSectionByMany(2, 4, [7, 8])
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 0, 7, 8, 1 ]

classes.name: stzListSorter
classes.brief: Orders a list and answers questions about its order: sorting, reversing, ranking, the extremes and the median.
classes.description: A sorter is built over a list with new stzListSorter(aList) or StzListSorterQ(aList); stzList has its own Sort methods and does not build one. It works on its own copy of the list, so the list you passed is never changed. The verbs (SortInAscending, SortInDescending, SortBy..., Reverse) reorder the held list in place and return nothing, the Q form returning the sorter so calls chain; the past-tense forms (SortedInAscending, SortedBy, Reversed) return a sorted copy and leave the sorter alone. Read the held list with Content. Numbers sort by value and come before texts, which sort by character code, so Hebrew, Arabic and emoji texts are ordered by code point and a capital letter comes before a small one. Min, Max, Median and the Nth forms compare numbers only and answer 0 for a list of texts. SortBy takes a text expression where @item is the current item: len(@item) works, while an expression using lower() or upper() as the key does not order alphabetically. Ranks and positions count from 1.
classes.example:
? @@( o1.SortedInAscending() )
#--> [ 1, 2, 5, 7, 9 ]
? @@( o1.Ranked() )
#--> [ 3, 2, 5, 1, 4 ]
? o1.NthLargest(2)
#--> 7
o1.SortInDescending()
? @@( o1.Content() )
#--> [ 9, 7, 5, 2, 1 ]
o2 = new stzListSorter([ "שלום", "אבא", "בית" ])
? @@( o2.Ranked() )
#--> [ 3, 1, 2 ]
o3 = new stzListSorter([ "b😀", "a😀", "😀" ])
? @@( o3.Ranked() )
#--> [ 2, 1, 3 ]

classes.name: stzLocale
classes.brief: Holds a locale such as fr-FR and answers its country, language, script, currency, week days, time patterns and number symbols.
classes.description: A stzLocale is a locale code kept as text with an underscore (fr_FR). Build it from a code, a language name, a country name, a hash of parts, :System or :Default; the library's own tables then answer the facts: CountryName, LanguageName, CurrencyInfo, the first day of the week (monday for fr-FR, sunday for en-US, saturday for ar-EG), time patterns, DecimalPoint and GroupSeparator. The week methods come in three faces, English, native (the locale's own language) and the abbreviation and one-letter symbol of each, all counted from the locale's first day. A locale the tables do not know answers empty text. The case methods are Unicode-wide and follow the Turkish and Azerbaijani dotted and dotless i. Day names exist only for ten languages; the others answer English.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds the locale from a code such as fr-FR or ar_Arab_TN, a language or country name, a hash of parts, :System or :Default.

parameters.name: pLocale
parameters.role: a locale code with - or _ between its parts, a language name such as French, a country name such as France, [ :Language = ..., :Script = ..., :Country = ... ], :System or :Default

notes: a language code alone completes to its default country (fr gives fr_FR); :System gives the C locale and :Default gives the library's default locale (en_US when probed); the code is stored with an underscore
warnings: a code the library does not know (xx-YY) is kept as given and every lookup answers empty text; a hash with none of the three keys raises Can't create the stzLocale object!; a number builds an empty locale without an error

methods.name: TrainingSetQ
methods.brief: THE HELD SET IS LIVE THROUGH HERE.
methods.detail: Ring COPIES an object into an attribute, so the set handed to the constructor is a SNAPSHOT: growing the caller's own object afterwards would NOT reach this learner. Grow it through this accessor -- oLearner.TrainingSetQ().AddExample(...) -- which reaches the real held set (accessor + method call is live in Ring).

methods.name: Train
methods.brief: THE LOOP RUNS IN THE ENGINE (numeric phase 5), and the arithmetic is deliberately unchanged rather than merely equivalent.
methods.detail: Gradient descent is a feedback loop -- each step's weights decide the next step's gradient -- so a last-bit difference does not stay a last-bit difference, it compounds. This class promises reproducible runs, and moving the loop is only allowed to keep that promise. So `logistic.zig` keeps the updates sequential per example, accumulates the dot product in index order (a lane-parallel reduction would be faster and would change every model), and saturates at the same |z| > 35. Only the weight update vectorises, and only because `w[f] += c * x[f]` is elementwise: lane width cannot change an individual result. Measured, 5000 examples x 16 features x 100 epochs: 10.0s -> 0.062s (161x), and 20000 x 32 x 100 -- previously out of reach -- in 0.71s. Hoisting the old Ring loop by hand (the label test done once instead of once per epoch, the feature row never passed as an argument) gave 5.0s with bit-identical weights, so half of what was paid was interpreter overhead and half was arithmetic. The engine collects both. The drift against the old loop was measured, not assumed, and it is never zero: 1e-16 after ONE epoch, 1e-15 at ten, 1e-14 at a hundred and still 1e-14 at five hundred. That is the one thing that could not be held fixed -- Ring's exp is the C library's, the engine's is Zig's, they agree to within an ulp, and gradient descent feeds each step into the next so the difference grows about a decade per five hundred epochs. Against weights of magnitude 1 to 10 it stays around 1e-15 relative, and both loops classify identically.

methods.name: Probability
methods.brief: SCORED BY THE RULE IT WAS FITTED BY.
methods.detail: This goes through the engine too, and not for speed -- one row is dominated by marshalling. It is here because Ring's exp and Zig's exp agree only to within an ulp, and a model whose predictions come from a slightly different function than its fit is a question nobody should have to think about. One definition, both ends.

methods.name: Probabilities
methods.brief: Probabilities for many rows in ONE crossing.
methods.detail: TrainingAccuracy() below is the reason this exists: it scores every training example, and a round trip per row would have made the diagnostic cost more than the fit it diagnoses.

methods.name: TrainingAccuracy
methods.brief: How well the model fits the data it was TRAINED on.
methods.detail: This exists because the way this class fails is SILENT and CONFIDENT. Gradient descent on UNSCALED features diverges: with values in the tens of thousands and the default learning rate, each weight update is thousands wide, the sigmoid saturates, and the model settles on a confidently WRONG answer -- Probability() returns exactly 1 or 0, which reads as certainty. Measured on identical data: features 1000..79000 gave weights [5350, 5350] and misclassified a training-range point, while the SAME data scaled to 0..1 gave weights [8.06, 8.06] and answered correctly. Needing standardised features is the normal requirement for stochastic gradient descent, not a defect here -- but nothing surfaced the failure. This does: a diverged model scores around chance on data it has already seen, where a converged one scores near 1.

classes.name: stzMathDiagram
classes.brief: Solves and draws a mathematical diagram: objects and relations laid out so that every rule about them holds.
classes.description: A diagram is made of three parts: a domain (set theory, geometry, graphs), a substance that declares the objects and asserts relations between them, and a style that turns each object into shapes and each relation into rules. Nothing is drawn by hand. The first question asked of the diagram solves it, a contradictory substance gives a picture that says it is not lawful instead of an error, and every shape, number and mark can be read back, which is what lets a caption quote the picture. The figure can be pinned, dragged, windowed, marked and written out as SVG or PNG.
classes.receiver: os = new stzMathSubstance(StzSetTheoryDomain()); os.DeclareAll("Set", [ "A", "B" ]); os.Assert("Subset", [ "B", "A" ]); os.AutoLabelAll(); o1 = new stzMathDiagram(StzSetTheoryDomain(), os, StzEulerStyle())
classes.example:
? @@( o1.Shapes() )
#--> [ "A.icon", "A.text", "B.icon", "B.text" ]
? o1.IsFeasible()
#--> 1
? o1.ShapeOf("B.icon")[:kind]
#--> circle
? o1.Fact(:count, [ "shapes" ])[:message]
#--> the picture reports 4 shapes

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a diagram from what it is about, the rules that read it and the look that draws it; nothing is solved yet.

parameters.name: poDomain
parameters.role: the domain, such as StzSetTheoryDomain(), that gives the kinds of object and relation

parameters.name: poSubstance
parameters.role: the stzMathSubstance holding the declared objects and what is asserted of them

parameters.name: poStyle
parameters.role: the style, such as StzEulerStyle(), that turns each object into shapes and rules

notes: the picture is solved on the first question asked of it
warnings: a domain, substance or style that is not an object raises the error stzMathDiagram: give a domain, a substance and a style.

methods.name: SetFont
methods.brief: Sets the font and size the names are drawn and measured in, and marks the picture to be solved again.

parameters.name: poFont
parameters.role: a stzFont

parameters.name: pnSize
parameters.role: the size, as a number

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: without a font the picture still solves and draws with the default one; SetFontQ is the same call

extensions.name: SetFontQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SetVariation
methods.brief: Sets the seed the starting shapes are drawn from: the same text or number always gives the same picture.

parameters.name: pVariation
parameters.role: a text, folded to a seed, or a number, used as the seed

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: a different value gives a different picture of the same content (tried with a text and with a number); SetVariationQ is the same call

extensions.name: SetVariationQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SolveProfile
methods.brief: Returns where the last solve spent its time, in milliseconds, with the number of rounds.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: text, compile, minimise, read, fold, rounds, rounds0, rounds1, worst1

methods.name: Relayout
methods.brief: Solves the picture again starting from where the figure stands, so the shapes settle near their present places.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the pinned shapes stay where they are; RelayoutQ is the same call

extensions.name: RelayoutQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: DragTo
methods.brief: Moves the centre of a shape to a point, holds it there while the rest of the figure re-solves, then lets it go unless it was pinned.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, such as A.icon, as Shapes lists them

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the x of the new centre, in pixels

parameters.name: pnY
parameters.role: the y of the new centre, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: DragToQ is the same call
warnings: a shape whose centre no rule left to the solver, such as a polygon derived from a triangle, raises the error ... has no free centre

extensions.name: DragToQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Pin
methods.brief: Holds every free value of a shape where it is through any later solve, until Unpin.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: PinQ is the same call
warnings: a path that is not a shape raises the error ... is not a shape any rule minted, and a shape with nothing left free raises the error ... has nothing a rule left free

extensions.name: PinQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Unpin
methods.brief: Lets the free values of a shape move again in later solves.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: a path that is not a shape changes nothing; UnpinQ is the same call

extensions.name: UnpinQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: UnpinAll
methods.brief: Lets every pinned shape move again.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsPinned
methods.brief: TRUE if the shape is held in place by a pin.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: Pins
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the shapes that are pinned.
methods.returns: a list of text; empty when nothing is pinned

methods.name: Draggable
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the visible circles, rectangles, ellipses and texts whose centre is free, which a pointer can take hold of.

methods.name: PickAt
methods.brief: Returns the path of the nearest draggable shape whose body, or a ten-pixel reach around its centre, holds a point.

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the x of the point, in pixels

parameters.name: pnY
parameters.role: the y of the point, in pixels

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the point is on the paper

methods.name: OnPress
methods.brief: Starts a gesture: takes hold of the shape under the pointer, if there is one.

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the x of the pointer, in pixels

parameters.name: pnY
parameters.role: the y of the pointer, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OnMove
methods.brief: Moves the pointer of a gesture in progress and previews; nothing is solved.

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the x of the pointer, in pixels

parameters.name: pnY
parameters.role: the y of the pointer, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: it does nothing when no shape was taken hold of

methods.name: DragPreview
methods.brief: Returns where the held shape is to be painted during a gesture.
methods.returns: a list [ path, x, y ]; an empty list when no gesture is going on

methods.name: OnRelease
methods.brief: Ends a gesture: drops the held shape at the pointer, which is the one drag that re-solves the figure.

parameters.name: pnX
parameters.role: the x where the pointer was released, in pixels

parameters.name: pnY
parameters.role: the y where the pointer was released, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the shape goes where it is released, not where OnMove last said

methods.name: UiState
methods.brief: Returns the state of the gesture: idle, or dragging after a press that took hold of a shape.

methods.name: Layout
methods.brief: Solves the picture if it has not been solved since the last change.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: every question about the picture calls it first; LayoutQ is the same call

extensions.name: LayoutQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsFeasible
methods.brief: TRUE if every rule is satisfied, to within a hundredth of a pixel.

methods.name: Violation
methods.brief: Returns the largest amount, in pixels, by which a rule is broken; 0 for a lawful picture.
notes: a contradictory substance gives a positive number instead of an error: a subset that is also disjoint gave 14.31

methods.name: Violations
methods.brief: Returns every rule the picture could not satisfy, one finding each.
methods.returns: a list of [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ] findings; empty when every rule holds
notes: the findings are in the shape the rule report takes; a contradictory substance gave four

methods.name: Energy
methods.brief: Returns the final value of the quantity the solver minimised.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when every rule is satisfied

methods.name: Rounds
methods.brief: Returns how many penalty rounds the solve took.

methods.name: Evaluations
methods.brief: Returns how many times the solver evaluated the energy.

methods.name: LayoutMs
methods.brief: Returns how long the last solve took, in milliseconds.
notes: a clock reading, so it differs from run to run

methods.name: NumberOfUnknowns
methods.brief: Returns how many free values the solver had to choose.

methods.name: NumberOfConstraints
methods.brief: Returns how many rules the picture was compiled into.

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence saying whether the picture is lawful and after how many rounds.

methods.name: CanvasWidth
methods.brief: Returns the width of the paper, in pixels, as the style fixes it.

methods.name: CanvasHeight
methods.brief: Returns the height of the paper, in pixels, as the style fixes it.

methods.name: ShapeOwnerOf
methods.brief: Returns the name of the object a shape draws, such as A for A.icon.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: a text; an empty text for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: IsHidden
methods.brief: TRUE if the shape is not drawn.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: PropOf
methods.brief: Returns one property a shape was given, such as n for a polygon or fill, or a default when it has none.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the property name, such as fill or n

parameters.name: pDefault
parameters.role: what to answer when the shape or the property is absent

methods.name: ShapeOf
methods.brief: Returns the solved geometry of one shape, whose keys depend on its kind.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, cx, cy, r for a circle; cx, cy, w, h for a text; x1, y1, x2, y2 for a line; and so on; an empty list for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: ValueOf
methods.brief: Returns the solved value of any name the picture holds: an unknown, a constant or a derived one.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name, such as A.icon.cx

notes: a name the picture does not hold gave 0 (A.cx on a picture that holds A.icon.cx)

methods.name: Shapes
methods.brief: Returns the path of every shape, in the order the rules made them.
methods.returns: a list of text such as A.icon, A.text

methods.name: NumberOfShapes
methods.brief: Returns how many shapes the picture holds.

methods.name: DrawIndexOf
methods.brief: Returns the place of a shape in the drawing order, 1 being painted first and so at the back.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape, as Shapes lists them

methods.returns: a number; 0 for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: PolygonOf
methods.brief: Returns the vertices of a polygon, or the control points of a spline, in order.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a polygon or spline shape

methods.returns: a list of numbers [ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... ]; empty for any other shape

methods.name: SplinePointsOf
methods.brief: Returns the polyline a spline is drawn as, in pixels, from a centripetal Catmull-Rom curve through its control points.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a spline shape

methods.returns: a list of numbers [ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... ]; empty for any shape that is not a spline
notes: twelve samples per span unless the shape says otherwise

methods.name: CurvePointsOf
methods.brief: Returns the polyline a geodesic curve is drawn as, in pixels.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a curve shape

methods.returns: a list of numbers [ x1, y1, x2, y2, ... ]; empty for any shape that is not a curve

methods.name: MarkStrokesOf
methods.brief: Returns the strokes a mark such as a right-angle sign is drawn as.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of a mark shape

methods.returns: a list of polylines, each a flat list of numbers; empty for any shape that is not a mark

methods.name: ToCanvas
methods.brief: Draws the picture on a new canvas, in drawing order, and returns it.
methods.returns: a stzCanvas holding an engine scene
notes: call Free on the canvas when done with it; ToSVG and ToPNG do so for you

methods.name: ToSVG
methods.brief: Returns the picture as the text of an SVG document.

methods.name: Rendition
methods.brief: Returns the picture as a vector rendition: a value that says what it is and carries the SVG.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, mime, content, locator, title

methods.name: RenditionKinds
methods.brief: Returns the ways the picture can show itself.
methods.returns: a list of symbols: vector, image, graph, text

methods.name: RenditionAs
methods.brief: Returns the picture as a rendition of the kind asked: its SVG, a PNG file, the graph behind it, or the sentence saying why it is as it is.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: vector, image, graph or text

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, mime, content, locator, title
notes: the graph kind carries Graphviz text, the text kind carries Why
warnings: an unknown kind raises an error naming the four; the image kind writes a file called rendition_ then the domain name in the current folder, which was read from the code and not run, so use RenditionAsXT to choose the path

extensions.name: RenditionAsXT
extensions.adds: the extended form: more parameters than the base method

methods.name: Substance
methods.brief: Returns the substance the picture is about.
notes: Ring copies an object on assignment, so changing the answer does not change the picture; SetSubstanceData does

methods.name: ToPNG
methods.brief: Draws the picture, writes it to a PNG file and returns the PNG bytes.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the file to write, as text

methods.returns: a text holding the bytes of the PNG, which begin with the PNG signature
notes: the file is overwritten

methods.name: Fact
methods.brief: Answers one question about the picture, in the shape a caption can quote: a kind, a subject, a value, a unit and a message.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: expr, value, distance, angle, datum, position, count, tapenodes, arg, term or verdict

parameters.name: paArgs
parameters.role: a list of the arguments the kind needs, such as [ "A.icon", "B.icon" ] for distance, or [ "shapes" ] for count

methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: kind, subject, value, unit, where, message
notes: the angle is read at the second point; tapenodes takes an expression, shared or unshared, and its variable names as the third argument; value, expr and distance are in pixels
warnings: an unknown kind raises an error naming the eleven, a datum the substance does not carry raises an error, and a kind asked without the argument it needs raises an error such as value needs argument 1; paArgs given as a bare text and not as a list raises the error R21 (tried with value and with count), so write [ "shapes" ]

methods.name: ConstraintText
methods.brief: Returns the text of a rule as the solver was handed it, chosen by words from the rule's own line.

parameters.name: pcMatch
parameters.role: words that all appear in the rule's line, such as lessthan v000

notes: the first rule matching every word is taken
warnings: a phrase that matches no rule raises an error saying a rule is addressed by words from its own line

methods.name: SetPictureTheme
methods.brief: Changes the theme the picture is coloured in, such as dark or light, without solving it again.

parameters.name: pcTheme
parameters.role: the theme name, such as dark or light

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the paper changed from #FFFFFF to #333333 with dark; a colour the style gave as a literal does not change

methods.name: SetSubstanceData
methods.brief: Changes a number the substance carries about one object, and marks the picture to be solved again.

parameters.name: pcObject
parameters.role: the name of the object

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the name of the datum

parameters.name: pnValue
parameters.role: the new number

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the marks the picture carried are dropped

methods.name: SetWindow
methods.brief: Shows only a part of the picture, a window centred on a point, scaled up to the paper.

parameters.name: pnCx
parameters.role: the x of the window's centre, in pixels

parameters.name: pnCy
parameters.role: the y of the window's centre, in pixels

parameters.name: pnW
parameters.role: the width of the window, in pixels

parameters.name: pnH
parameters.role: the height of the window, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the facts keep reading the whole figure's own coordinates; names keep their size
warnings: a width or height that is not positive raises an error

extensions.name: SetWindowQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: WindowOn
methods.brief: Shows a window centred on a shape, with a reach around it.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape to centre on

parameters.name: pnReach
parameters.role: the half size of the window, in pixels

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: WindowOnQ is the same call

extensions.name: WindowOnQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: ClearWindow
methods.brief: Shows the whole picture again.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain

methods.name: HasWindow
methods.brief: TRUE if the picture shows only a window of itself.

methods.name: Window
methods.brief: Returns the window shown.
methods.returns: a list [ cx, cy, w, h ]; an empty list when the whole picture shows

methods.name: WindowScale
methods.brief: Returns how much bigger the view is than the figure.
methods.returns: a number; 1 when there is no window
notes: a window of 180 pixels on the 800 by 700 paper gave 3.89

methods.name: IsInWindow
methods.brief: TRUE if any part of the shape falls in the window shown.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; TRUE when there is no window

methods.name: VisibleShapes
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the shapes a reader can see: not hidden and in the window.
methods.returns: a list of text, in drawing order

methods.name: Emphasis
methods.brief: Changes how one shape reads: focus gives it a heavy stroke, dim fades it, ring draws a circle around it.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the path of the shape

parameters.name: pcMode
parameters.role: focus, dim or ring

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: only ring adds a shape, and it is counted in Marks
warnings: any other mode raises an error naming the three

methods.name: Measure
methods.brief: Draws a line between the centres of two shapes with the distance written beside it.

parameters.name: pcA
parameters.role: the path of the first shape

parameters.name: pcB
parameters.role: the path of the second shape

parameters.name: paOpts
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: stroke, text with {value} and {unit} holes, size

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the number is the picture's own distance fact; the label is solved off the other ink; the two-set picture gave 79.68 px between A and B

methods.name: Callout
methods.brief: Writes a sentence near a shape and joins them with a leader line.

parameters.name: pcTarget
parameters.role: the path of the shape

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the sentence, which may hold {value}, {unit}, {message} and {subject} holes

parameters.name: paOpts
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: fact and args to fill the holes from a fact, size

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: a hole other than those four stays in the text as written

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Draws the boundary a rule only states: the circle of a leash or of a clearance around a circle.

parameters.name: pcRuleMatch
parameters.role: words that all appear in the rule's line, such as lessthan v000

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the circle is a mark, counted in Marks
warnings: a rule whose boundary is not such a circle raises an error saying so, and so does a phrase that matches no rule (tried with greaterthan)

methods.name: Region
methods.brief: Tints the area a clearance rule forbids: the strip around a line or the disc around a circle.

parameters.name: pcRuleMatch
parameters.role: words that all appear in the rule's line, such as disjoint ABC.lc

methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the area is a mark, counted in Marks
warnings: a rule that is not a disjoint rule raises an error saying it encloses no area (tried with greaterthan), and so does a disjoint rule whose subject is neither a line nor a circle

methods.name: Marks
methods.brief: Returns what the picture carries that a mark added, as [ path, kind ] pairs.
methods.returns: a list of pairs; empty when no mark was added

methods.name: NumberOfMarks
methods.brief: Returns how many shapes marks added.

methods.name: ClearMarks
methods.brief: Removes every shape the marks added.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: focus and dim rewrite the stroke of the shape and are not undone by it: after Emphasis A focus and ClearMarks the stroke of A was still heavy (width 3, tried once)

methods.name: FillOf
methods.brief: Returns the colour a shape is filled with, after its rule is resolved.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape

methods.returns: a text, a hex colour or a colour name; an empty text for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: StrokeOf
methods.brief: Returns the colour a shape's outline is drawn with, after its rule is resolved.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the shape

methods.returns: a text, a hex colour; an empty text for a path that is not a shape

methods.name: Background
methods.brief: Returns the colour of the paper in the theme now set.

methods.name: MatchCandidates
methods.brief: Returns how many candidate bindings the last compile tried when matching the rules to the objects.
notes: a count and not a clock, so it is the same on every run

methods.name: StartsTried
methods.brief: Returns how many starting layouts the last solve tried.

methods.name: AdvisoryUnmet
methods.brief: Returns how many crossing rules were left unmet when the start was not planar and the rule was therefore advice.
methods.returns: a number; 0 for a planar start and for a picture with no crossing rule

methods.name: StartUsed
methods.brief: Returns the kind of start the last layout began from.

methods.name: StartedPlanar
methods.brief: TRUE if the last layout began from a planar embedding of the graph.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the style asked for none or the graph could not give one

methods.name: OuterFace
methods.brief: Returns the face the planar start was built on, as object names in cycle order.
methods.returns: a list of text; empty when there was no planar start
notes: the cube Q3 gave [ v001, v011, v010, v000 ]

methods.name: Touch
methods.brief: Forgets the cached values, colours, ink and names, so the next question reads the picture afresh.
methods.returns: the diagram itself, so calls chain
notes: the picture is not solved again; the setters that change colours call it for you

methods.name: Ink
methods.brief: Returns every stroke drawn as a segment with its owner.
methods.returns: a list of [ x1, y1, x2, y2, owner, path ] rows
notes: kept once per solve

methods.name: Texts
methods.brief: Returns the paths of the names drawn: the visible text shapes that say something.

classes.name: stzMathDomain
classes.brief: Declares the vocabulary of a field of mathematics: its types, the predicates over them and the functions between them.
classes.description: A domain says what can be said, and a substance says it. Types may be kinds of other types (Hydrogen of Atom), and an object of a kind matches wherever its parent is asked for, at any depth. A predicate has argument types, and may be symmetric when its two arguments are of one type. A function, or a constructor whose name is its output type, maps typed arguments to a typed result. Every name check ignores case, and every declaration that names an undeclared type raises an error. Ready-made domains: StzSetTheoryDomain, StzLinearAlgebraDomain, StzGeometryDomain, StzGraphDomain and others. Picture: a rule over Atom drew two Hydrogen and one Helium alike, the bonded pair side by side and the Helium apart (domain_atoms.png in the wave scratch folder).
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzMathDomain("molecules"); o1.AddType("Atom"); o1.AddSubtype("Hydrogen", "Atom"); o1.AddSymmetricPredicate("Bonded", [ "Atom", "Atom" ])

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty vocabulary for a field of mathematics: no type, no predicate and no function yet.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the domain's name

methods.name: Name_
methods.brief: Returns the domain's name, trimmed and in lower case.

methods.name: AddType
methods.brief: Declares a type of object, such as Set or Atom, and returns the domain so calls chain.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the type's name, which must not be empty or already declared in any case

methods.returns: the domain itself, so calls chain
notes: AddTypeQ is the same call
warnings: an empty name or a type declared twice raises an error

extensions.name: AddTypeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddSubtype
methods.brief: Declares a type that is a kind of an earlier one, so that wherever the earlier is expected the new one is accepted.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the new type's name

parameters.name: pcSuper
parameters.role: the type it is a kind of, which must be declared already, else an error is raised

methods.returns: the domain itself, so calls chain
notes: Hydrogen is declared a kind of Atom, so a rule over Atom draws a Hydrogen
warnings: the subtype can itself be the super of another, to any depth

extensions.name: AddSubtypeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasType
methods.brief: TRUE if the domain declares a type, in any case.

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the type's name

notes: ATOM finds Atom

methods.name: Types
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared types, as written, in the order declared.
notes: subtypes are in the same list

methods.name: TypeMatches
methods.brief: TRUE if an object of one type may stand where another type is asked for: the same type, or a kind of it at any depth.

parameters.name: pcActual
parameters.role: the type of the object

parameters.name: pcWanted
parameters.role: the type that is asked for

notes: Hydrogen matches Atom, Atom does not match Hydrogen, and two kinds of Atom do not match each other

methods.name: AddPredicate
methods.brief: Declares a relation over objects of given types, such as Subset over two Sets.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the predicate's name, not empty and not declared already

parameters.name: pacArgTypes
parameters.role: the types of its arguments in order, or one type name for a one-argument predicate

methods.returns: the domain itself, so calls chain
notes: the number of types is the arity, so Joins over Bond, Atom, Atom has arity 3
warnings: a name declared twice raises an error

extensions.name: AddPredicateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: AddSymmetricPredicate
methods.brief: Declares a two-argument relation whose arguments may be swapped, such as Disjoint.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the predicate's name

parameters.name: pacArgTypes
parameters.role: exactly two types, both the same

methods.returns: the domain itself, so calls chain
notes: the substance's Holds then answers TRUE for either order
warnings: one type, or two different types, raises an error

extensions.name: AddSymmetricPredicateQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: HasPredicate
methods.brief: TRUE if the domain declares a predicate, in any case.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the predicate's name

methods.name: PredicateArity
methods.brief: Returns how many arguments a predicate takes.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the predicate's name, in any case

methods.returns: a number; -1 for a predicate the domain does not have

methods.name: IsSymmetric
methods.brief: TRUE if the predicate was declared symmetric.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the predicate's name, in any case

methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE for a predicate the domain does not have

methods.name: Predicates
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared predicates, as written, in the order declared.

methods.name: AddFunction

classes.name: stzMathFigure
classes.brief: Declares a mathematical figure by its kind and keys, solves its picture, and answers for it: its sentence, its facts, its SVG and PNG.
classes.description: A figure is declared (a kind such as function, numberline, fraction, matrix, complexplane, boxplot, surface, stemplot, residualplot or codedtable, and its keys), computed (the engine samples or tabulates it), then solved (the diagram engine places every name). It is already solved when built. Ring hands back a copy of any object a method returns, so Diagram and Substance are copies: change the figure through SetTheme and SetDatum, never through them. The readers for samples, pieces, window and marks belong to the function kind only.

methods.name: init

methods.brief: the live samples in the author's units, for a check: [ [ x, y ], ... ]

methods.brief: a frame, offscreen: the same composition the window shows -------------- a fresh canvas with the settled picture and the live curve on it; the caller frees it.
methods.detail: The overlay path of the window draws the two as separate layers; here they are one canvas, since a saved frame is one picture.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: A file or folder path, as text.

methods.brief: the window loop ---------------------------------------------------------- THE PLAYER: the settled picture retained in one canvas, the live curve redrawn each frame in an overlay; the first parameter on left/right, the second on up/down, a hundredth of its range per frame held; the picture settles when no key is held and something moved.
methods.detail: Escape closes.

methods.name: State
methods.brief: declared STATES ---------------------------------------------------------- A STATE is a caption and the acts that reach it from the state before.
methods.detail: An act is a list led by its verb: [ :DragTo,   "A.icon", x, y ]      a free shape to a place [ :DragBy,   "A.icon", dx, dy ]    the same, from where it stands [ :SetData,  "fr", "ymax", 2 ]     a datum into the substance [ :SetTheme, "dark" ]              the picture's theme [ :Set,      "a", 2 ]              a parameter (a :Function motion) A state with no act is the picture as it stands -- the opening frame.

methods.name: Apply
methods.brief: THE LIVE PASS: the acts of one state, on the motion's own picture.
methods.detail: States are steps, so state n is reached from state n-1; a caller that jumps is asking for the acts of n from wherever the picture stands, which is what it gets and what Applied() then says.

methods.name: ExportTo

methods.detail: The storyboard takes its own copy of the picture from where it stands now, replays each state's acts on that copy through its own Act (so the frame it closes is the picture AFTER the acts), binds each fact to be computed on that frame, writes the frame as a PNG in the folio, and the narration beside them. A :Function motion settles per state and hands each settled figure in as a frame; its parameters are put back afterwards, so the export leaves the motion where it found it in both cases.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: A name, as text.
