methods.detail: A :Function motion drawn live composes its frame, any other draws its picture as it stands.

classes.name: stzMathStyle
classes.brief: Turns a substance into a picture by rules: which shapes each object gets and which constraints each relation imposes.
classes.description: A style is data. ForAll adds a rule for every object (or every pair) the selector names, ForAllWhere only where a relation holds, and each row is a shape to draw, a variable for the solver to own, a field or override, a constraint (ensure) or an objective (encourage), or a layer order. Colours are roles that the theme resolves. The canvas, the margin, the start placements the solver tries and the label order are settings of the style. Rows are checked when added, so a mistake is refused at its line. Known defect: StartTrying given one mode as text, not in a list, raises error R21. Picture: the Euler style under the dark theme with a margin drew a large disk A holding a smaller B near its lower edge and a separate C, light strokes and white names on a dark paper (style_euler_dark.png).

classes.name: stzMathSubstance
classes.brief: Holds the content of a mathematical diagram: named objects of the domain's types, relations between them, definitions, data and labels.
classes.description: A substance is written in one domain, and every statement is checked against it when it is made: an object of an unknown type, a relation with the wrong arguments or a function of the wrong arity is refused at the line that made it. Names are case sensitive and head every path a style writes. Define declares an object as a function's result, SetData puts a number on an object for a style to read, Label and AutoLabelAll set what is written, and ToGraph reads the substance as a stzGraph. Known defect: SetData and SetDataFrom on an object that is not declared raise no error and the number is lost. Picture: a 3 by 4 table of products drawn as a heat map from numbers set on its cells, paler for 1 and deeper indigo for 12, digits legible on every cell (substance_heat.png).

classes.name: stzMatrex
classes.brief: Tests whether a matrix of numbers fits a pattern written in a small regex-like language, such as {size(3x3) & property(symmetric)}.
classes.description: A pattern is text in braces made of terms: size, shape, element, property, row, col, diagonal, pattern, determinant and sum, written like size(3x3) or element(0..10). Terms are joined by & (all must hold), | (one must hold) and -> (a sequence, all must hold), @! negates a term, and parentheses group. Match tests one matrix and, on success, records its size, properties and matrix as the matched parts; MatchingMatrices, CountMatchingMatrices and the other list methods test a whole list. SimilarityScore, MostSimilarMatrix and CommonProperties compare matrices. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: the terms row, col, pattern, determinant and sum accept every matrix and diagonal every square one, size(<n), size(>n) and sizes with m or n in place of a number accept every matrix, quantifiers are parsed but never applied, MatchesNone answers the opposite of its name, Not_ negates only the first term, Andd and the JSON methods raise errors, and CommonProperties never reports square.

classes.name: stzMatrix
classes.brief: Holds a rectangle of numbers and edits it in place, searches it, and answers linear-algebra questions such as determinant, inverse, rank and eigenvalues.
classes.description: A stzMatrix is a list of rows of numbers, all of the same length, or a zero matrix built from a [ rows, columns ] pair. Positions are [ row, column ] and start at 1. Methods that add, multiply, replace or transpose change the matrix itself and answer nothing; methods that ask a question (Sum, Rank, Determinant, Inverse, SVD, the matrix functions such as MatrixExp) answer a plain Ring list or number and leave the matrix alone, and their Q forms wrap the answer in a stzMatrix. The heavy numeric work runs in the Softanza engine. Power raises every element to a power, while MatrixPower and GeneralPower raise the matrix itself. Several decompositions refuse what has no real answer (a singular matrix has no logarithm, a defective one no full set of eigenvectors) with an error rather than a wrong number. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: Section reads its corners as [ column, row ] and FindElementsInSection returns [ column, row ] pairs, so ReplaceSection changes the wrong cells on a non-square rectangle; MultiplyByInRow scales a column; Add given a matrix adds it and then raises; Diagonal1 answers nothing.

notes: [ [ 1, 1 ], [ 0, 1 ] ] is defective
warnings: raises an error unless the matrix is square

methods.name: IsDiagonalizable
methods.brief: TRUE if the matrix has a full set of independent eigenvectors.
notes: the opposite of IsDefective
warnings: raises an error unless the matrix is square

methods.name: EigenVectors
methods.brief: Returns the unit eigenvectors as the columns of a matrix, in the same order as the eigenvalues.
methods.returns: a list of rows; column j is the eigenvector of eigenvalue j
notes: orthonormal for a symmetric matrix
warnings: raises an error unless the matrix is square, for a defective matrix, and when an eigenvector is complex

methods.name: IsSymmetric
methods.brief: TRUE if the matrix equals its transpose within a relative tolerance of one part in 10^12.
notes: a matrix that is not square answers FALSE

methods.name: ConditionNumber
methods.brief: Returns the ratio of the largest to the smallest singular value, a measure of how much a solve can lose; infinite when singular.
methods.returns: a number, inf for a singular matrix
notes: works for any shape; 10^k costs about k digits

methods.name: SVD
methods.brief: Returns the singular value decomposition A = U S V' as a hash of three parts.
methods.returns: a hash with the keys u, singularValues and v: u and v are lists of rows with one column per singular value
notes: singular values come back non-negative and in descending order
warnings: raises an error when the sweeps do not converge

methods.name: LeftSingularVectors
methods.brief: Returns the left singular vectors, one per column, an orthonormal basis of the column space.
notes: ordered by the size of the singular value

methods.name: RightSingularVectors
methods.brief: Returns the right singular vectors, one per column, an orthonormal basis of the row space.
notes: ordered by the size of the singular value

methods.name: SingularValues
methods.brief: Returns the singular values, never negative, largest first.
methods.returns: a list of min(rows, columns) numbers
notes: works for any shape

methods.name: Rank
methods.brief: Returns the number of singular values that are not negligible next to the largest.
notes: works for any shape; an all-zero matrix has rank 0

methods.name: IsSingular
methods.brief: TRUE if the rank is smaller than the number of columns, so the columns are dependent.
notes: for a wide matrix it is always TRUE, because the rank cannot exceed the row count; the IsRankDeficient form answers the same

methods.name: IsFullRank
methods.brief: TRUE if the rank equals the number of columns.
notes: for a wide matrix it is always FALSE

methods.name: IsPositiveDefinite
methods.brief: TRUE if the matrix is symmetric with only positive eigenvalues, tested by attempting its Cholesky factor.
notes: a matrix that is not square answers FALSE

methods.name: Inverse
methods.brief: Returns the inverse of a square matrix as a list of rows, leaving the matrix itself unchanged.
methods.returns: a list of rows, the same size as the matrix
notes: the Inverted form answers the same and the InverseQ form returns a stzMatrix
warnings: raises an error unless the matrix is square, and when it is singular

extensions.name: InverseQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: InvertedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Invert
methods.brief: Replaces this matrix by its inverse, changing it in place.
methods.returns: nothing; the matrix changes in place
notes: the verb that changes the matrix, where Inverse hands back the answer
warnings: raises an error unless the matrix is square, and when it is singular

extensions.name: InvertQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Transpose
methods.brief: Swaps rows and columns, so a 2x3 matrix becomes 3x2, changing the matrix in place.
methods.returns: nothing; the matrix changes in place
notes: the TransposeQ form returns the matrix itself for chaining

extensions.name: TransposeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Transposed
methods.brief: Returns the transposed rows as a list, leaving this matrix unchanged.
methods.returns: a list of rows, columns by rows
notes: the TransposedQ form returns a stzMatrix

extensions.name: TransposedQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Diff
methods.brief: Returns the differences between neighbouring elements of each row, a list of rows one column shorter.
methods.returns: a list of rows with one fewer column
notes: the matrix is not changed; a 3x3 gives 3x2

methods.name: SubMean
methods.brief: Subtracts the mean of its row from every element, changing the matrix in place so each row sums to zero.
methods.returns: nothing; the matrix changes in place
notes: the SubMeanQ form returns the matrix itself for chaining

extensions.name: SubMeanQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: SubtractMean
methods.brief: Subtracts the mean of its row from every element, changing the matrix in place so each row sums to zero.
methods.returns: nothing; the matrix changes in place
notes: the same as SubMean

extensions.name: SubtractMeanQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the matrix to the console as a bordered grid of right-aligned numbers, without trailing zeros.
notes: the matrix is not changed; an empty matrix prints an empty frame
warnings: seen in the gallery: a cell holding 0.001 prints as 0, the same as a true zero, because Show uses Ring's global decimals() (2 by default); the data is intact

methods.name: Shwo
methods.brief: Prints the matrix as a bordered grid, the misspelt twin of Show.
notes: the misspelling is in the name as shipped

classes.name: stzMBarPlot
classes.brief: Draws several series of numbers over the same categories as grouped bars, with a legend.
classes.description: The data is a hash list of series, each series a hash list of category = number pairs, such as :Sales = [ :Q1 = 25, :Q2 = 35 ]. Categories come from the first series. ToString draws one cluster of bars per category with a different character for each series and a legend line; ToSVG and ToPNG draw coloured bars and a legend, with no values above the bars. It inherits the axis, label and size settings of stzBarPlot. The average line raises an error in every form, SetLegendLayout is obeyed only by ToStringInRing, and AddValues draws nothing in the text picture; see the warnings. Gallery: doc/gallery/stzMBarPlot/quarters.png (three series over four quarters), seen right by stzlib-docs visual pass (a model reading the PNG), 2026-10-05, not a person; twoseries.png (two series over six months), seen uncertain by the same pass because the legend touches the last bar; terminal.txt is the text picture, read as text and judged right. The pixel labels are in lower case, the text ones capitalised.

parameters.name: paMultiSeriesData

notes: a series that is not a hash list raises "Each series must be a hashlist of category:value pairs" and a negative or non-number value raises "All values must be positive numbers"

notes: the legend is always drawn, no values are written above the bars, and :ShowAverage = 1 adds an average line that the text picture cannot
warnings: Only the series names, the categories and the values carry over to pixels, so the legend switch, the bar characters, the spacing and the sizes set on this object do not

parameters.name: n

parameters.name: n

methods.name: SetBarSpace

classes.name: stzMemoryBlobStore
classes.brief: Stores binary objects by key in memory, with the same four verbs as the file store; it is gone when the process ends.
classes.description: It is a real store for the length of the process, and the service registry reports it as ephemeral so that a production check can refuse it. Keys follow the same rules as the file store: exact comparison, 1024 bytes at most, never empty. Each instance keeps its own objects.
classes.example:
o1.Save("a/1", "abc")
o1.Save("a/2", "de")
o1.Save("b/1", "f")
? o1.TotalBytes()
#--> 6
? @@( o1.KeysWithPrefix("a/") )
#--> [ "a/1", "a/2" ]
? o1.IsEphemeral()
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty store that holds its objects in memory, numbered so that each store keeps its own.
notes: two stores never see each other's objects

methods.name: IsLocalReal
methods.brief: TRUE if the store is a genuine local equivalent of a real object store rather than a fake.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; always TRUE for this class

methods.name: IsEphemeral
methods.brief: TRUE if the stored objects vanish when the process ends.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; always TRUE for this class, which is why a production check flags it

methods.name: Save
methods.brief: Stores bytes under an object key, replacing the object when the key already exists.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key, any text up to 1024 bytes

parameters.name: pcBytes
parameters.role: the content to store, as text

notes: SaveQ is the same call and returns the store; keys are compared exactly: "photo.jpg" and "Photo.JPG" are two objects
warnings: an empty key and a key over 1024 bytes raise an error

extensions.name: SaveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Fetch
methods.brief: Returns the bytes stored under a key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to read

methods.returns: a text; the empty text when the key is absent, which Exists tells apart from a stored empty object
warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if an object is stored under the key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to look for

warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Remove
methods.brief: Deletes the object stored under a key; deleting an absent key also succeeds, as an S3 DELETE does.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to delete

warnings: an empty key raises an error

extensions.name: RemoveQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Size
methods.brief: Returns the number of bytes stored under a key.

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the object key to measure

methods.returns: a number; 0 when the key is absent
warnings: an empty key raises an error

methods.name: Keys
methods.brief: Returns the keys of the stored objects.
methods.returns: a list of text, in the order saved

methods.name: KeysWithPrefix
methods.brief: Returns the keys that begin with a prefix, the way an S3 listing by prefix does.

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the beginning the keys must have, compared with case

methods.returns: a list of text, in the order saved; [ ] when none matches

methods.name: NumberOfBlobs
methods.brief: Returns how many objects the store holds.

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if the store holds no object.

methods.name: TotalBytes
methods.brief: Returns the sum of the sizes of all stored objects, in bytes.

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Deletes every object of this store, leaving other stores alone.

extensions.name: ClearQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints a one-line summary: how many objects and how many bytes, marked EPHEMERAL.

methods.brief: pWhat is :Cube / :Sphere / :Plane, or a list: [ :Cube, nSize ]   [ :Sphere, nRadius, nSegments, nRings ] [ :Plane, nSize ]  [ :Obj, cObjText ] [ :Custom, aComponentCounts, aVertices, aIndices ]

methods.name: IsAlive
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is alive.

methods.name: Stride
methods.brief: Floats per vertex.

methods.name: Format

classes.name: stzMetric
classes.brief: Holds one named series of measurements, a counter, a gauge or a timer, and answers the questions that its kind allows.
classes.description: The kind is fixed at birth. A counter counts events (Increment, IncrementBy, Value, RatePerSecond); a gauge holds a sampled level (Set, Mean, Min, Max, SlopePerMs); a timer records durations in milliseconds (Record, RecordWatch, then P50, P95 and P99 from a bucketed histogram, ExactPercentile over the recent samples, and an exact SumMs and MeanMs). A call that belongs to another kind raises an error that names the right kind. The samples are kept in the engine, so a copy of a metric is a second face on the same samples: recording through either is read through both. PromText and OtelMetricJson render the metric in the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry formats. Free a metric with Destroy when done. Readings that depend on the clock, such as RatePerSecond and SlopePerMs, should be tested with ranges and signs, not exact values.
classes.example:
o1.Record(5).Record(15).Record(25)
? o1.Count()
#--> 3
? o1.SumMs()
#--> 45
? o1.MeanMs()
#--> 15
? o1.ExactPercentile(50)
#--> 15
? o1.P50()
#--> 20
o2 = StzMetric("app.requests", :Counter)
o2.Increment().IncrementBy(4)
? o2.Value()
#--> 5
? o2.RatePerSecond() >= 0
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named metric of one kind, :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer, whose samples live in the engine; any other kind raises an error.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the metric's name, such as app.requests

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: the kind: :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer, matched without regard to case

notes: StzMetric(name, kind) is the usual way to build one; a copy of a metric shares the same samples
warnings: a kind that is not one of the three raises stzMetric: kind must be :Counter, :Gauge or :Timer

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the metric's name as given.

methods.name: Kind
methods.brief: Returns the metric's kind, in lower case.
methods.returns: the text counter, gauge or timer

methods.name: IsCounter
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric counts events.

methods.name: IsGauge
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric holds a sampled level.

methods.name: IsTimer
methods.brief: TRUE if the metric records durations.

methods.name: SetHelp
methods.brief: Sets the description that the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry outputs carry, and returns the metric.

parameters.name: pcText
parameters.role: the description, as text

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Help
methods.brief: Returns the description set with SetHelp.
methods.returns: a text; empty until one is set

methods.name: LabelPairs
methods.brief: Returns the label pairs of a metric that is a child of a family.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs; an empty list for a metric made on its own

methods.name: Increment
methods.brief: Adds one to a counter and returns the metric.
methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: each call is one sample on the counter's timeline
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: IncrementBy
methods.brief: Adds a number to a counter and returns the metric.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: how much to add

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: RatePerSecond
methods.brief: Returns the counter's events per second over the retained samples, read from the slope of its own timeline.
methods.returns: a number, 0 or more; it depends on the clock, so test it with a range
notes: the rate is measured, never configured
warnings: a gauge or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the counter kind

methods.name: Set
methods.brief: Records a level on a gauge and returns the metric.

parameters.name: nValue
parameters.role: the level to record

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: RecordGauge is the same call
warnings: a counter or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the gauge kind

methods.name: SlopePerMs
methods.brief: Returns the trend of a gauge, in units per millisecond, over the retained samples.
methods.returns: a number; positive for a rising gauge, negative for a falling one
notes: it depends on the clock, so test its sign, not its value
warnings: a counter or a timer raises an error saying the call belongs to the gauge kind

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: Returns the mean of the retained samples of a gauge or a timer.
notes: a timer's lifetime mean is MeanMs
warnings: a counter raises an error and points to RatePerSecond

methods.name: Min
methods.brief: Returns the smallest retained sample.

methods.name: Max
methods.brief: Returns the largest retained sample.

methods.name: Record
methods.brief: Records a duration on a timer in milliseconds and returns the metric; on a gauge it records a level, as Set does.

parameters.name: nMs
parameters.role: the duration in milliseconds

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
warnings: a counter raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: RecordWatch
methods.brief: Records the reading of a stopwatch, running or stopped, as one duration and returns the metric.

parameters.name: poStopwatch
parameters.role: a stzStopwatch, as StzStopwatch() builds it

methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain

methods.name: P50
methods.brief: Returns the median duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
notes: with the samples 5, 15 and 25 it gave 20; ExactPercentile gives 15
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: P95
methods.brief: Returns the 95th percentile duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: P99
methods.brief: Returns the 99th percentile duration of a timer as the upper bound of its histogram bucket.
methods.returns: a number in milliseconds, rounded up to a bucket bound
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: ExactPercentile
methods.brief: Returns the percentile of the recent samples of a timer, computed by sorting them, with no bucket rounding.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentile, from 0 to 100

notes: only the last 1024 samples are kept
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: SumMs
methods.brief: Returns the total of all the durations recorded on a timer since it was built.
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: MeanMs
methods.brief: Returns the exact mean of all the durations recorded on a timer, and 0 before any.
notes: the sum is kept exactly; only the buckets are rounded
warnings: a counter or a gauge raises an error saying the call belongs to the timer kind

methods.name: Value
methods.brief: Returns the metric's current reading: a counter's total, a gauge's level, or a timer's last duration.
notes: Last is the same call

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many samples were recorded on the metric.

methods.name: SeriesQ
methods.brief: Returns the series object that holds the metric's recent samples.

methods.name: Percentile
methods.brief: Returns the percentile of the recent samples, whatever the kind.

parameters.name: nP
parameters.role: the percentile, from 0 to 100

warnings: for a timer it is the same as ExactPercentile

methods.name: PromName
methods.brief: Returns the name in the Prometheus vocabulary, with dots and dashes folded to underscores.

methods.name: PromText
methods.brief: Returns the metric in the Prometheus exposition format: help line, type line and samples; a counter gets _total.
notes: a timer gives the quantiles 0.5, 0.95 and 0.99, then _sum and _count

methods.name: OtelMetricJson
methods.brief: Returns one OpenTelemetry metric as JSON text: a sum for a counter, a gauge, or a summary for a timer.
notes: the time stamp in it is the wall clock, so compare the rest

methods.name: Explain
methods.brief: Returns the metric's state as a list of plain lines: its total or level, its rate or trend, and its percentiles.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the lines that Explain returns.
methods.returns: nothing; it writes to the console

methods.name: Destroy
methods.brief: Frees the engine handles of the metric and returns it; a later call builds fresh, empty ones.
methods.returns: the metric itself, so calls chain
notes: free every metric when done, since the engine holds the samples

classes.name: stzMultiObjectiveSolver
classes.brief: Looks for trade-offs between several objectives at once: a front of solutions none of which beats another on every objective.
classes.description: Declare variables and bounds, add two or more objectives with maximize and minimize (each call appends one), then call solve with nsga_ii, a seeded genetic search, or epsilon_constraint, which bounds the secondary objectives and solves for the first. The search is deterministic: the same seed gives the same front, and SetSeed changes it. NSGA-II refuses a problem that has constraints, and the epsilon-constraint method is only a rough tool today: its greedy sub-solver reads a lower bound as an upper bound, so the front repeats the same few points. exportParetoFrontCSV raises R41. Objective values of a maximize goal are stored negated, so smaller is always better inside the individuals.
classes.example:
o1.addVariable("x", 0, 10)
o1.maximize("x")
o1.maximize("-x")
o1.setNSGAParameters(8, 3, 0.1, 0.9)
o1.solve("nsga_ii")
? len(o1.paretoSolutions())
#--> 8
? o1.status()
#--> optimal
? o1.dominates([ :objectives = [ -2, -2 ] ], [ :objectives = [ -1, -1 ] ])
#--> 1

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty multi-objective problem, with no variable, constraint or objective and the generator seed set to 42.

methods.name: clear
methods.brief: Empties the problem: variables, constraints, objectives, the front found so far and the status are dropped, and the seed returns to 42.
methods.returns: nothing; the problem is empty again
notes: the NSGA-II settings made with setNSGAParameters are kept

methods.name: addVariable
methods.brief: Adds a continuous variable with a lower and an upper bound, in declaration order.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: lowerBound
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: upperBound
parameters.role: the largest value it may take, never below the lower bound

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: all three arguments must be given (R19 otherwise); a name that is not text, bounds that are not numbers and an upper bound below the lower bound each raise an error

methods.name: addIntegerVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable marked integer, with the same arguments and checks as a continuous one.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

parameters.name: lowerBound
parameters.role: the smallest value the variable may take

parameters.name: upperBound
parameters.role: the largest value it may take

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: the genetic search floors the values it draws for such a variable, but the epsilon-constraint method does not enforce the mark

methods.name: addBinaryVariable
methods.brief: Adds a variable bounded between 0 and 1 and marked binary.

parameters.name: varName
parameters.role: the variable's name, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Variables
methods.brief: Returns the declared variables in order, each as a list of name, lowerbound, upperbound and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable; [ ] when none is declared
notes: the keys are lower case

methods.name: Vars
methods.brief: Returns the same list of declared variables as the longer accessor does.
methods.returns: a list with one list of [ key, value ] pairs per variable

methods.name: VariableNames
methods.brief: Returns the names of the declared variables, in declaration order.

methods.name: addConstraint
methods.brief: Adds one linear constraint: an expression such as "x + y", a comparison and a number.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the left side, as text

parameters.name: operator
parameters.role: the comparison: "<=", ">=" or "="

parameters.name: value
parameters.role: the number the expression is compared with

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: a value that is not a number, even the text "5", raises an error; the NSGA-II method refuses to run when any constraint exists

methods.name: constraints
methods.brief: Returns the declared constraints in order, each as a list of expression, operator and value pairs.
methods.returns: a list of lists of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: addObjective
methods.brief: Appends one objective: an expression and the goal to maximize or minimize it.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text, such as "3*x + 2*y"

parameters.name: type
parameters.role: the goal: "maximize" or "minimize"

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: an expression that is not text, or any other goal, raises an error

methods.name: maximize
methods.brief: Appends an objective to make as large as possible; earlier objectives are kept.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: unlike the single-objective solver, calling it twice gives two objectives

methods.name: minimize
methods.brief: Appends an objective to make as small as possible; earlier objectives are kept.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.role: the objective, as text

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: objectives
methods.brief: Returns the declared objectives in order, each as a list of expression and type pairs.
methods.returns: a list of lists of [ key, value ] pairs; [ ] when none is declared

methods.name: setNSGAParameters
methods.brief: Sets the population size, the number of generations and the mutation and crossover rates of the genetic search.

parameters.name: populationSize
parameters.role: how many individuals each generation holds, 50 by default

parameters.name: generations
parameters.role: how many generations to breed, 100 by default

parameters.name: mutationRate
parameters.role: the chance, from 0 to 1, that a variable is redrawn, 0.1 by default

parameters.name: crossoverRate
parameters.role: the chance, from 0 to 1, that a child takes a variable from the first parent, 0.9 by default

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
warnings: nothing is checked: any value is stored

methods.name: solve
methods.brief: Finds a set of trade-off solutions with the named method, "nsga_ii" (the default) or "epsilon_constraint", and keeps it.

parameters.name: cMethod
parameters.role: the method's name, an empty text selects nsga_ii

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain
notes: maximize x and maximize -x on 0..10 with 8 individuals and 3 generations gives a front of 8, since no point beats another
warnings: the argument cannot be left out (R19), pass an empty text for the default; no variable, no objective, a single objective or an unknown method raise an error; the status becomes optimal in every case

methods.name: solveWithNSGAII
methods.brief: Returns the non-dominated individuals of a genetic search that breeds a seeded population for the set number of generations.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives, rank, crowdingdistance, dominatedsolutions and dominationcount pairs
notes: the same seed gives the same front (three runs agreed), and another seed gives another; the objectives of a maximize goal are stored negated
warnings: raises an error when the problem has any constraint, because the search does not enforce them; the front can hold several copies of one point; it is approximate

methods.name: solveWithEpsilonConstraint
methods.brief: Returns one solution per combination of bounds on the secondary objectives, each found by the greedy solver on the first objective.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives and rank pairs
notes: the iteration count is set to 10 per objective
warnings: the front collapses: for maximize x and maximize y with x + y <= 10 all eleven solutions are x = 10 and y = 0 (the true trade-off is the line x + y = 10), and with minimize x + y and maximize x - y most solutions repeat, because the greedy solver reads ">=" bounds as "<=" and always raises a variable to its maximum; only the first two secondary objectives are used

methods.name: initializePopulation
methods.brief: Returns the starting population: one random solution per individual, with no objective values yet.
methods.returns: a list of individuals, each a list of solution, objectives, rank and crowdingdistance pairs
notes: rank starts at 0 and objectives is empty

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: Sets the state of the pseudo-random generator that drives the genetic search.

parameters.name: n
parameters.role: the starting state, a positive whole number, zero or less is replaced by 42 when numbers are drawn

methods.returns: the solver itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Seed
methods.brief: Returns the state of the pseudo-random generator, 42 until it is set or numbers are drawn.
notes: the state moves each time a number is drawn, so it differs after a run

methods.name: generateRandomSolution
methods.brief: Returns one random solution within the bounds, whole numbers for integer and binary variables.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs, one per variable
notes: continuous values come in steps of 0.01

methods.name: evaluateObjectives
methods.brief: Returns the value of every objective for a solution, with maximize goals negated so that smaller is always better.

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per objective
notes: x = 3 and y = 4 under maximize x, minimize x + y and maximize y gives -3, 7 and -4

methods.name: calculateObjectiveValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of an expression for a solution.

parameters.name: cExpression
parameters.role: the expression, as text

parameters.name: _aSolution_
parameters.role: a list of [ name, value ] pairs

notes: 3*x + 2*y with x = 3 and y = 4 gives 17

methods.name: nonDominatedSort
methods.brief: Returns the fronts of a population as lists of positions, and writes each individual's rank and domination data into the population itself.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: a list of individuals, each with an objectives list, it is changed in place

methods.returns: a list of fronts, each a list of positions in the population, the last one empty
notes: three individuals with objectives (-1,-1), (-2,-2) and (-3,0) give the fronts [ [ 2, 3 ], [ 1 ], [ ] ] and the ranks 2, 1 and 1

methods.name: dominates
methods.brief: TRUE if the first individual is no worse than the second on every objective and better on at least one.

parameters.name: _individual1_
parameters.role: an individual with an objectives list

parameters.name: _individual2_
parameters.role: an individual with an objectives list

notes: objectives are compared as smaller is better; an individual never dominates itself

methods.name: calculateCrowdingDistance
methods.brief: Returns the population with a crowding distance set on each individual: 999999 at the ends of a front, the spread of its neighbours inside.

parameters.name: _aFronts_
parameters.role: the fronts returned by nonDominatedSort

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the population those fronts index

methods.returns: the population, a list of individuals

methods.name: sortFrontByObjective
methods.brief: Returns the positions of a front ordered from the smallest to the largest value of one objective.

parameters.name: _front_
parameters.role: a list of positions in the population

parameters.name: objIndex
parameters.role: the number of the objective to sort by

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the population the positions index

methods.brief: Returns the next generation: one child per individual of the population size, made by tournament selection, crossover and mutation.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: the current population, each individual with solution and objectives

methods.returns: a list of individuals with no objective values yet
warnings: with fewer than two usable individuals it prints a warning line and returns a fresh random population

methods.brief: Returns the better of two distinct usable individuals drawn at random: the lower rank, or on a tie the larger crowding distance.

parameters.name: _aPopulation_
parameters.role: a list of individuals

methods.returns: an individual; [ ] when fewer than two individuals have a solution and objectives
notes: the draw uses the seeded generator

methods.brief: Returns a child that takes each variable from the first parent with the crossover rate and from the second otherwise.

parameters.name: parent1
parameters.role: an individual with a solution

parameters.name: parent2
parameters.role: an individual with a solution

methods.returns: an individual with a solution, no objectives and rank 0

methods.name: mutate
methods.brief: Returns the individual after redrawing each variable at random between its bounds, with the mutation rate as the chance for each.

parameters.name: individual
parameters.role: an individual with a solution

methods.brief: Returns every combination of eleven evenly spaced bounds for the secondary objectives, for the epsilon-constraint method.
methods.returns: a list of lists of numbers: 11 rows of one bound with two objectives, 121 rows of two bounds with three or more

classes.name: stzNaturalEngine
classes.brief: Reads a narration written in plain words, turns it into Ring code on a text, list or number, runs it and keeps what it understood.
classes.description: Build it with Naturally("..."), NaturallyIn(lang, "...") or NaturallyXT(context, "..."): the narration runs when the engine is built, so Result, Answers and Understood are ready at once. A narration creates an object (Create a string with 'ring'), applies methods (Uppercase it), asks questions (Is it lowercase ?) and may name objects (called basket, Use basket) or keep values (Keep it as sep). Execution is permissive: a word the language does not know degrades to data and is listed by Unresolved; SetStrict(1) turns that into an error, and SetAllowedOperations limits what may be said. A narration that creates no object raises Unsupported object type!. Understood paraphrases the reading back, Analyze checks a narration without running it, and SuggestNext offers the next words. Most roots are the internal steps of Execute (tokenising, resolving words, writing the code); the reader methods are Result, Answers, Understood, Unresolved, Tokens and Values. Only the English pack covers the full lexicon: other languages (ha, ar and more) understand the words of their pack.
classes.receiver: o1 = Naturally("Create a string with 'ring' Uppercase it")
classes.example:
? o1.Result()
#--> RING
? o1.Understood()
#--> create a string with ring -> uppercase
? Naturally("Create a string with 'ring' Is it lowercase ? Does it contain 'g' ?").AllYes()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Analyze("Create a string with 'abc' Flibber it") )
#--> [ [ "understood", 0 ], [ "unresolved", [ [ "Flibber", "" ] ] ] ]

classes.name: stzNotation
classes.brief: Declares a diagram domain as data: its node kinds and glyphs, its colours, its well-formedness rules and its layout grammar.
classes.description: A notation is a profile over the one diagram foundation, not a second renderer. It declares a vocabulary of kinds with a glyph, a fill and a scale each (AddKind, AddKindXT, AddKindXTT), closes it when unknown kinds must be findings (Close), adds rules by the name of a check (Forbid for SelfLink, SecondParent and Cycle, ForbidFor for Inbound and Outbound on one kind), and amends the grammar: direction, routing, arrowheads, one ink, layout mode, where names are written. Check sweeps a diagram against the rules in the house rule shape [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; MayLink answers the same rules for one link, so an editor can refuse it at the gesture. StzRegisterNotation puts a profile in the registry, StzNotation(name) fetches it, and a diagram takes one with SetNotation. A name that is not registered gives the default profile, not an error. SetNameInside, SetNameOutside, SetPeerChildren and SetBranchSide return nothing, so a chain stops at them. A picture of a diagram under a notation needs a font passed to ToPNGXT; without one no label is drawn. Picture: a start, two states and an end drawn under a closed machine profile with LeftRight showed a small green start dot, two blue rounded boxes named Idle and Running, a small red end dot, and arrows left to right; the return arrow from Running to Idle had no arrowhead in the box glyphs (notation_machine.png).
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzNotation("machine"); o1.AddKindXT("state", "rounded", "Info.Solid"); o1.AddKind("start", "circle"); o1.AddKind("end", "circle"); o1.ForbidFor("end", :Outbound, "nothing leaves the end")

classes.name: stzNumber
classes.brief: Holds one number, exact or rounded, and answers questions about it and its written form.
classes.description: A stzNumber keeps the number as text, with its own round (the decimals it prints), so what you put in is what it holds. Reach for it when the value matters as a number AND as written: signs, digits, bases, exactness. For plain arithmetic on many numbers use stzListOfNumbers.

sections.title: checking if the number is a char
getting the unicode (code point) of the number
checking if the number is digit
checking if the number is multiple of a given number
integer & fractional parts (called also decimal parts)
multiplying the number by an other number
units, hundreds, thousands, millions, and billions

classes.name: stzNumbrex
classes.brief: Tests whole numbers against a small pattern language that describes number structure, such as prime, three digits or a multiple of five.
classes.description: A pattern is written in braces and made of tokens: @Property(Prime), @Digit3 or @Digit(1..5)+, @Factor4, @Relation(Mod:5=0), @Approx(~3.14), @Part(Integer), @Divisor(3) and @Multiple(4). Tokens are joined by -> or & (all must hold) or by a vertical bar (any may hold), and @! negates one. Match answers TRUE or FALSE for a number and, on success, records its digits, factors and properties for Digits, Factors and Properties. MatchingNumberAfter, MatchingNumbersBetween and CountMatchingBetween search for numbers instead of testing one. A digit or factor token with no quantifier means exactly one digit or one factor, so write @Digit3, not @Digit. Several things do not work as the grammar suggests today: a pattern with no readable token matches every number, @Digit(7) can never match, and @Factor(prime) can never match; each is flagged in its entry. The parser steps (NormalizePattern, ParsePattern, the Parse and Check methods) are internal and are listed for completeness.

classes.name: stzObject
classes.brief: Holds one value and gives every class of the library its common ground: naming, identity, kind tests, natural chains and constraints.
classes.description: stzObject is the ancestor of every class of the library. A stzString, a stzList, a stzNumber and every other class inherits from it, without writing a line, the questions about what an object is (IsA, Is, IsEitherA, IsOneOfTheseTypes), a variable name and a unique identifier (SetVarName, SetUuid), the self-description that answers plain-English questions about the class (Ask, ExplainMethod, HowTo, DoIntent), the grammar words of natural chains (Only, Exactly, AtLeast, AtMost, MoreThan, LessThan, About, IfSo, Otherwise, and the filler words such as Which or Their that change nothing), constraints that can be declared, verified and enforced at the update point (AddConstraint, EnforceConstraint), a recorded past that tense words can ask about (WasEver, UsedToBe, IsStill), and converters to the other classes (ToStzString, ToStzList, ToStzNumber). Several families here are overridden by the subclasses that know better, so for a stzString the answer to IsAString, Content, Repeat or IsEqualTo comes from stzString, and the version of this class is the one a bare stzObject, a stzNumber or a class with no override of its own runs. A bare stzObject wraps an object, or the global variable whose name is given as text. Some methods of the class raise today and are said so in their blocks: Values, AttributesAndValues, ToPointer, IsListOrString, WhichAreBoth, the time-value family, the OccursForThe...Time family and several of the Of... forms.
classes.example:
? o1.IsA(:String)
#--> 1
o1.SetVarName("oFruit")
? o1.VarName()
#--> oFruit
o1.AddConstraint("lower", :Lowercase)
? o1.VerifyConstraint("lower")
#--> 1
? Q("AnnIE").AtLeast(2).VowelNB()
#--> 1

classes.name: stzOidcClient
classes.brief: Acts as the application side of a sign-in with an external identity provider: builds the sign-in address and decides whether the returned id-token may be believed.
classes.description: Give it the issuer, the client id and the provider's public keys (AddKey, or SetJwks with the provider's JWKS document). AuthorizationUrl sends the user to the provider with a state and a nonce, and PKCE when you pass a challenge. VerifyIdToken then checks, in order, the shape, the key, the signature, the issuer, the audience, the expiry, the not-before time and the nonce, and answers a list whose why names the first failure instead of a bare 0. The algorithm is taken from the key the client holds, never from the token. In tests, use stzOidcSandbox to mint tokens offline.
classes.example:
? o1.AuthorizationUrl("https://idp.invented.test/authorize", "s1", "n-1")
#--> https://idp.invented.test/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=client-demo&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.invented.test%2Fcb&scope=openid%20profile%20email&state=s1&nonce=n-1
? o1.PkceChallengeOf("dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk")
#--> E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
? o1.VerifyIdToken("junk", "n-1")[:ok]
#--> 0
? o1.Why()
#--> the token is not a well-formed JWT

methods.name: VerifyIdToken
methods.brief: Decides whether an id-token may be believed, at the present time: signature, issuer, audience, expiry, not-before and nonce.

parameters.name: pcToken
parameters.role: the id-token returned by the provider

parameters.name: pcExpectedNonce
parameters.role: the nonce this login sent

methods.returns: a list [ :ok, :subject, :email, :claims, :why ]: ok is 1 with the identity, or 0 with why naming the first check that failed
notes: the key is chosen by the token's kid (the only key when the token names none) and the algorithm comes from that key, never from the token
warnings: a refusal is returned, never raised, and each one is also noted in the security ledger by issuer and reason, never with the token

methods.name: VerifyIdTokenAt
methods.brief: Decides whether an id-token may be believed at a given time, so that expiry can be tested without waiting.

parameters.role: the id-token to check

parameters.name: pnNow
parameters.role: the time to judge by, in seconds since 1970

notes: the token is expired when pnNow is past exp plus the clock allowance
warnings: the checks run in order and stop at the first failure: shape, key, signature, issuer, audience, exp, nbf, nonce; a token with no exp is refused

classes.name: stzOperatingSystem
classes.brief: Answers what machine and operating system the program runs on, with a predicate for each family and width.
classes.description: It reads the processor facts (architecture, pointer width, byte order) from the engine and the operating-system family from Ring, and offers one TRUE or FALSE question per family and per width, so a program branches on the machine instead of parsing a name. Name gives the family as a lower- case word, Info gathers the facts in a list of pairs, and PathSeparator, LineEnding, NormalizePath and ExecutableExtension answer what a path or a program file looks like here. It only reads: nothing is changed on the machine.

classes.name: stzOptimModel
classes.brief: Holds a linear or integer optimisation model that you write as variables, an objective and constraint texts, then solves it.
classes.description: Declare the variables with Vars or AddVar, set Maximize or Minimize, add constraints with SubjectTo, and Solve. A variable is bounded below (0 by default) and optionally above, and may be :integer or :binary. The built-in solver is a simplex with branch-and-bound; the :highs tier is refused because it is not vendored, so Why always names the engine that ran. Check IsOptimal before reading Solution: an infeasible or unbounded model leaves placeholder values. Violations re-checks the answer against the model. Known limit: a model with no constraint at all raises an error when solved, give it at least one constraint.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOptimModel() o1.Vars([ :x = [0, 40], :y = [0, :integer] ]) o1.Maximize("3*x + 2*y") o1.SubjectTo([ "x + y <= 50", "2*x + y <= 80" ])
classes.example:
o1.Solve()
? o1.IsOptimal()
#--> 1
? o1.Objective()
#--> 130
? @@( o1.Solution() )
#--> [ [ "x", 30 ], [ "y", 20 ] ]
? o1.Branched()
#--> 1
? o1.IsFeasibleAnswer()
#--> 1

parameters.role: the constraint's name, kept in lower case

parameters.name: pnIndex

methods.name: AST
methods.brief: Returns the model as a plain list that two descriptions can be compared by, rather than their answers.
methods.returns: a list [ :sense, :vars, :obj, :objconst, :cons ]; each var row is [ name, lb, ub, bounded, integer ] and each constraint row [ name, coefficients, operator, right side ]

methods.name: ASTCore
methods.brief: Returns the same list as AST with the constraint names dropped.

methods.name: Show

methods.brief: Solves the model with a named tier of the solver and keeps the answer.

parameters.name: pcTier
parameters.role: :auto, :floor or the empty text for the built-in simplex and branch-and-bound

methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain
notes: whole-valued variables make the solver branch; Why names the engine that ran
warnings: raises an error for :highs (not vendored), for any other tier, when no objective is set, and for a model with no constraint at all, which the engine refuses today although the code says it solves

methods.name: Solve
methods.brief: Solves the model with the automatic tier.
methods.returns: the model itself, so calls chain

methods.name: IsSolved
methods.brief: TRUE if a solve has run, whatever it found.

methods.name: Status

methods.brief: TRUE if a solve ran and found the optimum.

methods.name: Objective
methods.brief: Returns the value of the objective at the answer, constant included.

methods.name: Solution
methods.brief: Returns each variable with its value at the answer.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value ] pairs in declaration order
notes: the values are placeholders when the model is infeasible or unbounded

methods.name: ValueOf
methods.brief: Returns the value of one variable at the answer.

parameters.name: pcName

methods.name: Nodes
methods.brief: Returns how many branch-and-bound nodes the last solve explored.

methods.name: Iterations
methods.brief: Returns how many simplex iterations the last solve took.

methods.name: Branched
methods.brief: Returns 1 when the solve used branch-and-bound, which it does when a variable is whole-valued.

methods.name: Engine

methods.brief: Returns the solver's account of itself: the tier chosen, the result, the objective and the point, and the work done.

classes.name: stzOrgChart
classes.brief: Models an organisation as positions, people and departments, draws its reporting lines, and checks them against governance rules.
classes.description: An org chart is a diagram whose nodes are positions and whose edges run from supervisor to subordinate. Positions have a level (executive, management, staff), people are assigned to them, and the chart answers vacancy, span-of-control and succession questions, validates itself (BCEAO, segregation of duties, span, vacancy, succession), writes reports, highlights subsets with the View calls and saves to the .stzorg text format. Records are hash lists with lowercase keys. Several calls hold known defects, listed in their warnings: the succession check and the level colours read a key that is never written, and a few View calls raise.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzOrgChart("TechCo"); o1.AddExecutiveXT("ceo", "CEO"); o1.AddManagerXT("vp", "VP Sales"); o1.ReportsTo("vp", "ceo")

classes.name: stzOverlay
classes.brief: Describes an institution's adaptation of the core program, laid over it file by file, and judges it before it is used.
classes.description: An overlay is a folder with overlay.zknw (its name, the program it extends, the languages it speaks, its brand, the worlds it replaces) and optional worlds, courses and governance folders. It adds and shadows; it never forks the core: it may replace a world and add chapters and exercises, but a file that would replace a core chapter or a core exercise is refused. Check is its court and returns findings in the house shape; the overlay is valid when none is an error.
classes.example:
? o1.Name()
#--> bank
? @@( o1.Languages() )
#--> [ "fr", "en" ]
? o1.Brand()
#--> sahel-savings
? @@( o1.ReplacedWorlds() )

classes.name: stzPairs
classes.brief: Is another name of stzListOfPairs: a list of pairs [ first, second ], with every method of it.
classes.description: The class adds nothing: it is built, ordered and queried exactly as a stzListOfPairs, and Copy answers a stzListOfPairs.

classes.name: stzPanel
classes.brief: Lays out an interface document with the RmlUi engine and hands the result over as triangles, text commands, boxes and events.
classes.description: A panel is neither a window nor a renderer: it computes where things go and leaves drawing to a canvas, so the same layout reaches an SVG on a machine with no graphics card. The markup is loaded as a text (LoadMarkup), never from a file, because it is meant to be emitted by a higher layer. After Layout the panel answers where an element sits (BoxOf), what lies under a point (ElementAt), which elements the keyboard reaches (TabRing) and what input produced (Events, drained by the caller and never dispatched back into Ring). SetTextOf and SetStyleOf change one element without loading the document again. RML has no default stylesheet, so give a div display: block and the body width: 100% to fill the panel. Pointer verbs act on the layout, so call Layout first. The event queue and the counters belong to the engine and are shared by every panel. Needs stz_gui.dll; ask StzGuiAvailable() first. Free the panel when done.
classes.example:
o1.LoadMarkup('<rml><head><style>body { width: 100%; height: 100%; } div { display: block; } #bar { height: 48px; background-color: #2b6cb0; } .b { width: 100px; height: 30px; tab-index: auto; }</style></head><body><div id="bar"/><div id="one" class="b"/><div id="two" class="b"/></body></rml>')
o1.Layout()
? @@( o1.BoxOf("bar") )
#--> [ 0, 0, 320, 48 ]
? @@( o1.TabRing() )
#--> [ "one", "two" ]
? o1.ElementAt(10, 10)
#--> bar
? o1.TriangleCount()
#--> 2

classes.name: stzPaymentsPort
classes.brief: Speaks the BCEAO's PI-SPI payment verbs to a hub: sends money, asks for it, verifies webhooks and raises refusals as problems.
classes.description: An application sends money with Pay, asks for it with RequestPayment, hears about payments with RegisterWebhook and ReceiveWebhook, and reads a refusal with StzLastPaymentsProblem. The port speaks the verbs of the BCEAO's API Business to any backend that has a Request method, so the code tested against the twin (StzPiSpiSandboxQ) is the code that talks to a participant. WHERE THIS STANDS: behind the twin every verb runs and is tested; behind the live adapter (stzPispiHttpAdapter) the port has been proven against the twin served over real HTTP and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so treat that path as unperceived. WHAT THE PORT ADDS: a txId is an idempotency key, since sending it again answers the current state and sends nothing (replayed is 1); money out (Pay, PayInBulk, ReturnFunds, accepting a request or a cancellation) needs a committed plan on a governed port, which is how a port starts; an amount carries its currency and only XOF is spoken; a status of 400 or more raises, and StzLastPaymentsProblem reads it; a webhook is verified before it is believed. The amount is forwarded as built and nothing is added to it. The journal, the webhook secrets and the events already seen are kept per port in shared tables, so copies of a port agree. The card verbs (Authorize, Capture, Refund) are not here: they belong to stzCardPaymentsAdapter. The practical guide is docs/payments-guide.md.
classes.example:
oOrder = StzPaymentOrderQ().WithTxId("APP-2026-000001").FromAlias(oHub.BusinessAlias()).ToAlias(oHub.Alias("fatou")).WithAmount(StzAmountQ("25000", "XOF")).WithoutConfirmation()
aR = o1.Pay(oOrder)
? aR[:statut]
#--> ENVOYE
oHub.AdvanceSeconds(25)
? o1.StatusOf(aR[:end2endId])[:statut]
#--> IRREVOCABLE
o1.RegisterWebhook(StzWebhookQ().CallingBack("https://app.example/pispi").OnEvents([ "PAIEMENT_RECU" ]))
oHub.SimulateIncomingPayment("fatou", 18500, "APP-2026-000002")
aEv = o1.ReceiveWebhook(oHub.LastCallbackBody(), oHub.LastCallbackSignature())
? aEv[:accepted]
#--> 1
? aEv[:events][1][:motif]
#--> APP-2026-000002

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a port in front of a hub, the one object an application calls to send money, ask for it and hear about it.

parameters.name: poBackend
parameters.role: the hub to talk to: the twin (StzPiSpiSandboxQ), a live adapter, or any object with Request(method, path, query, body) answering [ status, body ]

notes: the port keeps its journal, its webhook secrets and its plan authorisations per port, so two ports on one hub do not share them
warnings: raises an error when poBackend is not an object with a Request method

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend is the in-process twin, which moves no money; a registry reads it to refuse the twin in production.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: the port only asks its backend

methods.name: IsConformance
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend talks to the BCEAO's sandbox, which speaks the real protocol with virtual money; a registry refuses it in production.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: UNPERCEIVED: the adapter that answers TRUE here has been proven against the twin over real HTTP and has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: RequiresCertificate
methods.brief: TRUE if the backend presents a mutual-TLS client certificate, which a registry then expects to find in a secret store.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; FALSE when the backend does not say so
notes: UNPERCEIVED: only a live adapter answers TRUE, and no live adapter has been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: CertificateSecretName
methods.brief: Returns the name of the secret that holds the backend's client certificate, so a registry can check it exists and has not expired.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the backend has none
notes: UNPERCEIVED: only a live adapter names one, and none has been run against the BCEAO's sandbox

methods.name: Backend
methods.brief: Returns the hub object the port talks to, for a test that must drive the twin directly, such as moving its clock.
methods.returns: the backend object exactly as it was given to the port
notes: in a test it is the twin, which has AdvanceSeconds and SimulateIncomingPayment

methods.name: AllowUngovernedPayouts
methods.brief: Lets this port send money without a committed plan: the loud, named exception that a test of the twin uses.
methods.returns: the port itself, so calls chain
notes: the exception belongs to this port only; every other port stays governed
warnings: a registry in a production phase refuses a port that did this (ungoverned- payouts-in-production)

methods.name: AllowsUngovernedPayouts
methods.brief: TRUE if this port was told to send money without a plan.

methods.name: IsGoverned
methods.brief: TRUE if payouts on this port need a committed plan, which is how a port starts.
methods.returns: TRUE or FALSE; the opposite of AllowsUngovernedPayouts
notes: asking for money, refusing a request and moving money between the platform's own accounts need no plan on a governed port

methods.name: AuthorisePayout
methods.brief: Records that a committed plan allows one payout of one amount on this port, after checking that the actor may authorise money out.

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor authorising, an object that must be effectful and not sandboxed

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the plan that authorises, kept for the record

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: what is authorised: pay, bulk, return, answer-cancellation or answer-request

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the txId of a payment, the instructionId of a bulk, or the end2endId for the other kinds

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount in francs that the payout must equal

notes: an application rarely calls it: stzPayoutDesk does when a person commits a plan; authorising the same kind and key again replaces the earlier row and makes it usable again
warnings: an actor that is not effectful, is sandboxed (a language-model actor) or is not an object raises payout-refused and is written to the security ledger as payout.refused

methods.name: AuthorisedPayouts
methods.brief: Returns the payouts a plan has authorised on this port, oldest first, each with whether it has been used.
methods.returns: a list of records [ kind, key, amount, plan, used ]; used is 1 once the payout was sent

methods.name: IsFinal
methods.brief: TRUE if a payment status will not change again: IRREVOCABLE, REJETE, ANNULE or ACCEPTE.

parameters.name: pcStatut
parameters.role: the status word as the hub gave it, in capitals

notes: ENVOYE and INITIE are not final: pending is a state, not an error

methods.name: ReasonMeaning
methods.brief: Returns the plain meaning of a reason code such as AM04, the one a rejected payment carries in statutRaison.

parameters.name: pcCode
parameters.role: the ISO 20022 reason code, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text for a code it does not know
notes: it knows the codes a platform meets first, not every enum of the hub

methods.name: JournalSize
methods.brief: Returns how many transactions this port remembers by their identifier, the memory that makes a retry safe.
notes: one entry per txId or instructionId sent; a send the hub refused as a duplicate (DU03) is not remembered

methods.name: ResolveAlias
methods.brief: Returns who an alias belongs to before it is paid: the client's name, country and category, and the alias key.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the PI-SPI alias, a UUID

methods.returns: a record [ client, alias ]; client is [ nom, pays, categorie ]
notes: a 404 is read with StzLastPaymentsProblem
warnings: raises stzPaymentsProblem 404 for an alias the hub does not know

methods.name: Accounts
methods.brief: Returns the platform's accounts at its participant, each with number, type, opening date and status.
methods.returns: a list of records [ numero, type, dateOuverture, statut ]

methods.name: Account
methods.brief: Returns one account with its balance, type and status.

parameters.name: pcNumero
parameters.role: the account number, as Accounts lists it

methods.returns: a record [ type, numero, solde, statut, dateOuverture ]
notes: solde is a whole number of francs

methods.name: Aliases
methods.brief: Returns the aliases attached to an account, each with its key, type and creation date.

parameters.name: pcNumero
parameters.role: the account number

methods.returns: a list of records [ cle, type, compte, dateCreation ]

methods.name: CreateAlias
methods.brief: Adds a new alias to an account so that customers can be paid to it, and returns it.

parameters.name: pcNumero
parameters.role: the account number

parameters.name: pcType
parameters.role: the alias type: SHID or MCOD

methods.returns: a record [ cle, type, compte, dateCreation ]
notes: the new alias key is in cle
warnings: any other type raises a 400 problem that names the field type

methods.name: DeleteAlias
methods.brief: Removes an alias from an account so it can no longer be paid; an unknown key raises.

parameters.name: pcNumero
parameters.role: the account number

parameters.name: pcCle
parameters.role: the alias key (cle), as Aliases lists it

warnings: an alias key the hub does not hold raises stzPaymentsProblem 404

methods.name: Participants
methods.brief: Returns the hub's participants, banks and issuers, each with its code, name and whether it is enabled.
methods.returns: a list of records [ codeMembre, nomMembre, codeBanque, statut ]; codeBanque is present for banks only, statut is ENBL or DSBL

methods.name: TransferBetweenAccounts
methods.brief: Moves money between two of the platform's own accounts and returns the transfer, which is final at once.

parameters.name: pcTxId
parameters.role: the platform's own unique id for the transfer

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the number of the account debited

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the number of the account credited

parameters.name: poAmount
parameters.role: an amount built with StzAmountQ, in XOF

methods.returns: a record [ txId, payeurNumero, payeNumero, montant, dateEnvoi, statut, dateIrrevocabilite ]
notes: it is not money out, so it needs no plan on a governed port
warnings: a bare number or an amount in another currency raises an error before any request is made

methods.name: Pay
methods.brief: Sends money to a payee from an order and returns the payment as the hub states it, ENVOYE until it is final.

parameters.name: poOrder
parameters.role: a stzPaymentOrder with its txId, payer, payee, amount and confirmation set

methods.returns: a record with the hub's fields (statut, end2endId, montant, payeNom...) plus replayed, 1 when the txId had already been sent
notes: UNPERCEIVED behind a live adapter: that adapter has been proven against the twin over real HTTP and has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox. ENVOYE is pending, not done: only IRREVOCABLE and REJETE are final. Sending the same txId again answers the current state and sends nothing, whatever the second order says. The amount is forwarded as built and nothing is added to it
warnings: on a governed port, the default, it raises payout-without-plan unless a committed plan authorised this txId, payout-amount-differs when the amount is not the planned one, and payout-already-released when the authorisation was used; a refusal by the hub raises stzPaymentsProblem, readable with StzLastPaymentsProblem

methods.name: ConfirmPayment
methods.brief: Answers the confirmation step of a payment made with confirmation: yes sends it, no cancels it.

parameters.name: pcTxId
parameters.role: the txId of the payment waiting for confirmation

parameters.name: pbYes
parameters.role: TRUE to send the payment, FALSE to cancel it

methods.returns: the payment record; statut is ENVOYE after yes and ANNULE after no
notes: the order must have been built with WithConfirmation
warnings: on a governed port a yes raises payout-without-plan when no plan authorised that txId; a no for a payment already confirmed raises a 403 problem

methods.name: SentPayment
methods.brief: Returns one payment the platform sent, found by the txId it chose, with its current status.

parameters.name: pcTxId
parameters.role: the txId the platform gave the payment

warnings: raises stzPaymentsProblem 404 for a txId the hub does not hold

methods.name: ReceivedPayment
methods.brief: Returns one payment the platform received, found by the txId the hub gave it.

parameters.name: pcTxId
parameters.role: the txId of the received payment, as ReceivedPayments lists it

notes: the twin names incoming txIds IN- followed by the end2endId; the platform did not choose them
warnings: raises stzPaymentsProblem 404 for an unknown txId

methods.name: SentPayments
methods.brief: Returns the payments the platform sent, filtered, as a list; the hub gives 20 per page unless asked otherwise.

parameters.name: paFilter
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs: a field name, with an operator in brackets as in montant[gte], plus page, size (1 to 100) and sort (a leading minus sorts down)

notes: pass [ ] for no filter; the paging data is dropped, SentPaymentsPage keeps it
warnings: a size outside 1 to 100 raises a 400 problem

methods.name: ReceivedPayments
methods.brief: Returns the payments the platform received, the list to reconcile on motif and end2endId.

parameters.name: paFilter
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs as SentPayments takes them

notes: motif carries the label the payer typed, such as the reference put in a QR code

methods.name: SentPaymentsPage
methods.brief: Returns the whole answer for the sent payments, data and meta, for a caller that pages through many.

parameters.name: paFilter
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs as SentPayments takes them

methods.returns: a record [ data, meta ]; meta is [ total, page, size ]

methods.name: StatusOf
methods.brief: Returns the current state of a payment by its end2endId: pending, final or rejected, with the reason code if rejected.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the hub's id for the payment, found in the answer of Pay

methods.returns: a payment record whose statut is ENVOYE while pending, then IRREVOCABLE or REJETE; statutRaison holds the ISO code of a rejection
notes: a payment the payee's bank refuses is not an exception: it is a payment whose statut became REJETE. The twin's clock moves by hand with AdvanceSeconds
warnings: raises stzPaymentsProblem 404 for an unknown id

methods.name: ReturnFunds
methods.brief: Sends back a payment received, as a new movement of the same amount; the hub allows it within 90 days.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of the payment received

methods.returns: the received payment's record, with retourStatut set (INITIE just after)
notes: the amount authorised must equal the amount the hub holds for that payment
warnings: it is money out: a governed port raises payout-without-plan, and payout- already-released on a second try with the same authorisation

methods.name: RequestCancellation
methods.brief: Asks the payee to cancel a payment already sent; the payee may refuse, since a payment is irrevocable.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of the payment to cancel

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the reason code, such as DUPL or FRAD

methods.returns: the sent payment's record, with annulationStatut and annulationMotif
notes: asking is not money out and needs no plan; the hub allows it within 90 days

methods.name: AnswerCancellation
methods.brief: Answers a cancellation request that a payer made against a payment received: accepting gives the money back.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of the payment the request concerns

parameters.name: pbAccept
parameters.role: TRUE to accept, FALSE to refuse

methods.returns: the payment record, with annulationStatut ACCEPTE after an accept
warnings: accepting is money out: a governed port raises payout-without-plan unless a plan authorised it; refusing needs no plan

methods.name: RequestPayment
methods.brief: Asks a payer for money with a request to pay and returns it as the hub states it, ENVOYE or INITIE until it is final.

parameters.name: poRequest
parameters.role: a stzPaymentRequest with its txId, payer, payee, amount and category set

methods.name: PayInBulk
methods.brief: Sends many payments as one batch under one instructionId and returns the batch status with its counts.

methods.name: Bulk

parameters.role: the instructionId of the batch waiting

parameters.role: TRUE to send, FALSE to cancel

methods.returns: the batch status; statut is CONFIRME after yes and ANNULE after no

methods.name: ReceiveWebhook

parameters.name: pcBody

parameters.name: pcSignature

notes: UNPERCEIVED: only calls signed by the twin have been verified, and no callback from a real hub has been seen. Every refusal is noted in the security ledger. Answer 204 first and work afterwards, since the hub retries what it did not see acknowledged
