classes.name: stzPaymentsProblem
classes.brief: Holds the refusal a hub returned, as the RFC 7807 fields: a status, a title, a detail and the fields found wrong.
classes.description: When a hub answers 400 or more, stzPaymentsPort raises an error and keeps the problem; StzLastPaymentsProblem hands it over. Read Status to decide what to do, Detail to log what the hub said, and InvalidParams to see which field of the message was refused. A payment that the payee's bank refuses is not a problem: it is a payment whose statut became REJETE.
classes.receiver: oHub = StzPiSpiSandboxQ(); oPay = StzPaymentsPortQ(oHub); oPay.AllowUngovernedPayouts(); try oPay.Pay(StzPaymentOrderQ().WithTxId("BIG- 1").FromAlias(oHub.BusinessAlias()).ToAlias(oHub.Alias("fatou")).WithAmount(StzAmount Q("20000000", "XOF")).WithoutConfirmation()) catch o1 = StzLastPaymentsProblem() done
classes.example:
? o1.Status()
#--> 403
? o1.Detail()
#--> Plafond de paiement depasse
? o1.InvalidParams()[1][1][2]
#--> montant

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a problem from the body the hub returned with a refusal, a list of pairs in the RFC 7807 shape.

parameters.name: paBody
parameters.role: the problem as a list of [ key, value ] pairs

notes: an application rarely builds one: StzLastPaymentsProblem hands over the one the port just recorded

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: Returns the HTTP status the hub gave the refusal, such as 403 or 404.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the problem is empty

methods.name: Title
methods.brief: Returns the short, general name of the refusal, such as Forbidden.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the hub gave none

methods.name: Detail
methods.brief: Returns the hub's sentence about this refusal, the one to log or show a developer, such as Plafond de paiement depasse.
methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the hub gave none
notes: the twin writes it in French

methods.name: Type
methods.brief: Returns the problem's type address, which is about:blank when the hub gave none.

methods.name: InvalidParams
methods.brief: Returns the fields the hub found wrong, each with the reason, for a refusal of a malformed message.
methods.returns: a list of records [ name, reason ]; an empty list when the hub named none

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the whole problem as a list of pairs, exactly as the hub returned it.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs; an empty list when the problem is empty

classes.name: stzPaymentsSandbox
classes.brief: Names the card-gateway double under its historical name, with no behaviour of its own beyond stzCardPaymentsAdapter.
classes.description: The class was renamed when the card verbs were moved out of the payments port, and this name stays because the payments checks and the registry's examples use it. It adds nothing: every method is that of stzCardPaymentsAdapter. Build it with parentheses or with StzPaymentsSandboxQ(), because a paren-less new skips init and every object built that way shares one gateway.

classes.name: stzPayoutDesk
classes.brief: Takes a payout plan from proposal to release: rehearse it, judge it, and let a person commit it, with a journal of every attempt.
classes.description: Money out is a plan a human commits, and the desk is where that happens. Rehearse writes the plan into a workbench, a twin of the disk, so nothing real moves. Judge reads the rehearsed document and applies the policy. Commit checks the policy, that the rehearsed document is the plan that will be paid, and that the actor may change reality; a language-model actor and a sandboxed actor are refused. Only then does the plan cross into a real file, the durable record of what was authorised, visas included, and the port is told exactly which payouts to allow and for how much before each is released. A refusal never raises: it is a journal row and an event. One plan, one workbench. Everything here was run against the in-process twin, which moves no money.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a desk that rehearses, judges and commits payout plans for one port under one policy, keeping its journal in a folder.

parameters.name: poPort
parameters.role: the stzPaymentsPort that will be told what to allow and then release

parameters.name: poPolicy
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPolicy that judges every plan

parameters.name: pcDir
parameters.role: the folder where a committed plan is written as its journal file

notes: each desk has its own journal, and a plan is known only to the desk it was rehearsed on

methods.name: PathOf
methods.brief: Returns where a plan is written, in the desk's folder: the rehearsed document in a workbench and the journal file once committed.

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the plan's identifier

methods.name: Rehearse
methods.brief: Writes a plan's document into a workbench, a twin of the disk, so it can be judged without anything real moving.

parameters.name: poPlan
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPlan to rehearse

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench number returned by StzOpenAgentWorkbench

methods.returns: the desk itself, so calls chain
notes: the proposer acts in the workbench under the plan's proposer name, and no real file exists yet
warnings: the desk keeps the plan as it is now: visas added to the plan afterwards are not seen until it is rehearsed again, and rehearsing again overwrites the document; one plan, one workbench

methods.name: Judge
methods.brief: Returns the verdict of the policy on the plan document held in the workbench, in the house rule report.

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench the plan was rehearsed into

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the identifier of the plan to judge

methods.returns: a stzRuleReport: IsSound is 1 when no rule fails and Errors lists the failing ones, each naming its rule
notes: a verdict is not a payment: a sound plan still pays nothing until a person commits it

methods.name: Commit
methods.brief: Lets an actor who may change reality release a judged plan: its journal file is written, then each item is paid through the port.

parameters.name: pnBench
parameters.role: the workbench the plan was rehearsed into

parameters.name: pcPlanId
parameters.role: the identifier of the plan to commit

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the actor committing it, such as HumanActor("tresorier")

methods.returns: a list [ committed, reason, detail, results, file ]: committed is 1 or 0, results holds one answer per item, file is the journal path
notes: money out is a plan that a human commits: a refusal is a journal row and a payout.refused event, a commit is a journal row, a payout.committed event and a real file
warnings: a refusal never raises: committed is 0 and reason is unknown-plan, already- committed, policy, rehearsal-differs, actor or crossing, with the cause in detail; a language-model actor, a sandboxed actor and a value that is not an object are all refused for actor; the checks run in that order and the policy is judged before the actor; a plan commits once; an item the port refuses is that item's error in results while the others still go

methods.name: Journal
methods.brief: Returns the desk's record of every commit attempt, oldest first, whether it was refused or went through.
methods.returns: a list of records [ seq, plan, outcome, reason, actor, total, visas ] where outcome is committed or refused
notes: a second desk has its own empty journal

classes.name: stzPayoutPlan
classes.brief: Holds a proposed payout as a plan to be judged and committed by a person, since money out is never a method call.
classes.description: Money out is a PLAN a human commits. A plan names what it pays, whether one payment, a bulk, the return of a payment received, or the acceptance of a request to pay or of a cancellation, and carries the visas of the people who approve it. Building a plan moves nothing: a stzPayoutDesk rehearses it into a workbench, a policy judges the rehearsed document, and only an actor who may change reality, never a language model, can commit it, after which the port releases exactly what the plan names. The weight of a plan is the sum of what it pays, so a payroll cannot be cut into small lines to slip under a threshold. The policy that judges it is the platform's own data. The whole path was run against the in-process twin, which moves no money.
classes.example:
o1.WithId("SUP-2026-10").ProposedBy("treasury-agent")
o1.Returning("E2E-0001", 40000)
o1.Visa("comptable", "A. Issoufou")
o1.Visa("DAF", "M. Garba")
? o1.TotalAmount()
#--> 40000
? o1.NumberOfDistinctVisas()
#--> 2

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an empty plan that pays nothing yet, to be filled by naming what it pays and who gives a visa.
notes: a plan is a proposal: building it, filling it and rehearsing it move no money, and only a person's commit through a stzPayoutDesk releases it

methods.name: WithId
methods.brief: Sets the identifier of the plan, which names its rehearsed document and the file written when it is committed.

parameters.name: pcId
parameters.role: the plan's identifier, as text

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the rehearsed document lives at <folder>/<id>.plan.json, so the id is also a file name

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the identifier of the plan.
methods.returns: a text; empty until WithId is called

methods.name: ProposedBy
methods.brief: Sets the name of whoever proposes the plan, an agent or a person.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the proposer's name, as text

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: a policy built with ProposerCannotVisa refuses a plan whose proposer is among its visas

methods.name: Proposer
methods.brief: Returns the name of whoever proposed the plan.
methods.returns: a text; empty until ProposedBy is called

methods.name: Paying
methods.brief: Adds one payment to the plan, kept with the order behind it so that the commit can release exactly that order.

parameters.name: poOrder
parameters.role: the stzPaymentOrder to pay, whose id and amount are read

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the item is recorded as kind pay, keyed by the order's transaction id
warnings: a value that is not an object raises error R13 at once

methods.name: PayingBulk
methods.brief: Adds a whole bulk of payments to the plan as one item whose amount is the sum of the batch.

parameters.name: poBatch
parameters.role: the stzPaymentBatch to pay, whose instruction id and total are read

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the item is recorded as kind bulk, keyed by the batch's instruction id
warnings: a value that is not an object raises error R13 at once

methods.name: Returning
methods.brief: Adds the return of a payment that was received, by its end-to-end id and the amount the hub holds for it.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the payment received

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount the hub holds for it, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the port refuses the movement at the commit if this amount differs from the hub's (payout-amount-differs); the plan still commits and the refusal is that item's result

methods.name: AcceptingRequest
methods.brief: Adds the acceptance of a request to pay somebody sent us, which is money out, by its end-to-end id and amount.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the request received

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount of the request, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: at the commit the desk answers the request with acceptance through the port

methods.name: AcceptingCancellation
methods.brief: Adds the acceptance of a cancellation request, which returns funds, by its end-to-end id and amount.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end-to-end id of the payment to cancel

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the amount to return, in francs

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: refusing a cancellation is not money out and needs no plan

methods.name: Items
methods.brief: Returns what the plan pays, one record per item, in the order they were added.
methods.returns: a list of [ kind, key, amount ] where kind is pay, bulk, return, answer-request or answer-cancellation

methods.name: Objects
methods.brief: Returns the order or batch behind each item, in the same order as Items.
methods.returns: a list with the stzPaymentOrder or stzPaymentBatch for a pay or bulk item, and an empty text for the other kinds

methods.name: NumberOfItems
methods.brief: Returns how many items the plan pays.

methods.name: TotalAmount
methods.brief: Returns the weight of the plan: the sum of every item it pays.
notes: a policy judges this sum, so a payroll cannot be cut into small lines to slip under a threshold

methods.name: Visa
methods.brief: Records the role and the name of a person who approves the plan; the same person signing twice counts once.

parameters.name: pcRole
parameters.role: the role of the signer, such as comptable or DG

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the signer's name

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: visas added after a rehearsal do not reach the desk until the plan is rehearsed again

methods.name: Visas
methods.brief: Returns every visa recorded, in the order given.

methods.name: NumberOfVisas
methods.brief: Returns how many visas were recorded, signatures and not people.

methods.name: NumberOfDistinctVisas
methods.brief: Returns how many different people gave a visa; the same name in another case is one person and an empty name counts for none.

methods.name: Document
methods.brief: Returns the plan as one JSON text: its id, proposer, items and visas, which is what is rehearsed, judged and committed.
notes: the document holds no credential, and the object behind a pay or bulk item is not in it

classes.name: stzPayoutPolicy
classes.brief: Holds the rules of who must approve a payout plan, as data a platform writes, and judges a plan against them.
classes.description: The rule of which people must approve what is a platform's, so it is data in a policy and never a constant in the port. A policy counts people, not signatures: a person who signs twice, in any case, is one visa. The first rule says above, so a total exactly equal to the threshold needs none. A verdict is a list of findings in the house shape [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ], which joins stzRuleReport, the one CI gate. A policy only judges: it moves nothing and commits nothing. StzDikoPayoutPolicyQ builds one platform's policy, four visas above 100 000 FCFA.
classes.example:
o1.RequireVisasAbove(100000, 4).ProposerCannotVisa()
oPlan = StzPayoutPlanQ().WithId("P1").ProposedBy("agent").Returning("E2E-0001", 250000)
oPlan.Visa("DAF", "M. Garba")
? o1.JudgePlan(oPlan)[1][:rule]
#--> payout-over-100000-needs-4-visas

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a named policy with no rule, which finds fault only with a plan that pays nothing.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the policy's name, as text

notes: the rule of who must approve what is a platform's data, never a constant of the port: add yours with RequireVisasAbove and ProposerCannotVisa

methods.name: Name
methods.brief: Returns the title the policy was given when it was built.

methods.name: RequireVisasAbove
methods.brief: Adds a rule: a plan whose total is strictly above an amount needs a number of visas from distinct people.

parameters.name: pnAmount
parameters.role: the threshold in francs, a total exactly equal to it needs no visa

parameters.name: pnVisas
parameters.role: how many distinct people must have given a visa

methods.returns: the policy itself, so calls chain
notes: several rules may be added and each one that fails gives its own finding named payout-over-<amount>-needs-<visas>-visas

methods.name: ProposerCannotVisa
methods.brief: Adds separation of duties: the person who proposed a plan may not be one of its visas.
methods.returns: the policy itself, so calls chain
notes: the names are compared without regard to case, and a plan with no proposer is never refused by this rule

methods.name: JudgePlan
methods.brief: Returns the findings of this policy on a plan object, by judging the document the plan would write.

parameters.name: poPlan
parameters.role: the stzPayoutPlan to judge

methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; an empty list means the plan is sound
notes: a desk judges the rehearsed document and not the plan object, so this is for a quick look before rehearsing

methods.name: JudgeDocument
methods.brief: Returns the findings of this policy on a rehearsed plan document, which is what a desk judges and commits.

parameters.name: pcDocument
parameters.role: the plan's JSON text, as Document of the plan returns it

methods.returns: a list of findings, each [ rule, subject, where, severity, message ]; an empty list means the plan is sound
notes: the findings join stzRuleReport, the one CI gate; where is the plan's id
warnings: a plan with no item gives the finding payout-plan-empty whatever the rules

methods.name: Center
methods.brief: ── the choice you must make ──
methods.detail: THE NAME FORM CARRIES THE SEMANTICS, which is a Softanza law rather than a style: an ACTIVE verb -- Standardize(), Center() -- DOES the thing and returns nothing; the PASSIVE form -- Standardized(), Centered() -- returns the transformed DATA and leaves the object alone; and the Q twin does the thing and returns the object so calls chain. The first version of this class had Standardized() mutating the analysis and returning This, which got both halves wrong at once: a passive name for an active act, and a plain method returning an object where plain methods return data. CENTER each feature on its mean and leave the units alone -- covariance PCA. The features that vary most, in their own units, dominate.

extensions.name: CenterQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Standardize
methods.brief: CENTER and then divide each feature by its standard deviation -- correlation PCA. Every feature counts equally, whatever it was measured in.

extensions.name: StandardizeQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Centered
methods.brief: ── and the passive forms, which return the prepared DATA ── The data centered on the column means, original untouched.
methods.detail: This is what a covariance PCA actually decomposes, so it is worth being able to look at.

methods.name: Standardized
methods.brief: The data centered AND divided by the column standard deviations. What a correlation PCA decomposes.

methods.name: IsStandardized
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is standardized.

methods.name: UseSampleVariance
methods.brief: ── the variance convention, from the library's one authority ──

extensions.name: UseSampleVarianceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: UsePopulationVarianceQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

extensions.name: FitQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: IsFitted
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is fitted.

methods.name: Components
methods.brief: The DIRECTIONS: row i, column j is how much feature i contributes to component j. A component is a weighted blend of your features, not one of them.
methods.detail: The sign is fixed by convention (the largest loading of each component is made positive) because a direction has no preferred sign -- v and -v are the same axis explaining the same variance -- and without a convention two runs can look like they disagree.

methods.name: Scores
methods.brief: The data in component coordinates: row i is sample i, column j its position along component j.
methods.detail: Centered by construction, so each column averages zero.

methods.name: ExplainedVariance
methods.brief: How much variance each component accounts for, in the units of the prepared data.
methods.detail: These SUM to TotalVariance() -- the decomposition redistributes the variance and cannot create or destroy any.

methods.name: ExplainedVarianceRatio
methods.brief: The same, as fractions of the total. This is the number people quote.

methods.name: NumberOfComponentsFor
methods.brief: How many components to keep to retain a given fraction of the variance -- the usual way the number of components is chosen.

methods.name: Mean
methods.brief: The centering that was applied, kept because projecting NEW data needs exactly the same one.
methods.detail: Data centered on its own mean lands in a different space.

methods.name: Inverse
methods.brief: Project rows the fit has not seen into the component space, using the FIT's centering and scaling. -- THE INVERSE, AND IT IS THE TRANSPOSE
methods.detail: This is where PCA differs in KIND from the rest of the embedding family, not merely in quality. The forward map is a ROTATION onto an orthonormal basis, so undoing it needs no second model, no training and no lookup: multiply by the same loadings the other way round, put the scale back, put the mean back. t-SNE and UMAP have no analytic inverse at all. They must fit a DECODER to (position, row) pairs, and what comes back is a plausible row rather than a recovered one. Here the arithmetic was already sitting in the fit. -- AND THE ERROR IS NOT MYSTERIOUS EITHER -- It is exactly the variance living in the components you dropped. Not approximately: the residual IS the projection onto the discarded eigenvectors, so the mean squared reconstruction error over the training rows EQUALS the sum of their eigenvalues -- the numbers ExplainedVariance() already reports. Keep every component and the reconstruction is the data back, to rounding. That identity is checked in the guard, and it is a far stronger statement than any reconstruction number the learned inverses can offer. It says the arithmetic is RIGHT, where they can only say the result looked plausible.

methods.name: Reconstructed
methods.brief: the training rows put through Transform() and back again -- what the analysis retained of the data it was given, which is the picture worth looking at when deciding how many components are enough

classes.name: stzPispiHttpAdapter
classes.brief: Carries the payments contract over HTTP to a participant's API Business, with OAuth2, an API key and optional mutual TLS.
classes.description: UNPERCEIVED. This adapter is proven against the twin served over real HTTP (stzPiSpiHttpFront), plain and with mutual TLS, and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox. No payment made through it has been watched landing in a real dashboard by a named person, and until one has it stays unperceived: built, not yet proven in the world. It is the live backend of the payments port, answering the same Request(method, path, query, body) as the twin, which is why the port cannot tell the two apart. Before each call it takes an OAuth token with the client credentials read from a secret store, reuses it until a minute before it lapses, retries once on a 401, and sends the API key; it presents a client certificate on an https address when the participant requires one. A hub's problem comes back as the same [ status, problem ] the twin gives, while a transport failure raises. The base address is configuration, nothing in the adapter names a bank, and it promises no homologation. The payments guide, docs/payments-guide.md, is the desk's own account.

classes.name: stzPiSpiHttpFront
classes.brief: Serves the twin of the PI-SPI hub over HTTP, with a token endpoint, an API key and scopes, so a live adapter has a real server to talk to.
classes.description: UNPERCEIVED, the live adapter this front exists to test. stzPispiHttpAdapter is proven against this twin over real HTTP, plain and with mutual TLS, and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox: a green run against the front says the adapter and the twin agree, not that a participant's hub agrees, and no payment made through the adapter has been watched landing in a real dashboard. The front puts the twin's single Request() behind an application server and adds what a participant puts in front of the contract: an OAuth2 client-credentials token endpoint, an x-api-key, a scope for each operation, and optional mutual TLS. It moves no money, the twin holds virtual francs. The token is not bound to the certificate it was taken under, which the real hub's is, because the engine does not show the peer certificate to a handler. EnableControl adds /_twin/ routes for a test, with no credential asked. All its state is process-wide, so run one front per process, and run it in a process of its own since RunFor blocks its caller.

parameters.name: pcClientSecret
parameters.role: the client secret it accepts

parameters.name: pcApiKey
parameters.role: the key every API call must send in x-api-key

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
notes: the values are test values the caller generates, never a participant's credentials
warnings: with no API key set every API call is refused with a 401 problem

methods.name: WithScopePrefix
methods.brief: Sets the text that every scope of a token must carry, which is piz/ in the BCEAO's sandbox.

parameters.name: pcPrefix
parameters.role: the text such as piz/, an empty text for none

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: a call whose token lacks the prefixed scope its operation needs is refused with a 401 problem naming the scope

methods.name: WithBasePath
methods.brief: Sets the path under which the contract is served, /piz/v1 unless changed.

parameters.name: pcBase
parameters.role: the path prefix such as /piz/v1

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: any other path, apart from the token endpoint and the control routes, answers a 404 problem

methods.name: WithTokenLifetime
methods.brief: Sets how many seconds a token issued from now on stays valid, 3600 unless changed.

parameters.name: pnSeconds
parameters.role: the lifetime in seconds, which the token response reports as expires_in

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: the adapter refreshes a token a minute before it lapses, so a lifetime under a minute makes it fetch one for every call

methods.name: EnableControl
methods.brief: Turns on the /_twin/ routes with which a test drives the twin behind the wire.
methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
notes: they advance the clock, settle what is pending, make a customer pay, ask or cancel, change how a customer answers, read the queued webhooks and the counters; a server that holds real money never enables them
warnings: those routes ask for no credential at all, so anyone who can reach the port can advance the clock, make the twin pay or ask, and revoke tokens, and loopback only is a matter of the host given to Start and is not enforced here

methods.name: Hub
methods.brief: Returns a face onto the twin the front serves, for a caller in the same process.
methods.returns: an stzPiSpiSandbox on the same hub
warnings: the face shares its state with the served twin, so a payment made through it is seen over HTTP

methods.name: Start
methods.brief: Binds the front to a port and an address and returns 1, without serving anything until RunFor is called.

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free one

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the address to bind, an empty text meaning 127.0.0.1

notes: UNPERCEIVED, for the live adapter this front is built to serve: stzPispiHttpAdapter is proven against this twin over real HTTP and has NOT been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so a green run here says the adapter and the twin agree, not that a participant's hub agrees
warnings: raises an error when the port cannot be bound or the front already runs

methods.name: StartTls
methods.brief: Binds the front to a port and an address behind TLS, with mutual TLS when a CA is given, and returns 1.
usage: StartTls(pnPort, pcHost, pcCert, pcKey, pcCa, pbRequireClient)

parameters.name: pnPort
parameters.role: the port to listen on, 0 for any free one

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the address to bind, an empty text meaning 127.0.0.1

parameters.name: pcCert
parameters.role: the server certificate PEM file

parameters.name: pcKey
parameters.role: the server private key PEM file

parameters.name: pcCa
parameters.role: the CA PEM file that checks client certificates, an empty text for none

parameters.name: pbRequireClient
parameters.role: TRUE to demand a client certificate, so that a client without one gets no response at all

notes: UNPERCEIVED: mutual TLS is proven only between the adapter and this twin with the engine's throwaway test certificates, never against the BCEAO's sandbox or a participant
warnings: raises an error for a certificate, key or CA file that cannot be used, naming the code -13, -14 or -17; the token is not bound to the certificate it was fetched under, as the real hub's is, because the engine does not show the peer certificate to a handler

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port the front listens on, the real one when 0 was asked for.
methods.returns: a number, 0 before the first start

methods.name: RunFor
methods.brief: Serves requests for the given time and then returns, the call that makes the front answer.

parameters.name: pnMs
parameters.role: how long to serve, in milliseconds

methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: it blocks its caller, so an adapter running in the same process cannot be served: run the front in a process of its own, as the library's live-adapter guard does

methods.name: Stop
methods.brief: Closes the listener and keeps the routes for a later start.
methods.returns: the front itself, so calls chain
warnings: a front that is not running is left as it is

classes.name: stzPispiQr
classes.brief: Builds the PI-SPI interoperable QR payload, the short text a camera reads, and refuses to build one that would print wrong.
classes.description: The library builds the QR STRING and does not draw the picture, and no QR it made has been scanned by any wallet or bank app: the black and white matrix a phone's camera reads is a second step this library does not do, so hand the string to a QR-drawing component of your front end. The string follows the BCEAO's published merchant-presented format: the receiver's PI-SPI alias, the currency XOF, an optional whole-franc amount, a country of the union, a reference label of at most 25 characters and a checksum. A static code serves many payments and a dynamic code one sale. The builder refuses a bad alias, country, label or amount when the payload is asked for, and StzPispiQrParse reads a string back without raising and says what is wrong. It is a builder, not a payment: the payer's banking application makes an ordinary payment to the alias. The checksum matches an independent implementation, which proves the string is well formed and nothing about a scan.

methods.name: WithAlias
methods.brief: Sets the PI-SPI alias of the receiver, the one account the code pays.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the receiver's PI-SPI alias, a UUID of 36 characters such as the twin's BusinessAlias()

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the UUID shape is checked, not the version
warnings: an alias that is not in the shape of a UUID is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: InCountry
methods.brief: Sets the country of the receiver, in capitals whatever case is given.

parameters.name: pcCountry
parameters.role: the country code, one of BJ BF CI GW ML NE SN TG

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
warnings: a country outside the union is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: AsStatic
methods.brief: Makes the code a static one, printed once and read for many payments, with channel 000.
methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: in a static code the payer types the amount unless WithAmount fixes it; the last of AsStatic and AsDynamic called wins

methods.name: AsDynamic
methods.brief: Makes the code a dynamic one, made for one sale, with channel 400.
methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the last of AsStatic and AsDynamic called wins

methods.name: WithReference
methods.brief: Sets the label the payer's application shows and the receiver reconciles the payment on.

parameters.name: pcLabel
parameters.role: the reference label, 1 to 25 printable ASCII characters

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the payment received carries it as its motif
warnings: a label that is empty, over 25 characters or outside printable ASCII is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: WithAmount
methods.brief: Fixes the amount the payer is asked for, which must be whole francs in XOF.

parameters.name: poAmount
parameters.role: the stzAmount to ask for, in XOF, above zero and of at most 13 digits

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error at once for an amount in another currency or an amount that is not above zero; without it the payer types the amount

methods.name: WithPurpose
methods.brief: Sets the optional purpose text carried in the additional data of the code.

parameters.name: pcPurpose
parameters.role: the purpose, in printable ASCII

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
warnings: a purpose outside printable ASCII is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: WithCustom
methods.brief: Adds an additional-data tag of the receiver's own to the code.

parameters.name: pcTag
parameters.role: the tag, exactly two characters, digits or capital letters

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the tag's value, as text

methods.returns: the builder itself, so calls chain
notes: the receiver's tags are written after the standard ones, in the order of their names
warnings: a tag that is not two characters of digits or capital letters is not refused here but when Payload is asked for

methods.name: Payload
methods.brief: Returns the QR string, whose last four characters are its checksum, after refusing any value that would print a bad code.
methods.returns: a text: the payload string, not a picture
notes: the library builds this string and does not draw the picture, and no code it made has been scanned by any wallet or bank app: StzPispiQrParse reads it back and checks the checksum, which proves the string is well formed and not that a phone accepts it
warnings: raises an error naming the cause when AsStatic or AsDynamic was not called, or the alias is not a UUID shape, or the country is outside the union, or the label is missing, over 25 characters or not printable ASCII, or a custom tag is malformed, or the amount has more than 13 digits

classes.name: stzPiSpiSandbox
classes.brief: Answers the PI-SPI hub contract in process as a twin, with virtual francs and a clock moved by hand, so a platform can be tested without a bank.
classes.description: The twin implements the REST contract of the hub in one method, Request(method, path, query, body), which the payments port and the live adapter both speak. It enforces what the reference enforces, so code that pays twice, sends a field the schema refuses or exceeds the quota fails in a test: a txId replayed is answered REJETE with reason DU03, a payment is pending and becomes final 20 seconds later on the twin's own clock, and the hub's webhooks are signed. It declares itself a fake, so a registry refuses it in a production phase. It holds virtual francs and takes no fee, montantFrais is absent because the participant's fee is the participant's contract. It is a model of the contract, not the hub: the live adapter has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so how closely the twin matches that hub is unperceived. The live adapter that talks to a real hub is UNPERCEIVED for the same reason. The state lives in process-wide tables, so a copy of the object is the same hub.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a new twin hub of its own, with a clock, a set of customers and 50 000 000 virtual francs on the platform's account.
notes: the state lives in process-wide tables and the object carries only the hub number, so a copy of the object is the same hub
warnings: the twin holds virtual francs and takes no fee, montantFrais is absent because the participant's fee is the participant's contract

methods.name: IsSandbox
methods.brief: Answers TRUE always, so that a registry takes the twin for a fake and refuses it in a production phase.
warnings: stzServiceRegistry

methods.name: Id
methods.brief: Returns the number of the hub this object is a face of.
methods.returns: a number, 1 for the first hub of the process

methods.name: AdoptHub
methods.brief: Points this object at a hub that already exists, so that two objects drive the same twin.

parameters.name: pnId
parameters.role: the number a hub's Id answered

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: the HTTP front uses it to reach the twin it serves

methods.name: Request
methods.brief: Answers one call of the hub contract in process, as [ status, body ], the method the port and the live adapter both speak.

parameters.name: pcMethod
parameters.role: GET, POST, PUT or DELETE

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the contract path such as /paiements-envoyes or /comptes

parameters.name: paQuery
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs for paging and filters, a non-list meaning none

parameters.name: paBody
parameters.role: the body as a list, a non-list meaning none

methods.returns: a list of two items, the HTTP status and the body as a list, or an empty text for a 204
notes: the twin enforces what the reference enforces, so that code which pays twice or sends an unknown field fails in a test, but it is a model of the contract and not the hub: the live adapter has not been run against the BCEAO's sandbox, so how closely the two agree is unperceived
warnings: each call moves the twin's clock forward one second; a missing resource is a 404 problem, a field the schema does not know a 400, a txId used twice answers 200 with statut REJETE and statutRaison DU03, and over the quota a 429

methods.name: Now
methods.brief: Returns the twin's clock as an ISO timestamp, which starts at 2026-10-05T09:00:00.000Z.
warnings: the clock moves only by one second per request or when asked, never with the wall clock, so a test never waits twenty seconds

methods.name: AdvanceSeconds
methods.brief: Moves the twin's clock forward and settles every payment that has come due, a pending one becoming final after 20 seconds.

parameters.name: pn
parameters.role: the number of seconds to move the clock forward

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: the webhooks the settlement announces are queued if a registered webhook listens to them

methods.name: SettleEverything
methods.brief: Makes every pending payment and request final now, as if 20 seconds had passed.
methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: SetRateLimit
methods.brief: Sets the hub's quota, so that calls beyond it answer a 429 problem.

parameters.name: pnPerMinute
parameters.role: how many calls the hub accepts in a minute of its own clock

parameters.name: pnPerDay
parameters.role: how many it accepts in a day

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: the minute window follows the twin's clock, so advancing it past a minute lifts the limit

methods.name: Alias
methods.brief: Returns the PI-SPI alias, a UUID, of one of the twin's customers by short name: business, fatou, boutique, kdi, blocked or stubborn.

parameters.name: pcWho
parameters.role: the customer's short name, matched without regard to case

methods.returns: a text; a name the twin does not know comes back unchanged

methods.name: BusinessAlias
methods.brief: Returns the alias of the platform's own account on the twin.

methods.name: BusinessAccount
methods.brief: Returns the account number of the platform's own account on the twin.
methods.returns: a text, the same for every hub

methods.name: Balance
methods.brief: Returns the platform's balance in francs, 50 000 000 at birth.
warnings: a payment sent lowers it at once and a payment received raises it at once, before any settlement

methods.name: SetCounterparty
methods.brief: Sets how one customer's side answers: a payment, a request to pay and a cancellation.

parameters.name: pcWho
parameters.role: the customer's short name or alias

parameters.name: pcPay
parameters.role: ok or the ISO reason code that rejects a payment to this customer, such as AM04

parameters.name: pcRtp
parameters.role: pay or the reason code that declines a request to pay

parameters.name: pcCancel
parameters.role: accept or the reason code that refuses a cancellation

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error for a customer the twin does not know, naming it; a payment to a customer set to AM04 ends REJETE with that reason

methods.name: AddCounterparty
methods.brief: Adds a customer to the twin that accepts every payment, request and cancellation until SetCounterparty says otherwise.

parameters.name: pcAlias
parameters.role: the new customer's alias, a UUID text

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name shown to the platform

parameters.name: pcCountry
parameters.role: the two-letter country code such as NE

parameters.name: pcCategory
parameters.role: the category letter, P, B or C as the seeded customers carry

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: the customer is known by its alias, not by a short name

methods.name: SimulateIncomingPayment
methods.brief: Makes a customer pay the platform, raising the balance at once and queueing a PAIEMENT_RECU webhook.

parameters.name: pcWho
parameters.role: the customer's short name or alias

parameters.name: pnMontant
parameters.role: the amount in francs

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the label the payer wrote, an empty text for none

methods.returns: the end2endId of the payment, a text of 35 characters
warnings: raises an error for a customer the twin does not know; the webhook is queued only if a registered webhook listens to PAIEMENT_RECU, so a twin with no webhook shows no delivery

methods.name: SimulateIncomingRequest
methods.brief: Makes a customer ask the platform to pay, queueing an RTP_RECU webhook.

parameters.name: pcWho
parameters.role: the customer's short name or alias

parameters.name: pnMontant
parameters.role: the amount asked in francs

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the label the customer wrote

methods.returns: the end2endId of the request, a text of 35 characters
warnings: raises an error for a customer the twin does not know; the webhook is queued only if a registered webhook listens to it

methods.name: SimulateCancellationRequest
methods.brief: Makes a customer ask to cancel a payment the platform received, queueing an ANNULATION_DEMANDE webhook.

parameters.name: pcEnd2EndId
parameters.role: the end2endId of a payment the platform received

parameters.name: pcMotif
parameters.role: the reason the customer gives

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: raises an error when the id is not a received payment

methods.name: FailNextAnswer
methods.brief: Makes the hub reject the next answer the platform gives to a request to pay or to a cancellation.
methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
warnings: it exists so that RTP_REPONSE_REJETE and ANNULATION_REPONSE_REJETE can be seen

methods.name: NumberOfDeliveries
methods.brief: Returns how many signed webhooks this hub has queued since birth, delivered or not.

methods.name: NumberOfUndelivered
methods.brief: Returns how many queued webhooks no one has taken yet.

methods.name: Deliveries
methods.brief: Returns every queued webhook, oldest first, without marking any as taken.
methods.returns: a list of records with the keys hookId, callbackUrl, evCode, body, signature and delivered; [ ] when none

methods.name: DeliverTo
methods.brief: Hands each webhook no one has taken to a handler and marks it taken, one call per webhook.

parameters.name: poHandler
parameters.role: an object with ReceiveWebhook(body, signature), such as the payments port

methods.returns: how many webhooks were handed over, a number
warnings: the answer of the handler is not read, so a refused webhook is still marked taken

methods.name: TakeUndelivered
methods.brief: Returns every webhook no one has taken, oldest first, and marks them taken, what a hub's delivery loop would post.
methods.returns: a list of records with the keys hookId, callbackUrl, evCode, body and signature; [ ] when none
warnings: a second call right after answers [ ]

methods.name: LastCallbackBody
methods.brief: Returns the JSON body of the newest queued webhook.
methods.returns: a text, empty when no webhook was queued
warnings: the body is the thing the signature signs, so pass it unchanged to the port

methods.name: LastCallbackSignature
methods.brief: Returns the signature of the newest queued webhook, 64 hexadecimal characters.
methods.returns: a text, empty when no webhook was queued

methods.name: LastWebhookSecret
methods.brief: Returns the secret the hub gave when the newest webhook was registered or renewed.
methods.returns: a text of 64 hexadecimal characters, empty when no webhook was registered
warnings: the hub shows the secret once, here it can be read again; it is a test value of the twin

methods.name: NumberOfPayments
methods.brief: Returns how many payments this hub holds on one side, ENVOYE for those the platform sent and RECU for those it received.

parameters.name: pcSide
parameters.role: ENVOYE or RECU

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one line giving the hub number, its clock, the payments sent and received, the balance and the webhooks.

classes.name: stzPispiSecret
classes.brief: Describes one of the five secrets a live payment needs, by name and kind, as a token that can expire.
classes.description: The five parts are the OAuth client, the API key, the mTLS private key, its certificate and a webhook secret. A descriptor is a stzToken underneath, because a token is the one kind of secret the store already knows how to expire, and its kind says which part it is. It carries no value until a source is given: the value comes from an environment variable, a file outside the repository or a vault, and is shown by no output. Use invented values in a test and never write a real one in a source file, a memo or an example. A descriptor that is only a name is refused by the registry in production, as is one whose certificate has lapsed.
classes.example:
o1.FromEnv("INVENTED_MTLS_CERT_PATH")
? o1.Kind()
#--> pispi-mtls-cert
? o1.Part()
#--> mtls-cert
? o1.Descriptor()
#--> <secret 'pispi-bia-mtls-cert' (pispi-mtls-cert) from env:INVENTED_MTLS_CERT_PATH>

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an unset descriptor for one of the five parts of a live payment: a name and a kind, and no value.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the name the descriptor is registered under in the store

parameters.name: pcPart
parameters.role: one of client, api-key, mtls-key, mtls-cert or webhook-secret, in any case

notes: a descriptor with no value is a name, not a credential: give it a source with FromEnv, FromFile or FromVault, and its kind becomes pispi- followed by the part
warnings: raises an error naming the five parts when pcPart is anything else, an empty text included

methods.name: Part
methods.brief: Returns which of the five elements of a live payment this descriptor stands for, in lower case.
methods.returns: a text: client, api-key, mtls-key, mtls-cert or webhook-secret

classes.name: stzPivotTable
classes.brief: Cross-tabulates a table: groups its rows by one or two label columns against a column of labels, and aggregates a value column in each cell.
classes.description: Give it a source table, then name the row labels, the column labels and the value column, with SetRowLabels, SetColumnLabels and SetValues (or By and Analyze). Value, RowTotal, ColumnTotal and GrandTotal read the cells, ToTable returns the result as a table and Show prints it. The pivot is generated again whenever a setting changes. Use the supported shape: one column label, one or two row labels, one value column; that shape runs in the engine. Known limits, all reproduced: the totals of every function but SUM and COUNT are sums of the cells; any other shape runs in a Ring fallback that drops the first source record; Show raises for two column labels; SaveToFile writes an empty file.
classes.receiver: o1 = new stzPivotTable([ [ "CITY", "YEAR", "SALES" ], [ "Tunis", 2023, 10 ], [ "Tunis", 2024, 5 ], [ "Sfax", 2023, 20 ], [ "Gabes", 2024, 3 ] ]) o1.SetRowLabels(:CITY) o1.SetColumnLabels(:YEAR) o1.SetValues(:SALES)
classes.example:
? o1.Value("Tunis", 2023)
#--> 10
? o1.RowTotal("Tunis")
#--> 15
? o1.ColumnTotal(2023)
#--> 30
? o1.GrandTotal()
#--> 38
o1.SetNullValue("-")
? o1.Value("Sfax", 2024)
#--> -

parameters.name: paLabels

methods.brief: Sets how the values of one cell are combined, and names the totals after it.

classes.name: stzPlatform
classes.brief: Wraps a stzApp world in what makes it operable: build and deploy of its parts, governed capabilities, a Commons of identities and messages, and a world registry.
classes.description: A stzApp models the world and lacks the operational envelope; the platform is that envelope, in five duties. It owns a deployment profile whose parts Build and then Deploy (Build records the compiler command of each part and Deploy lowers it to an artifact text, neither runs anything). SetWorld takes a world, and Generate writes a shell file for each of its reaches. A capability such as the camera is requested with AddCapability and decided by Granted against a governance regime. OpenCommonsOn turns an open database into identities (salted PBKDF2 hashes, never the secret), sessions, messages and a key-value store. ServeBody serves the world and the Commons over HTTP on 127.0.0.1. PushWorld, Bond and CallAcross keep a registry in which a call between worlds goes through only if both are active, a bond names the action and governance agrees. The runs behind this reference were in memory only: no shell file was written and no port was opened.

classes.name: stzPlatformProfile
classes.brief: Describes a whole solution: its development system and its parts, each with the system it deploys to.
classes.description: The architect's common ground. Declare the solution with DevelopedOn and WithApp, WithServer, WithSuperApp or WithPart, then check it with Validate. Feature code is authored per part (ReadPinIn, SpawnIn, ConnectIn and the others) and checked at once against that part's target: an operation the target forbids raises an error, one the live machine cannot perform is rehearsed and recorded for deploy-time lowering. The profile only describes: it builds and deploys nothing, and it is saved as a small .stzplatform text. A part obtained with App and assigned to a variable is a copy; chain the calls instead.

#--> 2
? o1.App(:firmware).DeploymentOSName()
#--> espidf

#--> 1
? o1.IsSound()

? @@( o1.Validate() )
#--> [ ]

methods.brief: THE ROOTS ------------------------------------------------------- The companion matrix of the MONIC form of this polynomial: the matrix whose characteristic polynomial is p, and therefore whose eigenvalues are p's roots. THE COMPANION MATRIX of the monic form, as DATA.
methods.detail: Assembled by the engine, not here. It looks like four lines of glue -- the sign, which row carries the coefficients, the monic division, the leading-zero case -- and every one of those is a decision a second implementation gets subtly differently. poly.zig owns it, so every language over the engine builds the same matrix.

methods.name: Times
methods.brief: Convolution of the coefficient lists -- the definition of a product of polynomials. MULTIPLICATION IS A CONVOLUTION, which is why this has two paths.
methods.detail: The coefficients of a product are the convolution of the coefficients of the factors, so multiplying polynomials is exactly the operation an FFT does in O(N log N) instead of the double loop's O(n*m). stzFourier owns that convolution; nothing is reimplemented here. THE DOUBLE LOOP IS KEPT FOR SMALL DEGREES, and not out of caution: it is EXACT for integer coefficients, while the FFT route goes through irrational twiddle factors and comes back a few rounding errors away from a whole number. Below the crossover the direct method is both faster and more accurate, so preferring it is not a compromise. Above it, O(n log n) wins by enough that the rounding is worth paying.

classes.name: stzProgram
classes.brief: Opens a learning program, a folder of courses, skills, levels and teaching worlds, and lets an institution lay its own overlay over it.
classes.description: A learner or a teacher starts here: CourseQ takes a course by its slug, WithWorld chooses the world the chapters reason over, and the Review methods say how far each translation has been checked by a person. The program is a folder read through its .zknw manifests; every file is looked up in the overlay first and the core after, so an institution replaces a world or adds an exercise and never writes into the core. Set the overlay and the world BEFORE CourseQ: Ring copies the program into the course, so a later WithOverlay does not reach it. WithOverlay, WithoutOverlay and WithWorld change the program and have a Q twin that returns it for chaining. LIMITS, stated where you meet them: the translations (fr, ar, ha) are drafts, 0 of 35 units of each reviewed by a person when this was written, and only ReviewCoverage gives the live figure; the cells of the chapters run on the desktop only, not in a browser, and the Run methods start Ring processes whose executable path must not contain a space; no institution has adopted the system, and the two overlays shipped, bank and university, are references.

classes.name: stzProject
classes.brief: Holds a level project: a brief, and a guard that judges a learner's folder by running it.
classes.description: A level is earned by a project that passes, never by a score. The project is a folder with a brief in each language, guard.ring (the court, run in a fresh process with the library loaded, exactly like an exercise's harness), promise.ring (the lines the guard must print for a pass) and wrong/ and right/ sample folders that must be refused and accepted. The guard runs on the desktop only. The fr, ar and ha briefs are drafts, 0 of 35 units reviewed by a person.
classes.example:
? o1.Id()
#--> project-s0
? o1.HasGuard()
#--> 1
? @@( o1.Promises() )
#--> [ "cells five or more: yes", "every cell has a promise: yes", "every promise kept: yes", "stored output: no" ]
? o1.Check(o1.RightSamples()[1]).Passed()
#--> 1

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Judges a learner's project folder by running the project's guard on it in a fresh process with Softanza loaded.

parameters.name: pcLearnerFolder
parameters.role: the learner's project folder to judge

methods.returns: the stzExerciseCheck of the run: Passed(), Output() (what the guard printed) and Why() (a sentence for the learner)
notes: the evidence it carries is the hash of every file in the folder, so a folder changed after a pass no longer counts; CheckMany(pacFolders) judges several folders in one run and returns the list of checks (it is not a root of its own in the record, ProveItself uses it)

methods.name: ProveItself

classes.name: stzReactive
classes.brief: Is the short name of stzReactiveSystem, so every method and every form is the same.
classes.description: Use whichever name reads better at the call site; the class adds nothing of its own.

methods.name: Call_
methods.brief: THE SYNCHRONOUS CALL. It has to actually call.
methods.detail: This built the task, handed it to AddTask, and returned it unexecuted. Its async sibling below calls Execute() on the local task; this one relied on the engine running it later, and the engine never saw it: @oEngine is an attribute, so AddTask appends to a COPY of the reactive system. Measured -- the real engine's task list stayed at zero, and after Start() the wrapped function had run zero times. Call_ did nothing whatsoever. AddTask is kept because CallAsync does the same and both are equally copy-bound; that is the engine-identity problem, not this method's, and papering over it here would hide it. Execute() on the LOCAL task is what makes the result real, which is exactly how CallAsync has always worked.

methods.name: CallAsync
methods.brief: CallAsync() for normal operations computations that should yield control to other operations

methods.name: SetReactor
methods.brief: The reactor is what makes the request path ASYNC -- _CanAsync answers FALSE without one and every verb falls back to the blocking task. NULL is therefore a legitimate value: it means "no reactor, go blocking".
methods.detail: Anything that is neither is refused rather than stored, because a bad reactor does not fail here; it fails later inside _SubmitAsync or DrainPending, a long way from the call that caused it.

methods.name: DrainPending
methods.brief: Called by the run loop each tick: dispatch every finished job.
methods.detail: The curl path returns the BODY directly (headers stripped) and reports the HTTP status; success = a 2xx code (same callback contract as the blocking download() path).

classes.name: stzReactiveObject
classes.brief: Turns attributes into values that notify: a change runs watchers, recalculates dependent attributes and updates bindings.
classes.description: A reactive object holds named attributes, made from nothing or wrapped around an existing object. SetAttribute stores a value and, when it changed, calls the functions registered with Watch, recomputes the attributes declared with Computed from the attributes they depend on, and writes to the targets given to BindTo. WaitForAttributetoSettle calls a function once an attribute stops changing, and Batch notifies a group of changes together afterwards. An error inside a watcher, a calculated attribute or a batch does not stop the caller: it is recorded (Errors, LastError, ErrorCount) and passed to the OnError handler, or printed when there is none. Names are not case sensitive. Two members do not work as intended today: a binding reaches its target only once, when it is made, and StreamAttribute never emits.
classes.example:
gLog = []
o1.Watch(:name, func(oSelf, attr, oldV, newV) { gLog + [ oldV, newV ] })
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Ann")
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Bob")
? @@( gLog )
#--> [ [ "", "Ann" ], [ "Ann", "Bob" ] ]
o1.Computed(:greeting, func oSelf { return "Hello " + oSelf.GetAttribute(:name) }, [ :name ])
o1.SetAttribute(:name, "Cy")
? o1.GetAttribute(:greeting)
#--> Hello Cy
o1.OnError(func(w, m) { })
o1.Watch(:age, "not a function")
? o1.LastError()
#--> Watch callback is not a function

methods.name: OnError
methods.brief: Sets the handler that receives each error the object catches instead of printing it, and returns the object.

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: a function taking two arguments, the place that failed and the message

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: without a handler the error is printed as [stzReactiveObject.place] message, and recorded either way

methods.name: Errors
methods.brief: Returns the errors recorded so far, as pairs of the place that failed and its message, oldest first.
methods.returns: a list of [ place, message ] pairs; at most 50 are kept
notes: the places look like Watch:name, Watcher:name, Computed:name, Binding:name->target or Batch

methods.name: LastError
methods.brief: Returns the message of the newest recorded error.
methods.returns: a text; empty when nothing was recorded

methods.name: LastErrorWhere
methods.brief: Returns the place of the newest recorded error, such as Watch:age or Batch.
methods.returns: a text; empty when nothing was recorded

methods.name: ErrorCount
methods.brief: Returns how many errors were seen, including the ones dropped once 50 were kept.

methods.name: ErrorsDropped
methods.brief: Returns how many errors were counted but not kept, because the record holds 50.

methods.name: HasErrors
methods.brief: TRUE if at least one error was recorded since the last ClearErrors.

methods.name: ClearErrors
methods.brief: Empties the error record and its counters, then returns the object.
methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Init
methods.brief: Builds the reactive object around an existing object, or around nothing when given an empty text, and keeps the engine that serves it.

parameters.name: existingObject
parameters.role: the object to wrap, or an empty text for an object made of attributes only

parameters.name: reactiveEngine
parameters.role: the stzReactive system that serves timers and streams

notes: the attributes of a wrapped object are read into the storage and the cache when it is built
warnings: the wrapped object is stored as a copy: changing the original afterwards does not reach the reactive object, and setting through the reactive object does not change the original

methods.name: BraceStart
methods.brief: Runs when Ring opens a brace block on the object, and does nothing today.

methods.name: BraceEnd
methods.brief: Runs when Ring closes a brace block on the object, and notifies the changes queued during the block.

methods.name: BraceError
methods.brief: Runs when a call in a brace block fails, and hands the error text to the failure function of every SetAsync made so far.
warnings: the SetAsync records are never removed, so a later failed brace call reaches the failure handlers of earlier, finished SetAsync calls as well

methods.name: SetAttribute
methods.brief: Sets an attribute, creating it when new, and on a real change runs its watchers, dependent attributes and bindings.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name, which is lowercased

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the value to store

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the name is lowercased, so :Name and :name are one attribute
warnings: inside Batch the notifications are queued and the value is stored at once; an equal value triggers nothing

methods.brief: Sets an attribute from a pair of its name and its value, so that a set reads like an assignment.

parameters.name: paAttr
parameters.role: a list of two items, the attribute's name and its value

notes: it calls SetAttribute and, unlike it, does not return the object

methods.name: GetAttribute
methods.brief: Returns the current value of an attribute, matched without regard to case.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.returns: the value; an empty text when the attribute is unknown

methods.name: GetAttributeValue
methods.brief: Returns the value of an attribute, reading the cache first, then the wrapped object, then the storage.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

methods.returns: the value; an empty text when the attribute is unknown
warnings: a value written with SetAttributeValue is not read back while the cache holds an older one

methods.name: SetAttributeValue
methods.brief: Writes a value into the storage, the wrapped object and the object's own attribute, without any notification and without touching the cache.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _value_
parameters.role: the value to write

notes: it is the call a binding makes on its target
warnings: GetAttribute keeps answering the older value for an attribute already in the cache; use SetAttribute to set and notify

methods.name: Watch
methods.brief: Registers a function called as f(object, name, oldValue, newValue) each time the attribute changes, and returns the object.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to watch

parameters.name: fCallback
parameters.role: a function taking four arguments: the reactive object, the attribute's name, the old value and the new value

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the function runs on every real change, in order of registration; an error inside it is recorded as Watcher:name
warnings: a value that is not a function is refused: nothing is stored and the error Watch callback is not a function is recorded

methods.name: Computed
methods.brief: Creates an attribute whose value is calculated by a function from other attributes, now and again each time one of them changes.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the name of the calculated attribute

parameters.name: _fnComputer_
parameters.role: a function taking the reactive object and returning the value

parameters.name: _aDependencies_
parameters.role: the names of the attributes it depends on, as a list

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: a watcher on the calculated attribute also fires when it is recomputed
warnings: a function that is not one, or dependencies that are not a list, are refused and recorded, and nothing is created

methods.name: BindTo
methods.brief: Binds an attribute to an attribute of another reactive object, copying its current value to the target at once.

parameters.name: oTargetObject
parameters.role: the reactive object that receives the value

parameters.name: _cSourceAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute of this object to follow

parameters.name: _cTargetAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute to write in the target, or an empty text for the same name

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: the starting value is written to the object you passed
warnings: a later change of the source does not reach the target object you passed, because the binding keeps a copy of the target: the target holds the value of the moment of binding; a target that is not an object is refused and recorded

methods.name: SetAsync
methods.brief: Sets an attribute at once, completes a task with the value, calls the success function, and returns the task.

parameters.name: _cAttribute_
parameters.role: the attribute's name

parameters.name: _newValue_
parameters.role: the value to set

parameters.name: fnSuccess
parameters.role: a function taking the value, or an empty text

parameters.name: fnError
parameters.role: a function taking the error text, or an empty text

methods.returns: a stzReactiveTask, already completed or failed
notes: the error is also recorded as SetAsync:name
warnings: the name suggests a deferred update, but nothing waits: the value is set before the call returns

methods.name: Batch
methods.brief: Runs a function in which attribute changes are stored at once but notified together afterwards, then returns the object.

parameters.name: fnUpdates
parameters.role: the function with no argument that makes the changes

methods.returns: the object itself, so calls chain
notes: each changed attribute is notified once
warnings: the watcher receives the first change of an attribute, with its old value and the value it had then, not the last: after sets of 1, 2 and 3 on an attribute that held 10 it is told 10 and 1 while the attribute holds 3; an error in the function is recorded as Batch and the changes already made stay

classes.name: stzReactiveStream
classes.brief: Carries values one by one through steps (transform, filter, accumulate) to the functions that subscribed to it.
classes.description: Values enter with Recieve (spelt Receive, Feed, Emit or Send as well) and leave through the functions given to OnPassed, after the steps added with Transform and Filter, in the order they were added. Accumulate replaces the per-value output with one final result, handed to the subscribers when the stream concludes: by Conclude, or by itself after a quiet delay once the loop runs. SetOverflowStrategy bounds the buffer and decides what is lost when it is full; OverflowStats counts what was lost. A stream made with new is inactive and ignores values until Start is called, and one made by stzReactive.CreateStream is already started. Known faults: OnBufferFull functions are never called, and a stream that concluded at once through RecieveMany can conclude a second time when its pending timer fires.
classes.example:
gOut = []
o1.Transform(func p { return p * 2 })
o1.Filter(func p { return p >= 100 })
o1.OnPassed(func v { gOut + v })
o1.SetAutoConclude(0)
o1.Recieve(30)
o1.Recieve(60)
o1.Recieve(80)
? @@( gOut )
#--> [ 120, 160 ]
o2 = oRs.CreateStream("sum")
gSum = []
o2.Accumulate(func(t, x) { return t + x }, 0)
o2.OnPassed(func t { gSum + t })
o2.SetAutoConclude(0)
o2.Recieve(5)
o2.Recieve(7)
? @@( gSum )
#--> [ ]
o2.Conclude()
? @@( gSum )
#--> [ 12 ]

methods.name: SetOverflowStrategy
methods.brief: Sets what happens to a value that arrives when the buffer is full, and the buffer's size, and returns the stream.

parameters.name: _strategy_
parameters.role: :BUFFER, :DROP, :BLOCK or :LATEST, and :BUFFER for any other word

parameters.name: maxBufferSize
parameters.role: how many values the buffer holds

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OnOverflow
methods.brief: Registers a function called as f(buffered, size) each time a value arrives while the buffer is full, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.role: a function taking two arguments, how many values are buffered and the buffer's size

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OnBufferFull
methods.brief: Registers a function meant to be called when the buffer is full, then returns the stream.

parameters.name: handler

methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain

methods.name: HandleOverflow
methods.brief: Calls the overflow functions, then drops the value that met a full buffer or evicts the oldest one, by strategy.

parameters.name: data
parameters.role: the value that did not fit

notes: HandleBackpressure is the same call

methods.name: ProcessAnItemFromBuffer
methods.brief: Takes the oldest buffered value, runs it through the steps and hands it to the subscribers; does nothing when the buffer is empty.

methods.name: ProcessAllInBuffer
methods.brief: Processes every buffered value, oldest first, and returns the stream.
methods.returns: the stream itself, so calls chain

methods.name: OverflowStats

methods.returns: a hashlist with the keys bufferSize, currentBuffer, isOverflowActive, droppedCount and strategy
notes: the keys are lower case when listed; reading o1.OverflowStats()[:droppedCount] works; BackpressureStats is the same call

classes.name: stzReactiveSystem
classes.brief: Declarative reactive programming: schedules timers and tasks, makes functions and objects reactive, makes streams and non-blocking HTTP calls, and runs them all in one loop.
classes.description: Create one system, register what should happen (RunAfter, RunEvery, CreateTimer, CreateTask, HttpGet, the stream makers), then call Start: the loop runs the pending tasks, ticks the timers and drains the HTTP answers until nothing is left, the patience runs out or a callback calls Stop. The system sits on a stzReactor when the engine library is present, and falls back to a polling loop when it is not. Callbacks always run on the Ring thread. Timers are named by the id that RunAfter and RunEvery answer; StopTimer and StopAllTimers end them. Reactivate wraps a function or an object so that calls take success and error handlers. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: StopSafe and its five aliases raise the STOPPED banner from the timer they schedule, and BindObjects binds copies, so neither object you pass changes.

methods.name: Status
methods.brief: WHAT HAPPENED, AFTER THE FACT
methods.detail: The class recorded a status, a result and (now) an error, and offered no way to read any of them. A caller whose task failed could not ask what went wrong; a caller whose task succeeded could not collect the answer unless they had registered a handler first.

methods.name: Error
methods.brief: "" when the task has not failed.

methods.name: HasFailed
methods.brief: TRUE if the object has failed.

methods.name: WasReported
methods.brief: Did the failure reach anyone -- a raise, a handler, or stdout? Only ERROR_IGNORE answers FALSE, and it is the one mode that asked to.
methods.detail: Without this the fallback arm had no observable effect at all: removing it left every assertion green, because recording a reason is not reporting it.

methods.name: Complete
methods.brief: AN OUTCOME PRODUCED OUTSIDE Execute()
methods.detail: Not every task computes. stzReactiveObject.SetAsync already HAS the value it is going to store, and its attempt to wrap one in a task function -- `func { return _newValue_ }` -- raised R24, because a Ring lambda cannot read a caller's local. These two let a caller that did the work itself still report it through the same task surface, so Status()/Result()/ Error() mean the same thing however the work happened.

methods.name: CheckAndTick
methods.brief: Drive the timer from the manager's poll loop. Returns isActive so the manager can prune completed one-shot timers.

classes.name: stzReactor
classes.brief: Runs timers, TCP and HTTP clients, child programs and servers on a libuv event loop that lives on a thread of its own, and hands the results to Ring by polling.
classes.description: Ring stays synchronous: you submit work and get a job id back at once, then Poll, Await or JobState that id, and no callback ever crosses into Ring. The calls come in families: Submit, Await, Poll and a LastStatus reader for timers, TCP, spawned programs and HTTP, plus one-call forms (TcpRequest, Spawn, HttpGet, HttpPost). A listener (Listen, ListenHttp, ListenStzm and the TLS forms) queues events that ServerPoll or ServerAwait drain as [ :accept, nConn, "" ], [ :data, nConn, cBytes ] or [ :closed, nConn, "" ]; ServerWrite and ServerCloseConn answer on a connection, and the Connect calls dial out and give a channel that is used the same way. A job id is spent once it is drained. The last-status readers (TcpLastStatus, SpawnLastStatus, HttpLastStatus, TlsClientStatus) hold one value for the whole process. The loop starts at the first call and Destroy stops it. Known gap today: Spawn and SubmitSpawn raise error R21 when given a plain text instead of a list.

classes.name: stzRecursiveRegexMaker
classes.brief: Describes a pattern as named levels nested inside one another, each with its own piece of pattern and quantifier.
classes.description: A level has a name, a pattern text, a parent, children and a quantifier. AddLevel adds a top level, AddChildLevel adds one inside an existing level, and AddQuantifier gives a level its repeat suffix. The tree can be read back with LevelNames, LevelParent, LevelChildren and Info. With named recursion on, which is the state at birth, each level is meant to become a named capture group. Pattern and SubPattern, which should join the levels into one regular expression, raise error R19 today for any maker that has a level, so the tree is readable but not yet convertible. stzNestedRegexMaker is another name for this class.
classes.example:
o1.AddLevel("open", "\(")
o1.AddChildLevel("open", "inner", "[^()]*")
o1.AddLevel("close", "\)")
? @@( o1.LevelNames() )
#--> [ "open", "inner", "close" ]
? @@( o1.LevelChildren("open") )
#--> [ "inner" ]
? o1.LevelParent("inner")
#--> open
o1.AddQuantifier("inner", "+")
? o1.Info()[2][:quantifier]
#--> +

classes.name: stzRegex
classes.brief: Holds a regular expression compiled by the PCRE2 engine and answers whether, where and how a text matches it, including partial and recursive matches.
classes.description: Build it with a pattern, then call a match method with a text: the text and the outcome of the last call are kept in the object, and the readers (Matches, FindMatches, CaptureGroups, NamedGroups, CaptureByName, the partial and recursive readers) work on that last call. Match asks whether the pattern covers the whole text; MatchFirst and MatchAt search inside it. MatchAsYouType and the partial family serve form validation while a person is still typing, and MatchRecursive handles nested brackets through (?R). A pattern that does not compile does not raise: IsValid answers FALSE and every match call answers FALSE. Known gaps today, each carried as a warning on its method: FindMatches and FindCapture skip a character after each match, PartialMatchLength is one too small, RecursiveDepth counts matches rather than nesting, LastError and PatternErrorOffset are stubs, Explain raises for a pattern the library does not know by name, and MatchWordsIn stacks word boundaries on the pattern each time it is called.

classes.name: stzRegexLookaroundMaker
classes.brief: Builds a look-around regular expression: a main pattern that must, or must not, come before or after another pattern.
classes.description: One look-around is held at a time: MustBeFollowedBy and CantBeFollowedBy build a look-ahead, MustBePrecededBy and CantBePrecededBy a look-behind, and the Word, Number and Space forms fill in the common patterns. A second call replaces the first. ThenMatch sets the main pattern, which Pattern writes after the look-around, so a look-behind reads correctly: (?<=\$)\d+ finds the digits that follow a dollar sign. A look-ahead followed by a main pattern does not read as the name says: (?=ing)[a-z]+ tests what the main pattern starts on, so it finds ing in walking and not walk. A look-behind of variable length, such as the Number and Space forms, finds nothing in the engine.
classes.example:
o1.MustBePrecededBy("\$").ThenMatch("\d+")
? o1.Pattern()
#--> (?<=\$)\d+
o2 = new stzRegex(o1.Pattern())
o2.MatchFirst("cost $42 now")
? @@( o2.Matches() )
#--> [ "42" ]

classes.name: stzRegexMaker
classes.brief: Builds a regular expression piece by piece from calls, then hands it over as one text with Pattern.
classes.description: Each Add call appends a fragment: a class such as [abc] or [a-z] with a repeat suffix (AddRange, AddAmongChars, AddCharsRange and their digit forms), a literal, a shorthand class, a group, a flag or an assertion. Pattern joins the fragments in order. The calls that add ranges also record a sequence, the same call in data form, so Sequences and Fragments are two views of one pattern; literals and groups add a fragment and no sequence, so the two lists do not stay aligned. Groups made with DefineGroup are remembered and can be reused or referred back to. The text is not escaped or validated: a literal goes in as given. Several public names are broken today and raise errors: NumberOfSequences and its aliases, the CommandAndFragment family, ComposePatterns in the or and sequence modes, MatchSameContentAs, the named-parameter forms CanContainAChar and CanContainADigit, and the five names that forward to the misspelled NumberOfFragments; each is flagged in its own entry. For ready-made patterns by name use AddCommonPattern or StzRxp.

methods.detail: A participant signs the RAW BODY it POSTs, nothing else: no method, no path, no timestamp, no nonce. That is a different message from the canonical string above and the same job: a keyed MAC, compared in constant time, with a replay cache and a ledger line for every refusal.
