classes.name: stzTukeyLine
classes.brief: Fits Tukey's resistant three-group line through paired values, so one wild point barely moves it.
classes.description: The line is R's line(): the points are split into three groups by x, the slope comes from the medians of the outer groups, and passes over the residuals refine it. Call Fit first; Slope, Intercept, Iterations and Residuals raise an error until then. Fit(n) matches R's iter = n + 1. Known defect: points that all share one x give slope 0 and intercept 0 without an error.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a resistant line to be fitted through paired values, x against y.

parameters.name: paX
parameters.role: the x values, a list of numbers

parameters.name: paY
parameters.role: the y values, a list of numbers of the same length, at least three points

methods.name: Fit
methods.brief: Fits Tukey's three-group line, then improves it with passes over the residuals, as R's line does.

parameters.name: pnIterations
parameters.role: the number of passes over the residuals after the first fit

methods.returns: the line itself, so calls chain
notes: on x 1 to 12 with y near twice x it gives slope 2.0056 and intercept 0.0444 after 5 passes, and one wild y barely moves it
warnings: Fit(0) equals R's line with iter 1 and Fit(1) equals iter 2, so the count here is one less than R's; points that all share one x give slope 0 and intercept 0 with no error, which is a defect

extensions.name: FitQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: Slope
methods.brief: Returns the slope of the fitted line.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Intercept
methods.brief: Returns the intercept of the fitted line, its y at x equal to 0.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Iterations
methods.brief: Returns how many residual passes the last Fit made.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Residuals
methods.brief: Returns each y minus the line's value at its x, in the order given.
warnings: Raises an error until Fit has run

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence that gives the fitted equation and the number of passes.
methods.returns: a text; before Fit it says the line is not yet fitted

classes.name: stzTukeyOneWay
classes.brief: Fits groups of numbers by one-way median polish: a common value, an effect per group and a residual per value.
classes.description: The common value is the median of the group medians, each effect is a group's median minus it, and each residual is a value minus its group's median. Diagnostics does not need Polish: it warns when the spread of the groups grows with their level, with the power to try.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a one-way table of groups of numbers, to be fitted by median polish.

parameters.name: paGroups
parameters.role: at least two groups, each a non-empty list of numbers, of lengths that may differ

methods.name: NumberOfGroups
methods.brief: Returns how many groups the table has.

methods.name: Polish
methods.brief: Fits the groups by medians: a common value, an effect per group and a residual per value.
methods.returns: the fit itself, so calls chain
notes: for 1, 2, 3 / 4, 5, 9 / 10, 12, 20, 30 the common value is 5 and the effects are -3, 0 and 11
warnings: Common, Effects, Residuals and Check raise an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Common
methods.brief: Returns the median of the group medians.
notes: 5 for the groups above
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Effects
methods.brief: Returns each group's median minus the common value.
methods.returns: a list of numbers, one per group
notes: -3, 0, 11 for the groups above
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Residuals
methods.brief: Returns each value minus the median of its group.
methods.returns: a list of lists, one per group, in the order given
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Check
methods.brief: Returns the largest gap between a value and common plus effect plus residual, which is 0 when Data equals Fit plus Residual.
warnings: Raises an error until Polish has run

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns a warning when the spread of the groups grows with their level, from the slope of log fourth-spread on log median.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the groups are called in the rows

warnings: it does not need Polish; the rule is spread_tracks_level and the message gives the suggested power

methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the fit: the common value, the effects, and how well Data equals Fit plus Residual.

classes.name: stzTukeyReexpression
classes.brief: Measures whether a two-way table needs a change of scale, and recommends the power that makes it additive.
classes.description: Each rung of the ladder -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 2 is tried and the slope of the residuals on comparison values is measured; a recommendation fires only when the slope at power 1 passes the threshold 0.5. A table that is the product of a row factor and a column factor gives the log. Known defect: a table holding a zero cannot take the negative powers or the log, and Recommend can then fire with power 1, as is.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a two-way table whose need for a change of scale is to be measured.

parameters.name: paRows
parameters.role: the table as a list of rows, each a list of numbers

methods.name: Threshold
methods.brief: Returns the measured limit that the slope at power 1 must pass for a re-expression to be recommended.

methods.name: NonAdditivity
methods.brief: Returns the slope of the residuals on the comparison values of the table as it stands, and the power it suggests.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys slope, intercept, power and ok
notes: a table of 1, 2, 4 / 2, 4, 8 / 4, 8, 16 / 8, 16, 32, a product of a row and a column factor, gives slope 1 and power 0

methods.name: Ladder
methods.brief: Returns every rung of the ladder of powers, from -1 to 2, with the slope and the residual scale found after raising the table to it.
methods.returns: a list of rows [ power, slope, residual scale, ok ]; ok is 0 for a rung that cannot be taken
notes: for the product table above the log rung, power 0, has slope 0 and residual scale 0
warnings: the engine is crossed once and the answer kept

methods.name: Rung
methods.brief: Returns one row of the ladder.
methods.returns: a list [ power, slope, residual scale, ok ]

methods.name: Recommend
methods.brief: Returns the verdict on the table: the power with the flattest slope when the slope at power 1 passes the threshold, else leave it as it is.
methods.returns: a hash list with the keys power, name, slope, fires and evidence
notes: the product table gives power 0, log, fires 1; an additive table 1, 2, 3 / 2, 3, 4 / 3, 4, 5 / 4, 5, 6 gives power 1, fires 0
warnings: when the table holds a zero the negative powers and the log cannot be taken, and the verdict can come out as fires 1 with power 1, as is, which says to re-express and to leave it at once; seen on two tables

methods.name: LadderTable
methods.brief: Returns the ladder as a text table with one line per rung, a star on the recommended one and the evidence beneath.

methods.name: Diagnostics
methods.brief: Returns a warning when the table is not additive enough, with the evidence and the power to try.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the table is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when the table is left as it is
notes: the rule is non_additive

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence on the table's size and the evidence for or against a re-expression.

classes.name: stzTukeySmoother
classes.brief: Smooths a series resistantly with Tukey's medians-of-three family, Hanning and 4253H, and spots a level shift.
classes.description: The kinds 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R and 3RSR are R's smooth, run in the engine; on 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 all six equal R 4.5.1's output. Hanning and 4253H copy their ends, and 4253H equals a hand computation. Rough returns data minus smooth, and Twice adds the smooth of the rough back. ChangePoint is a verdict with a measured threshold, made from 40 values. A series of fewer than 4 numbers is refused.

methods.brief: Builds a smoother over a series of numbers, kept in the order given, with Tukey's end rule.

parameters.name: paNumbers
parameters.role: the series, a list of at least four numbers

methods.brief: Returns the series as it was given.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many values the series holds.

methods.name: SetEndRule
methods.brief: Chooses how the two end values of a smooth are treated: Tukey's end-point rule, or copied from the data.

parameters.name: pcRule
parameters.role: Tukey or Copy, in any case

notes: on 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2 the first value of Smooth3 is 3 under Tukey and 4 under Copy

extensions.name: SetEndRuleQ
extensions.adds: does what the method does, then returns the object, so the call can be chained

methods.name: EndRule
methods.brief: Returns the end rule in force.

methods.name: SetSplitEnds
methods.brief: Switches on or off the splitting of two-flats at the ends too, as R's do.ends.

parameters.name: pbOn
parameters.role: 1 to split at the ends as well, 0 for not, the default

methods.returns: the smoother itself, so calls chain
notes: it changed nothing on the series 4, 1, 3, 6, 6, 4, 1, 6, 2, 4, 2

methods.name: Smooth
methods.brief: Returns the smooth of a given kind, as R's smooth does with the end rule and the split-ends setting in force.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R or 3RSR, in any case

methods.returns: a list of numbers of the same length as the series

methods.brief: Returns the smooth of a kind with the smooth of its rough added back, as R's twiceit.

parameters.name: pcKind
parameters.role: 3, 3R, S, 3RSS, 3RS3R or 3RSR, in any case

methods.brief: Returns the series smoothed by the weights 1/4, 1/2 and 1/4, with the two end values copied.

methods.name: Smooth4253H
methods.brief: Returns the 4253H smooth: medians of 4 and 2, then 5, then 3, then Hanning, with the ends copied at every stage.

classes.name: stzTukeySummary
classes.brief: Summarises a batch of numbers resistantly: median, hinges, fences, letter values and spread, with no mean and no p-value.
classes.description: The summary is built on medians, so one wild value does not move it. Tukey's fourths are the default hinges and percentile quartiles are available with SetConvention; Why says which is in force. Fences at 1.5 and 3 fourth-spreads give the outside and far-out values, LetterValues gives the ladder from the median outward, and Skewness, TailWeight and Shape read the form of the batch against thresholds measured on seeded batches (a shape verdict is made from 100 values). Diagnostics returns the verdicts in the house rule shape. There is no inference here. Known defect: Skewness, TailWeight, Shape and Diagnostics raise error R2 for a batch of fewer than 5 values. Checked by hand on 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25: median 6, fourths 4 and 10.5, quartiles 4 and 9.75, trimean 6.625, MAD 2.5.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a resistant summary of a batch of numbers, kept in the order given.

parameters.name: paNumbers
parameters.role: the batch, a non-empty list of numbers

methods.name: Numbers
methods.brief: Returns the batch as it was given, in the same order.

methods.name: Count
methods.brief: Returns how many values the batch holds.

methods.name: SetConvention
methods.brief: Chooses which pair of hinges the summary uses: Tukey's fourths, or percentile quartiles.

parameters.name: pcConvention
parameters.role: Fourths, Tukey or Hinges for Tukey's fourths, the default

methods.returns: the summary itself, so calls chain
notes: on 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25 the upper hinge is 10.5 under fourths and 9.75 under percentile
warnings: it changes Hinges, FourthSpread, Fences, Outside and FarOut; Fourths and Quartiles always answer their own pair

extensions.name: SetConventionQ

methods.name: Convention

methods.brief: Returns the lower and upper limits at a multiple of the fourth-spread beyond the hinges, under the convention in force.

methods.brief: Returns the fences at 3 fourth-spreads beyond the hinges.

methods.brief: Returns the values beyond the outside fences, in the order given.

methods.name: FarOut
methods.brief: Returns the values beyond the far-out fences, in the order given.
methods.returns: a list of numbers; empty when none is far out
notes: none for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25, and 100 when the last value is 100

methods.name: LetterValues
methods.brief: Returns the ladder of letter values from the median outward: depth, lower, upper, mid and spread at each level.

parameters.name: pnLevels
parameters.role: how many levels, from 1 for the median alone

methods.returns: a list of rows [ letter, depth, lower, upper, mid, spread ] with letters M, F, E, D, C and on
notes: for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25: M is 6 at depth 4.5, F is 4 and 10.5, E is 3 and 18.5
warnings: the ladder stops when the depth reaches 1, so a batch of 8 gives 4 rows even when 10 are asked

methods.name: Trimean
methods.brief: Returns Tukey's trimean, the mean of the lower hinge, twice the median and the upper hinge.

methods.brief: Returns the letter values laid out as a text table with one line per level and a note on how depths are found.

parameters.name: pnLevels
parameters.role: how many levels, from 1

methods.brief: Returns the median absolute deviation from the median, not scaled to estimate a standard deviation.

methods.name: Biweight
methods.brief: Returns the biweight midvariance, a resistant variance that gives distant values little or no weight.

parameters.name: pnC
parameters.role: the tuning constant in units of the MAD

methods.returns: a number in squared units, a variance and not a standard deviation

methods.name: Skewness
methods.brief: Returns how far the mid-summaries drift from the median, in fourth-spreads; positive leans right.
methods.returns: a number; 0 when the fourth-spread is 0
notes: 0.69 for 2, 4, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 25; a shape verdict is made from 100 values

methods.brief: Returns the sixteenth-spread over the fourth-spread, divided by the Gaussian ratio 2.2745; 1 is Gaussian.

methods.brief: Returns the verdicts on the batch in the house rule shape: each far-out value is an error, a lean or heavy tails a warning.

parameters.name: pcSubject
parameters.role: what the batch is called in the rows

methods.returns: a list of rows [ :rule, :subject, :where, :severity, :message ]; empty when all is well
notes: the rules are far_out, skewed and heavy_tailed, and each message names the measurement and its threshold
warnings: Raises error R2 (index out of range) for a batch of fewer than 5 values, through Shape

methods.name: Why
methods.brief: Returns one sentence naming the convention in force, with the hinges, median, fourth-spread and the counts outside and far out.

classes.name: stzTutor
classes.brief: Asks a learner the question that points at the gap in their attempt, and never writes the answer, without any language model.
classes.description: The tutor keeps three rules: it never writes the learner's code before the exercise is passed, never explains ahead of where the learner is, and never answers before the learner has tried. It keeps them by construction: every reply is built from templates that carry no code, and a last filter blanks any word a right answer calls (ForbiddenWords). What it does: it asks one open question, naming the first step of the exercise that the submitted program does not show, in English, French, Arabic or Hausa; with a course laid on, it names a chapter that is ahead of the learner and does not explain it, and recalls a chapter behind with that chapter's own recap. What it does not do: it does not run or understand the program (it matches words the exercise lists for each step), it does not confirm a solution (only the checker's run does), it answers no question about a method, and it uses no language model and no network. The fr, ar and ha wording is a draft: no native speaker has reviewed it (0 of 35 units reviewed in each language). The programs it reads were run on the desktop only, and no institution has adopted the system yet.
classes.example:
? o1.Ask("Give me the answer")
#--> I will not write the answer for you: that is the one thing a tutor must never do. Try first. Write your attempt and submit it; then I will tell you what is still missing, as a question.
o1.WithCourse(oC)
? o1.Ask("How do I use KnowRelation?")
#--> That belongs to chapter 12, 'Teach a world'. You are on chapter 1, and the later chapter stands on what this one teaches, so I will not explain it yet. Which step of your current exercise is still open?
? o1.FilteredCount()
#--> 0

methods.name: IntentsOf
methods.brief: the intent slot: parsed, recorded, DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED
methods.detail: StzZui's finding 2. The founding inversion says every UI element must trace to at least one intent, and until a phase binds a panel to a flow, every element in every file is an orphan by that test. The request was not to build the binding -- it was to let the FIELD EXIST NOW, so a file written this month is complete when the binding lands rather than needing a pass over every declaration. THE FINDING OFFERED A CHEAPER ANSWER AND IT DOES NOT APPLY. It said to look at Roles() first, because if that were already an intent concept the slot belonged beside it. It is not: Roles() is a closed ARIA vocabulary whose own comment says "a role is NOT a meaning" -- it is the accessibility projection's term, in the family of `display: block`. An intent is the opposite kind of thing. So the finding's own proposal is what is built. NOTHING IS RESOLVED. There is no .zui to resolve against from here, and resolution stays StzZui's. The court checks the SHAPE of a name and nothing else -- an intent this plane cannot find is not an error, because this plane is not where intents live. AND NO WARNING ON AN ORPHAN. Every existing document would raise on every element, which is noise rather than a trail, and the finding did not ask for one. `Orphans()` answers the question instead, so the inversion's test is available the moment anyone wants it. The intents one declaration claims to satisfy, [] when it claims none.

methods.name: Orphans

classes.name: stzUMAP
classes.brief: Draws a map of high-dimensional samples in 2 dimensions from a neighbour graph, using UMAP, and can place new rows in it.
classes.description: Built for LOOKING at data, not for measuring it: distances and cluster sizes in the map mean nothing, and the neighbour count changes the picture, so try two values. The usual pipeline is ReduceWithPCA(30) then Fit. The default of 15 neighbours needs more than 15 samples, so small data needs SetNeighbors first. The neighbour graph is held in the engine after the first Fit: changing the minimum distance, the spread, the epochs or the seed redoes the layout only, while changing the neighbours, the labels or the PCA step drops the graph. LearnFromLabels reweights the graph with known classes, and the separation it gives is an input, not a finding. Unlike t-SNE, Transform places new rows against the frozen map, and LearnMapping makes that exact for the training rows. PreserveDensity adds the densMAP term, and LearnInverse trains a network that goes back from the map to the data.
classes.example:
o1.SetNeighbors(4)
o1.SetEpochs(100)
o1.Fit()
? o1.HasGraph()
#--> 1
? len(o1.Embedding())
#--> 12
? o1.Trustworthiness() > 0.9
#--> 1

classes.name: stzUpdatePlan
classes.brief: Holds the rehearsed operations of a twin as the one artifact that may cross into reality, narrated, ranked for risk and gated.
classes.description: A twin changes only its own memory; reality changes when a plan is executed. The plan can tell its story in plain words (Narration), rank what deserves a second look (Risks), re-check itself against reality as it is now (Validate), let a reviewer reject steps, and say whether its executor may commit at all (MayCommit). Execute then passes each active operation through three gates, the reviewer, the commit scope and the executor's capabilities, before the bridge touches anything, and records every decision in the audit trail. Narrate and rehearse freely; execute with intent.
classes.receiver: v = new stzVirtualFileSystem(); v.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha"); v.DeleteFile("/w/old.txt"); o1 = v.GenerateUpdatePlan()
classes.example:
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 2
? @@( o1.Risks() )
#--> [ [ 2, "DESTRUCTIVE: delete file '/w/old.txt'" ] ]
? @@( o1.MayCommit() )
#--> [ 1, "no executor set -- unguarded (a human at the keyboard)" ]

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Scope

methods.returns: the stzCommitScope; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: SetExecutor

parameters.name: poActor
parameters.role: the stzSystemActor that commits

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: without an executor the plan is unguarded, as a human at the keyboard

methods.name: Executor
methods.brief: Returns who commits the plan.
methods.returns: the stzSystemActor; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: SetGovernance
methods.brief: Sets an optional governance that demands a declared trust posture of the executor and keeps the decision lineage.

parameters.name: poGov
parameters.role: the stzGovernance to consult

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the plan keeps a copy, so read its lineage through Governance

methods.brief: Returns the governance set on the plan.
methods.returns: the stzGovernance; an empty text when none is set

methods.name: AuditTrail
methods.brief: Returns the decisions the plan took when it was executed.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, outcome, type, actor ] rows, the outcome committed or refused
notes: an operation refused by a scope, or rejected by a reviewer, leaves no row

methods.name: NumberOfAuditEntries
methods.brief: Returns how many decisions the audit trail holds.

methods.brief: Marks one operation as rejected by a reviewer, so Execute skips it.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the operation in the plan, from 1

parameters.name: pcBecause
parameters.role: the reason for rejecting it

methods.returns: the plan itself, so calls chain
notes: the reason is kept with the rejection, and the narration shows the operation with an x

methods.name: IsRejected
methods.brief: TRUE if the operation at that position was rejected.

parameters.name: pnIndex
parameters.role: the position of the operation, from 1

methods.name: Narration
methods.brief: Returns the plan as a plain-language story, one numbered line per operation, rejected ones marked.

methods.name: ShowNarration
methods.brief: Prints the narration of the plan.

methods.name: Risks
methods.brief: Returns the operations that deserve a second look: deletions, moves, removed variables and spawned commands.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, warning ] rows; an empty list when none is risky

methods.name: ShowRisks
methods.brief: Prints the risks of the plan, one line each.

methods.name: Validate
methods.brief: Re-checks the plan against reality as it is now, because reality may have moved since the rehearsal.
methods.returns: a list of [ index, warning ] rows for a delete, copy or move whose target or source is absent; an empty list when all is present
notes: it reads reality through the bridge and changes nothing

methods.name: MayCommit
methods.brief: Tells whether the executor could commit this plan at all, without touching anything.

methods.name: Execute
methods.brief: Commits every active operation through the bridge after the reviewer, scope and capability gates, and returns a summary with the log.
methods.returns: a list [ [ committed, n ], [ skipped, n ], [ log, rows ] ], each row [ index, status, text ] with a status COMMITTED, FAILED, REJECTED, REFUSED-BY-SCOPE or REFUSED-BY-GOVERNANCE
notes: refusals reach the security ledger as scope.refused, capability.refused and posture.refused
warnings: this is the one place reality changes, and with a file or environment bridge it writes the disk or the process: rehearse in the twin and read Narration and Risks first; a governance that finds no declared posture refuses the whole plan with a single row of index 0

methods.name: ExecuteStepByStep
methods.brief: Commits the plan as Execute does, printing each row of the log as it comes.
warnings: the same warning as Execute: it commits for real

classes.name: stzUrl
classes.brief: Parses a URL with the engine and gives its parts, with setters that rebuild the text; it never fetches anything.
classes.description: Reach for it to read or change the scheme, user information, host, port, path, query and fragment of one URL, or to move between a file URL and a local file path. The parse is done by the engine (stz_url) and is lazy: a part is read the first time it is asked. The setters change the object in place and rebuild Content from the parts, leaving out ports 80 and 443. It is not a fetcher (stzHttpClient is) and it does not split a query into pairs. A relative reference parses poorly: d.html has an empty path and sub/d.html is read with sub as the host. The class sits in network/stzUrl.ring, which neither stzlib.ring nor stzBase.ring loads, so a caller loads the file itself.
classes.example:
? o1.Host()
#--> example.com
? o1.Port()
#--> 8080
? o1.FileName()
#--> guide.html
o1.SetQuery("a=2")
? o1.Content()
#--> https://bob:pw@example.com:8080/docs/guide.html?a=2#top

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a URL object by parsing the text with the engine; nothing is fetched, and an empty text builds an empty object.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the URL as text, for example https://example.com:8080/a/b.html?x=1#top

notes: text that does not parse is kept as given: IsValid answers FALSE and the parts are empty
warnings: the class is in network/stzUrl.ring but neither stzlib.ring nor stzBase.ring loads that file, so load it by hand before use

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Returns the URL as text; when the object is empty it is rebuilt from its parts.
notes: Url and ToString are the same call

methods.name: SetContent
methods.brief: Replaces the URL by parsing new text; every part is read again from it.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the new URL as text

notes: it does what SetUrl does

methods.name: Copy
methods.brief: Returns a new independent stzUrl built from the current text.

methods.name: SetUrl
methods.brief: Replaces the URL by parsing new text, freeing the previous parse and clearing every cached part.

parameters.name: pcUrl
parameters.role: the new URL as text

notes: the new text is parsed at once, so Host, Path and the others answer for it

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the engine parsed the text as an absolute URL with a scheme and a host.
notes: a relative reference such as d.html or /a/b?q=1 answers FALSE even though its path and query are read; the empty object and text such as :::: also answer FALSE

methods.name: IsEmpty
methods.brief: TRUE if no URL text is held, which is the case for a new empty object and after Clear.
notes: it reads the held text, so an object built from garbage text is not empty

methods.name: Clear
methods.brief: Forgets the URL and every part, leaving an empty object.

methods.name: Scheme
methods.brief: Returns the scheme, the part before ://, as written in the URL.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the case is kept: HTTP://h/ answers HTTP, while IsHttp compares without regard to case

methods.name: SetScheme
methods.brief: Sets the scheme and rebuilds the URL text from the parts.

parameters.name: pcScheme
parameters.role: the new scheme, for example https

notes: IsHttps and the other type checks follow at once

methods.name: Host
methods.brief: Returns the host name, without user information or port.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: Domain and Server are the same call

methods.name: SetHost
methods.brief: Sets the host and rebuilds the URL text; the port, path and query are kept.

parameters.name: pcHost
parameters.role: the new host name

methods.name: Port
methods.brief: Returns the port written in the URL, or -1 when none is written.
notes: a URL without a port answers -1 even for http and https

methods.name: PortWithDefault
methods.brief: Returns the port of the URL, or the given number when no port is written.

parameters.name: nDefault
parameters.role: the number to answer when the URL has no port

notes: 0 counts as no port

methods.name: SetPort
methods.brief: Sets the port and rebuilds the URL text.

parameters.name: nPort
parameters.role: the new port number

notes: the text drops ports 80 and 443 whatever the scheme, so SetPort(80) on https removes the port from Content

methods.name: Path
methods.brief: Returns the path, from the first slash after the host up to the query.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the engine reads a bare reference such as sub/d.html with sub as the host and /d.html as the path; d.html alone has an empty path

methods.name: SetPath
methods.brief: Sets the path and rebuilds the URL text; a missing leading slash is added.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the new path

methods.name: FileName
methods.brief: Returns the last segment of the path, the part after the final slash.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the path is empty
notes: Section(n + 1, n) is out of range; /a/b answers b and an empty path answers an empty text
warnings: Raises error today when the path ends with a slash, on /a/b/ and on / alike: the section call is given an end before its start

methods.name: Query
methods.brief: Returns the query, the text between ? and #, without the question mark.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: HasQuery
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL carries a query after a question mark.

methods.name: SetQuery
methods.brief: Sets the query and rebuilds the URL text; give it without the question mark.

parameters.name: pcQuery
parameters.role: the new query, for example a=2&b=3

methods.name: Fragment
methods.brief: Returns the fragment, the text after #, without the hash sign.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: HasFragment
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL carries a fragment after a hash sign.

methods.name: SetFragment
methods.brief: Sets the fragment and rebuilds the URL text; give it without the hash sign.

parameters.name: pcFragment
parameters.role: the new fragment, for example end

methods.name: UserName
methods.brief: Returns the user name written before the @ of the authority.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none

methods.name: Password
methods.brief: Returns the password written after the colon in the user information.
methods.returns: a text; empty when there is none
notes: the password stays readable in Content and Authority: do not log a URL that carries one

methods.name: UserInfo
methods.brief: Returns the user name and password joined by a colon, or the user name alone.
methods.returns: a text; empty when neither is set

methods.name: SetUserName
methods.brief: Sets the user name and rebuilds the URL text with it before the host.

parameters.name: pcUserName
parameters.role: the new user name

methods.name: SetPassword
methods.brief: Sets the password and rebuilds the URL text; it shows only when a user name or password is set.

parameters.name: pcPassword
parameters.role: the new password

methods.name: SetUserInfo
methods.brief: Sets the user name and password from text of the form user:password, or only the user name when there is no colon.

parameters.name: pcUserInfo
parameters.role: the user information, for example zed:pp

notes: text without a colon clears an earlier password

methods.name: Authority
methods.brief: Returns the user information, host and port joined as user:password@host:port, leaving out what is absent.
notes: it prints a port of 80 or 443 when one is set, which Content leaves out

methods.name: SetAuthority
methods.brief: Sets the user information, host and port from text such as kim:k1@host:9000 and rebuilds the URL text.

parameters.name: pcAuthority
parameters.role: the authority as text

notes: the parts that are given replace the old ones; the others stay
warnings: an authority with no user information or no port does not clear the old ones: SetAuthority("plain.net") on a URL that had kim:k1 and port 9000 leaves kim:k1@plain.net:9000

methods.name: IsRelative
methods.brief: TRUE if the URL has no scheme, as /a/b or d.html.

methods.name: IsLocalFile
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is file, compared without regard to case.
notes: the same test as IsFileScheme

methods.name: IsHttp
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is http, compared without regard to case; https answers FALSE.

methods.name: IsHttps
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is https, compared without regard to case.

methods.name: IsFtp
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is ftp, compared without regard to case.

methods.name: IsFileScheme
methods.brief: TRUE if the scheme is file, compared without regard to case.
notes: the same test as IsLocalFile

methods.name: IsParentOf
methods.brief: TRUE if the given URL lies under this one, by host and path, and is longer.

parameters.name: oOtherUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to test, where anything that is not an object answers FALSE

notes: the scheme, port and query are not compared; http://h/a/b/ is parent of http://h/a/b/c but not of itself, and a path with no final slash also matches a longer name (/a/b matches /a/bc)

methods.name: ResolvedWith
methods.brief: Returns a new stzUrl made of this URL with the path of the given reference put in place of its own.

parameters.name: oRelativeUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to resolve against this one

methods.returns: a new stzUrl; an empty one when the argument is not an object
notes: a path that does not start with a slash is joined to the base path up to its last slash, but only when the engine gave it a path
warnings: resolution is right only for a reference with a leading slash (/c/d.html) or a full URL: d.html parses with an empty path and leaves the base unchanged, and sub/d.html is read with sub as the host so it answers http://plain.org/d.html instead of /a/b/sub/d.html

methods.name: ToLocalFile
methods.brief: Returns the file path of a file URL, without the leading slash before a drive letter.
methods.returns: a text; empty when the scheme is not file
notes: file:///C:/data/x.txt answers C:/data/x.txt and file:///tmp/x.txt answers /tmp/x.txt

methods.name: FromLocalFile
methods.brief: Raises error R19 today instead of returning a file URL for the given path.

parameters.name: pcFilePath
parameters.role: the file path to turn into a file URL

notes: the call that was meant to turn backslashes into slashes is the one that fails
warnings: Raises error R19 today whatever the path, on a drive path with backslashes and on /tmp/y.txt: it calls ReplaceSubstring with two arguments where that method takes a start, an end and a replacement

methods.name: ReconstructUrl
methods.brief: Rebuilds the stored URL text from the scheme, user information, host, port, path, query and fragment.
methods.returns: nothing; read the result with Content
notes: every setter calls it; ports 80, 443 and -1 are left out of the text

methods.name: Swap
methods.brief: Exchanges the URLs of this object and the given one, in place on both.

parameters.name: oOtherUrl
parameters.role: the stzUrl to exchange with, where anything that is not an object does nothing

methods.name: Content
methods.brief: Public methods

methods.name: IsNull
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is null.

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is valid.

methods.name: ToBytes
methods.brief: ToBytes: hex-decode the 32 hex chars (sans hyphens) into a list of 16 byte values. Pure Ring -- no engine call needed.

methods.name: IsValid
methods.brief: TRUE if the object is valid.

methods.name: LastStatus
methods.brief: the HTTP status of the last request (0 = no answer) -- for diagnostics

methods.name: Resolve
methods.brief: the contract ------------------------------------------------------ The value of the field the locator names.
methods.detail: Raises -- never returns "" -- when the vault refuses, has no such secret, has no such field, or does not answer.

methods.name: Has
methods.brief: 1 when the vault holds the path AND the field, 0 otherwise (a refusal or an unreachable vault raises: "cannot tell" is not "absent").

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: A name, as text.

methods.name: Register
methods.brief: seed a value under a vault locator (dev/test). A real resolver would FETCH from the external manager instead of holding values here.

methods.name: Resolve
methods.brief: THE CONTRACT METHOD: given a vault locator, return its value; raise if the vault has no such entry.
methods.detail: Replace this body with a call to your vault client.

methods.name: init
methods.brief: paVectors is a list of equal-length lists of numbers -- one row per vector.

methods.name: SetTrees
methods.brief: More trees means better recall at the same budget, and a bigger index.

methods.name: SetMetric
methods.brief: :Euclidean compares positions, :Cosine compares directions. Text embeddings almost always want :Cosine.

methods.name: SetSeed
methods.brief: The forest is random; the seed makes it reproducible, so a recall figure is a property of the code and not of the run that produced it.

methods.name: Search
methods.brief: The k nearest neighbours, as [ [index, distance], ... ], nearest first. Indexes are 1-based into the vectors this index was built from.
methods.detail: The distance is SQUARED Euclidean over the stored vectors -- squared because the square root changes nothing about the ordering and costs a call per candidate. In :Cosine mode the vectors are unit-length, so the distance is 2 - 2*cos and CosineSimilarityTo() reads it back as a cosine.

methods.name: SearchWithBudget
methods.brief: The same, with the candidate budget stated. Bigger budget, better recall, more work. 0 asks for the default.

methods.name: SearchExact
methods.brief: The exact answer by full scan -- O(n) and the ground truth. Use it on a small corpus, or to measure what the approximate path is missing.

methods.name: RecallAgainstExact
methods.brief: RECALL@K over a set of queries: the fraction of the true k nearest neighbours that the approximate search actually returned. 1.0 means it missed nothing.
methods.detail: THIS IS THE METHOD THAT MAKES THE INDEX HONEST. Measure it on your own vectors before trusting a budget -- recall depends on the data, not just on the settings, and no default can promise a number.

methods.name: CosineFromDistance
methods.brief: Cosine similarity of a stored vector to a query, recovered from the stored distance.
methods.detail: Only meaningful in :Cosine mode, where both are unit vectors and d^2 = 2 - 2*cos.

classes.name: stzVirtualEnvironment
classes.brief: Rehearses changes to variables, the working directory and processes in memory, without touching the real environment.
classes.description: The environment twin of stzVirtualSystem. SetVar, UnsetVar, ChangeDirectory and Spawn read like the real verbs but only record an operation in the twin; Var, HasVar, Cwd and the other readers answer from the twin, not from the process. MirrorReality fills the twin from the live environment first when a rehearsal should start from what is really there. A rehearsal becomes a narrated, reviewable plan with GenerateUpdatePlan, and only executing that plan reaches reality.
classes.example:
o1.SetVar("MODE", "dev")
o1.ChangeDirectory("/srv/app")
o1.Spawn("make test")
? o1.Var("MODE")
#--> dev
? o1.Cwd()
#--> /srv/app
? @@( o1.PendingSpawns() )
#--> [ "make test" ]

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds an environment twin with an empty state, a bridge to the live environment and no history.

methods.name: SetVar
methods.brief: Rehearses setting a variable; the real environment is not touched.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

parameters.name: pcValue
parameters.role: the value, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: a variable mirrored from reality keeps its mirrored origin after its value is set

methods.name: UnsetVar
methods.brief: Rehearses removing a variable; the real environment is not touched.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent name is recorded as an operation and changes nothing in the state

methods.name: ChangeDirectory
methods.brief: Rehearses changing the working directory; no real directory is entered.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the directory to move to, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain

methods.name: Spawn
methods.brief: Rehearses starting a process by queueing its command; nothing is run.

parameters.name: pcCommand
parameters.role: the command line, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: the command only runs if a plan holding it is executed through the real bridge

methods.name: MirrorReality
methods.brief: Replaces the twin state with a copy of the live environment: its variables and its working directory.
methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it reads the real environment, which can hold secrets, so show counts and names, never values

methods.name: Var
methods.brief: Returns the value of a variable in the twin.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: a text; an empty text when the twin has no such variable

methods.name: HasVar
methods.brief: TRUE if the twin holds a variable of that exact name.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.name: OriginOfVar
methods.brief: Returns where a variable of the twin came from.

parameters.name: pcName
parameters.role: the variable name, matched with case

methods.returns: mirrored for one read from reality, virtual for one set in the twin; an empty text when absent

methods.name: Cwd
methods.brief: Returns the working directory of the twin.
methods.returns: a text; empty until mirrored or changed

methods.name: PendingSpawns
methods.brief: Returns the commands queued by Spawn, in order.

methods.name: NumberOfPendingSpawns
methods.brief: Returns how many commands are queued.

methods.name: Vars
methods.brief: Returns every variable of the twin with its origin.
methods.returns: a list of [ name, value, origin ] rows

methods.name: NumberOfVars
methods.brief: Returns how many variables the twin holds.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints one summary line of the twin state: variables, directory and queued commands.

classes.name: stzVirtualFileSystem
classes.brief: Rehearses file and folder changes in memory, so a change can be read, narrated and reviewed before the disk is touched.
classes.description: The file twin of stzVirtualSystem. CreateFile, WriteFile, CreateFolder, DeleteFile, DeleteFolder, CopyFile and MoveFile read like the real file verbs but only record an operation in an in-memory tree; Exists, ContentOf, SizeOf, Paths and the other readers answer from the twin, not from the disk. MirrorFile and MirrorFrom start a rehearsal from what the disk holds. GenerateUpdatePlan turns the rehearsal into a narrated plan, and only executing that plan reaches reality. The twin does not check what a verb names: it accepts a copy of a file it does not hold, which the plan's Validate then flags against the disk.
classes.example:
o1.CreateFolder("/w")
o1.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha")
o1.CopyFile("/w/a.txt", "/w/b.txt")
? o1.Exists("/w/b.txt")
#--> 1
? o1.ContentOf("/w/b.txt")
#--> alpha
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 3

methods.name: init
methods.brief: Builds a file twin with an empty in-memory tree, a bridge to the disk and no history.

methods.name: CreateFile
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a file with its content; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the content, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: a path that already exists has its content replaced, without an error

methods.name: WriteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses writing content into a file; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

parameters.name: pcContent
parameters.role: the content, as text

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it is recorded as a write, so the narration says write rather than create

methods.name: CreateFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses creating a folder; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: the folder that holds it is not required to exist

methods.name: DeleteFile
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a file; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the file

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: an absent path is recorded and changes nothing; the plan flags the delete as destructive and Validate flags a target absent from the disk

methods.name: DeleteFolder
methods.brief: Rehearses deleting a folder; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path of the folder

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: the files below it stay in the twin; delete them first, as the real folder delete refuses a folder that is not empty

methods.name: CopyFile
methods.brief: Rehearses copying a file to another path; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the path of the file to copy

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the path of the copy

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: a source the twin does not hold makes an empty file at the destination, which the disk would refuse; Validate catches it against the disk

methods.name: MoveFile
methods.brief: Rehearses moving a file to another path; the disk is not touched.

parameters.name: pcFrom
parameters.role: the path of the file to move

parameters.name: pcTo
parameters.role: the path it moves to

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: a source the twin does not hold makes an empty file at the destination, which the disk would refuse; the plan flags a move as removing its source

methods.name: MirrorFile
methods.brief: Reads one real file into the twin, marked as mirrored, so a rehearsal starts from what the disk holds.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the real path of the file

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
notes: it reads the disk and changes nothing; the mirrored file is not counted in the history
warnings: an absent file changes nothing

methods.name: MirrorFrom
methods.brief: Replaces the twin tree with the files of one real folder, each marked as mirrored.

parameters.name: pcDir
parameters.role: the real folder to read, one level only

methods.returns: the twin itself, so calls chain
warnings: it reads the disk and changes nothing; whatever the twin held before is dropped

methods.name: Exists
methods.brief: TRUE if the twin holds a file or folder at that path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

notes: it answers from the twin, not from the disk

methods.name: ContentOf
methods.brief: Returns the content the twin holds at that path.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: a text; an empty text for a folder or an absent path

methods.name: SizeOf
methods.brief: Returns the size of the content the twin holds at that path, in bytes.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: a number; 0 for a folder or an absent path

methods.name: OriginOf
methods.brief: Returns where a path of the twin came from.

parameters.name: pcPath
parameters.role: the path

methods.returns: mirrored for one read from the disk, virtual for one born in the twin; an empty text when absent

methods.name: Paths
methods.brief: Returns every path the twin holds, in the order added.

methods.name: NumberOfNodes
methods.brief: Returns how many files and folders the twin holds.

methods.name: TreeView
methods.brief: Returns the twin as text, one line per node with its type, its path and its origin.

methods.name: Show
methods.brief: Prints the number of nodes of the twin and its tree view.

classes.name: stzVirtualOperation
classes.brief: Holds one change to a system as an object, with its type, its parameters, who proposed it and why.
classes.description: A twin rehearses operations and a plan commits them, so the change is a value that can be read, narrated, scoped and audited before anything real happens. The type names the change (create_file, write_file, create_folder, delete_file, delete_folder, copy_file, move_file, set_var, unset_var, change_dir, spawn_process) and the parameters are [ key, value ] pairs. Describe writes it in plain words, Impact lists what it touches for a commit scope, and RequiredKind says what a committer must be allowed to do.

parameters.name: pcType

parameters.name: paParams
parameters.role: a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.brief: Returns the kind of change, in lower case.

methods.name: Params
methods.brief: Returns the parameters the operation was built with.
methods.returns: a list of [ key, value ] pairs

methods.brief: Returns the value of one parameter.

classes.name: stzVirtualSystem
classes.brief: Rehearses changes to a system in memory, keeps their history, and turns them into a plan; the generic core of every twin.
classes.description: A twin drives a state object that can apply an operation to itself and clone itself, and a bridge that is the only thing touching reality. ExecuteOperation applies one operation to the state and records it; UndoLast, CreateSnapshot and RollbackTo move back through the history; GenerateUpdatePlan hands the history to a plan. The twin holds no reference to reality, so nothing real changes until a plan is executed. o1.CreateFile("/w/a.txt", "alpha")
o1.CreateFile("/w/b.txt", "beta")
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 2
o1.UndoLast(1)
? o1.NumberOfOperations()
#--> 1
? o1.History()[1].Describe()
#--> create file '/w/a.txt' (5 bytes)

methods.name: NativeHandle
methods.brief: the platform's own handle
methods.detail: THE OPERATING SYSTEM'S NAME FOR THIS WINDOW: an HWND on Windows, an NSWindow on macOS, an X11 Window id on Linux. 0 when there is none. This exists for ONE reason and it is worth naming, because a raw platform handle is otherwise an invitation to reach around the library: **every accessibility adapter attaches to it.** AccessKit's `accesskit_windows_subclassing_adapter_new`, `accesskit_macos_subclassing_adapter_for_window` and `accesskit_unix_adapter_new` all take exactly this, and there is no route to a screen reader that does not pass through here -- a UIA provider must answer `WM_GETOBJECT` on the window's own handle, so no out-of-process arrangement can substitute. The engine has answered this since GR5; it was simply never exposed. It crosses as an f64, which holds integers exactly to 2^53. Real handles sit far below that on every platform here, but a caller that means to pass it back to a C API should check rather than assume -- the house has already paid once for an f64 boundary, on epoch nanos.

classes.name: stzWorkflow
classes.brief: Models a business process as steps and arrows, or as a state machine, with actors, durations and SLAs, and reports its critical path, bottlenecks and violations.
classes.description: A workflow is a diagram of one of three types. A sequential workflow is built from steps (AddStepXTT) joined by Then, given actors with AssignStepTo and hours with SetStepDuration and SetStepSLA; it then answers CriticalPath, Bottlenecks, SLAViolations and the three Validate methods, which return the house verdict shape. A state machine is built from AddState and AddTransition, and SetExceptionEvents marks the transitions that mean trouble. A bpmn workflow takes the BPMN notation, and ExpandEndingsPerArrival gives each arrow into an end its own marker. ToWorkflow writes the sequential part as .stzflow text and ImportFlow reads it back. The View methods display the diagram and were not run for this reference. Known today: CriticalPath raises an error when no path has a duration above zero, and for every state machine.
classes.example:
o1.AddStep_("pack")
o1.AddStep_("ship")
o1.Then("pack", "ship")
o1.SetStepDuration("pack", 4)
o1.SetStepSLA("pack", 3)
o1.SetStepDuration("ship", 8)
? o1.TotalDuration()
#--> 12
? o1.SLAViolations()[1][:overrun]
#--> 1
? o1.CriticalPath()[:path][2]
#--> ship

classes.name: stzXml
classes.brief: Holds an XML document as text and reads it by path, with the parsing done by the engine.
classes.description: Reach for it to read values out of an XML document without walking a tree: TextAt, NumberAt and AttributeAt take a path such as library/book[2]/title (names joined by /, an optional [n] index counted from 1, no namespace prefix). NodeQ returns a node that remembers a path, so reads can go deeper step by step. The object keeps only the text and parses it again at each read. A document with a DOCTYPE or an ENTITY declaration is refused on purpose, which closes XXE: IsValid answers 0 and every read answers the empty text. To build XML rather than read it, use stzXmlBuilder; its values are escaped.
classes.example:
? o1.Root()
#--> library
? o1.NumberOf("library/book")
#--> 2
? o1.TextAt("library/book[2]/title")
#--> Emma
? o1.AttributeAt("library/book[2]", "id")
#--> b2
? o1.NodeQ("library/book[1]").NumberOf("price")
#--> 1

classes.name: stzXmlBuilder
classes.brief: Builds an XML document element by element, escaping every value so a value cannot change the shape of the document.
classes.description: Reach for it instead of pasting strings: the values given to AddElement and SetAttribute are escaped, so & and < stay text. Open and Close nest elements, and Content gives the finished text, or raises an error while an element is still open. Element and attribute names are written as given and are not checked. The Q forms (AddElementQ, OpenQ, CloseQ) return the builder so calls can be chained; the plain forms return nothing.
classes.example:
o1.AddElement("name", "A & B")
o1.Open("items")
o1.AddElementXT("item", "pen", [ [ "qty", "2" ] ])
o1.Close()
? o1.Content()
#--> <shop><name>A & B</name><items><item qty="2">pen</item></items></shop>

classes.name: stzXmlNode

classes.description: A node holds the document text and the path that reaches the element, nothing else, so it stays valid and can be chained: NodeQ(...) on a node adds to its path. Number raises an error on text that is not a number.
classes.example:
? o1.Path()
#--> library/book
? o1.Attribute("id")
#--> b1
? o1.TextAt("title")
#--> Dune
? o1.NodeQ("price").Number()
#--> 12

classes.brief: Runs map, filter and reduce steps over a list, each chosen by the name of an operation, with the work done in the engine.
classes.description: Reach for it to transform, select or fold a list without writing a loop: Map applies one named operation to every item, Filter keeps the items that pass a named test, Reduce folds the list to one value. The result of Map and Filter is a new list and the held list is unchanged, unless the Q form (MapQ, FilterQ) is used, which keeps the result and returns the object for chaining. A name that is not known does nothing and raises no error. MapIndexed is broken today (it answers the text <list> for each item).
